## v3.66.703 -- MOD-4 (Batch C / M4): TS-safe ffmpeg binary pin

The first Batch-C arch wave, and the smallest (S / low-risk by the scoping plan's own
sizing -- confirmed against source before starting).

FINDING: BD had NO central ffmpeg resolver. Modules each called bare
`shutil.which("ffmpeg")` and simply took whatever was first on PATH. The scope said
7 such modules; the RED-first tests found **8** -- a SECOND ffprobe resolver inside
thumbnail_gen, and integrity.py, which resolved ffprobe at MODULE IMPORT time (so a
pin set afterwards could never have reached it at all). A pin with a hole in it is
worse than no pin: the missed site keeps using the PATH binary while everything else
honours the pin -- the exact mixed-build inconsistency the pin exists to remove.

This is not academic. The project's own footgun list records that the static ffmpeg
build (johnvansickle 7.0.2) SEGFAULTS on HLS+HTTPS and the distro build must be used.
`healthcheck._ffmpeg_capability` already PROBED for that class (does it run; does it
have mpegts + https) -- but a probe only tells you the binary on PATH is bad. It gave
no way to point BD at the good one. This cut is that missing half.

NEW `bulk_downloader/ffmpeg_bin.py` -- the one resolver:
  * order: the `ffmpeg_path` global-config pin (a DIRECTORY holding the build), then
    `shutil.which` -- so an EMPTY pin (the default) is BYTE-IDENTICAL to today;
  * a pin pointing at nothing degrades back to `which` rather than hard-failing:
    resolution fails OPEN, because it is the capability PROBE -- not the resolver --
    whose job is to fail closed on a bad binary;
  * ffprobe is taken from the SAME directory as the pinned ffmpeg (mixing an ffmpeg
    from one build with an ffprobe from another is the very inconsistency being removed);
  * healthcheck now probes THE BINARY BD WILL ACTUALLY RUN -- probing PATH while the
    runner used a pinned build would have reported on the wrong binary entirely.

The pin is a GLOBAL_CONFIG key, NOT a per-site CFG_FIELDS key. Verified empirically
first: adding a global_config key does NOT move the config-surface inventory
(178 -> 178), so it does not trip the count-coupled settings-center pins that took 702
RED on stash. It is also the right home -- which ffmpeg the HOST runs is a deployment
concern, not a per-site one.

9 new import edges (the 8 consumers + ffmpeg_bin -> global_config); baseline re-frozen
in this cut (1303 -> 1312). Non-guard: 7 release guards byte-identical. No route.
RED-first: 24 tests (22 RED on pristine source), including the two controls that found
the missed resolution sites.

STASH-RED FIX (pre-deploy): the refactor MOVED two long-standing TEST SEAMS and the
derived band did not carry the suites that use them.
  * hls_downloader kept its own ffmpeg cache while ffmpeg_bin cached too -- so
    _reset_ffmpeg_cache_for_tests() cleared only ONE, leaving a WARM resolver cache
    that served the old path straight through a patched `shutil.which`. Two caches,
    one reset: the resolver's is now cleared as well.
  * integrity._FFPROBE was DELETED, but it is a long-standing test seam (setting it to
    None must still mean "ffprobe absent"). Restored as a module attribute, now LAZY +
    pin-aware via a sentinel -- so it keeps the seam AND (unlike the old import-time
    resolution) an ffmpeg_path pin actually reaches it.
ROOT CAUSE of the missed band: test_v3_43_63_library_extractors exercises
hls_downloader and test_v3_43_60_coverage_gaps patches integrity._FFPROBE -- under
test-file names that mention NEITHER module. No filename stem and no import edge points
at them, so the deriver was structurally blind. Mechanized as a SEAM-COUPLING rule
(SC-FFMPEG-RESOLUTION) in bd-band-derive, the same shape as the count-coupling rule
that 702 earned.

## v3.66.701 -- F5 Phase 2: browser-in-netns launch wiring (fork 2b)

Wires the 699 shim into the real browser launch path, so a site that opts into
`netns_isolation` now runs the BROWSER itself inside its per-capture namespace
(689 already confined the yt-dlp/gallery-dl subprocesses; Playwright spawns
Chromium itself, so there was no argv to wrap).

Composition (the open question from 700), settled by a LIVE probe on a real
kernel with the real stealth Chromium -- not by reading:

  * `executable_path=` CANNOT be passed through cloakbrowser: it calls
    `pw.chromium.launch(executable_path=binary, **kwargs)`, so the same kwarg
    raises `TypeError: got multiple values`. The shim therefore cannot replace
    cloak's binary that way.
  * The seam is cloakbrowser's own `CLOAKBROWSER_BINARY_PATH` local-binary
    override: cloak is pointed at the shim, and the REAL cloak binary is handed
    to the shim via `NETNS_BROWSER_BIN` in the per-launch `env`. The shim WRAPS
    cloak's stealth Chromium; it never replaces it.
  * Playwright backend: `executable_path=<shim>` directly (a real param there).
    A cloak->playwright fallback re-plans, so a fallback can never silently drop
    isolation.

Thread-safety: `CLOAKBROWSER_BINARY_PATH` is read in-process at launch and BD's
workers are THREADS, so the override window is lock-serialized and always
restored, and the lock is only taken once isolation has actually been used --
a site that does not opt in pays nothing and its launch path is unchanged. The
shim also now passes through (`exec "$NETNS_BROWSER_BIN"`) when `NETNS_NS` is
unset; when it IS set the exec still always goes through `ip netns exec`, so a
missing namespace fails closed rather than escaping.

Lifetime: the browser is owned by the WORKER, not by one URL, so `_worker_loop`
brackets its whole body in `capture_netns` (an ExitStack, torn down in the
existing finally AFTER the browser closes -- tearing the ns down under a live
browser would strand it). `NetnsRequiredError` exits the worker WITHOUT ever
launching an un-isolated browser (mirrors the VPN fail-closed guard).

Live-validated in-sandbox (CAP_NET_ADMIN + iproute2/nftables): 8 browser PIDs
inside the ns (net inode != host), `page.goto` -> HTTP 200 through the namespace,
`navigator.webdriver` false + spoofed UA (stealth survived the wrap), the env
override clean afterwards, and a NON-isolated launch immediately after -> 200.

Env naming stays `NETNS_*` (the 700 lesson); the env-tranche gates pass.
New import edge runner -> netns_isolation; import-graph baseline re-frozen in
this cut (1301 -> 1303). Non-guard: 7 release guards byte-identical.

## v3.66.700 - 700: FIX the v3.66.699 stash RED -- drop the BD_ prefix from the netns shim env vars. 699 named the Phase-2 browser-shim env vars BD_NETNS / BD_BROWSER and went RED on stash against TWO gates: test_v3_66_319_env_tranche_4_3d (open env_vars remain: BD_NETNS, BD_BROWSER) and test_v3_66_305_config_danger (open_runtime_tunable count bumped). ROOT CAUSE, and a correction to the received env-tranche lore: tools/config_surface_inventory.py does NOT only scan os.environ.get("BD_...") read sites -- it ALSO does a bare token-boundary scan for any BD_[A-Z0-9_]+ literal anywhere in a .py file (line ~126). So a BD_* name inside a STRING (the shim script body) or as a DICT KEY is registered as an operator-tunable env var even though nothing ever reads it via os.environ. FIX: these two names are an internal BD<->shim calling convention (closer to argv than to configuration) and are never operator-tunable, so the BD_ prefix is dropped entirely (NETNS_NS / NETNS_BROWSER_BIN) rather than classifying them deploy-only -- removing the tripwire at the root. New guard test freezes it: no BD_* token may appear in netns_isolation.py. Both previously-failing gates are sandbox-runnable and now GREEN (8/8); full netns family 57/57. No functional change to the shim mechanism (still exec ip netns exec, quoted argv passthrough, env-supplied ns+binary). No new route, no new import edge, no declared config field.

## v3.66.699 - 699 (F5 Phase 2, fork 2b): launch the BROWSER inside a per-capture netns [safety]. Phase 1 (689) routed the yt-dlp/gallery-dl SUBPROCESS fallbacks through the netns engine, but the browser -- the primary capture path -- still egressed un-isolated, because Playwright spawns Chromium itself via its in-process API (launch_persistent_context/chromium.launch), leaving no argv to wrap with ip netns exec. FORK RESOLVED (operator confirmed 2b, avoiding 2a in-process setns and its much heavier CAP_SYS_ADMIN): exploit Playwrights executable_path seam (already used by cloak.py) and point it at a tiny shim that re-execs the real browser binary inside the namespace -- exec ip netns exec "$BD_NETNS" "$BD_BROWSER" "$@". Playwright spawns the shim believing it is the browser; exec (not fork) keeps Playwrights child handle pointing at the browser so its lifecycle management still works. New primitives: netns_browser_shim (pure script source), write_browser_shim (idempotent, chmod 0755), browser_launch_env (BD_NETNS/BD_BROWSER; empty dict when either is missing -> caller launches normally, unchanged path). The ns name and browser path arrive via the ENVIRONMENT, never interpolated into the script body, so no caller-supplied text is baked into an executable; "$@" is quoted because Playwright passes ~40 args (several containing =) and unquoted $@ would re-split them. Needs only CAP_NET_ADMIN. LIVE-VALIDATED against a real kernel before this cut: the netns substrate (686 default-drop, 697 move-into-ns + tunnel default route, 698 /etc/netns/<ns>/resolv.conf override + teardown cleanup) all execute rc=0 in the exact generated order, and a process launched through the shim reports the target netns identity, sees only lo (no eth0), and receives argv unmodified. Wiring the shim into runner_browser._launch_browser is the next cut (needs a live browser to validate). No new route, no new import edge, no declared config field; 686/689/697/698 regression suites unchanged (48/48).

## v3.66.698 - 698 (F5 per-ns DNS): complete controlled egress with a per-namespace resolver [safety]. 697 moved a WireGuard tunnel into a per-capture netns and made it the only route, but a fresh netns does NOT inherit the host /etc/resolv.conf -- a tunnel-confined process could egress but not resolve names (the standard wg-in-netns DNS gotcha). This writes the ns own /etc/netns/<ns>/resolv.conf (the standard netns DNS override, read when a process enters the ns) so name resolution also goes through the tunnel. EgressSpec gains an optional dns IP; egress_commands appends the resolv.conf write AFTER the tunnel is up; ns_resolv_conf_path exposes the path. The dns value is IP-validated (ipaddress) before any interpolation -- a mis-typed value can never smuggle shell content into the write. teardown_commands/destroy gain an optional egress= param so a per-ns resolv dir is removed on teardown (netns resolv.conf files outlive the ns otherwise); default None keeps teardown byte-identical (686 exact-equality invariant holds). capture_netns threads egress through create+destroy end-to-end. egress_spec_from_cfg reads the optional dns from the undeclared backend-only cfg. Pure/unit only via the injected runner; LIVE exercise deferred with the rest of F5 (CAP_NET_ADMIN). 686/689/697 regression suites unchanged. No new route, no new import edge, no declared config field.

## v3.66.697 - 697 (F5 controlled egress): route a per-capture netns through a WireGuard tunnel (VPN-into-ns) [safety]. The @686 engine created an egress-LESS namespace (loopback + nftables default-drop) so a confined capture could not reach the network; this adds the unbuilt piece that lets an opted capture egress ONLY through the VPN. New EgressSpec (wg_iface/wg_conf/address/mtu) + egress_commands (pure argv for the canonical wireguard.com/netns sequence: create the wg iface in the init ns, wg setconf, MOVE it into the ns, assign the tunnel address, up, default route -- wg0 becomes the ns only route so it is fail-closed by construction, tunnel-down halts all traffic, no killswitch needed). setup_commands/create gain an egress= param (supersedes default-drop when given; byte-identical @686 default-drop when omitted). egress_spec_from_cfg reads the UNDECLARED backend-only cfg netns_isolation.egress:{...} (invisible to the config/env inventory; incomplete -> None, degrade to default-drop). capture_netns wires it end-to-end, posture-aware + fail-closed. Pure/unit only (injected runner, no root); the LIVE exercise (a real wg tunnel in a real ns) needs CAP_NET_ADMIN on the stash service and is deferred like every runtime-gated F5 piece. Fork-independent foundation for Phase 2/3. No new route, no new import edge, no declared config field; 686/689 regression suites unchanged.

## v3.66.688 - F6 bg_scheduler idle scaling (adaptive poll cadence: idle_poll_interval/note_activity/is_idle; back off when idle, wake-on-demand)

Batch A / F6 (closes Batch A). The bg_scheduler coordinator polled on a
fixed 30s cadence. It now scales that cadence with activity: fast
(ACTIVE_POLL_S=30) while work is recent, backing off to IDLE_POLL_S=300
while idle (fewer wakeups). The idle cadence is capped at the fastest
registered task interval (300s) so an idle back-off never starves a due
task.

  * idle_poll_interval(last_activity, now) -- pure policy;
  * note_activity() -- public wake-on-demand signal: refreshes the active
    window AND wakes a sleeping coordinator immediately so new work is
    picked up without waiting out the back-off;
  * _mark_activity() -- internal refresh used by _run_one (a task firing
    keeps the cadence active without self-waking / re-polling);
  * is_idle() + new status() fields (idle, poll_interval_seconds,
    seconds_since_activity) for operator visibility.

The loop's inter-poll wait is now interruptible via a wake Event; stop()
also sets it so an idle back-off never delays shutdown. No route/DB/config
or import-graph change.

cadence_hours; this exposes them as an iCalendar feed an operator can
import into or subscribe from any calendar client.

New pure generator capture_schedules.schedules_to_ics builds an RFC-5545
VCALENDAR with one recurring VEVENT per schedule: RRULE
FREQ=HOURLY;INTERVAL=cadence_hours, DTSTART from next_run_ts, SUMMARY from
the label (falling back to "Capture: <site_id>"), STATUS CONFIRMED/CANCELLED
from enabled, and an escaped DESCRIPTION. Schedules with cadence_hours <= 0
are skipped. No new dependency (icalendar is NOT required) -- correct CRLF
line endings, RFC-5545 TEXT escaping, and 75-octet line folding are done in
pure string code.

New route GET /api/schedules/export.ics (app_schedules) serves it as
text/calendar with a Content-Disposition attachment, mirroring the existing
activity export.csv download. No DB/config-schema change.

## v3.66.686 - F5 per-capture netns isolation engine (netns_isolation.py: create/destroy/run_in_netns/isolated + nft drop-egress; sandbox-verified, launch-routing is a CAP_NET_ADMIN-gated follow-on)

Batch A / F5. Defensive per-capture network-namespace isolation [safety],
NOT evasion. A fresh Linux netns has only loopback and no routes, so a
process confined to one cannot egress on the host clear interface. New
standalone module netns_isolation ships the reusable MECHANISM:

  * netns_name -- deterministic, netns-safe naming;
  * setup_commands / teardown_commands / netns_exec_argv -- pure command
    generation (create ns, bring loopback up, install an nftables
    default-drop output policy as defence in depth; delete);
  * create / destroy / run_in_netns / isolated (context manager) -- run
    through an INJECTED command runner (default subprocess.run) so the unit
    suite needs no root. create is FAIL-CLOSED: if any step errors (e.g. no
    CAP_NET_ADMIN) the partial ns is torn down and False is returned;
  * site_wants_isolation -- the opt-in config flag.

Verified end to end in a root sandbox: a real integration test creates an
isolated ns, asserts it has no default route, runs a command inside it, and
tears it down (auto-skips when not root / no iproute2, so the suite stays
portable -- on an unprivileged host it skips rather than failing).

Standalone module (not yet imported by the runner): no route/DB/config or
import-graph change. Routing the actual browser/download launch through
netns_exec_argv is a deliberate follow-on -- it is a deep launch-path change
AND requires the service to hold CAP_NET_ADMIN on the deploy host (the Linux
kill-switch is process-level today precisely to avoid needing it).

## v3.66.685 - F4 rotating proxy pool with health checks (proxy_pool.py: select/record_result/probe_pool; opt-in via proxy_pool site-cfg, wired in runner_transport._download_proxy_url; egress-resilience only)

Batch A / F4. Egress-resilience infrastructure -- the same class as the
shipped per-site egress and VPN kill-switch, NOT anti-bot evasion (the
pool does not touch captcha/flaresolverr/behavior-sim surfaces).

Per-site egress offered a single static `proxy`. New module proxy_pool
adds an opt-in rotating POOL: select_proxy round-robins over the currently
healthy members; health is tracked by cooldown after failures
(record_result, N consecutive failures -> cooldown window) and by an
active health-check sweep (probe_pool, using an INJECTED probe function so
the unit suite never touches the network). healthy_urls reports the live
set; default_probe is the one I/O helper (a TCP-connect check) for a
production sweep. The module is pure and network-free apart from
default_probe; state is a plain dict the caller owns/persists.

Wired into runner_transport._download_proxy_url: an explicit per-site
`proxy` still wins; when none is set and a `proxy_pool` list is configured,
a healthy member is selected and acts as the explicit proxy (so it wins
over the tunnel exactly as a static proxy does). The VPN fail-closed
posture is untouched. Opt-in -- with no `proxy_pool` configured the
behavior is byte-identical to before. No route/DB/config-schema change.

## v3.66.684 - F8/PIT template-set restore-to-known-good-date (selector_versions.plan_set_restore/restore_set_to_date; user_templates.restore_template_set single-writer apply)

Batch A / F8. selector_versions already ships PER-TEMPLATE version history
and revert (record_template_version / list_versions / revert_selectors).
This adds the SET-WIDE point-in-time restore: roll every template back to
the state it was in as of a given date.

New pure/read-only helpers in selector_versions (module posture: never
raise, write nothing): plan_set_restore (for every template, choose the
latest version recorded at or before the cutoff timestamp; returns a
reviewable {as_of, restore[], skipped[]} plan sorted by template_id;
templates with no version at/before the cutoff are skipped, not emptied)
and restore_set_to_date (the {template_id: selectors} convenience view).

The apply half, user_templates.restore_template_set, computes the plan and
(unless dry_run) re-saves each template's chosen historical selector block
through save_user_template -- the SINGLE WRITER -- preserving
name/description/patterns and swapping only learned. Non-destructive: a
template absent from the current store, or with no pre-cutoff version, is
skipped and never created or emptied. Library-only (consistent with the
routeless per-template revert); no route/ENDPOINT_CATALOG/DB/config change.

## v3.66.683 - F1/CAP-1 record-time selector auto-narrow (auto_detect; default-on, opt-out via record_time_narrow cfg key)

Batch A / F1. api_prune_selectors narrows a site's learned selectors by
RUNTIME miss-ratio (needs accumulated hit/miss data). This adds the
complementary RECORD-TIME step: a fresh detection emits a spray of
candidate selectors per role with no runtime data yet, and these reduce
that spray to a minimal, stable set using structural signals only, so a
new site starts lean instead of carrying redundant/fragile candidates.

New pure/offline helpers in auto_detect (reuse the in-module
_looks_hashed_class; no new import edge): narrow_selectors (dedupe by
structural shape -> drop fragile candidates when a stable one survives ->
cap to max_keep; non-destructive: a non-empty input never yields an empty
kept set) and narrow_detected_block (applies it to row_selectors /
trigger_selectors; keeps a parallel-list url_attribute index-aligned to
the surviving rows per the merge_learned v3.43.10 alignment invariant;
scalar roles untouched; does not mutate its input).

Wired into _apply_detected_selectors: detected login/download blocks are
narrowed before merge_learned. Default-on; opt out per-site with
cfg["record_time_narrow"] = False. The dropped candidates are recorded
under cfg["_record_time_narrow"] for audit/reversibility. No route, DB,
or config-schema change.

## v3.66.681 - B2 batch: template federation (P5) + OIDC/SSO login (P6)

FE + route-ceremony cut batching two features:

- P5 C7-11.2 template federation: peers exchange site templates as signed,
  redacted bundles (reusing marketplace.sign_bundle/verify_signature/_redact).
  Received templates land in a review-on-receive queue (fed_pending_templates)
  and only reach the store on operator approval, which writes a NON-DESTRUCTIVE

  HMAC); pending_templates (GET); pending_review (operator POST, CSRF). New FE
  review panel in Cluster. All heavy imports function-local (no new import edge).
- P6 C7 SSO/OIDC: single configurable OIDC provider via standard discovery
  (config keys oidc_enabled/issuer/client_id/client_secret/redirect_uri/scopes;
  client_secret auto-redacted by the shared secret SoT). New oidc module +
  app_oidc blueprint: /api/auth/oidc/status|login|callback. id_token verified
  with authlib.jose against the provider JWKS; OIDC subject provisioned as a BD
  operator on first login. New "Sign in with SSO" button on the login page.
  Adds authlib (imported function-locally; app runs without it when SSO is off).

## v3.66.668 - Phase 12.2: redaction/SSRF critical-predicate mutation gate

A dependency-free, targeted realization of the "mutation gate on critical paths"
intent -- NOT a mutmut integration (no new shipped dep, no slow per-mutant full
run). New tools/redaction_mutation_gate.py verifies, for each security-critical
predicate, that it is BOTH toothed and load-bearing:

- TEETH: the intact predicate rejects a known-bad input (not a stub).
- LOAD-BEARING: mutating the predicate to its INSECURE constant makes a
  downstream enforcement probe REGRESS (secret leaks / host allowed) -> the
  mutant is killed. A mutation that changes nothing = the protection path does
  not depend on the predicate (dead/bypassed/toothless) -> SURVIVED -> gate fails.

Targets: the redaction SoT key-secret predicate (capture_artifact_redact.
_kv_key_is_secret, probed through redact_value -- KILLED) and the SSRF host guard
(provider_resolve_impl._common._is_safe_public_host -- teeth-only, enforcement
needs request context). Each mutation is restored in a finally so the gate never
leaves a predicate weakened. Extend via the CRITICAL registry.

Scoped down from the original 12.2 framing: mutmut (needs a new dep + slow gate)
and the corpus-replay redaction diff (needs real capture artifacts absent from
the release tree) stay DEFERRED. Tools-only; no source/route/guard/SPA change.
RED-by-construction (new tool) -> GREEN 5/5, incl. self-teeth (the gate detects a
seeded surviving mutant + a toothless predicate).

## v3.66.667 - CAP-3: saved-search -> scheduled-export chaining

The last deferred FEAT-MAX feature that was genuinely sandbox-buildable. A
scheduled export can now be LINKED to a saved search via a new nullable
scheduled_exports.source_saved_search column (lazy-migrated; null => today's
behavior, byte-identical). When set, the export resolves its rows through the
SAME FTS path the saved search uses (db_search_fts(query, site_id, status)) at
run time, so the export tracks the LIVE search criteria -- edit the search and
the export follows -- instead of a frozen filter_json snapshot.

- saved_searches.criteria_for(id) returns {query, site_id, status} or None
  (missing/disabled).
- scheduled_exports._resolve_source_rows(id) -> FTS rows, or None -> caller
  falls back to filter_json (FAIL-OPEN if the search is deleted).
- exporters (to_csv/to_json/to_ndjson/to_m3u) gain an optional rows= override
  (backward-compatible: rows=None -> existing filter_dict path).
- /api/scheduled_exports/add accepts source_saved_search (extends the existing
  route; no new route). Backend-only; no guard/route/import-edge/FUNCTION_INDEX
  (function-local imports). RED 7/7 -> GREEN; export + saved-search families clean.

## v3.66.666 - 665 stash-RED corrective: parity ledger + gui_parity regen fix

665's capture went RED (5 failures), all derived-artifact drift from the 665
cut, no code-logic defect. Fixed here:

- CFG_FIELDS parity (3 failures): the two new site_keys added in 665
  (ytdlp_concurrent_fragments, download_rate_limit) were runtime-tunable but not
  ledgered gui_exposure=full, so they showed as "open". Both are gui-safe
  (non-gated) and already render in the schema-driven site editor, so they are
  now ledgered "full" in reports/config_gui_manifest.json. This drops
  open_runtime_tunable back to 0, fixing test_v3_66_305 (danger/exposure
  baseline) and test_v3_66_310 (inventory + manifest ledger all site_keys full).
- gui_parity regen drift (2 failures): the 665 build's gui_parity_inventory.json
  shipped MISSING scrape_listing.api_scrape_listing. Root cause: bd-cut's step-3
  regen runs `python3 tools/gui_parity_inventory.py` under bare system python
  WITHOUT the prestaged PYTHONPATH, so httpx is absent and the httpx-dependent
  scrape_listing blueprint fails to register (989 rules instead of 990) - the
  route is silently dropped from the inventory. On stash (full venv, httpx
  present, 990 rules) this surfaced as test_v3_66_302 itemset drift
  (only-regen=[scrape_listing]) and test_route_index_in_sync (its spa_wired join
  reads the broken inventory). Regenerated gui_parity_inventory.json + ROUTE_INDEX
  under the venv/prestaged PYTHONPATH so scrape_listing is retained; rebuild runs
  bd-cut with PYTHONPATH=/tmp/prestaged_site_packages so the regen stays correct.

LESSON: adding a CFG_FIELDS site_key requires ledgering it full in
config_gui_manifest.json (band test_v3_66_305 + test_v3_66_310); and all index
regens must run under the service venv / prestaged PYTHONPATH, never bare python3,
or httpx-gated routes (scrape_listing) drop. Both added to the route/CFG_FIELDS
band going forward. No guard/route/import-edge touch; the 665 feature code is
unchanged.

## v3.66.665 - FEAT-MAX 2.2/2.5: yt-dlp segment-parallel + bandwidth cap

Threaded two config-driven flags into the yt-dlp fallback command builder
(_build_ytdlp_cmd), the sole yt-dlp cmd path:

- --concurrent-fragments N (config key ytdlp_concurrent_fragments): segment-
  parallel HLS/DASH downloads. Threaded only when N>1; N<=1 omits it (yt-dlp's
  default of 1), keeping the cmd byte-identical for unconfigured sites.
- --limit-rate RATE (config key download_rate_limit): per-download bandwidth
  cap, a yt-dlp rate string (e.g. "2M", "500K"). Threaded only when the value
  matches a strict numeric[+K/M/G] pattern; any other value (empty, flag-
  looking, shell metacharacters) is dropped -> unlimited, so a config value can
  never smuggle a flag into yt-dlp's option surface (mirrors F-RUN01-02).

Both keys are registered in CFG_FIELDS + DEFAULTS (inert defaults 0 / "") so
the operator can set them through the normal config-save API and they surface
in the read-only Settings Center (schema auto-derived from CFG_FIELDS). Backend
only; no guard/route/import-edge touch. Settings Center field counts move
232->234 unique / 205->207 editable. gallery-dl left out of scope (no segment
concurrency; rate cap deferred). RED 7/7 -> GREEN; builder + settings-center
families regression-clean.

## v3.66.664 - MNT-3: flake quarantine (isolation-first) + 663 pin fix

MNT-3 quarantine-skip half, choice B (isolation-first). Two tiers in run_tests.py, both
INERT by default -- the release band (capture.sh) sets neither env var, so the on-stash full
suite always runs everything and never suppresses a test:
  Tier 1 (default, safe): _quarantine_files reads the flake registry; a file with a CHRONIC
    flake is pre-isolated to the serial lane (reusing the pinned-file mechanism via
    _partition_serial) so the parallelism collision that makes it flake can't recur. The test
    still RUNS, still counts, and a real failure in isolation still fails -- nothing is masked.
    Active only when BD_FLAKE_REGISTRY names a populated registry.
  Tier 2 (opt-in): _load_skip_manifest reads a file-level quarantine manifest
    ({"<file.py>": {reason, expires}}); under BD_QUARANTINE_SKIP=1 only, listed files are
    skipped entirely, each reported loudly (SKIP (quarantined: ...)), and every entry carries
    an expiry so a stale skip auto-lifts -- never a silent, permanent skip. This turns the
    "NEVER run test_perf_lab / nav_guard in sandbox" tribal rule into data.
Auto-skip of chronic flakes (option C) was deliberately NOT built -- masking risk.

Also folds the 663 stash-RED fix: test_v3_66_302_gui_parity_reconcile's gated blueprint count
pin for data_layer 14 -> 15 (the OBS-3 /api/data/storage_tiers route from 662). That pin is
not in the route-count gate's cross-check sources, so a data_layer route add must update it
explicitly.

## v3.66.663 - POS-1: operator-selectable backup-encryption scope

backup.py already did opt-in, operator-passphrase (PBKDF2->Fernet, nothing stored),
whole-archive encryption (BDBK magic wrapper). This adds the operator-selectable SCOPE:
create_backup(encrypt_scope="sensitive") encrypts only the secret/session members in-place
(secrets*.json, vault_tokens.json, cookies/*, state/*) -- ciphertext under their normal
arcnames -- leaving the rest of the backup plaintext + directly inspectable. The manifest
carries {encryption: {scope, algo, salt, iterations, members}} so restore_backup knows which
members to decrypt; it derives the key from the manifest salt and validates the passphrase
up front against one member so a wrong/missing passphrase fails closed BEFORE any file is
written (no partial restore). Per-member plaintext sha256 checksums (CAP-4) still verify
after decrypt. scope="all" (default) keeps the whole-wrap behavior; no passphrase = plaintext
(opt-in preserved); the passphrase is never stored. /api/backup/create threads encrypt_scope
from the request (validated to all|sensitive); sensitive-scope output stays a valid .zip
(only whole-wrap becomes .bdbk).

## v3.66.662 - OBS-3: read-only storage-tier dashboard

storage_rebalance.inventory() already returned per-path occupancy/headroom (total/free/used
GB, free_pct, mount_id, file_count), but the only surfaces were POST /api/storage_rebalance/*
(operator supplies paths) and GET /api/storage/validate (single path) -- no read-only fleet
view. New collect_storage_tiers() gathers the configured download dirs from the live s_cfg
(deduped, blanks dropped, fail-open), runs inventory over them, and returns per-tier
occupancy + fleet totals (total/free/used GB, pct_free) + low-headroom flags (a tier under
10 GB or under 10% free). Exposed via GET /api/data/storage_tiers, the existing data-layer
collector pattern (thin d_storage_tiers -> _safe(collect_storage_tiers)). No writes, no
rebalance -- surfacing only; structural counts + GB, no secrets. Read-only GET, route
ceremony (baseline 989->990).

## v3.66.661 - healthcheck yt-dlp freshness shape fix (657 loose end)

healthcheck._check_ytdlp treated ytdlp_updater.current_version()'s return as a dict
(info.get("age_days")), but current_version() returns a version STRING (or None) -- so a
normal install raised 'str' object has no attribute 'get', caught and degraded to a noisy
WARN that became visible in the boot selftest once 657 folded this probe into startup. Now
reads ytdlp_updater.status_dict() (the purpose-built {installed, version, age_days, stale}
dict), so the check reports real freshness (e.g. "yt-dlp is 114 days old - consider
updating") instead of the attribute-error leak, and the exception fallback reports the
exception type name rather than its raw message. Pure robustness; no runtime behavior change
beyond correct severity + a clean message.

Backlog note: the rest of the IDEA-HARDEN reliability items premise-checked as already built
-- ROB-2 (migrations.py dry_run + _backup_db_before_migration + abort), ROB-4
(test_seeded_orphan_is_recovered_after_restart), ROB-5 (test_critical_state_writers_commit_
atomically "locks the ROB-5 invariant"), MNT-2 (covered by the general import_graph_gate);
CAP-4's archive integrity is already handled by wacz_export's datapackage.json per-resource
SHA-256 + eol_export verify_chain.

## v3.66.660 - MNT-3: flake-registry expiry (the "expiring" half)

The flake registry (run_tests._{load,update,save}_flake_registry + _chronic_flakes) tracked
flakes with count/first_seen/last_seen and surfaced chronic ones, but nothing EXPIRED stale
entries -- a test that stopped flaking lingered in the registry forever. The MNT-3 spec
requires the quarantine to be "visible + expiring, never silent". New
_prune_flake_registry(registry, now, max_age_days) drops entries whose last_seen is older
than the TTL (default 30d, BD_FLAKE_MAX_AGE_DAYS), wired into the update flow
(load -> update -> PRUNE -> save) so the registry self-cleans and a long-quiet test ages
out. Pure function: never mutates the input, never raises, treats a malformed/last_seen-less
entry as fresh (kept), and max_age_days <= 0 disables pruning. MNT-1 (dead-route gate) was
already enforced by test_nav_reachability (SPA orphans + server-page reachability + external
nav). Runner-only change; no app runtime effect.

## v3.66.659 - POS-4: notify path-secret mask + windows.bat ffmpeg check

POS-4: notify_apprise._safe_url_display masked userinfo credentials but left PATH-embedded
secrets visible (path[:60]). Several apprise services carry the secret in the path, not
userinfo -- Discord (discord://webhook_id/webhook_token), Slack (slack://TokenA/TokenB/...),
generic webhooks -- so a failed-send log line could leak the token. The masker now also
masks path segments >= 16 chars (a token) while keeping short segments (numeric chat IDs,
channel names) readable, so an operator can still tell destinations apart. POS-3 (egress
fail-closed selftest) was already built (selftest.check_egress_fail_closed).

windows.bat: install_windows.bat installed Python deps + Playwright but never checked for
ffmpeg, so a fresh Windows box silently fails the v3.66.657 ffmpeg_hls startup selftest and
real HLS/TS downloads. Added a non-fatal ffmpeg presence check-and-warn step (where ffmpeg;
ASCII, CRLF, escaped-paren lint-clean) that points to winget install Gyan.FFmpeg. Surfaces
the gap at install time; never blocks the install.

## v3.66.658 - OBS-2: expose the per-route p50/p95 latency panel

dev_metrics.route_percentiles() (the "OBS-2 core" -- {rule: count/p50/p95/max} over the
recent-request ring buffer) already existed but had NO consumer, so the p50/p95 timing-panel
data was unreachable. This exposes it via a thin read-only dev route
GET /api/dev/route_timing, delegating to a new dev_suite.route_timing() wrapper that sorts
the percentile map by p95 -- mirroring the existing slow_endpoints / error_rate pattern
exactly (same dev_bp, _dev_mode_guard, dev_suite delegation). OBS-4 (per-site capture-success
trend) was already served by /api/hourly_stats over db_hourly_success_rate, so only OBS-2's
route was missing. No new import edge (perf_metrics->dev_metrics already baselined via
slow_endpoints; app_dev_obs->dev_suite already present). Read-only GET, backend-only.

## v3.66.657 - ROB-3: startup selftest covers ffmpeg HLS/TS + extractor freshness

The startup selftest battery (selftest.run_all) lacked two health signals that
healthcheck.py already computes on-demand: ffmpeg HLS/TS-over-https capability (the
static-ffmpeg segfault / missing-mpegts-or-https class) and yt-dlp extractor freshness
(yt-dlp goes stale fast, breaking sites). This folds both into the startup battery via two
thin selftest checks -- check_ffmpeg_hls and check_extractor_freshness -- that DELEGATE to
the proven healthcheck._check_ffmpeg / _check_ytdlp probes (no probe logic reimplemented),
map their {severity, message} shape to selftest's _result shape, and are best-effort (a probe
blow-up degrades to WARN, never propagates at startup). So a broken ffmpeg build or a stale
extractor is now caught at boot, not only when the health page is opened. ROB-3's other asks
(orphaned tempfiles, stale locks, disk headroom) were already in the battery. New edge
selftest -> healthcheck (baseline re-frozen). Read-only, backend-only.

## v3.66.656 - IDEA-HARDEN closers: CAP-1 warm-up trigger + OBS-1 collect-loop budget

Two hardening closers in one cut. Premise-check found ROB-1 already built @602 (WAL at
init + first-run-OK selftest) and OBS-1's request-budget substantially built @641 (hard
REQUEST_BUDGET_MS ceiling + after-hook over-budget flagging), so only two gaps remained.

CAP-1 (warm-up trigger): aiassist.warmup()/provider.warmup() existed but had no caller, so
the model was never pre-loaded and the first inference paid the cold load (open L19 thread).
New aiassist.warm_once() warms the configured provider exactly once per process on FIRST
inference use -- idempotent, thread-safe, best-effort (a warm failure is swallowed and still
counts as attempted, no retry storm), never on a disabled provider. Wired into the two
inference entry points: aiassist._call_model (all aiassist inference) and ai_chat.chat (the
llm_exec.execute path). Availability precheck (ai_status) and the blank/whitespace model
strip (via ai_provider.make_provider) already existed.

OBS-1 (fold): the 641 after-hook flags any over-budget request but two collect routes loop
UNBOUNDED at the route level with no budget -- collect_workflow_analytics (every draft/review
JSON) and collect_site_health (a per-site DB query per site). The capture_diagnostics/replay
routes are already tool-budgeted (budget_s), so they're untouched. New app_data_layer
_budget_tick() at those two loop boundaries cooperatively raises RequestBudgetExceeded when a
request outruns the budget (-> the app errorhandler's retryable 503); it no-ops outside a
request context, so background/test calls are unaffected. New edge app_data_layer ->
dev_metrics (baseline re-frozen).

## v3.66.655 - INTEROP-GH-1: yt-dlp / gallery-dl external-plugin provenance gate

The interop_registry keystone (GOV-1, 638) defined the ytdlp_plugin and gallerydl_plugin
kinds, but -- unlike chromium_extension (runner_browser) and jd_plugin (runner_integrations)
-- nothing consulted the gate at plugin-load time. This closes that gap at the subprocess
cmd-build layer in runner_extractors.py. New _permitted_plugin_dirs(kind, config) resolves
the operator-configured external plugin dirs (config keys ytdlp_plugin_dirs /
gallerydl_plugin_dirs -- no new BD_ env var) and, when interop_governance_enabled is on,
keeps only dirs the registry permits (registered + risk-acknowledged + enabled + live
content hash matches the pin), exactly mirroring the two existing gates. Governance off ->
configured dirs pass through; empty config (the default for every site) -> no dirs -> byte-
identical prior cmd, zero behavior change. _build_ytdlp_cmd now threads each permitted dir
as --plugin-dirs DIR (yt-dlp 2026.03.17) and _build_gallerydl_cmd as -X DIR (gallery-dl
1.32.5 --extractors), both before the -- terminator so a dir can never be smuggled into the
URL slot. Pure builders; the gate lives in the caller. No live plugin execution -- that
stays operator-gated. Real CLI surfaces verified in-sandbox before writing.

## v3.66.654 - S3.3 (X-RED-1): redaction-dial report dev-loop gate

New tools/redaction_dial_report.py reports how the active redaction profile deviates from
safe defaults (which tunable grey categories are dialed down) and whether the profile is
reduced_redaction (retains more than defaults -> captures LOCAL-ONLY, never circulate).
--check exits 1 when reduced below safe -- a standing dev-loop signal. Read-only + advisory;
the unconditional secret-redaction FLOOR is not a dial and is never reported as reducible;
no runtime change. (The full corpus-replay diff across dials is a heavier follow-on; this
delivers the dial-delta gate on redaction_profile's own primitives. Other S3.3 pieces --
error/defect taxonomy tools/defect_patterns.py, metrics_prom.py SLA surface -- already
existed; the mutmut mutation gate remains deferred as a separate heavier cut.)

## v3.66.653 - S3.2: dependency-freshness advisory scanner (POS-2)

New tools/dep_freshness.py reads requirements*.txt vs installed versions and reports
drifted pins (installed outside the declared specifier), unpinned packages, and pinned-
but-missing packages. Advisory only -- never edits requirements, installs, or upgrades;
--check exits 1 on drift. CLI-only (a dependency change is an operator decision), mirroring
the ytdlp_updater report-don''t-act posture. No runtime/route change.

## v3.66.652 - S3.1 final: live EME page-hook recorder (detection only)

New bulk_downloader/eme_detect.py installs a document-start hook (EME_INIT_JS) on every
BrowserContext (runner_browser._install_stealth, ungated -- independent of the stealth
toggle) that records navigator.requestMediaKeySystemAccess calls on window.__bd_eme,
then calls straight through. classify_eme_records / summarize_eme map recorded
key-systems to protection categories via drm_detect. Pure OBSERVATION -- never requests
a license, drives a CDM, extracts keys, or alters playback. Closes the case of EME/
CDM-DRM pages with no parseable manifest. Completes S3.1. Verified end-to-end in headless
chromium (wrap+record fires when the EME API is present).

## v3.66.651 - S3.1 follow-on: manifest-body DRM category at the parse site

deep_detect.manifests parse_hls_master / parse_dash_mpd now carry drm_category
(none / downloadable-aes / clearkey / cdm-drm) + drm_system alongside the existing
drm_or_encryption_detected bool, folding drm_detect.classify_protection into the
(unguarded) manifest-body parse site -- so an encrypted HLS/DASH manifest is labeled
downloadable-AES (fetchable key, in scope) vs CDM-DRM (un-circumventable) at parse
time. Detection only; never decrypts/strips/extracts. Additive dict keys (existing
consumers unaffected); no new route. Completes S3.1's body-level detection; the live
EME page hook remains the last S3.1 piece.

## v3.66.650 - S3.1: DRM/EME protection classifier (detection only)

New bulk_downloader/drm_detect.py classify_protection() distinguishes downloadable
encrypted playback (HLS AES-128/SAMPLE-AES with a fetchable key -- in scope, yt-dlp
handles it) from CDM-DRM (Widevine/PlayReady/FairPlay -- un-circumventable) and Clear
Key, from an EME key-system string, HLS/DASH manifest text, or a URL marker.
netlog_classify now carries a drm_category on each MediaItem (existing drm bool
unchanged). DETECTION ONLY -- never decrypts, strips, extracts keys, requests a
license, or drives a CDM. Per the charter review (DRM_EME_DETECTION_DECISION.md):
detect + label, no refusal gate, no decryption path. Base DRM detection (URL markers,
drm bool, "DRM - never bypass" badge) was already built; this adds the structural
downloadable-vs-CDM classification. Read-only; no new route.

## v3.66.649 - S2.1: search/saved-search result facets

app_search gains a read-only /api/search/facets that groups matching history rows by
site and by status (the same filter fields a saved search uses), so the UI can show
"N matches across M sites" and drill down. Pure db GROUP BY. (The other S2.1 reactions
were already built: saved_searches.run_one does FTS new-match detection + enqueue/notify
actions + run_due scheduling; similar-sites is app_recommendations /similar.)

## v3.66.648 - S2.3: extractor -> sites-affected blast-radius map

app_ytdlp_status gains a read-only /api/ytdlp/sites_affected mapping each extractor
backend (aylo / ytdlp / gallerydl / search / playwright-default) to the configured sites
that depend on it, folding in yt-dlp staleness -- so a broken/stale extractor's affected
sites are visible at a glance. Config-derived, read-only; passes route parity without FE
wiring (read-only GET, not operator-facing-mutating).

## v3.66.647 - S2.3: library-doctor duplicate + size-drift detection

Extends the library audit (same /api/library/audit route -- no new route) with two
cheap advisory signals. list_duplicate_candidates() groups video files by exact byte
size to surface likely duplicate copies (stat-only; a size collision is a candidate,
not confirmed) and reports reclaimable space. list_size_drift() flags history rows
(status=done) whose recorded file_size differs from the file's actual on-disk size --
a truncated or altered download. audit() now returns duplicate_groups /
duplicate_reclaimable_gb / size_drift plus samples. (The disk/quota alert rule from the
S2.3 scope was already built: alerts_engine has a built-in disk_low rule + bd_disk_free_gb.)

## v3.66.646 - S2.2 / CAP-4: backup/restore integrity via a checksum manifest

create_backup() now emits a per-file sha256 map in _manifest.json (checksums +
checksum_algo), and restore_backup() verifies it: a dry_run over a checksummed backup
is an integrity check that reports checksum_failures + integrity_ok without touching
the filesystem, so a corrupted/truncated backup is caught before a real restore clobbers
live state. Back-compatible -- a pre-checksum backup restores with integrity_ok=True
(nothing to verify). Built in backup.py (the actual matched export/import round-trip)
rather than app_export/app_import (a CSV dump + URL-list import, not a round-trip).

## v3.66.645 - X-PLUG-1: @healthcheck plugin kind (K7) + selftest fold

Adds a seventh plugin extension kind: a plugin can contribute a zero-arg healthcheck
probe (returns {ok, message}) that the host runs under full error isolation -- a
throwing probe is isolated and quarantine-counted, never a crash. CAP_HEALTHCHECK is
documented in known_events(); register_healthcheck / list_healthchecks / run_healthchecks
mirror the K5 sink contract. selftest.check_plugin_health() folds all probe results into
one health-page row (OK when all pass / none registered, WARN when any is unhealthy).
Additive: capabilities are not a closed set, so existing plugins are unaffected.

## v3.66.644 - Durable-state integrity: crash-recovery proof + atomic-write guard

Closes S1.4 (ROB-4 + ROB-5). ROB-4: a seeded crash-recovery proof -- an interrupted
download (a stale .part with a .meta sidecar) is surfaced by scan_for_orphans after a
restart, proving an in-flight download is recoverable rather than silently lost, plus
the too-fresh and still-active exclusion rules. ROB-5: a sweep confirmed every critical
config-state writer already commits atomically (temp + os.replace); this locks that
invariant with a regression guard so a future edit cannot silently regress a state
writer to a torn write-in-place. Regenerable output (AI-review reports, export tars,
payload .part bytes) is intentionally excluded. Test-only; no production code change.

## v3.66.643 - ROB-2: crash-safe migrations (preflight abort + backup/restore)

Hardens migrations.apply_pending() against a bad migration wedging startup. Before
mutating the live DB it now runs the existing in-memory dry-run as a PREFLIGHT: if any
pending migration would fail, the whole batch aborts with zero applied and the DB
untouched -- no half-migrated state. It also copies the live DB aside first
(<db>.premigration.bak, WAL-checkpointed) and, if a migration fails at apply time
(a data-dependent failure the schema-only dry-run cannot catch), restores the
pre-migration DB (abort-to-prior). Default-on via backup_first; no new route or surface.

## v3.66.642 - Session-1 selftest battery: tempfile hygiene + egress fail-closed

Three new selftest checks wired into run_all(), all pure/read-only (ROB-3-remainder +
POS-3). check_orphan_tempfiles() WARNs on stale .part/.tmp artifacts a crashed
download or capture left behind; check_stale_locks() WARNs on *.lock files a crashed
process never released; check_egress_fail_closed() VERIFIES the fail-closed egress
invariant -- a vpn_required site whose tunnel is down makes effective_download_proxy()
raise instead of falling open to a clear-interface download (a fail-open regression is
caught as FAIL). No new route, env var, or button; surfaced through the existing health
checklist.

## v3.66.641 - OBS-1: enforcing request budget + OBS-2 percentile core

Adds a per-request wall-clock ceiling on top of the existing slow-request soft-warn.
Flask here is synchronous/threaded, so a running request cannot be force-killed from a
hook -- the budget is a cooperative deadline: dev_metrics.check_budget(g._dev_t0) lets a
long collect-style route abort with a clean 503 (RequestBudgetExceeded -> retryable, with
elapsed/budget fields + Retry-After) instead of running unbounded. The after_request hook
additionally flags ANY over-budget response via over_budget(), so a non-cooperative slow
route is still visible in the log before it wedges. The ceiling is a module constant
(REQUEST_BUDGET_MS, a sibling of SLOW_REQUEST_MS) -- not a BD_ env var or config field, so
it adds no config surface. Also ships the OBS-2 computable core: route_percentiles()
aggregates p50/p95/max per rule from the existing recent-requests buffer (no new
collection). The status panel that surfaces those percentiles needs a new route and is a
separate follow-on; this cut ships only the pure, sandbox-testable core.

## v3.66.640 - INTEROP-JD-1: jd_plugin governance gate

Wires the second interop_registry consumer (after the v3.66.638 chromium_extension
gate): the JD download path. When interop_governance_enabled is set, a URL is
routed to a JDownloader hoster plugin only if that plugin -- keyed by the URL host,
since JD plugins are per-hoster -- is registered, risk-acknowledged, and enabled in
the interop_registry. An un-acked host is refused at the top of _try_jd_download and
falls through to the teach path, exactly like an unreachable JD. Default-OFF: with
the toggle absent, JD behaves exactly as before (the v3.43.21 contract is unchanged).
No new route, env var, or operator button -- the app_interop API and Maintenance
panel already register/acknowledge/enable every interop kind. Live plugin execution
still requires an external JD runtime and stays operator-gated; this cut ships only
the provenance+gate layer.

## v3.66.639 - INTEROP-GOV-1b: interop registry operator surface (API + UI)

Completes GOV-1. The keystone + extension gate landed at 638 but the registry could
only be populated programmatically; this adds the operator surface. New app_interop.py
blueprint over the interop_registry keystone: GET /api/interop/registry (list items +
kinds), POST /api/interop/register (record provenance; a chromium_extension dir is
hashed server-side so the operator never supplies a hash), POST /api/interop/acknowledge
(set risk-ack; 400 if unregistered), POST /api/interop/enable (set enabled; 400 if
unregistered). Charter unchanged: records provenance + requires ack+enable, not an
allowlist; BD ships nothing.

Wired into the Maintenance page (Interop governance section): all four /api/interop/*
routes are called from frontend/src as full literals -- register/acknowledge/enable
are spa_wired and operator_facing_unwired stays 0. The operator registers an item,
acknowledges its risk, and enables it; the gate (interop_registry.is_permitted) is
consulted at load time (e.g. the chromium-extension gate in runner_browser). Additive:
+4 routes (982 -> 986), +2 import edges (1271 -> 1273: app -> app_interop -> interop_registry),
0 guard changes.

## v3.66.638 - INTEROP-GOV-1: interop provenance + risk-ack registry (keystone) + extension gate

Adds the governance keystone every interop track (chromium extensions / JDownloader
plugins / yt-dlp + gallery-dl plugins) loads through. New module
bulk_downloader/interop_registry.py records provenance for an item (source, sha256,
commit) and requires an explicit risk-acknowledgment AND enable before is_permitted
is true. Off by default: a freshly-registered item is neither acked nor enabled, an
unregistered item is never permitted, and re-registering with a changed content hash
resets the ack (the pin -- an item cannot silently change on disk under an existing
acknowledgment). Disk-backed JSON under BD_HOME.
Governance posture per the interop roadmap: an OPEN loader with consent + provenance,
NOT an allowlist; BD ships nothing and keeps no catalog.

First consumer: the EXT-1 chromium-extension loader (runner_browser._launch_args) is
now gated on the registry when interop_governance_enabled is set -- an extension dir
loads only if registered + risk-acknowledged + enabled AND its live content hash
still matches the pinned provenance (an un-acked or tampered extension is refused).
Default-OFF: with the toggle absent, extension loading is unchanged (EXT-1 behavior
byte-identical). EXT-1's loader was already built (v3.66.468); this governs it.

Backend-only: new module + 1 import edge (runner_browser -> interop_registry,
1270->1271), 0 routes, 0 guard changes. The registry path is under BD_HOME (no new
env var, so no config-surface classification needed). The operator surface
(register/ack/enable API + UI) is the GOV-1b follow-cut.

## v3.66.637 - C4: persistent flake registry

Closes the last C4 (dev/QA standing gates) gap. run_tests._retry_failures_serial
already classifies REAL vs FLAKY per run, but the knowledge was ephemeral -- printed
then gone, and KNOWN_FLAKES.md was never machine-consumed. Adds a persistent flake
registry: pure helpers _update_flake_registry (accumulate per-test count +
first/last-seen, never mutating the input), _chronic_flakes (surface tests at or
above a threshold, count-descending), and opt-in I/O (_load_flake_registry /
_save_flake_registry). main() persists this run's flakes and prints CHRONIC offenders
when BD_FLAKE_REGISTRY names a path.

Mirrors the sibling _files_over_budget: informational-only (never changes the exit
code) and default-OFF -- with BD_FLAKE_REGISTRY unset (as in the release band) it is
a no-op, so there is zero tracked-tree churn and no behavior change. run_tests.py-only;
no route, no module, no import edge, no guard change. Env: BD_FLAKE_REGISTRY (path),
BD_FLAKE_CHRONIC_THRESHOLD (default 3).

## v3.66.636 - C5 finish: replication lifecycle controls + SPA wiring

Completes the C5 replication surface begun at v3.66.635. Adds the operator-facing
lifecycle controls that were deferred, wrapping the already-built fail-closed
db_replication primitives: POST /api/replication/start (start the Litestream
sidecar), POST /api/replication/stop (idempotent), and POST /api/replication/restore
(reconstruct a configured store from its replica). Before this, start_replication
was uncallable at runtime -- the engine had no control surface.

Security posture: restore requires a db_name that is one of the configured stores
(an arbitrary name is refused before any filesystem access) and restores to a
server-chosen staging path -- the caller never supplies a filesystem destination
(the write-side dual of the F-APP03-02 file-read fix). All three are POST-only and
charter default-OFF / fail-closed (start and restore return ok=False with no binary).

Wired into the Backup page (Continuous replication section): all four
/api/replication/* routes are called from frontend/src as full literals, so the
three mutating routes are spa_wired and operator_facing_unwired stays 0. Additive:
+3 routes (979 -> 982), 0 new import edges (1268->1270 baseline unchanged since 635),
0 guard changes.

## v3.66.635 - C5: expose replication status route (durability signal)

Added a read-only GET /api/replication/status route (app_replication.py
blueprint) that exposes db_replication.replication_status() -- the continuous
SQLite replication (Litestream) durability snapshot: enabled flag, litestream
binary presence, configured stores, replica root, and running pid. The
db_replication engine (Cut 622) shipped complete and unit-tested but as an
island: nothing outside its tests imported it and no API route reached the
status function, so the durability signal that strengthens the A0 gold-backup
keystone was unreachable at runtime. This closes the sandbox-buildable half of
that follow-cut; live WAL shipping remains an on-stash concern (needs the
binary), and the mutating lifecycle controls (start/stop/restore) stay out of
scope here (they are operator-facing writes requiring frontend wiring).

Route is GET-only, safe whether or not the litestream binary is present, and
charter default-OFF. Additive: +1 route (978 -> 979), +2 import edges
(1268 -> 1270), no guard changes.

## v3.66.634 - C7: surface federation trust + drift in Cluster.tsx

Renders the 632 backend trust-tier + peer-drift fields in the Cluster page (they
were returned by /api/fed/peers + /api/fed/status but not shown).

- Extended the fed types (FedPeer.trust_tier, new FedPeerDrift, FedPeersResponse.
  drift, FedStatus.peers_behind).
- Cluster.tsx peer table gains a trust column (a per-peer blocked/observed/trusted
  select that calls the new useFedSetTrust mutation -> POST /api/fed/set_trust) and
  a behind column (per-peer replication lag, amber when > 0); the status bar shows
  peers_behind.
- Frontend-only: no backend routes, no Python changes, no new import edges, no
  release-guard files touched. Frontend suite green (107 files / 424 tests, incl.
  a useFedSetTrust wiring test). Note: Cluster.tsx has no full-component vitest
  harness (its AppShell import tree does not resolve under jsdom -- a pre-existing
  gap), so the trust control is covered at the hook level + tsc + app-boot smoke.
- Completes the C7 follow-on trio (login page @633, this) after SSO/OIDC was
  decided against for a self-hosted single-operator tool.

## v3.66.633 - C7: standalone login page + sign-in guard

Adds a sign-in surface + an app-wide auth guard, gated so the single-operator
experience is completely unchanged. (SSO/OIDC was evaluated and decided against
for a self-hosted single-operator tool -- it needs a new dep + outbound network to
an IdP for near-zero benefit; reverse-proxy header SSO remains the recommended
path if ever needed.)

- New routes/Login.tsx (username + write-only password, Enter-to-submit) that
  calls auth.ts login() and invalidates whoami on success.
- New components/AuthGate.tsx wraps the app Routes. SAFETY-CRITICAL no-op
  contract: it renders the Login wall ONLY on a definitive whoami result of
  multi_user === true AND user == null. With multi-user off (the default), while
  whoami is loading, or on a whoami error, it always renders the app -- a broken
  or slow whoami can never lock the sole operator out.
- Frontend-only: no backend routes, no Python changes, no new import edges, no
  release-guard files touched. operator_facing_unwired == 0 unchanged. Frontend
  suite green (106 files / 422 tests, incl. 5 AuthGate no-op/gate contract tests).

## v3.66.632 - C7 11.2: federation trust tiers + peer drift

Hardens the existing download-coordination federation (peer registry + URL claim
+ history feed, already routed via app_fed) with the two genuinely-missing 11.2
pieces. Scope-confirm found the plan's "template push/pull" describes a different
feature already covered by the marketplace export/import; this cut adds trust +
drift to what exists rather than a redundant template protocol.

- Trust tiers: fed_peers gains a trust_tier column (blocked | observed | trusted;
  default observed, with an ALTER migration for pre-11.2 tables). New
  set_peer_trust / peer_trust engine fns. register_peer (announce) never changes
  the tier -- only an operator can, so a peer cannot self-elevate. A blocked peer
  is refused claim_url (trust gates coordination). New POST /api/fed/set_trust
  (operator-gated, non-sensitive); fed blueprint route count 6 -> 7.
- Peer drift: new peer_drift() reports per-peer replication lag (local max history
  id minus the peer's reported last_history_id); status() gains a peers_behind
  count; /api/fed/peers now returns trust tiers + drift alongside the peer list.
- Backend-only (drift surfaced via existing routes; no frontend change). Route
  surface re-baselined (redirect + _BASELINE_SHA re-pin); ROUTE_INDEX /

## v3.66.628 - REDACT-SOT cut 1: config-domain secret-key unification

Security (redaction floor): unify the drifted config-domain secret-key predicate
behind a single source of truth, closing real reachable leaks. (Supersedes the
stash-RED 627 build, which regressed three pre-existing tests; see below.)

- New shared predicate site_editor.is_secret_config_key (SECRET_FIELDS exact
  UNION a curated distinctive-substring floor). This is the config-field-domain
  SoT, distinct from the URL/query SoT (capture_redact.SENSITIVE_QS_KEY). The
  shared predicate is fail-open (decision D1): its floor excludes the bare
  ambiguous terms key/sid/session/auth/login, so a real non-secret config field
  is never wrongly redacted by the shared predicate itself.
- Migrated four drifting call sites to it via the memoized lazy-import pattern:
  app_settings_center._is_secret, vpn._redact_config, vpn_config (@cred:
  indirection), user_templates._strip_secrets / _secret_keys_in.
- Closes leaks: private_key, cookies, cookies_b64, passphrase, preshared_key,
  master_password, vault_token, client_secret were each missed by one or more of
  those modules and are now caught.
- vpn / vpn_config KEEP their deliberate conservative over-redaction posture
  (documented policy: bare key/private/auth over-redact because leaking key
  material is far costlier than masking a benign field) by UNIONing the shared
  floor with their existing VPN-domain hints. Net effect for vpn: strictly more
  coverage (adds cookies/passphrase leak-closure) with no behavior removed.
- audit._is_secret_key was already SoT-unified (F-COREBD17-03) and is unchanged.
- Decisions: D1 fail-open (shared predicate), D2 anchored middle-ground.
  Backend-only. Three new intended import edges (vpn/vpn_config/user_templates ->
  site_editor) re-frozen in the import-graph baseline. No release-guard files
  touched.
- 627->628 corrective: restored vpn's conservative posture (Option A) and updated
  the stale white-box test_no_broad_cookie_regex (asserted the removed _SECRET_RE
  symbol) to check the new SoT floor structure; behavior preserved.

## v3.66.625 - C7 sub-wave 11.1a: multi-user accounts + roles (default-OFF)

The identity foundation for C7 (federation, 11.2, gates receive-on-identity so
11.1 lands first). A self-contained accounts + roles engine plus a reachable auth
API - all default-OFF and backward-compatible: with zero accounts (the single-
operator default) every current behaviour is byte-identical, and role enforcement
activates only when the operator creates accounts AND turns on `multi_user` in
app_config.json. New `user_accounts` module (named to avoid overloading the
existing site-credential `app_accounts`/`account_health`): a `user_accounts.json`
store with PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 password hashing (200k iters, per-user salt, stdlib
only), roles admin > reviewer > operator (only reviewer/admin may promote), and a
signed, expiring `bd_user` session token (HMAC over username.exp) - a PARALLEL
identity layer that does NOT touch the existing `bd_session` pairing cookie or
app.py's auth hot path. New `app_auth` blueprint (distinct `auth` blueprint,
/api/auth/*): POST login (sets bd_user cookie), POST logout, GET whoami, POST
users (bootstrap first account when empty, else admin-gated), GET users (admin-
gated). The template-promote route (`/api/template_manager/promote`) now gates on
the reviewer role - default-no-op when multi-user is off, best-effort so a store
error never 500s the route. Route surface regenerated (5 new routes, +1 blueprint):
ROUTE_INDEX 981 -> 986, route_map baseline re-frozen (+5, sha re-pinned),
ENDPOINT_CATALOG 1012 -> 1017, gui_parity 1193 -> 1198, blueprint count 154 -> 155;
three new import edges, baseline re-frozen 1258 -> 1261. No guard files touched.
Follow-ups: multi-user UI, set-role/delete-user routes, optional SSO/OIDC, then
11.2 federation (signed template push/pull, trust tiers) on the existing
federation.py scaffold.

## v3.66.624 - C2: semantic search over the capture index + template corpus

The marquee RAG feature: three dependency-free modules plus a reachable API.
`embeddings` is a feature-hashing text embedder (word tokens + per-word char
3-grams -> fixed-dim L2-normalized vector) - deterministic, stdlib only, no model
download and no native extension, so semantic retrieval works on any box (a neural
Ollama `/api/embeddings` backend and a `sqlite-vec` ANN speed path are both
detected/gated follow-ups, never required). `vector_index` is a single-file
(`vector_index.json`) brute-force cosine store with top-k search - correct at any
single-operator corpus size. `semantic_search` indexes the Phase-1 `captures`
metadata index (`db.db_captures_all`) and the user-template corpus, then answers
an NL query with the right prior capture or template (`reindex`/`search`/`status`);
only capture metadata (host/name/dir/kind) is indexed, never bodies. A new
`app_semantic_search` blueprint surfaces it: GET `/api/semantic/status`, POST
`/api/semantic/search` ({query, k}), POST `/api/semantic/reindex` (both POSTs
CSRF-gated). Config lives in the `semantic_search` block of app_config.json (read
directly; NO settings-center field, so the editable-field count pins are
untouched). Route surface regenerated (3 new routes, +1 blueprint): ROUTE_INDEX
978 -> 981, route_map baseline re-frozen (+3, sha re-pinned), ENDPOINT_CATALOG
1009 -> 1012, gui_parity 1190 -> 1193, blueprint count 153 -> 154; six new import
edges, baseline re-frozen 1252 -> 1258. No guard files touched.

## v3.66.623 - C3: DOM authoring completion (selector versioning + named library)

Two new backend modules complete the DOM-authoring loop (the scoring engine
`selector_check` and the repair engine `aiassist.diff_repair` already existed;
this adds the history and reuse halves). `selector_versions` records a template's
selector block (its `learned` dict) each time the template is saved, to an
append-only `selector_history.json`, so an operator can see what changed and
revert: record/list/get/diff/revert, de-duplicated (a no-op save adds no version),
fail-open (never breaks a save), never-raise on read, revert fail-closed on an
unknown template/version. `selector_library` is a store of reusable named
selectors (`selector_library.json`) plus a resolver that expands `@lib:<name>`
references; resolution is pass-through for any value that is not a live reference,
so it is byte-identical for every template that uses none. Two additive,
behavior-preserving wirings: `user_templates.save_user_template` records a version
on every save (best-effort), and `template_assist.template_to_learned_download`
expands `@lib:` references before materializing selectors so named selectors are
runtime-usable. Backend only - no new routes, no settings-center fields, no guard
files touched. Two new import edges (user_templates -> selector_versions,
template_assist -> selector_library), baseline re-frozen 1250 -> 1252.

## v3.66.622 - C5: SQLite continuous-replication (Litestream) plumbing

New `db_replication` module: continuous replication of the SQLite stores
(queue.db and friends) via Litestream, feeding a durable file replica so a
disk failure loses at most the un-shipped WAL tail instead of everything since
the last one-click backup zip. Strengthens the A0 gold-backup the automation
program gates L2 autonomy on. Default-OFF per charter: replication is disabled
unless the operator opts in via the `replication` block in app_config.json AND
the litestream binary is present; every entry point (start/restore) fails closed
otherwise. Deterministic config generation, store enumeration, status, the
lifecycle guards, and restore-then-verify (reusing backup_verify.verify_db_dump)
are all unit-tested in-sandbox; live WAL shipping validates on-stash. Backend
only - no new routes, no settings-center fields, no guard files touched.

## v3.66.620 - C6 (8.4): gallery-dl fallback extractor + status/update API

gallerydl_updater.py (semver-adapted: current_version/status_dict; version_age_days

(POST /api/gallerydl_update). Config: use_gallerydl_fallback (default False). The URL

## v3.66.619 - C4 (12.1): per-file test timeout budgets in the report

run_tests already emits slowest-N and enforces a hard per-file wall timeout
(_FILE_TIMEOUT_S, 900s, which FAILS the file). This adds a SOFT budget: a
per-file wall-time threshold (_FILE_BUDGET_S, env BD_TEST_FILE_BUDGET, default
120s; 0 disables) whose only effect is to SURFACE over-budget files in the
report -- a new OVER BUDGET section in the summary and a 'budget' block in the
JSON payload -- so a newly-slow file is visible long before it hits the hard
kill. It never changes pass/fail (exit stays gated on failures only). The math
is a pure helper (_files_over_budget: strictly-over, slowest-first). JSON
schema_version stays 2 (the 'budget' field is additive; older consumers ignore
it). Rest of the C4 plan already shipped: dead-route gate = nav_reachability,
new-edge gate = import_graph_gate, flake auto-detect + best-of-N retry =
_retry_failures_serial. Tools-only; no app/route/import-edge change.

## v3.66.618 - C1 security: SSRF choke-point + cookie-import path guard

Closes two confirmed audit-ledger findings (serial fix-chain):

- F-APP03-01 (medium, SSRF): POST /api/template/sandbox validated only
  the URL scheme, then fetched it in-request (browser page.goto or
  urllib) with no host guard. Now the URL host is classified against the
  canonical _is_safe_public_host BEFORE any fetch, covering both modes,
  and each urllib redirect hop is re-validated. Link-local/cloud-metadata,
  RFC1918 private, RFC6598 CGNAT, reserved and multicast targets are
  refused. Loopback (127.0.0.1/localhost) is deliberately exempted to
  preserve the intentional local selector-testing capability.
- F-APP03-02 (low, arbitrary-file-read): POST /api/sites/<sid>/cookies/import
  read the 'path' source with no allowlist check. Now the path is validated
  against the never-empty reveal-safe roots (_validate_reveal_path) before
  reading, so a path outside the download/allowlist roots is refused.

No new import edges (both guards delegate dynamically) and no route changes.

## v3.66.617 - Phase 2 Cut 2.1: queue lanes + dependencies + dead-letter

- Queue gains three capabilities (priorities already existed). db.py: `lane` and
  `depends_on` columns on the queue table (additive + lazy ALTER migration) plus
  db_queue_dead_letter / db_queue_requeue_dead_letter. New pure module queue_policy.py
  holds the decision logic: should_dead_letter, dependency_satisfied / _blocked, and
  order_ready_jobs[_by_lane] (priority-then-ord ordering, lane partitioning, excludes
  terminal/blocked/unmet jobs). runner.py worker loop gates dispatch on dependencies
  (a job waits for its dependency to be 'done'; a permanently-gone dependency
  dead-letters the dependent rather than requeue forever); runner_auth dead-letters a
  retry-exhausted job (terminal, not plain 'failed' which housekeeping re-picks).
  New routes GET /api/queue/dead_letter + POST /api/queue/dead_letter/requeue.
  One new edge runner->queue_policy (cycle-free). No guard touch.

## v3.66.616 - Phase 1 Cut 1.3: configurable capture store root + migrator

- dom_analyzer.py: capture resolution splits into a two-base model. Capture-OUTPUT
  dirs (captures, offline_out, offline_captures) resolve under an optional
  `capture_store_root` app-config key (default PROJECT_ROOT); template dirs
  (templates/drafts, templates/review_candidates) ALWAYS resolve under PROJECT_ROOT
  since they are managed by template_manager.DRAFTS_DIR independent of the capture
  store. Default (unset) is byte-identical. The FS-authoritative resolve gate is
  unchanged - store_root only changes WHICH base a capture-output token validates
  against, routed by token prefix; symlink/is_file/is_under still enforced under
  both bases. app.py + app_selftest.py thread the resolved store root into the
  selftest disk check so a relocated store's disk is the one checked; drift_repair
  and the picker inherit it via dom_analyzer. New tool relocate_capture_store.py
  moves the capture-output dirs (never the template dirs) + prints the config key
  to set. Three edges (dom_analyzer->global_config, app->dom_analyzer,
  app_selftest->dom_analyzer) re-frozen this cut; all cycle-free. No guard touch.

## v3.66.615 - Phase 1 Cut 1.2 corrective: capture helpers self-ensure their table

- db.py: db_captures_upsert / db_captures_all / db_captures_prune_missing now call
  _ensure_captures_table(cx) (CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS + indices) before touching
  the table. Fixes a 614 on-stash regression: Cut 1.2 repointed GET
  /api/analyzer/captures onto db_captures_all, but a bare client with no db_init in
  the current cwd hit 'no such table: captures' -> 500 (test_analyzer_endpoints

  ran in this cwd (the retention._ensure_tables pattern). db.py-only; no new edge; no
  guard touch.

## v3.66.614 - Phase 1 Cut 1.4: capture-retention engine (opt-in, keep-forever default)

- retention.py: a SECOND retention axis over the db `captures` index (Cut 1.1),
  distinct from the per-site download/history retention. find_capture_candidates /
  apply_capture_retention with TTL / size-cap / keep-N-per-host rules. Captures are
  KEEP-FOREVER by default (RETENTION_AND_TAKEDOWN_POLICY.md) - no rule configured
  means zero candidates. Reuses the safety machinery: apply defaults to dry_run=True;
  confirm_paths binds deletion to the previewed set (never deletes more/other).
  Deletion resolves via the FS-authoritative gate so a stale index row can't target
  an out-of-tree file. bg_scheduler gains a daily DRY-RUN capture sweep, skipped
  entirely unless opted in. The takedown floor (RATP section 3) is a separate non-negotiable
  path, not gated by these knobs. New edges bg_scheduler->global_config,
  retention->dom_analyzer re-frozen this cut; cycle-free. No guard touch.

## v3.66.613 - Phase 1 Cut 1.2: index-backed capture consumers

- app_captures.py / app_analyzer.py: repoint the capture read-consumers onto
  the durable db `captures` index (Cut 1.1), off the restart-ephemeral
  _SCAN_CACHE / FS-walk. POST /api/captures/scan now upserts the walked rows +
  prunes deleted ones (durable reconcile); GET /api/captures serves from the
  index (survives a restart, no re-walk); GET /api/analyzer/captures is

  Two new import edges (app_captures->db, app_analyzer->db) re-frozen this cut;
  cycle-free. No guard touch.

## v3.66.612 - Phase 1 Cut 1.1: captures index table + persistent writer

- db.py: new durable `captures` table in db_init() (additive CREATE TABLE IF
  NOT EXISTS + host/kind/captured_at indices) plus db_captures_upsert /
  db_captures_all / db_captures_prune_missing helpers. Ends the FS-walk class:
