## v3.66.611 -- Phase-0 finish (sub-items B + C), closing Phase 0. (B) supervisor -> app health: the health checklist (run_checklist) now includes a 'supervisor' item surfacing the in-app bandwidth supervisor's state (idle/active + global_bps). App-PROCESS supervision remains systemd's job and /api/health already reports uptime; this connects the in-app supervisor to the health view. New import edge healthcheck -> download_supervisor (cycle-free; baseline re-frozen 1236->1237). (C) soft cost ceiling: a pathologically slow request (>10s) now logs an immediate warning via the existing after_request timing (dev_metrics.slow_request_note); the per-endpoint aggregate (record_request) is unchanged -- this is the immediate 'something is hung' operator signal. No route or schema change.

## v3.66.610 -- Phase-0 finish (sub-items A + D). (A) healthcheck._check_disk (which powers /api/health/checklist) checked only per-site download_dirs -- the same download-dir-only blind spot fixed for selftest.run_all in 0.5, but in the other health system. It now also checks the capture-store/install root, even with no sites configured (first boot). (D) unknown-model clarity: an unknown Ollama model already fast-failed (404, no hang -- cold-load was 0.3, blank-model was 594), but 404 mapped to the generic 'bad_request' kind; OllamaProvider now classifies 404 as 'not_found' so the UI can say 'model not installed'. No route or schema change.

## v3.66.609 -- Cut 0.6 (Phase-0 close): the ffmpeg health check now probes CAPABILITY, not just presence. healthcheck._check_ffmpeg() previously only confirmed ffmpeg+ffprobe on PATH; a build that's present but crashes on invocation or lacks the mpegts muxer / https protocol still fails real HLS/TS-over-https downloads (the static-ffmpeg segfault class). New _ffmpeg_capability() runs -version (FAIL if it won't run) and checks the mpegts muxer + https protocol are present (WARN if missing); the healthy message now reads 'mpegts + https ok'. Already wired into the battery. No route or schema change.

## v3.66.608 -- Cut 0.5 (disk gauge gap): the startup health battery (selftest.run_all) now also checks free space on the CAPTURE-STORE root (PROJECT_ROOT / install dir), not only the configured download dirs. The capture store often lives on a different path/volume than downloads and a full store is a distinct 'disk full' class (7.1G/687 wacz seen in the field) the download-dir check missed. run_all() gains an optional captures_root param (folded into the deduped disk-check loop); app.py's startup selftest + the /api/health handler pass PROJECT_ROOT (computed from __file__, no new import). No route or schema change.

## v3.66.607 -- Fix the 606 config-surface collision: reap_orphan_tempdirs.py's module constant BD_PREFIXES matched config_surface_inventory's BD_* literal coverage scan, so it was flagged as an unreconciled env var -> on-stash FAIL of test_v3_66_319_env_tranche_4_3d (open env vars remain: ['BD_PREFIXES']) and a config-danger baseline count shift (test_v3_66_305). Renamed the constant to _TEMP_PREFIXES (off the BD_ prefix). No behavior change. No route or schema change.

## v3.66.606 -- Cut 0.4 (defensive) + tooling fix. (1) build_template's per-capture temp-dir leak (596-era) is VERIFIED already fixed (build_template reads the WACZ in-memory via ZipFile; 5 calls leak 0 temp dirs), so the planned lifecycle fix is moot; instead ship tools/reap_orphan_tempdirs.py -- a safe, prefix-scoped, dry-run-by-default reaper of stale BD-owned temp dirs (bdback_/bdrestore_/bd_plugin_upload_/bd-diag-/...) that CAN leak on error paths, as defense-in-depth for the /tmp-flood class. (2) slowest_tests.sh now runs under the service venv (auto-detect BD_PYTHON/venv, warns if flask is absent) instead of bare python3 (which mass-failed on missing flask/playwright/bs4), and gains a --from JSON mode to report from an existing durations file (e.g. capture.sh's) without re-running. No route or schema change.

## v3.66.605 -- Cut 0.3 (CAP-1): keep the Ollama model warm to close the L19 cold-load timeout. OllamaProvider.generate() now sends keep_alive (default 10m) so an idle gap between calls no longer forces a 30-60s model re-load that trips the request timeout, and a new OllamaProvider.warmup() (plus aiassist.warmup() passthrough) issues a 1-token keep_alive generate to pre-load the model before the first real call. No route or schema change.

## v3.66.604 -- Fix stale generated indices shipped in 602/603 + de-flake the bounded-scan timing test. ROUTE_INDEX.json and reports/gui_parity_inventory.json had been regenerated under an environment that does not register /api/scrape_listing, so the shipped indices dropped that route (and mis-set its operator_facing), tripping test_route_index_in_sync and test_v3_66_302_gui_parity_reconcile on-stash; both are regenerated with the route present. test_bug37b_scan_captures_bounded::test_bounded_scan_is_fast used an absolute 0.5s wall-clock bound that flaked under --workers load; it now takes the best of 3 runs vs a 3s ceiling (still catches a multi-minute unbounded regression). Adds slowest_tests.sh (slowest-N + duration distribution from run_tests.py --json). No route or schema change.

## v3.66.603 -- Cut 0.2 (OBS-1): bound + cache the capture_analytics collector. GET /api/data/capture_analytics -> collect_capture_analytics -> capture_analytics.analyze() opened/parsed every capture_*.json under the store unbounded and uncached (same hang class as the 596 diagnostics/replay bound). analyze() now takes a newest-first limit (skipped_artifacts reported; unbounded preserved for CLI), the collector caps to _HEAVY_LIMIT + caches via _cached, and the two internal _artifacts callers unpack the (arts, skipped) return. No route or schema change.

## v3.66.602 -- Cut 0.1 (ROB-1): selftest.check_database no longer false-positive WARNs on a first-run/not-yet-created DB -- a missing DB is a benign first-run condition (db_conn already sets WAL on init and it persists).

## v3.66.601 -- Fix analyzer pin host derivation: redacted captures (no url in archive) fall back to the filename/path host the picker uses; add host to /api/analyzer/load contract and surface it in the DOM analyzer pin controls. Unblocks the offline Build-draft path.

## v3.66.600 -- Fix two source-scan tests that pinned pre-BUG-2 forms of the noVNC embed (green-on-stash follow-up to 599; no behavior change). test_capture_iframe_clipboard extracts the live-session iframe tag by regex and asserted the literal src={novncUrl}; 599 renamed the binding to the frozen ref (frozenNovncUrl) so a window resize cannot remount the iframe and re-open the VNC socket, and a > character inside the new explanatory JSX comment truncated the regex-extracted tag before the allow= attribute. The test now accepts either novncUrl or frozenNovncUrl, and the JSX comment was reworded to contain no > or < so the iframe tag stays greppable (the allow=clipboard-read; clipboard-write pin is unchanged and passing). test_v3_66_98_cockpit_console and test_novnc_url_defaults asserted the exact embed query string; 599 gap-fills reconnect=true + reconnect_delay=2000, so those assertions now check that explicit resize/autoconnect are preserved AND the reconnect defaults are appended. SPA rebuilt (the reworded comment changes the bundle). No route or schema change.

## v3.66.599 -- Frontend + capture-workflow bug fixes from the Cowork live-test runs (BUG-2, BUG-5, BUG-8, and the BUG-3/7 picker refinement); full SPA rebuild. BUG-8 (video element eats the element-picker click): native media controls act on pointerdown/mousedown before click, so clicking a player to pick it toggled play/pause and the pick landed on nothing; the injected live-pick overlay now installs a capture-phase guard on pointerdown/mousedown/pointerup/mouseup that, only while a pick is armed and only over a <video>/<audio> element (or a media-part node), preventDefaults + stopImmediatePropagations so the element's own handlers and the UA default never fire, letting the trailing click derive the selector; non-media targets and shift-through are untouched. BUG-5 (stale row_selectors bled across capture sessions): starting a new capture now resets the draft fields to initial (fresh row_selectors.entries) and clears the AI suggestions panel + armed pick, so a later capture on a different host no longer shows the previous host's classes. BUG-2 (noVNC canvas drops on resize and re-prompts): the embed URL now also fills reconnect=true + reconnect_delay=2000 when absent (gap-only, explicit wins) so a socket bounced by an iframe reflow silently re-establishes instead of dropping to the manual connect screen, and the SPA freezes the iframe src on the first live URL with a stable key so a window resize cannot remount the iframe (which would open a fresh VNC socket). BUG-3/7 picker refinement: the DOM-analyzer capture picker now sends the recursive rel_path token (falling back to name) so onboarding/guided captures in subfolders both list and load via the same path the backend already resolves. No route or schema change.

## v3.66.598 -- Unwedge the release-gate suite on a large operator capture store (root-caused live via py-spy stacks). Three independent layers. (1) The heavy report collectors are now hard-bounded in TIME and per-file size, not just count: GET /api/data/capture_diagnostics builds a full template per .wacz (player-recognition regex over the page HTML), and on a store with hundreds of top-level wacz, some over 100MB, even a 200-capture bound ran for hours -- one request. capture_diagnostics.collect and replay_validator.collect now accept budget_s (wall-time deadline checked between captures) and max_bytes (oversize wacz are skipped, counted as skipped_oversize); the data-layer endpoints call them with limit=50, budget_s=20, max_bytes=25MB and cache the result for 600s (repeat views and route-scanning tests hit the cache; cached copies carry cache_age_s). (2) run_tests.py: the serial failure-retry re-ran a failed file IN-PROCESS with no timeout, so a single pathologically slow test wedged the whole run forever after its parallel-phase 900s timeout; the retry now uses the same isolated subprocess runner with the per-file wall timeout, which is env-tunable via BD_TEST_FILE_TIMEOUT (default 900). (3) test_secret_display_never: on a shard stall the scan now keeps every completed shard (bounded per-shard drain, coverage floor still enforced) instead of falling back to a full sequential re-scan that doubled the grind. No route or schema change.

## v3.66.597 -- Test-suite robustness fixes for the on-stash gate (no runtime code change). (1) test_v3_43_31_rate_limit fast-path check de-flaked: a single wall-clock sample flaked under a loaded parallel suite (one scheduler preemption exceeded the 50ms threshold); it now asserts the best-of-N (minimum over up to 15 acquires, perf_counter) is fast, which is immune to preemption noise while still failing on a real fast-path regression (mutation-verified: an injected 80ms slowdown fails). (2) test_secret_display_never endpoint scan is now multi-core: the sequential scan of every operator-facing GET exceeded run_tests' 900s file timeout on a large operator capture store because report endpoints do real work; the scan now forks worker processes after the one seeded boot (children inherit the app + DB) and shards the targets, so wall time is about the slowest single endpoint; adds a coverage floor so a broken pool cannot pass vacuously; teeth mutation-verified (an injected leaking route is caught). Falls back to sequential when fork is unavailable. (3) test_p9_analytics graceful capture-analytics check no longer assumes a capture-free repo tree (the operator capture store legitimately lives under the repo): it points analyze() at a deliberately nonexistent capture dir so the zero-artifact assertion holds by construction; the yield assertion is dirs-independent and unchanged.

## v3.66.596 -- Bound the capture-diagnostics and replay-validation report collectors (pre-existing scalability bug unmasked by a large capture store). GET /api/data/capture_diagnostics ran capture_diagnostics.collect(), which built a FULL template (open wacz + player recognition) for EVERY .wacz under the capture dirs, unbounded; GET /api/data/replay_validation ran replay_validator.collect(), which opened (load_capture) every .wacz. On a large capture store each was a multi-minute single-core walk that hung any route-scanning test (test_secret_display_never GETs every route) and, for diagnostics, leaked a build_template temp dir per capture. Both collect() functions now accept a limit and diagnose/validate at most limit .wacz newest-first (the two endpoints pass limit=200), reporting skipped_wacz. This is the actual cause of the reported test hang; the 595 scan_captures bound addressed a separate, lesser picker-endpoint regression. No route or schema change.

## v3.66.595 -- BUG-3/7 performance fix (regression introduced in 594). The 594 DOM-analyzer picker endpoint (/api/analyzer/captures) changed from a shallow non-recursive list_captures glob to an UNBOUNDED recursive scan_captures walk with a per-file stat + host-parse + redacted-sibling check; on a large capture store this made the endpoint an O(all-captures) multi-minute single-core walk (measured ~1316x slower than 593 at 8000 captures) that also hung any route-scanning test (test_secret_display_never GETs every route). scan_captures now takes an optional limit: it descends newest-directory-first and stops after limit captures, and the picker endpoint calls it with limit=1000, so the picker is bounded (newest 1000) instead of walking the entire store. The unbounded enumeration (limit=None) is preserved for token resolution and summaries. A just-finished onboarding capture (newest mtime) is still surfaced. No route or schema change.

## v3.66.594 -- Cowork live-test bug fixes (BUG-1, BUG-4, BUG-3/7), all RED-first. BUG-1: DELETE /api/sites/<sid> was a no-op for idle (never-started) sites -- config/meta removal was nested inside the 'if sid in runners' guard so a runner-less site was never removed yet the handler returned ok=True; removal (s_cfg/s_meta pop + queue_delete_site + _save_sites_config) is now unconditional and a truly-absent id returns 404. BUG-4: a blank AI model already fell back to the default, but a whitespace-only model name was truthy and bypassed the 'model or default' fallback, reaching Ollama as a literal name and hanging ~30s; ai_provider now strips before the fallback. BUG-3/7: the DOM-analyzer picker enumerated captures non-recursively (list_captures) so onboarding/guided captures in subfolders were invisible and unloadable; the picker endpoint now uses the recursive scan_captures and a new _resolve_capture_any resolves either a rel_path token or a unique bare basename (recursive fallback; ambiguous basenames refused). No route or schema change.

## v3.66.593 -- Security (F-APP06-01): /api/file/reveal no longer opens an arbitrary absolute path in the host file manager when path_allowlist is empty (the legacy-permissive default). A new reveal-scoped validator (_validate_reveal_path) requires the path to be within a reveal-safe root -- the configured path_allowlist if set, else BD download roots (BD_HOME, ~/Downloads/bulk_downloader, and any configured download_dir). _validate_path (cookie_file/download_dir/config) keeps its existing empty-allowlist behavior for backward compatibility. No route or schema change.

## v3.66.592 -- Security (F-COCKPIT01-03): the cockpit report viewer rendered .md reports via python-markdown (which passes raw inline HTML through) and the client set rv.innerHTML = d.html unsanitized -- a stored-DOM-XSS surface. The report endpoint now routes markdown output through a dependency-free allowlist sanitizer (_sanitize_report_html): only markdown own safe tags/attrs survive; script/style/iframe/object tags, on* handlers, and javascript:/data: URLs are dropped, failing closed to escaped text on any parse error. No route or schema change.

## v3.66.591 -- Security (F-CBD03-01): aiassist now defends the ollama LAN-only endpoint against DNS rebinding. validate_endpoint only checked the resolved IP at save time (and trusted .local/.lan suffixes with no lookup), while the request path re-resolved at connect time. _post_json now pins the resolved LAN IP at request time via _pin_lan_endpoint: re-resolve the host, refuse unless every address is loopback/private/link-local/reserved, and connect to a validated IP with the original Host header preserved. Loopback names and IP-literal endpoints handled without DNS. No route or schema change.

## v3.66.590 -- Security (F-CAP01-01): live_recorder.watch() now enforces the cam-site host allowlist (_SITE_PATTERNS) on the site_override/room_override path, not just URL shape. Previously supplying both overrides skipped parse_live_url host gate, letting an override aim streamlink/ffmpeg at any http(s) host (e.g. cloud metadata or an internal service) -- an SSRF. An override may still relabel site/room but the URL host must be a recognized live-cam site. No route or schema change.

## v3.66.589 -- Security (F-APP04-01 + F-COCKPIT03-01, Batch B auth-gate posture): the default-ON dev + cockpit-shell surfaces are no longer reachable unauthenticated from the network. _dev_mode_guard now requires an authorized request (loopback, same-origin browser/SPA, a valid session, or the master bearer/X-BD-Token) in addition to dev-mode being on, closing the gap where a box with no global auth token configured left /api/dev/* wide open. cockpit_console adds a self-contained origin/bind guard on /api/shell/*: the arbitrary-command web-shell refuses requests that are neither loopback nor same-origin, independent of the host app auth config. Both surfaces stay default-ON for single-operator SPA/local use. Scoped bdapi_ tokens still cannot reach /api/dev/*. No route or schema change.

## v3.66.588 -- Security (F-APP05-03 + F-CBD12-01): the Phase-121 outgoing-webhook subscription system now validates subscriber URLs against the operator-chosen SSRF policy established in v3.66.553 (hooks._validate_webhook_url). add_subscription rejects cloud-metadata/link-local/CGNAT/multicast/unspecified hosts and non-http schemes at registration; _deliver_one re-validates at delivery time (DNS-rebind / hand-edited-DB defense) before requests.post. RFC1918 LAN, loopback, and public receivers stay allowed (Plex/Jellyfin/Home Assistant targets). The add route returns an accurate 400 on rejection. No route or schema change.

## v3.66.587 -- Test-only fix: the F-RUN02-02 proxy binding added self._download_proxy_url() to runner_transport._do_probe_fetch, but the probe-mode test double (_FakeRunner in test_v3_66_274_probe_mode.py) did not implement that method, breaking 3 probe-outcome tests on the full suite (11089 3 fail). Add _download_proxy_url to the fake (None = degrade open) and add a behavioral fail-closed probe test (VPNRequiredError -> needs_review before any httpx.stream). No production source change.

## v3.66.586 -- Security (F-RUN02-02 + F-RUN02-03): route the two remaining in-process httpx clients through the fail-closed VPN download proxy. runner_transport._do_probe_fetch (GCW probe) now resolves self._download_proxy_url() and fails closed to needs_review on VPNRequiredError before threading proxy= into httpx.stream; session_keeper._heartbeat_httpx_fallback resolves download_egress.effective_download_proxy and fails closed before threading proxy= into httpx.Client. A vpn_required site whose tunnel is down or killed no longer samples media or heartbeats on the clear interface. Mirrors the Track-K _do_direct_http_download binding. No route or schema change.

## v3.66.585 -- Security (F-AUTH02-01): cookie_health.check_site now sends cookies through the jar so httpx enforces per-host domain (and path/secure) matching on every hop, instead of flattening the whole Netscape jar into a domain-blind name:value dict. This stops cookies scoped to other domains from leaking to the health-check URL and from being carried across cross-host redirects. Local expiry is neutralized before the request so the server, not the cookie file, decides validity (preserving the prior ignore_expires behavior). No route or schema change.

## v3.66.584 -- Security (F-APP05-02): /api/config/export now redacts the full secret-field set (site_editor.SECRET_FIELDS) instead of only the password field, so a default export no longer leaks plex_token, *_api_key, ha_token, tpdb_api_key, ai_api_key, or auth_token in cleartext. Config import preserves any existing secret when the imported value is blank, so a redacted export round-trips without wiping secrets. No route or schema change.

## v3.66.583 -- 3.66.583 - Security (F-COREBD11-02): jellyfin_deep now sends the API key via the X-Emby-Token header instead of the ?api_key= query parameter, so the key no longer leaks into access logs, the Referer header, or proxy request lines. Matches the basic refresh path in hooks.py. No route or schema change.

## v3.66.582 -- R6 secret-handling (F-COREBD02-01 + F-COREBD13-03): audit_security.secret_scan no longer echoes the credential it flagged. The finding 'context' field is now redacted by _redact_secret_context (keep the assignment target / label, mask the value; when there is no clear assignment, emit the shape length + a short sha1 instead of raw text), so the scanner's own output can never disclose a scanned secret -- closing the gap where the 40-char line preview included the value despite the 'never echo the matched secret' comment. diagnostics_bundle._attach_logs now line-redacts bd.log / runner.log / events.log through capture_artifact_redact.redact_value (JWTs, signed URLs, cookies, kv-secrets) before adding them to the 'redacted / safe to share' zip, closing the DP-08 redaction-scope gap where include_logs=True shipped raw log bytes while only the JSON snapshot was scrubbed. No runtime behavior change beyond redaction; the lazy import edge diagnostics_bundle -> capture_artifact_redact is re-frozen in-cut.

## v3.66.581 -- F-REC01-02 (high) + F-REC03-01: deep_detect runtime probe client now SSRF-guarded at the single choke-point. _build_default_http_client installs an httpx 'request' event hook (canonical _is_safe_public_host predicate, same pattern as tier_probe._ssrf_guard_hook) that fires on the initial request AND every redirect target, raising SSRFBlocked on private / loopback / link-local (169.254/16) / CGNAT (100.64/10) / reserved hosts. This guards all three page-derived-URL egress sinks (_probe_head, _fetch_manifest_capped, _poll_async_workflow) and the Tier-2 probe against a page steering a HEAD/GET/POST into internal space (incl. a public URL that 302-redirects inward); the sinks already catch the raised exception and record an errored probe. Public hosts unaffected; lazy import so no new module-level import edge.

## v3.66.580 -- F-COREBD13-02: honest docs for the (unimplemented) per-token rate limit -- shares.py's module docstring no longer advertises 'rate-limited per-token (default 60 req/min)' (no such control exists; the surface is a trusted-LAN operator tool), and api_tokens.py drops the dangling 'mirror shares._rate_ok' reference to a function that was never defined. No runtime behavior change (DP-13 documentation/reference fix).

## v3.66.579 -- F-COREBD13-01: share-token verify_token IP whitelist now fails CLOSED -- a token minted with a non-empty ip_whitelist is denied when the caller IP is empty/unknown or not in the list (the guard was 'if wl and client_ip:', which skipped the whitelist entirely whenever client_ip was falsy and admitted a whitelisted token with no caller IP). Listed IPs and tokens without a whitelist are unaffected.

## v3.66.578 -- R5 (part 2) redactor-unification: capture_scrub redacts all-alphabetic and all-numeric high-entropy opaque tokens (shared Shannon-entropy predicate in the masker) and scan_residual now flags any such residual, so an opaque token can no longer evade BOTH the redactor and the CLEAN verify (F-TOOLSO04-01). Benign structured text (CamelCase, long class names) stays below the entropy bar.

## v3.66.577 -- R5 (part 1) redactor-unification: scrub_recon scrub_capture now redacts inline script_tags_of_interest[].content (embedded signed URLs + floor-keyed apiKey/token/bearer/signature values in JSON/JS/query form) so credentials cannot ride into committed fixtures, matching the module docstring (F-TOOLS_OTHER07-01).

## v3.66.576 -- R4 redactor-unification (capture_redact SoT): SENSITIVE_QS_KEY covers csrf/xsrf/bearer query params and SENSITIVE_HEADER covers a bare csrf header, closing the DP-08 floor gap (F-COREBD17-01). Substring form (no benign key collision) also covers _csrf/x-xsrf/bearer_token.

## v3.66.575 -- R3 redactor-unification (element_pick): _scrub_dom_excerpt reuses the canonical capture_artifact_redact floor plus Authorization-header and input/meta value DOM passes so the CAP-01 I0008 floor (csrf/api_key/oauth code+state/otp/nonce/Authorization) cannot leak into DOM_RESULT.json (F-CBD03-02).

## v3.66.574 -- R2 redactor-unification (cockpit_core): redact() uses canonical capture_artifact_redact.redact_value covering the I0008 floor (F-COCKPIT02-01); posture_clean() fails closed with a leak sentinel on scanner error (F-COCKPIT02-02). Updated test_v3_66_99 (canonical <scrubbed> placeholder) and test_v3_66_108 (canonical redactor masks cookie session= in place instead of withholding) expectations to match the stronger redactor.

## v3.66.573 -- R1 redactor-unification: audit-log and autonomy staging/live secret-key redaction delegate to canonical I0008 SoT capture_artifact_redact._kv_key_is_secret (F-COREBD17-03, F-TOOLSO04-03).

## v3.66.572 -- FE batch (4 XSS/redaction findings): F-FE06-01 review-item href gated on an http(s) allowlist via isHttpUrl (non-http shown as inert text); F-FE04-01 pairing QR rendered as an <img> data-URL instead of dangerouslySetInnerHTML (script cannot execute); F-FE02-01 dropped the fake typed-confirm phrase labels across Library/Maintenance/Vpn for an honest labelled 1-click confirm; F-FE09-01 copySiteConfig clipboard redaction adds the OAuth/CSRF token class csrf/xsrf/bearer/otp/nonce/challenge/captcha/jwt/signature (code/state deliberately excluded).

## v3.66.571 -- F-CBD03-03: library scanner missing-pass now scopes on a path boundary via _fp_under_root (was fp.startswith(root), a raw prefix -- a sibling dir like /data/vids-backup was swept into the scope of root /data/vids); real descendants unaffected.

## v3.66.570 -- F-TO06-02: cap01_witnesses.py direct-CLI path fixed -- main() reads RESULTS dicts by key (was a 3-tuple unpack over 5-key dicts -> ValueError), dead empty loop removed, and the __main__ guard moved to EOF so every witness registers before main() runs.

## v3.66.569 -- F-SWEEP-N1: backup smoke_restore now confines archive extraction -- rejects .. traversal, absolute-path, and tar symlink/hardlink members before extract (tar-slip/zip-slip hardening); benign archives unaffected.

## v3.66.568 -- Security(sweep): F-SWEEP-N3 login success-URL match now requires a path-segment boundary (rejects prefix-sibling e.g. /dashboard-evil vs /dashboard); F-SWEEP-N6 bulk_url_transform rejects ReDoS-prone regex (nested unbounded quantifier or overlong pattern) with HTTP 400 before compile/subn.

## v3.66.567 -- Tier-A batch: F-RUN03-01 runner_queue.load_urls uses a distinct local for the playlist-expand result so the added-URL accumulator is no longer polluted with duplicates; F-COREBD08-01 vpn_wireguard writes the secret .conf private-from-birth via os.open 0o600 and creates CONF_DIR mode 0o700 (mirrors vpn_openvpn P13-A), closing the world-readable window between write and chmod.

## v3.66.566 -- Tier-A path-traversal batch: F-REC01-01 build_template_from_wacz default draft path slugifies the capture host; F-TOOLS_OTHER02-01 bulk_review_captures slugifies the host before the candidate path; F-TOOLS_OTHER07-02 runner_contracts narrows a bare except to (SyntaxError, UnicodeDecodeError) so non-parse errors surface.

## v3.66.565 -- Tier-A batch: F-COCKPIT01-01 cockpit captures/normalize uses canonical cc.confine (rejects prefix-sibling traversal); F-TO06-01 bd_decomp_lib.cmd_baseline guards an unknown target (rc 2, not KeyError); F-RUN03-03 runner_util._resolve_safe logs a typed indicator instead of the raw credential value.

## v3.66.564 -- Tier-A batch (path-traversal + error-contract): F-TOOLSO04-02 organize_captures._fs_safe rejects dot-only path segments; F-AUTH02-03 cookie_quality validates site_id charset before the cookies fallback join; F-COCKPIT01-02 cockpit /api/activity guards a non-numeric ?limit against a 500.

## v3.66.563 -- F-AUTH02-02: cookie_clipboard drops any cookie whose name/value/domain/path carries a TAB, CR, or LF before serializing to Netscape cookies.txt and to Playwright format, closing a cookie-line injection where a crafted value could forge an extra jar row.

## v3.66.562 -- F-SWEEP-N4: exports.to_csv neutralizes CSV formula injection -- a site-controlled cell beginning with = + - @ TAB or CR is prefixed with a single quote so it cannot execute as a formula when the export is opened in Excel or Google Sheets.

## v3.66.561 -- F-COREBD11-01: global_config.set_config restricts the persisted secret-bearing app_config.json to owner-only (0o600) before the atomic rename, so tokens/credentials in the global config are no longer group or world readable under the process umask.

## v3.66.560 -- F-COREBD18-02: dom_serialize.nodes_to_html validates tag and attribute NAMES at emit (invalid/injecting names dropped, wrapper skipped but children kept); text and attribute-value escaping already present. Closes an HTML-injection asymmetry reachable only on a crafted or tampered rrweb node tree.

## v3.66.559 -- Input validation (F-COREBD06-01): site_editor.validate_config now rejects non-finite numerics (NaN/+-inf) in NUMERIC_RANGES fields, mirroring the guarded validate_numeric_updates (VR-P08/I0004). NaN slipped the range check (nan<lo and nan>hi are both False), so a hand-edited or imported sites_config.json carrying e.g. wait=NaN validated ok=True and could persist into live config; it is now rejected with a 'finite number' error. The two validators share NUMERIC_RANGES and are now in parity on non-finite. +-inf were already caught by the range comparison; now rejected explicitly for a clearer message. No route/module/import-edge change.

## v3.66.558 -- Secret hygiene (F-CORE_BD14-01): marketplace/eol_export template export now redacts the full site_editor.SECRET_FIELDS SoT. marketplace._REDACT_KEYS covered only 2/10 (password/auth_token) and name-mismatched tpdb_key vs tpdb_api_key, so qb_password/captcha_api_key/stash_api_key/plex_token/jellyfin_api_key/ha_token/tpdb_api_key/ai_api_key leaked into the portable EOL/marketplace bundle template AND the import-preview config_preview/secrets_omitted -- an AUTOMATION_POLICY no-secrets-in-outputs violation and a broken secrets-omitted promise. _redact + preview now union SECRET_FIELDS via a memoized lazy import (superset per I-CORE_BD14) so an export can never fall behind a newly added secret field. No route/module change; new intended import edge marketplace->site_editor re-frozen.

## v3.66.557 -- Secret hygiene (F-CORE_BD10-01): user_templates now strips _SECRET_KEYS (password/api_key/cookies/auth_token/vpn creds/etc.) from every incoming template in both import paths before save, and from export_user_templates -- so the on-disk set and the downloadable export match the import-preview secrets-omitted promise (was a contract violation + an AUTOMATION_POLICY no-secrets-in-outputs leak).

## v3.66.556 -- SSRF hardening (F-RUN03-02): multi_conn.probe/download now validate the initial host via canonical _is_safe_public_host and re-validate every redirect hop via a response event-hook, refusing non-public targets (loopback, link-local/cloud-metadata, CGNAT, reserved, private) before connect. A download/media URL is never legitimately internal, so all non-public hosts are blocked (no LAN exception). follow_redirects kept True but hop hosts are re-classified.

## v3.66.555 -- SSRF hardening (F-CORE_BD15-01): candidate_filter.classify now rejects a download candidate whose host is a non-public IP literal (RFC1918, loopback, link-local/cloud-metadata, RFC6598 CGNAT, reserved) via the canonical _classify_ip, closing the transport extracted-URL SSRF (candidates were fetched with session cookies to internal infra incl. BD own loopback API). Literal-only in the hot classify path; an internal download candidate is never legitimate.

## v3.66.554 -- F-CORE_BD04-01 test fix (supersedes the 553 candidate): route the hook-sink tests through _hook_urlopen and use literal-IP targets. The 553 candidate regressed test_hooks.py -- the redirect-validating opener bypassed the urllib.request.urlopen mock, and the new DNS-resolving validator (correctly) rejected the tests synthetic hostnames. hooks.py is byte-unchanged from 553; the SSRF classifier and redirect guard are unchanged.

## v3.66.553 -- SSRF hardening (F-CORE_BD04-01): hooks._validate_webhook_url now resolves and classifies the target host across all six hook sinks, rejecting link-local/cloud-metadata, CGNAT, reserved, multicast, and unspecified addresses while allowing the intended LAN/loopback integration targets (plex/jellyfin/home-assistant/stash), and re-validates redirect hops via a custom opener. Operator-scoped: LAN allowed, dangerous ranges blocked.

## v3.66.552 -- SSRF read-primitive hardening (F-CBD12-02): selector_playground.fetch_page validates the target host via the canonical _is_safe_public_host before any fetch (both the requests and playwright branches), refuses non-global targets with no body returned, follows redirects manually with per-hop re-validation, and adds a per-request route guard to the browser branch. Route-reachable via POST /api/playground/test.

## v3.66.551 -- SSRF hardening (F-RUN03-04): TelemetryMixin._pick_fastest_mirror validates the target host via the canonical _is_safe_public_host before the speculative HEAD (scheme allowlist alone was insufficient) and stops following redirects; refuses non-global mirror/file_url targets. Opt-in speculative-mirror status-oracle defense-in-depth.

## v3.66.550 -- SSRF hardening (F-COREBD17-02): site_weather.probe_http validates the target host and every redirect hop via the canonical _is_safe_public_host before fetching; refuses non-global targets and follows redirects manually. Blind-SSRF defense-in-depth.

## v3.66.549 -- Reject non-finite (NaN/inf) config floats in the runner_transport size-sanity gate (min_size_pct) and the runner_auth pre-emptive-relogin gate (cookie_max_age_hours) via a per-module _finite_config_float helper, so a NaN cannot accept an undersized download and an inf cannot disable relogin (F-RUN02-01).

## v3.66.548 -- Reject non-finite (NaN/inf) config floats in runner disk/bandwidth gates via a shared _finite_config_float helper so a NaN disk_threshold_gb cannot disable the low_disk stop or disk-pressure throttle (F-RUN01-03).

## v3.66.547 -- Reject non-finite (NaN/inf) plugin-verdict confidence in detect.merge_plugin_recognitions so a NaN cannot evade the low-confidence demotion (F-COREBD05-01).

## v3.66.546 -- deep_detect numeric robustness: parse_hls_master catches OverflowError on an overflowing BANDWIDTH and treats a non-finite FRAME-RATE as missing (F-REC03-02); _flatten_download_candidates reuses the guarded resolution result instead of a second unguarded int() cast so a non-integer JSON-LD width/height no longer crashes the flatten (F-REC02-01). Backend-only; 7 release guards byte-identical.

## v3.66.545 -- Numeric isfinite backstop: admission._disk_hold and _common._honeypot_score_threshold reject non-finite (NaN/inf) config values after float() so a NaN threshold cannot silently disable the low-disk admission hold (F-COREBD18-01) or honeypot dropping (F-REC03-03). Backend-only; 7 release guards byte-identical.

## v3.66.544 -- Security F-CBD01-01: dev_suite._fetch_manifest_text validates the URL host via the canonical _is_safe_public_host before the outbound GET, refusing loopback/link-local (169.254)/RFC1918/RFC6598/ULA so the dev manifest-probe cannot be an SSRF read primitive against internal targets. Route 200+ok:false contract unchanged; the new import edge is function-local.

## v3.66.543 -- Security F-RUN01-02: _build_ytdlp_cmd inserts a bare -- options terminator before the URL so a leading-dash URL cannot be smuggled into yt-dlp flag surface (e.g. --exec).

## v3.66.542 -- SSRF: guard tier_probe -- probe_higher_tiers now installs an httpx request event hook that revalidates every candidate + redirect host via the canonical _is_safe_public_host and skips non-public targets; closes F-SWEEP-N2.

## v3.66.541 -- SSRF: guard /api/jsonapi/probe -- site_root and every extra_hosts entry are now validated via the canonical _is_url_public (rejects loopback/private/link-local/reserved/CGNAT) before probe_site; closes F-APP05-01. Sibling request-path entrypoints (template sandbox, manifest probe, webhooks) deferred pending per-endpoint policy.

## v3.66.540 -- SSRF: consolidate stale IP-publicity classifiers -- app._is_url_public and runner._scrape_listing_urls now delegate to the canonical _is_safe_public_host (rejects RFC 6598 CGNAT 100.64.0.0/10); closes F-APP01-01, F-RUN01-01. No route or frontend change.

The stash box runs cloakbrowser 0.4.5 driving stealth Chromium 146.0.7680.177.5 (STATE.json: resolve_backend()=cloakbrowser, "cloakbrowser Chromium 146 installed"); 0.3.31 predates that binary channel, so the old floor understated the real minimum. LESSON: requirements-cloak.txt carries a deliberate floor (not a hard pin) so offline + online install paths both resolve; when the verified live binary channel advances, raise the floor to match reality rather than hard-pinning, and give the floor a RED-first guard test so it cannot silently regress.

## v3.66.538 -- On-stash fix completion: the 4th consumer of the BD_WORK classification the 537 cut missed. test_editor_key_set_matches_deploy_only_source (test_v3_66_504) asserts the envfile-editor key set (_envfile.EDITOR_KEYS) equals (_DEPLOY_ONLY - _HOST_MANAGED). Verified: test_v3_66_504 (13/13) + full re-sweep green -- config_danger 305, env-tranche 315/319-a/b/c/d, env-parity 317/319-4.4/4.5, settings-center secret/slice4/slice5/wiring, config_parity_ratchet. LESSON: a new BD_* env var has FOUR classification consumers that must agree, not three -- config_surface_inventory's _DEPLOY_ONLY, reports/config_gui_manifest.json, AND _envfile.EDITOR_KEYS (via the test_504 deploy-only-source join). Classify a new promoted-tool env var in all of them in the same cut.

## v3.66.532 -- PHC-1 (B1) follow-up: cockpit writes now SEND a CSRF token. The @531 cut extended the global _check_csrf guard to /cockpit/api/, but the cockpit shell's api() fetch helper attached X-CSRF-Token from csrf(), which reads a meta[name=csrf-token] tag the cockpit _PAGE never embeds -- so api() sent an EMPTY token and every /cockpit/api/ write 403'd in a real browser session (a browser that loaded the SPA carries the bd_session cookie /api/csrf mints unconditionally with path=/; on-stash auth-allow-all has no bd_session, so the green suite + capture.sh never exercised it). Fix: api() now self-mints from /api/csrf when csrf() is empty, mirroring the existing apiRoot() helper (one helper edit, tools/cockpit_console.py). RED-first tests/test_phc1_cockpit_csrf_send.py (the can-supply-token guard RED on pristine 531 -> GREEN; plus minted-token-not-refused end-to-end + writes-route-through-api coverage pins). Non-route, non-guard, no new import edge; FUNCTION_INDEX/DEPENDENCY_GRAPH/gui_parity/import-graph baseline all unchanged. NOTE: tools/cockpit_console.py is deploy-excluded (operator live edits) -- hand-reconcile on stash; the shipped copy is fixed for fresh installs.

Non-route, non-guard, no new import edge.

## v3.66.527 -- VR-P11 (redirected): the PUT /api/sites numeric backstop now rejects non-integer values for the 8 integer-typed NUMERIC_RANGES fields (max_concurrent, max_retries, no_button_threshold, min_resolution, chunk_size_mb, prelogin_minutes, parallel_chunks, warmup_every). ## v3.66.525 -- VERIFY GUARD CUT (ships alone): VR-P13 + VR-P14. RED-first (tests/test_v3_66_525_perf_and_robustness.py, 13 cases) proven failing on pristine 524, GREEN after. VR-P13 (GUARD: bulk_downloader/extraction_core.py) segment_role was latently O(n^2) on a long pure-digit path segment -- the _RENDITION_SIGNAL regex carried an UNBOUNDED \d+ in its (?:\d+\s*fps) branch, so on a long digit run re.search retried every start position with linear \d+ backtracking (~9s at n=20000, scaling 4x per 2x n); the digit run is now bounded to \d{1,4} (fps is 1-4 digits) -> linear (about 11ms at n=20000). Detection of real fps / resolution descriptors (60fps, 120fps, 1920x1080, 1080p) is unchanged, and an opaque long-digit id is not promoted to rendition. GUARD SHA DECLARED: bulk_downloader/extraction_core.py d688aca9 -> 5b6248a5 -- this is the ONLY guard changed; the other 6 (session_capture 547d70c9, capture_session 27be68b9, dom_capture 0559903d, dom_recorder 1657d0a0, capture_bodies 2d851646, build_release e8142436) are byte-identical. VR-P14 (NON-guard: tools/build_template_from_wacz.py) build_template called cap.get(...) / e.get(...) on the raw json.loads of capture.json with no type guard, so a type-malformed capture (a non-dict root, or a dom_log / network_log that is not a list of dict events) raised AttributeError (L1698 / L1703 / L1716) instead of degrading to an empty template; build_template now normalizes the cap-derived collections at the function top (cap -> {} when non-dict; dom_log / network_log / action_timeline -> dict-event lists; storage_snapshot -> {} when non-dict). A well-formed capture is unaffected (additive). Scope note: leaf-value malformation (e.g. a network_log entry whose url field is a non-string) is out of scope -- handling it would harden extraction_core._network_patterns and expand the guard diff beyond the minimal P13 bound. ## v3.66.521 -- SECURITY HOTFIX: four read-only-VERIFY defects closed (VR-P01/P02/P03/P05). Backend-only: no route, no new import edge, no new tools/*.py, no guard-file change. RED-first (tests/test_v3_66_521_security_hotfix.py, 11 cases) proven failing on pristine 520, GREEN after. VR-P01 (HIGH) notify_apprise.send(): apobj.add(u) attached no tag while notify(tag=event) filters by tag, so every TAGGED runtime notification (download_complete etc.) matched zero services and was silently dropped; add() now passes tag=tag, so the runtime dispatch path actually delivers (driven through the real send()/_fire path against an in-process loopback receiver). VR-P02 (HIGH) app_settings_center._mask_secrets(): masking was non-recursive, so a nested secret (accounts[].password, and any nested api_key) was returned RAW on the read endpoints (GET .../effective); masking now recurses into dicts/lists via _mask_nested while the existing flat-secret presence-only behavior is preserved byte-for-byte. VR-P03 (MED-H) capture_artifact_redact._kv_key_is_secret(): the hand-kept _KV_SECRET_KEYWORDS tuple had drifted from the redaction SoT and was missing the anchored OAuth-fragment keys code/state plus apikey/challenge/captcha/nonce/otp, so an exchangeable OAuth '#code=...&state=...' redirect survived the always-on kv credential floor into capture.json; the credential class is now DERIVED from the SoT SENSITIVE_QS_KEY by subtracting the signing-metadata-only markers (expires/policy/hash/x-amz-), so the floor scrubs the real secret in a signed URL (X-Amz-Signature) while a keep_full surface still retains the non-secret signing params (X-Amz-Expires) -- resolving the AWS SigV4 overlap and NOT regressing test_v3_66_245 (Expires kept under keep_full). The three header-origin credential markers csrf/xsrf/bearer the original tuple carried (absent from the query SoT, they live in SENSITIVE_HEADER) are preserved explicitly so prior floor coverage is not dropped; the SoT-derived portion is a strict subset of the SoT, so the floor can never scrub a key the SoT would not flag. VR-P05 (MED) notify_apprise.validate_urls(): referenced apprise.AppriseURLBase, removed in apprise>=1.7, raising AttributeError and rejecting EVERY URL; now resolves whichever parser exists (URLBase or the legacy alias) and falls back to schema-from-string with Apprise.add() as the validity arbiter (no fail-closed on a missing parser symbol). 7 release guards byte-identical (none touched). ## v3.66.516 -- Post-515 sandbox batch (Items 1+2, non-route). Item 1 (2c-guard live-count tail): make the soft zero-live-match promote interlock built in 513 actually fire. The Test step now probes the trigger selector's live match count via /api/template/sandbox (matches.trigger_selector.match_count) using the build-derived trigger selector, stores it, and threads it into the promote preflight (runPromotePreflight -> promoteCheck(file, triggerMatchCount)) so a 0-match trigger surfaces the existing gate_warning; a "trigger: N matches on live" chip is shown in the Test step. New guidedCapture helpers triggerMatchCountFromSandbox (pure, defensive) + templateSandbox (thin client); the live fetch is stash-only (the sandbox has no network, so the count stays null/unknown there and the interlock stays silent rather than warning spuriously). Backend promote_check already consumed trigger_match_count (513) -- this is FE-only. Item 2 (B1 residual self-heal): a stale capture_in_flight marker can no longer persist forever when an onboarding capture dies WITHOUT producing a draft. The marker now records the capture-wrapper pid + started_at (run_capture_flow returns the detached Popen pid); /template_status self-heals on draft-exists OR (no draft AND the capture is provably gone) -- a pid-liveness check (os.kill(pid,0): dead -> clear; alive or not-ours -> keep) plus a conservative >=40-min age backstop used only when there is no usable pid. Errs safe in every direction (a live capture is never cleared, even a long one; NOT wacz-exists). No new import edge (os already imported); non-route.

## v3.66.507 -- Bucket 3b: raw vpn/widgets store-metadata editor + tunnel rekey (non-guard). vpn.* and widgets.* metadata (schema_version, tunnel_id, _saved_at) live in SEPARATE stores (tunnels.json / widgets.json), not global_config, with no per-key meta API -- so the GUI path is a raw JSON store-file editor. R2: vpn_config.rekey_tunnel(old,new) moves the secrets + rewrites embedded @cred refs + renames the tunnel atomically. For an already-approved host with every gate green and a good backup there is NO operator checkpoint (the template self-heals in place, staying in service); any uncertainty -- gate failure, drift over tolerance, or post-write verify regression -- stages for review or auto-restores, so live is never left broken. ## v3.66.464 -- scandir sweep (growth-prevention): route the remaining full-tree rglob("*") walks in tools/cockpit_core.py through one shared os.scandir helper. Companion to 463; both follow-ons from the BUG-2 warehouse work. Live data (build 3.66.462) put smart_search / release_readiness / next_best_action at 0.16-0.23s -- cheap NOW because the corpus is tiny (sites_loaded=0, empty store) -- so this is PREVENTION (protects against artifact-volume growth), NOT a current-live fix; the only endpoints over ~1s were warehouse (fixed at 462) and mission-control (fixed at 463). All three do a full-tree `for f in root.rglob("*")` walk. Unlike the 462 warehouse fix (whose win was deleting an O(N log N) sort), these use PLAIN rglob -- so the lever is different: rglob builds a Path object for every entry INCLUDING each directory and re-stats for is_dir, whereas os.scandir reuses the DirEntry.is_dir/is_file flags cached from readdir and builds a Path only for files. Measured ~2.2x faster on a dir-heavy tree (1500 dirs x 4 files: plain rglob 0.0808s vs scandir 0.0366s); both yield the identical file set. New module-level helper _scandir_files(root) yields every regular file under root as a Path via an iterative os.scandir walk -- a faithful drop-in for (f for f in root.rglob("*") if f.is_file()). The three call sites become `for f in _scandir_files(root):` with the now-redundant per-file f.is_file() guard removed (the helper yields only files). Ordering is arbitrary, exactly as the plain rglob walks already were, and all three consumers are order-independent (smart_search caps at [:100] on an already-unsorted set; release_readiness/next_best_action only count posture leaks), so output is preserved. LEFT UNSWEPT (out of scope, intentional): start_task uses sorted(out.rglob("*")) scoped to one output dir (benign + needs the sort for deterministic display); _review_queue_count / site_intelligence / review_items use TARGETED pattern rglobs (rglob("site_profile.json") etc.), not full-tree rglob("*") -- different, cheap, not part of this sweep. RED-first tests/test_v3_66_464_scandir_sweep.py (3): structural (each swept function uses _scandir_files and has no rglob in CODE -- comments/docstring stripped), helper-faithfulness (on a seeded nested tree _scandir_files yields EXACTLY the rglob+is_file file set, files only, no dirs), and performance (same-process ratio: scandir < 0.85x rglob on a dir-heavy tree, asserting the prevention premise actually holds). RED-proven on 463. SCOPE: tools/cockpit_core.py only (+ the new test + 3-part bump + PIN_INDEX). No new import (os + Path already imported -> dependency_graph 1169 IN-SYNC), no app.py / runner.py change (FUNCTION_INDEX no-op), no route/tool (gui_parity reconcile GREEN, ENDPOINT_CATALOG/ROUTE_INDEX no-op), 7 release guards byte-identical. Built backend-only over the 463 dist (FE 0/0/0); band from the extracted zip green under run_tests.py + real pytest (291 cockpit_core-consumer regression tests pass); verify_release --zip PASS exit 0. CLEAN OVERLAY (cockpit_core.py only). Caps the warehouse-class cluster as O(N) scandir walks that hold under load.

## v3.66.463 -- mission-control memoize: collapse the 2x+ sub-aggregation fan-out (live mission-control ~1.5s). Follow-on to the BUG-2 warehouse work: /cockpit/api/template/mission-control measured ~1.5s live (vs the standalone readiness primitive at ~0.16s). Traced: operator_mission_control() is an AGGREGATION, not a tree walk -- so the 464 warehouse scandir helper does nothing for it. The cost is REDUNDANT recomputation of the same expensive read-only primitives at multiple depths in one request: operator_mission_control() computes login_template_health / video_template_health / template_maturity_score / template_review_queue, and site_readiness() (which it also calls) recomputes those same four internally, AND template_review_queue() -> _template_review_items() recomputes login/video health again -> each runs 2-3x per request. Fix: a request-scoped memo in tools/cockpit_templates.py. @_mc_scope wraps operator_mission_control so its whole rollup runs inside one fresh per-request memo (a contextvars.ContextVar); the four @_mc_memoized sub-aggregations then compute ONCE per scope and serve the cached result to repeat callers at any depth. OUTSIDE a scope (every standalone endpoint -- login-health, video-health, maturity, review-queue, site-readiness) the wrapped functions are UNCHANGED: memo is None -> they recompute fresh, so there is no cross-request staleness. Only zero-arg calls are memoized; the results are read-only and never mutated by callers, so sharing the cached object is safe. Pure decorator additions -- the function bodies are untouched. RED-first tests/test_v3_66_463_mc_memoize.py (4): dedupe-within-scope (repeated in-scope calls return the SAME object = body ran once; fresh objects outside a scope), output-preservation (the memoized rollup is byte-identical to operator_mission_control.__wrapped__() -- the memo-free reference computed via the undecorated body), shape-intact, and inactive-outside-scope. TEST-DESIGN NOTE (the 462 lesson applied again): a memo does NOT reduce the NUMBER of call-attempts -- the call sites still call, they just get a cached result -- so counting calls is the WRONG proxy; these tests assert object identity + output equivalence (the real property), caught when an initial call-count test wrongly stayed RED. SCOPE: tools/cockpit_templates.py only (+ the new test + 3-part bump + PIN_INDEX). No app.py / runner.py / route / tool / guard / import-edge change: FUNCTION_INDEX no-op, dependency_graph 1169 IN-SYNC (contextvars + functools are stdlib, no tracked edge), gui_parity reconcile GREEN, ENDPOINT_CATALOG/ROUTE_INDEX no-op, G12 OK, 7 release guards byte-identical. Built backend-only over the 462 dist (FE 0/0/0); band from the extracted zip green under run_tests.py + real pytest (657 cockpit/template regression tests pass -- standalone endpoints unchanged); verify_release --zip PASS exit 0. CLEAN OVERLAY (cockpit_templates.py only; no deploy-excluded file). Expected to cut mission-control's 2-3x recompute toward a single pass.

## v3.66.462 -- BUG-2 warehouse traversal rewrite (the REAL fix; on-stash 461 left it still ~9.5s). The v3.66.461 cut trimmed cockpit_core.artifact_warehouse() from 3 stat syscalls/file to 1, but the live /cockpit/api/warehouse was STILL ~9.5s (was 10.4s) -- the 461 RED test asserted stat-COUNT (a proxy that improved 2.95 -> 0.95) while never measuring wall-clock, so it went green though latency barely moved. Profiling proved the miss: the per-file stats were only ~16% of the cost; the dominant ~84% is the traversal -- sorted(root.rglob("*")) materializes EVERY path across three roots into a list and sorts it (O(N log N) over N Path objects). This cut replaces that with an os.scandir iterative walk: one cached DirEntry.stat() per file, no full-tree Path materialize, no global sort; relative path via a cheap string slice off the absolute entry path; per-category lists sorted once at the end (small sort over dicts, not Paths) so the listing stays deterministic. Profiled ~4.5x faster on a 6k-file tree (0.120 -> 0.026s); expected to take the live ~9.5s down to roughly ~2s. Output contract preserved exactly (test_v3_66_99 + the 461 contract test stay green). RED-first tests/test_v3_66_462_warehouse_scandir.py (3): STRUCTURAL (artifact_warehouse uses os.scandir, no rglob in code -- comments stripped so a doc reference can't trip it), PERFORMANCE (faster than a faithful sorted-rglob reference run on the SAME seeded tree in the SAME process so environment variance cancels: ratio 0.97x on 461 -> well under 0.6 on 462), and CORRECTNESS (output byte-equivalent). This time the test asserts the ACTUAL metric (traversal shape + a same-process speed ratio), not a stat-count proxy. The now-dead `import stat as _stat` (added @461 for the S_ISREG check, unused once scandir's DirEntry.is_file() replaced it) is removed. SCOPE: tools/cockpit_core.py only (+ the new test + 3-part bump + PIN_INDEX). No app.py / runner.py / route / tool / guard / import-edge change: FUNCTION_INDEX no-op, dependency_graph 1169 IN-SYNC (import removed; stat is stdlib, no tracked edge), gui_parity reconcile GREEN, ENDPOINT_CATALOG/ROUTE_INDEX no-op, G12 OK, 7 release guards byte-identical. Built backend-only over the 461 dist (FE 0/0/0); band from the extracted zip green under run_tests.py + real pytest; verify_release --zip PASS exit 0. CLEAN OVERLAY: 462 touches NO deploy-excluded file (unlike 461's BUG-3 in cockpit_console.py), so it ships via a plain unzip -o overlay -- no hand-patch. LESSON: a perf fix's RED test must assert the user-visible metric (wall-clock / traversal shape via a same-process ratio), not a proxy like syscall count -- 461 passed its proxy and shipped a still-slow endpoint.

## v3.66.461 -- cockpit bugfix slice: three live-stash bugs from the v3.66.460 cockpit sweep, fixed together RED-first. BUG-1 (High): the bg_scheduler module-level init in app.py passed capture_enqueue_fn=_capture_enqueue as a BARE forward reference, but _capture_enqueue is def'd ~1500 lines later, so at module-load time the name was unbound -> NameError swallowed by the init except -> "bg_scheduler init failed: name '_capture_enqueue' is not defined" every boot, leaving the WHOLE background scheduler dead (saved-search enqueue, cookie_relogin, bitrot, alerts, site_weather, discovery, maintenance, scheduled_exports). Invisible to the test suite because the block is gated on BD_DISABLE_KEEPALIVE (=1 in tests); only the live process (no keepalive) hits it -- which is why the green on-stash suite coexisted with a dead scheduler. Fix: defer the reference in a lambda (lambda site_id, urls: _capture_enqueue(site_id, urls)) like its sibling getters, so the name resolves at CALL time. This removes the live blocker on OPV-F3.1 (the enqueue lane) and the periodic drivers behind F1.3/F1.4 (operator soak still required to sign those off). BUG-2 (Med-High): cockpit_core.artifact_warehouse() made THREE stat syscalls per file (Path.is_file + .stat().st_size + .stat().st_mtime) over an unbounded rglob of three roots -> ~10s on a large live tree (GET /cockpit/api/warehouse stuck on skeletons). Fix: one stat() per entry, file-ness via stat.S_ISREG on the already-fetched mode (per-file stats 2.95 -> 0.95, measured); the output contract is preserved exactly. BUG-3 (Med): the cockpit SPA go()/mountTab() did host.innerHTML = await PAGES[x]() with NO "still-active?" guard between the await and the write, so a slow prior tab resolved late and painted under the new tab's header (reproduced Readiness->noVNC and Queue-intel->Ops). Fix: a monotonic __navGen token captured at entry and re-checked after the await before the innerHTML write (tag-and-drop-stale; lighter than threading AbortControllers through every page builder). RED-first: tests/test_v3_66_461_cockpit_bugfix.py, 7 tests (6 RED on pristine 460 -> GREEN; 1 output-contract-preservation guard green throughout) under run_tests.py + real pytest. SCOPE: bulk_downloader/app.py (BUG-1; +4 doc lines -> FUNCTION_INDEX regenerated for the line shift, _capture_enqueue L3152 -> L3156), tools/cockpit_core.py (BUG-2 + import stat), tools/cockpit_console.py (BUG-3 inline JS). No new tools/routes/guards/import-edges: dependency_graph 1169 IN-SYNC, gui_parity reconcile GREEN (no new tool), ENDPOINT_CATALOG/ROUTE_INDEX no-op, G12 OK, 7 release guards byte-identical, PIN_INDEX regenerated for the bump. Built backend-only over the 460 dist (FE 0/0/0; no frontend/src change -- BUG-3 is the cockpit console's inline JS, not the React SPA). DEPLOY NOTE: tools/cockpit_console.py is deploy-excluded (merge-not-overlay; operator edits live) -- BUG-3 needs a hand-reconcile on stash, while BUG-1 + BUG-2 overlay normally via app.py + cockpit_core.py.

No route / no app.py / no runner.py change: FUNCTION_INDEX / ENDPOINT_CATALOG / ROUTE_INDEX / gui_parity all no-op; dependency_graph --check IN-SYNC (1167 edges, no new tracked edge); R0 import-graph gate PASS (baseline holds, 1167); G12 OK; PIN_INDEX regenerated. The lazy `import bulk_downloader.provider_resolve` is call-time only, so no import cycle. The `pr.resolve_provider_embed = spy` rebind and `pr._YT_CIPHER_YTDLP_PATH_CACHE[0] = ...` in-place mutation already work through the shim (deep_detect reads the shim attr at call time; the cache is a shared object via re-export). NOT FUNCTION_INDEX-tracked. ## v3.66.447 -- DECOMP-R0 + DECOMP-R1 (robustness track; tooling-only -- no route, app.py/runner.py, frontend, or release-guard change). Two Phase-0 decomposition robustness assets landed as one consolidated cut.

R0 (import-graph regression gate): new tools/decomp/import_graph_gate.py + frozen baseline tools/decomp/import_graph_baseline.json (1083 edges) + tests/test_import_graph_no_new_edges.py. The gate freezes the intended internal import-edge set (== DEPENDENCY_GRAPH package.out) and asserts a cut adds no edge outside it -- the complement to the route_map/surface-lock invariants (those prove nothing was REMOVED; this proves nothing NEW crept in: accidental coupling / lazy-accessor sprawl, hazard H-14). `--check` fails (exit 1) on any new edge; `--update` re-freezes the baseline (an intended new edge is DECLARED in the same cut, exactly like a guard-SHA change; an edge removed by a cut is reported but does not fail). The gate loads tools/dependency_graph.py BY PATH (not via a static import) so it contributes ZERO edge to the graph it measures -- DEPENDENCY_GRAPH.json is byte-identical after adding it (confirmed by regen + diff). RED-first: the test failed on the pristine tree (gate absent) and is GREEN after; plus an in-memory teeth test (a synthetic edge absent from the baseline must be flagged) and a live end-to-end demonstration (a real new tools->pkg import edge raised exit 1, then PASS once removed).

R1 (shim-over-rm generator): new tools/decomp/make_shim.py + tests/test_shim_reexport_completeness.py. Makes the ADD-only re-export shim the deploy default for .py->package leaf splits (hazard H-01: an `unzip -o` overlay cannot delete, so a removed monolith left as a stale file shadows the new package on stash -> dependency_graph re-counts the monolith -> in-sync FAIL). compute_required_reexports() derives the external importer-set -- INCLUDING private names (hazard H-04: an immovable release guard doing `from pkg.<target> import _private` must keep resolving) -- from the source tree; generate_shim() emits the shim re-exporting that full set; check_shim_complete() flags any shim that drops a required name (a private dropped under a bare `import *` is the precise failure mode, since `*` never re-exports underscored names). RED-first synthetic-fixture test (make_shim absent -> RED; GREEN after), including a teeth case proving an incomplete shim is reported.

Footprint: the tools/decomp/ files dodge the NON-recursive `tools/*.py` globs in dependency_graph (tool.total / tool_stems) and gui_parity_inventory (the operator-surface itemset), so hazard H-06 does NOT fire -- gui_parity_inventory regen is byte-identical (confirmed). No route change (route_map/G12 unchanged), no app.py/runner.py edit, FUNCTION_INDEX unchanged (tracks only app.py/runner.py), DEPENDENCY_GRAPH unchanged, 7 release-guard SHAs byte-identical. ## v3.66.392 -- VPN egress follow-ons (Track-K continuation), backend-only. Two in-process egress paths now honor the per-site VPN proxy that Track-K (@390) wired for payload downloads. (1) VPN-MULTICONN: the parallel-range multi_conn client gained a proxy-native path -- multi_conn.probe/download take a proxy= and thread it into EVERY per-worker httpx.Client (probe + internal probe + each worker); runner._try_multi_conn_download takes proxy_url and forwards it; the @390 gate that DISABLED multi_conn whenever a proxy was in effect (the "not proxy_url" guard) is removed, so VPN downloads keep multi-connection throughput. Safety preserved: a vpn_required site with a down tunnel already fails closed before the gate (the _download_proxy_url raise), so proxy_url here is None (degrade open) or a usable proxy; if multi_conn cannot honor it, the probe declines and the single-connection stream carries the same proxy -- never an unproxied multi-conn download. (2) VPN-CONTROLPLANE: the three discovery httpx.Client sites in runner.py (download-test, listing scrape, deep-detect live probe) now resolve _download_proxy_url() and thread proxy=_cp_proxy, with a VPNRequiredError fail-closed branch matching each site (queue-error+continue / raise RuntimeError / return None) -- so a vpn_required site whose tunnel is down is never probed on the clear interface during discovery. NOT a guard cut (runner.py + multi_conn.py are not release guards; all 7 byte-identical). No route/frontend change; FUNCTION_INDEX regenerated (runner.py line shift); DEPENDENCY_GRAPH unchanged (no new import edge). RED-first tests/test_vpn_egress_followons.py 9/9; regression green (track_k 8/8, rate_limit 24/24, vpn_probe 10/10). Carry-forward: live tunnel-drop validation is on-stash; httpx[socks] must be on the stash venv for the httpx fallback to honor the SOCKS proxy (curl_cffi native). BUG-RESETPOOL was found ALREADY FIXED @336 (poolPath doubled-segment), so this cut is backend-only.

## v3.66.390 -- Track-K (#10): fail-closed VPN binding for in-process payload downloads. The browser already routes through the per-site VPN tunnel and fails closed when a vpn_required site tunnel is down; the in-process download clients (curl_cffi / httpx / multi_conn) did not -- they derived their proxy only from the explicit per-site proxy config and ignored the tunnel, so a vpn_required site whose tunnel dropped could egress the payload on the clear interface. New pure module download_egress.effective_download_proxy reuses the SAME per-site resolver the browser uses (vpn_runtime.get_socks_url_for_site): explicit proxy wins; tunnel up -> tunnel SOCKS url; site not required -> None (degrade open -- opt-in via vpn_required preserved, unchanged posture); site required + tunnel down/killed -> raises, so the caller fails closed and never builds an unproxied client. Wired via new SiteRunner._download_proxy_url into _http_download (sequential + parallel), _probe_size, _do_direct_http_download (httpx.stream now proxied), and the mirror probe; multi_conn is skipped when any proxy is in effect (no proxy-native path). New import edge runner -> download_egress; DEPENDENCY_GRAPH regenerated. NOT a guard cut (no release guard sits on the download path; all 7 byte-identical). Control-plane fetches (listing scrape, deep-detect probe, download-test harness) are a separate narrower follow-on; OS-firewall (DNS + yt-dlp subprocess coverage) stays opt-in per the Linux hybrid decision. ## v3.66.384 -- Cut 9: a11y/responsive audit-and-fill. Frontend-only; no route/spa_wiring/guard/backend change. The audit confirmed a strong base (140 focus-visible / 168 aria-label): clickable rows/cards already have no keyboard gaps, icon-only buttons already carry text (collapsible title) or aria-label (BulkActionBar clear), and the theme control is reachable on mobile via Settings (a primary tab) -- so no change was needed there. Three genuine gaps were filled: (1) prefers-reduced-motion -- a @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) block in index.css neutralizes animations + transitions app-wide (animation-duration/transition-duration 0.01ms !important, scroll-behavior auto) so the OS reduce-motion setting is honored across react-grid drag, backdrop blurs, and hover transitions; (2) narrow-table overflow -- a @media (max-width: 480px) rule makes any .bd-table its own horizontal scroll container (display:block + overflow-x:auto), media-scoped so desktop tables stay display:table; (3) action-bar wrap -- BulkActionBar's outer row and actions group gain flex-wrap so the count + action buttons wrap instead of overflowing on narrow widths. RED-first a11y.fills.test.ts (3) proven failing on pristine then green; full vitest 89 files / 348 tests; tsc clean; both media queries compile into the dist bundle and an in-browser probe confirms reduce-motion collapses a 300ms transition to 0.01ms and a .bd-table computes display:block at 380px / display:table at 1280px. Guards 7/7 byte-identical.

Adopted bd-table on all 14 hand-rolled route tables (21 <table> elements: Secrets, Budget, PoolsMacros, Schedules, Maintenance, SitePayloadActions, Dedup, Cluster, Settings, Vpn, History, AlertRules, BatchOps, ImportsCenter) -- none had sticky headers before, so this consolidates the header treatment that had drifted across them. ## v3.66.381 -- Phase 9: Local LLM Platform Hardening + AI-Assisted QA (9.0-9.16). Turns ad-hoc Cut-7 LLM calls into a bounded platform layer; the model is never authority and every slice keeps a deterministic validator/fallback. (9.0) Shared execution contract llm_exec.execute(LLMCallSpec)->LLMResult: one path with input-length cap, image gating, secret-input blocking (default deny), bounded retry, schema-validated output, deterministic fallback, advisory-only result. (9.1) model_registry: capability registry (text/vision, reachable, lanes, fail-open defaults); text-only models rejected for vision. (9.2) prompts: named/versioned prompt registry + per-result metadata. (9.3) llm_schemas: reference output schemas + enum/required enforcement (any schema failure -> fallback). (9.4) llm_cache: opt-in input-hash cache (re-validates on read, never stores raw input, hits do not bypass review). (9.5) llm_audit: report-first observability (per-task counts, latency, cache hit-rate, fallback/review counts; never logs raw secrets). (9.6) llm_readiness + tools/llm_readiness.py: green/amber/red readiness check (tolerates implicit :latest tag). (9.7) llm_eval + tools/llm_eval_harness.py: fixture-driven harness (mock-first). (9.8) render_qa: deterministic route enumeration + drift guard + per-view QA + domain ownership. (9.9) ai_review: optional advisory screenshot review (vision-model-gated, off by default, non-gating). (9.10) ai_chat + POST /api/ai/chat: stateless scratchpad backend (respects master switch, fail-open, no persistence; FE deferred). (9.11) doc_drift: deterministic doc/runbook drift detection + advisory summary. (9.12) selector_check: deterministic selector resolver is authority; model cannot mark approved. (9.13) challenge_classify: detection-only challenge typing, no bypass content. (9.14) login_assist: N-step login inference (assist only; cannot persist credentials/enable host). (9.15) naming_template: bounded naming-template suggestion (no FS mutation). (9.16) dedup_preview: preview-only near-dup planning (exact-hash stays authority; no delete path). One new main-app route (/api/ai/chat, spa_wired:false); 7 capture guards byte-identical; G12 OK.

## v3.66.360 -- SPA UI/UX unification Slices 4c-4d + 5 (form controls + workflow primitive + danger treatment + dark-text fix; NON-guard, no route, frontend-only). Slice 4c (form controls): SecretField gains className + onKeyDown and the 8 remaining raw type="password" inputs (Backup x2, Notifications, SiteSettings, Settings x3 incl. the configured-token round-trip fields, AddSiteWizard x2) are converted to it (each now write-only + autocomplete new-password + aria-labelled); the Vpn key/value ConfigEditor secret field is intentionally left (SecretField is not the kv editor). New shared components/ui/FieldCard (label + required + hint + an inline-validation error slot that replaces the hint) consolidates AddSiteWizard's local Field and adds advisory, non-blocking URL validation on the Start/Login URL fields. The /queue PageHeader trailing action row now wraps to its own full-width row on mobile (max-sm), and the Queue button group wraps -- no 390px horizontal overflow, desktop header byte-for-byte identical. Slice 4d (workflow primitive): new shared components/ui/WorkflowSteps stepper (accessible aria-current=step) extracted from AddSiteWizard's local Stepper; the single-console pages (VPN/Cluster/Secrets/Template Manager/Rebalance/Imports) are not stepped wizards and keep the PageHeader treatment. Slice 5 (danger treatment + dark fix): text-muted-foreground (174 usages) was an unmapped/inert utility, so muted text inherited --ink and rendered near-white in dark mode (no hierarchy) -- aliased muted-foreground to the canonical --ink-3 token in tailwind.config so muted text dims correctly per active theme in both modes; new shared components/ui/Callout (Info/Caution/Danger, role note/alert) frames the Settings Security and access section as a presentational Danger zone (no behavior change, wording-convention-safe). RED-first vitest 99/99 (new FieldCard / WorkflowSteps / Callout / SecretField / PageHeader-mobilewrap / route-smoke / AddSiteWizard-integration suites); tsc 0 and vite clean; a new dark-text audit went 24 near-white -> 0; both-theme 21-tab sweep 0 overflow and dark control-leak NONE; wizard dialog + danger callout confirmed in both themes. 7 guards byte-identical; ENDPOINT_CATALOG / FUNCTION_INDEX / DEPENDENCY_GRAPH / gui_parity unchanged; PIN_INDEX regenerated after the bump. Deferrals tracked in docs/PHASE6_PLAN.md. 3-part bump 359 to 360.

## v3.66.356 -- ROUTE_INDEX portability fix (test/tooling, no route, non-guard): the v3.66.355 in-sync gate failed on stash only, because stash's venv is nested inside the repo (~/BulkDownloader/venv/.../site-packages), so Flask's built-in /static view resolved UNDER the repo root and build_route_index emitted a venv path that the sandbox (venv outside the repo) never produces. _src_loc now classifies any file under a site-packages / dist-packages / node_modules tree (or a venv dir at the repo root) as external and records its stable dotted module name (<flask.app>) instead of a path, which is venv-layout-independent. Adds a regression test exercising the stash nested-venv layout so the sandbox band catches this class without stash access. Only tools/build_route_index.py plus the test change; ROUTE_INDEX.json regenerated (only the /static line field, now null). Guards 7/7 byte-identical. 3-part bump 355 to 356.

## v3.66.355 -- KB Tier-A query layer (NON-guard, no route): three generated, gated indexes that turn audit-by-grep and pin-whack-a-mole into one-line queries. ROUTE_INDEX.json (tools/build_route_index.py) joins app.url_map with the gui_parity inventory into one (method, path) entry per route carrying blueprint/file/csrf/spa_wired/kind, answering route ownership from url_map truth not a string grep (the class behind the Phase-4 /api/library error). PIN_INDEX.json (tools/build_pin_index.py) is an AST scan of tests for the drift-prone hand-typed pin forms (version asserts and the count-dict form behind the v3.66.302 miss); AST makes fixture-vs-pin confusion structurally impossible since fixture pins live inside string literals. tools/bd_kb.py adds the query layer (routes / what-pins / can-i-retire) over both indexes plus DEPENDENCY_GRAPH, with a golden-question regression suite keeping the oracle itself honest. Each index ships its in-sync gate at birth, comparing the stable projection (line numbers informational) so gates fire on real changes not noise. DEPENDENCY_GRAPH regenerated (the new tools add tracked tool-nodes, tool.total 156 to 158 - a no-route cut that still needs a dep-graph regen). Guards 7/7 byte-identical; ENDPOINT_CATALOG / FUNCTION_INDEX / gui_parity unchanged. Also adds the kit-side bd-kb PATH wrapper (dev ergonomics, not in the release zip). 3-part bump 354 to 355.

## v3.66.349 -- Remove the Focus-layout trap (non-guard, no route). The selectable "Focus" layout applied .app.focus with a 0 1fr grid and hid the sidebar, so the main panel squished to a sliver (same root cause as the collapse bug fixed in 348) AND there was no way out: the layout switcher lives in the now-hidden sidebar, and the floating re-expand control only appears for the collapse state, not for this layout. Focus is removed as a layout; focus-via-collapse (the f key and the brand collapse button, which have a working toggle and a visible re-expand affordance) remains the supported way to hide the sidebar. Added a recovery guard so any device with a persisted layout of "focus" (or any unknown value) falls back to the Sidebar layout on load and re-normalizes storage -- operators already stranded auto-recover on the next page load. Verified in a real headless browser: a forced layout=focus reloads into a usable Sidebar with the switcher reachable and the content full-width, the f-key collapse still toggles both ways, and Focus no longer appears in the layout dropdown. Structural regression pin added. 7 guards byte-identical.

Added a structural regression pin for the single-column collapse grid. 7 guards byte-identical; no app.py, runner.py, or route change.

## v3.66.327 -- regression fix for the v3.66.326 password-vault cut (NON-guard, NO route added, guards 7/7 byte-identical). v3.66.326 made POST /api/sites and PUT /api/sites/<sid> REFUSE-before-create on a locked/plaintext secrets backend (401 secrets_locked / 400 secrets_plaintext, no id in the body), which broke the long-standing create contract: 19 on-stash tests do c.post("/api/sites", json={...with a password...}).get_json()["id"] and hit KeyError: 'id' (+ one HTTP 401). The sandbox's locked master_password backend masked it during the 326 cut. DESIGN CORRECTION: refusing the whole create is wrong -- only the CREDENTIAL is contingent on the vault, never the site. api_add now ALWAYS creates the site and returns {id}; the password is vaulted as a @cred: reference when the backend is unlocked-encrypted, and on a locked/plaintext backend the site is still created with NO password stored (never plaintext) and the 2xx body carries secrets_locked / secrets_plaintext so the SPA can prompt. api_update is symmetric: a new password on a locked/plaintext backend no longer refuses the whole update -- the other fields apply, the password is skipped (existing @cred ref preserved, no plaintext on disk), and the response flags the reason. Cascade fixes: (1) site_editor.export_config(include_secrets=True) now RESOLVES @cred refs to plaintext via secrets_store.resolve_password so an offline backup still contains the real secret (it omits and records a stripped field when the vault cannot decrypt the ref); (2) has_password meta staleness -- the password is popped before _create_site builds the cached meta, so api_add (after vaulting) and api_update (after its vault store, which runs after the pre-existing meta rebuild) now rebuild s_meta[sid] = _build_meta(s_cfg[sid]) so /api/status reports has_password=true for a freshly-vaulted credential. FRONTEND (AddSiteWizard): the create contract flipped from 401-on-locked to 2xx+secrets_locked, so the unlock trigger moved from onError to onSuccess -- on secrets_locked the site already exists, so the wizard stays open, remembers the created id, prompts to unlock, and on unlock PUTs the password to the EXISTING site (never re-POST, which would create a duplicate); secrets_plaintext toasts a switch-backend advisory; onError now handles only genuine create failures. Tests updated to the non-refusing contract: test_v3_66_326_password_vault_routing (2 cases now expect 200 + flag + site-created + no-plaintext); phase5 export-include-secrets, security blank-update, credential_persistence blank-update + has_password, and extension_endpoints _client all install an unlocked in-memory encrypted backend to drive the real create -> @cred -> resolve round-trip; secrets_endpoints plaintext-detector now SEEDS plaintext directly since create vaults. Sandbox: credential band 125/125, secrets_endpoints 14/14, session_keeper 21/21 (two timing tests are load/segfault flakes that pass in isolation and are unrelated to passwords). Frontend tsc clean + vite rebuilt (new bundle hash). 3-part bump 326->327.
