## v3.66.230 -- Track F F2.7 follow-through: HUD overlay is now DEFAULT-ON, persistent across navigation, CSP-immune, and operator-toggleable per-capture from the GUI. **Why:** 229 shipped the HUD call site behind a default-OFF `BD_HUD_OVERLAY` env flag that was NOT reachable per-capture from the GUI (cockpit_core spawns capture_session.py with the server env only), and the single pre-loop call site mounted the HUD exactly once -- so on a real login->app flow it flashed on the landing page and was wiped by the first navigation, and on strict-CSP sites `add_script_tag` was silently refused (fail-open, no log). Three operator-facing gaps, fixed together. **(a) Default-ON + per-capture GUI toggle:** the HUD is ON by default; `tools/capture_session.py` gains a `--no-hud` CLI arg and a `_hud_enabled(args, env)` resolver (`BD_HUD_OVERLAY != "0"` AND not `--no-hud`); `BD_HUD_OVERLAY=0` is now a global kill switch (the env var no longer needs to be SET to enable -- so the GUI-spawned subprocess gets the HUD with no env plumbing at all, dissolving the 229 reachability gap). `tools/cockpit_core.py _argv_for_capture` forwards `--no-hud` only when the GUI checkbox is unticked (blank/missing keeps default-on, command unchanged). `tools/cockpit_console.py` capture form gains a `cs_hud` checkbox, CHECKED by default, forwarded as `hud:$('#cs_hud').checked`. **(b) Persistence across navigation:** the inject moves OUT of the one-shot pre-loop site and INTO `_pump_dom`, which already re-runs every tick precisely because a page nav resets the in-page buffer -- so the HUD now re-mounts after navigation exactly like the rrweb drain does (the in-page `__bd_hud_mounted` guard makes same-page re-injects a no-op; a new frame after nav re-mounts). **(c) CSP-immune inject + honest fail log:** `bulk_downloader/dom_overlay.py inject_overlay` switches from `page.add_script_tag` (a real <script>, governed by the page `script-src` CSP) to `page.evaluate` (Playwright/CloakBrowser isolated/utility world -- NOT subject to page CSP), so the render-only widget mounts on sites that would refuse an injected script. CloakBrowser is a thin Playwright wrapper that returns the underlying Playwright page (no cloak-specific Page class; `evaluate` is the genuine CDP-backed call), so this is correct on stash; cloak is itself installable in-sandbox from `bd_cloak_combined_offline_pack.zip` (cloakbrowser-0.3.31 wheel). The caller logs `[hud] overlay not shown (closed page / no body)` once on a False return instead of silent fail-open (CSP is no longer a cause after the evaluate switch; closed-page/no-body still is). **WACZ-safe for default-ON:** the widget mounts inside a CLOSED Shadow root, which JS (and therefore rrweb) cannot read or serialise, so only an empty `<div data-bd-hud>` host marker reaches the capture -- the decorative HUD is never baked into the artifact. **GUARD CHANGE `tools/capture_session.py` 83adaa36 -> 57b10b02 (operator-declared):** `--no-hud` arg + `_hud_enabled` + HUD inject folded into `_pump_dom`; old one-shot default-OFF env gate removed. The `capture_session -> dom_overlay` edge already existed (229) -> DEPENDENCY_GRAPH unchanged. 3-part bump 229->230. ## v3.66.228 -- Track F gated chain step 1: NAV evidence instrument + opt-in capture wait-condition toggle. **Why:** the long-parked "capture nav-blocker" gating F2.7-live was, for its only candidate target (reptyle), a MISDIAGNOSIS -- reptyle's capture failure was the one site with an ENABLED reviewed template whose stale login selectors drove a broken auto-applied login flow (the runtime auto-applies enabled templates; app.py:11667), NOT a page.goto/load timeout. The CF challenges + zero-media were the stale-template login page sitting there, incidental. Fix on stash = disable the stale reviewed template; durable lesson = before re-capturing a site with an enabled reviewed template, disable it first and suspect the template before the browser/network. This cut ships the instrument to tell a REAL nav blocker apart from a downstream failure, plus an inert, evidence-gated mechanism to act on a confirmed verdict. **NEW `tools/nav_probe.py` (read-only diagnostic, no guard):** drives a real browser through a strategy ladder (`load` -> `domcontentloaded` -> `commit`+bounded readyState self-poll), reproducing the interactive-capture recorder request-holding pressure via a throwaway redacted DomCapture sink, and emits a verdict keyed on the FIRST wait condition that reaches a usable DOM: `LOAD_OK` (load resolves -> nav not the blocker, no change), `N1_DCL` (load times out unusable, DCL resolves usable -> fix=goto(wait_until=domcontentloaded)), `N3_COMMIT_SELFPOLL` (load+DCL time out, commit+poll reaches usable -> fix=goto(commit)+poll), `UNREACHABLE` (nothing resolves OR first goto is a transport net::ERR_* -> auth/cert/redirect/DNS, F2.7-live stays parked). Usability predicate is byte-identical to the guard's D2(a) test (readyState in {interactive,complete} AND body_len>=0) plus an off-about:blank gate so a non-committed goto can't false-positive; CRITICAL semantic: a `load` TIMEOUT with an incidentally-usable DOM is NOT LOAD_OK -- "usable" requires the wait condition to actually RESOLVE (goto returned normally), because that resolution IS the fix being validated. Strictly read-only / F2-clean: navigates and reads readyState/body LENGTH/title/url/error-class only -- never page text, never a write, never a persisted secret. Exit 0 for LOAD_OK/N1/N3, 3 for UNREACHABLE, 2 for no-Playwright. **GUARD CHANGE `tools/capture_session.py` 24818b0b -> 8f5586a9 (operator-declared):** opt-in / default-OFF override of the interactive-capture navigation wait condition via the `BD_CAPTURE_WAIT_UNTIL` env var (idiom matches BD_CAPTURE_RAW). NEW `_resolve_capture_wait_until()` returns the operator-selected value from {load,domcontentloaded,commit} (case/whitespace-normalised) or None for unset/blank/unrecognised; `_goto_or_continue_if_usable` passes `wait_until=` ONLY when set -- env UNSET keeps the bare `page.goto(start_url)` byte-for-byte the pre-toggle path (Playwright's implicit "load"). The existing TimeoutError-tolerant branch is unchanged and still applies either way (defence in depth). Default-OFF on purpose: the DOM recorder arms immediately after navigation (_pump_dom); resolving the goto at domcontentloaded arms it EARLIER in the page lifecycle on heavy SPAs -- the class that historically SIGTRAPped the renderer when armed at document-start (v3.66.165) -- so weakening the wait condition is an operator decision per capture, justified by nav_probe evidence on the specific target first, never a blanket flip. The other 6 guards stay byte-identical (build_release baseline 494aa319 unchanged; only capture_session is declared). No CLI arg added -- the deliberate "D2(b) not implemented" CLI surface (exactly 11 options, no --wait-until) is preserved. **In-sync:** DEPENDENCY_GRAPH regenerated (745->747 edges, tools 143->144: nav_probe -> {dom_capture, cloak} package edges + -> capture_session tool edge). ENDPOINT_CATALOG / FUNCTION_INDEX (app.py+runner.py only) / gui_parity UNCHANGED -- no route, no SPA wiring, app.py/runner.py untouched. Guards: 1 declared change + 6 byte-identical. 3-part bump 227->228. Parity floor 1 (no route, no legacy tranche moved). **Verification:** tests/test_nav_probe.py (22: is_usable contract, off-about:blank gate, load-timeout-NOT-usable, dcl/commit resolve, commit self-poll becomes/never usable, net-error decisive, classify each verdict incl first-net-err short-circuit, exit codes, no-body-text-leak shape, parser surface) + tests/test_capture_session_nav_resilience.py extended (6 new: env-unset bare goto / dcl+commit opt-in kwarg / invalid value falls back / opt-in still tolerates timeout-usable / resolver allowlist+normalisation; the 6 pre-existing D2(a) + CLI-surface tests stay green). 38/38 both nav suites; capture-adjacent regression (cockpit capture options/profile, at2 dom_capture, dom_drain, multitab, finish-sentinel, finish-endpoint) 92/92. nav_probe.py hand-dropped to stash earlier (C path) for the reptyle root-cause work -- this cut folds it into the tree, reconciling that bounded drift. ## v3.66.227 -- Track F Wave-3 batch: F4.3 scoped API tokens (NEW module + 2 routes + central-auth gate) + F4.2 retention preview-verbatim binding (destructive path). Two features, one bump. **F4.3 (scoped programmatic API tokens):** the master `Authorization: Bearer <BD_AUTH_TOKEN>` is all-or-nothing and the existing shares.py tokens are deliberately read-only + method-restricted ("a peek, not the keys"), so write-capable programmatic access needed its own surface. NEW module `bulk_downloader/api_tokens.py` -- SEPARATE table `api_auth_tokens` + audit table `api_auth_log` + SEPARATE signing secret `api_auth_token_secret` (never reachable through the share/vault gates). Wire format `bdapi_<token_id>.<nonce>.<sig>` (HMAC-SHA256, the prefix makes it unmistakable vs the master bearer / share tokens). Hierarchical scope `{read:1, enqueue:2, admin:3}`; functions create_token/revoke_token/list_tokens (METADATA only -- the full value is echoed exactly once, at creation)/verify_token (constant-time HMAC + DB state, bumps use_count). Enforcement is a NEW branch in the central `app._check_token` before_request hook, FAIL-CLOSED against a module-level `_API_TOKEN_ROUTE_POLICY` keyed by Flask rule (request.url_rule.rule, so dynamic `<sid>` segments match structurally, not by regex): a valid token reaches ONLY the (route, method) pairs enumerated for its scope level -- any unlisted route, wrong method, or insufficient scope -> 403; an invalid/expired/revoked token falls through to the normal 401 so it can never downgrade a request carrying other valid auth; the OPERATOR path (master bearer / session cookie) is authorized earlier and never hits this gate. A newly added route is unreachable by API tokens until deliberately added to the policy. Policy this cut: read = {capacity, dashboard, queue/v2, history}; enqueue = {queue/v2/add_url, sites/<sid>/queue_url}; admin = {retention/preview/<sid>, retention/apply, api_tokens, api_tokens/<token_id>}. NEW mgmt routes on the MAIN app (not a blueprint, so G12 per-blueprint counts + cockpit ==161 pins are unaffected): `POST /api/api_tokens` (mint), `GET /api/api_tokens` (list metadata), `DELETE /api/api_tokens/<token_id>` (revoke). CSRF: the existing `_check_csrf` already exempts any `Authorization: Bearer ...` request, so bdapi_ token POSTs aren't CSRF-blocked; `_check_token` runs first regardless. SPA: NEW self-contained `components/ApiTokensPanel.tsx` (scope select + label + TTL, shows the secret once on create, lists metadata, revoke) mounted in the Secrets route; wires `/api/api_tokens` + `` `/api/api_tokens/${id}` `` as FULL literals (parity credits spa_wired). **F4.2 (retention preview-verbatim binding):** the destructive `POST /api/retention/apply` recomputed candidates fresh at apply time, so a real delete could diverge from what the operator previewed. `retention.apply_retention` gains optional `confirm_ids` + `site_id`: with `confirm_ids` set, deletion is restricted to the INTERSECTION of those ids with the freshly computed candidates -- apply can delete FEWER than the preview disclosed (a file excluded/tagged/gone since preview is silently skipped) but can NEVER delete a file that wasn't previewed; `site_id` scopes the run to one site; omitting `confirm_ids` preserves the legacy unbound all-sites sweep (backward-compatible). ZERO new routes (additive body fields on the existing route; 400 if confirm_ids is non-list). Response gains `preview_bound` + `scoped_site`. SPA: useRetentionApply hook threads `confirmIds`/`siteId`; Maintenance.tsx real "Apply retention" is now preview-BOUND + site-scoped (sends the previewed candidate ids) and DISABLED until a preview is loaded (an unbound real sweep from the SPA is exactly what this prevents); dry-run binds to the preview when present, else stays an all-sites sim; misleading "across ALL sites" title corrected. **In-sync:** ENDPOINT_CATALOG regenerated (+3 entries: GET/POST /api/api_tokens, DELETE /api/api_tokens/<token_id>). FUNCTION_INDEX regenerated (+3 app.py defs: api_api_tokens_create/list/revoke). DEPENDENCY_GRAPH regenerated -- NEW edge (app.py imports api_tokens; unlike recent additive cuts this adds a real module node). gui_parity regenerated (3 new entries spa_wired; operator_facing_unwired stays 0; spa_wired_total -> 279). G12 route-count gate OK (new routes on main app, not a gated blueprint; blueprint count stays 11). Guards 7/7 byte-identical (no guard touched; build_release baseline stays 494aa319). 3-part bump 226->227. Parity floor 1 (the 2 new api_tokens routes are SPA-wired via full literals so never enter legacy_only; no legacy tranche moved). **Verification:** tests/test_v3_66_227_api_tokens.py (18: scope hierarchy, bad-scope reject, create/verify round-trip, non-bdapi reject, tampered-sig reject, revoked reject, expired reject, list-hides-secret; gate-active 401, operator master-bearer unaffected on an admin route, read allowed on read route, read DENIED 403 on admin, enqueue allowed-to-enqueue/denied-to-admin, admin allowed on destructive+mgmt, valid-token-on-unlisted-route 403, revoked->401, X-BD-API-Token header path, full create/list/revoke round-trip via operator) + tests/test_v3_66_227_retention_preview_verbatim.py (6: deletes-exactly-confirmed, forged-id-deletes-nothing, excluded-since-preview-skipped, dry-run-deletes-nothing-counts-intersection, site-scoping-isolates, unbound-legacy-sweep-flag). 24/24 new. ## v3.66.225 -- Track F Phase F3-a remainder: F3.4 honeypot-threshold suggestion chip + F3.5 rebalance suggested-moves list. Surfacing-only, no new route, no guard. **F3.4 (advisory per-site honeypot drop threshold):** the honeypot_threshold engine (learn_threshold / learned_drop_threshold / trap_scores_for_site, shipped earlier) had ZERO operator-facing surface. This cut surfaces a *learned* per-site drop threshold as an advisory chip -- it NEVER changes drop behaviour (the live filter remains the opt-in BD_HONEYPOT_SCORE_THRESHOLD path; there is no write path here). NEW app.py helper _m2_honeypot_suggestion(sid) -> (suggested_float_or_None, sample_count): lazy-imports honeypot_threshold + honeypot_score.DEFAULT_DROP_THRESHOLD (zero cold-path cost), reads the site's confirmed-trap honeypot_score history via trap_scores_for_site, and returns the learned low-quantile threshold ONLY when >= DEFAULT_MIN_SAMPLES (5) trap scores exist -- below that it returns (None, n) so the chip stays hidden on thin data; fail-soft to (None, 0) so a missing history column can never break the Sites tab. /api/sites/v2 gains two ADDITIVE per-entry fields (honeypot_threshold_suggested, honeypot_threshold_samples) -- additive on the EXISTING route, so no ENDPOINT_CATALOG / gui_parity / G12 churn. SPA: SiteEntryV2 gains the two optional fields (api-types.ts) and SiteDetail.tsx renders an advisory chip in the per-site card stack (between Profiles and Candidate inspector) ONLY when honeypot_threshold_suggested != null -- "Suggested honeypot drop threshold · 0.NN · from N trap(s) · advisory". **F3.5 (rebalance suggested-moves list):** the plan_rebalance engine + /api/rebalance/plan + /api/storage_rebalance/plan + RebalanceCenter.tsx (plan->execute, P1/P2) were already fully live; the plan response already carried moves[]. ## v3.66.224 -- Track F Phase F3 (closes F3-b): F3.2 drift -> AI repair candidate -- suggestion-only, AI-gated, server-side, NO new route, NO guard. When selector_drift flags a site stale (selectors stopped matching), a daily background sweep asks the AI assist diff-repair path for replacement selectors against the failing page's DOM and lands each proposal as a REVIEW-ONLY draft -- the same template-review lane the inventory surfaces. Promotion stays 100% human; an enabled template is never read-modified-written. NEW bulk_downloader/drift_repair.py (pure-ish + fail-soft): propose_repairs(host, *, broken_selectors, working_selectors, dom_excerpt, page_url, drafts_dir, ai_fn=None, status_fn=None) -> (1) AI availability gate via aiassist.ai_status() -- disabled/unreachable => INERT no-op (no draft, no error; the download pipeline is never blocked because this lives in a bg sweep off the hot extractor path); (2) calls aiassist.diff_repair(broken, working, dom_excerpt, page_url) -- any non-ok result is an inert skip (ai_error), never raises; (3) lands each proposed replacement via dom_analyzer.pin_candidate (the F2.6 writer) which FORCES status="draft_review_required" + review_required=True and runs the unconditional redact_artifact chokepoint, so enabled is always False -- with a belt-and-braces guard that drops any candidate that somehow came back enabled. Provenance is recorded on the draft as source_capture="drift_repair:<host>" (rule-side; dom_analyzer/pin_candidate untouched, so no F2.6 churn). scheduled_drift_repair(*, dom_provider=None, drafts_dir=None, reviewed_dir=None, ...) is the bg entry point: NO-OPS unless automation.drift_repair_enabled is on (default OFF -> registering the task is behaviour-neutral, one global_config read/day, mirrors lifecycle.drift_sweep + template_canary.daily); it sweeps selector_drift.status_all() flagged-stale sites, pulls page context from an injected dom_provider(site_id)->ctx|None, gathers working_selectors from the reviewed template when not supplied (_load_reviewed_selectors, best-effort), and calls propose_repairs. The default _default_dom_provider returns None (no captured DOM available -> sweep skips): pulling a stale site's most-recent captured DOM is the STASH-side capture-store integration, exactly as F2.7's live half is stash-only; the proposal / gating / draft-write logic is fully sandbox-tested via injected ai_fn / status_fn / dom_provider. WIRED: bg_scheduler.register_default_tasks registers drift_repair.daily (86400s), toggle-gated default-OFF. SOURCE CHECK: confirmed lifecycle_drift only CONSUMES a fresh_template (auto-flag/quarantine/refresh/repair) and contains no AI-repair-candidate generation -- F3.2 is the missing producer, no overlap. No route (ENDPOINT_CATALOG / gui_parity / G12 unchanged). FUNCTION_INDEX unchanged (bg_scheduler edit only; no app.py/runner.py function add). DEPENDENCY_GRAPH regenerated (+bg_scheduler->drift_repair; drift_repair's aiassist/dom_analyzer/selector_drift/template_manager/global_config imports are lazy in-function `from . import` so the tracker records them as out-edges). ## v3.66.223 -- Track F Phase F3: F3.1 watch rules -- saved-search action lane (notify | enqueue), backend only, NO new route, suggestion-grade automation inside the existing gates. A saved search can now carry action="enqueue": when its scheduled (or manual) run finds NEW history matches, those URLs are fed into the NORMAL download pipeline -- same site auto-detect, same admission gates, same review path, and the v3.66.221 F1.5 dedup preflight applies downstream -- instead of (or rather than) firing an apprise notification. saved_searches.py: (1) additive columns via _ensure_table ALTER (mirrors the migrations.py honeypot_score additive pattern; CREATE-IF-NOT-EXISTS can't add columns to an existing table): action TEXT DEFAULT 'notify', daily_cap INTEGER DEFAULT 25, enqueued_count INTEGER DEFAULT 0, enqueued_day TEXT DEFAULT '', enqueued_total INTEGER DEFAULT 0 -- defaults keep every existing rule on the byte-identical notify path. (2) add()/update() accept action (allowlist {notify,enqueue}; add coerces an unknown action to notify, update DROPS a bad action rather than silently flipping the lane) + daily_cap (clamped >= 0). (3) A module-level enqueue handler registry (set_enqueue_handler / _reset_enqueue_handler) so this module never imports app.py (app already imports it -- a registered callback avoids the circular import). When the handler is unregistered the enqueue action is a SILENT no-op (mirrors the F3 "automation unavailable -> skip" rule; never errors, never downloads without the gates). (4) NEW _do_enqueue(search, new_rows, enqueue_fn=None): within-batch URL de-dup (order preserved), per-rule daily cap on a UTC-day bucket (counter resets on a new day; cap=0 enqueues nothing), calls the handler with the capped batch, and records provenance RULE-SIDE (enqueued_count / enqueued_day / enqueued_total on the saved_searches row) -- jobs are not stamped, so the runner stays untouched. Fail-soft to (0, False) on any error. (5) run_one(search_id, *, enqueue_fn=None) branches on action: enqueue -> _do_enqueue; notify (default) -> the unchanged apprise block; the two are mutually exclusive (an enqueue rule does not also notify). Result dict gains action/enqueued/enqueue_capped. run_due() passes through the registered handler unchanged. app.py: registers _saved_search_enqueue_handler (wraps the existing _route_urls_internal -> runners[sid].load_urls, returns accepted count) via saved_searches.set_enqueue_handler at import, right after _route_urls_internal is defined; the existing POST /api/saved_searches gains additive action + daily_cap body fields (NO new route -- the list endpoint already returns dict(row) so the new columns auto-surface; in-place editing + distinct SPA marking are a deferred SPA tail). SOURCE-VS-DOC: the roadmap assumed F3.1 "adds /api routes", but source showed the enqueue capability ships purely additively on the existing add endpoint + run_one hook -- so this is a NO-route cut (ENDPOINT_CATALOG / gui_parity / G12 unchanged), matching the clean shape of 222. FUNCTION_INDEX regenerated (app.py gained _saved_search_enqueue_handler + line shift). DEPENDENCY_GRAPH unchanged (saved_searches already imported db + notify_apprise; the handler lives in app.py which already imported saved_searches -- no new module edge). Guards 7/7 byte-identical (no guard touched; build_release baseline stays 494aa319). 3-part bump 222->223. Parity floor 1. Tests: tests/test_v3_66_223_watch_enqueue.py (14: schema defaults / bad-action-coerce / cap-clamp / update-validation, _do_enqueue no-handler-silent / handler-called / cap-limits / within-batch-dedup / provenance-counters / same-day-accumulate / cap-exhausted-no-call, run_one notify-does-not-enqueue / enqueue-feeds-matches, run_due registered-handler).

## v3.66.222 -- Track F Phase F3: F3.3 template canary schedule (suggestion-only, read/alert, server-side; no route, no SPA, no guard touched). A toggle-gated daily background task that replays the synthetic-test HAR fixtures over the enabled templates and alerts when a site's pass-rate drops materially versus its last known-good run -- so a real selector breakage is detected by the canary BEFORE it manifests as a wave of job failures. NEW bulk_downloader/template_canary.py (pure + fail-soft throughout): compare_to_baseline(run, baseline, drop_pct=25, min_fixtures=2) returns per-site alert dicts for sites whose pass-rate fell >= drop_pct percentage points below baseline (first-sight establishes a baseline and never alerts; a single flapping fixture is below the min_fixtures floor and is ignored; alerts sort worst-drop-first); _next_baseline holds an alerting site's prior (higher) baseline so a sustained outage keeps alerting and only a clean run resets it; run_canary orchestrates replay->compare->persist->dispatch with a _run_all injection seam for tests; scheduled_canary is the bg entry point that NO-OPS unless automation.template_canary_enabled is on (default OFF) and honours a min-spacing guard; canary_status() returns a secret-free snapshot (enabled flag, last_run, aggregate+per-site pass-rates, alert list -- numbers only, no fixture bodies/URLs/PII). Alert dispatch reuses the EXISTING notify_apprise dispatcher (custom event tag "template_canary" -> per_event fire; fail-open if the notifier is disabled/absent). app_data_layer.collect_template_analytics() gains an additive `canary` field (fail-soft) surfaced through the existing GET /api/data/template_health -- NO new route. SOURCE-VS-DOC correction: the roadmap framed F3.3 canaries as hitting the live site ("authenticated-session lane; per-site rate floor so canaries never compete with real jobs"), but the actual synthetic_tests module is pure local HAR-fixture replay with NO HTTP (its own docstring is explicit), so a canary cannot compete with real download jobs -- the rate-floor-vs-jobs concern is moot for this implementation; the min-spacing guard is retained only to avoid redundant local work. No app.py/runner.py function added/renamed (FUNCTION_INDEX unchanged); no route (ENDPOINT_CATALOG / gui_parity / G12 unchanged); DEPENDENCY_GRAPH gains edges bg_scheduler->template_canary and template_canary->{synthetic_tests, notify_apprise, global_config} (regenerated; the app_data_layer->template_canary import is the file's existing `from bulk_downloader import` style, which the graph tool does not track as an edge -- same as its untracked cloak/dom_recorder/cookie_health imports). Guards 7/7 byte-identical (no guard touched; build_release baseline stays 494aa319). 3-part bump 221->222. Parity floor 1. ## v3.66.221 -- Track F Wave 3: F1-C re-scoped to F1.5 only (pre-download history-match dedup). **SOURCE VALIDATION corrected the F1-C scope:** the doc framed F1-C as a big "db migration + runner + SPA" cut across F1.5+F1.6+F1.7, but source showed F1.6 and F1.7 ALREADY shipped, so this cut is F1.5 alone (no migration). (1) **F1.7 priority lanes already live:** the queue table has `priority TEXT` (high/normal/low) + `ord` + set_priority/bulk_priority/queue_set_priority/queue_reorder + a queue_priority scoring path, and SiteRunner's next-job sort key already pops `priority=="high"` first then FIFO position (runner ~L2382). Remaining F1.7 delta is a SPA pin-to-front button on the existing /api/sites/<sid>/priority endpoint (deferred; SPA-only, no backend work). (2) **F1.6 ETA/rate already live end-to-end:** runner computes per-job `eta_s = (bytes_total-bytes_done)/speed` (~L7165) + a site-level ETA (~L4089); /api/queue/v2 already plumbs `eta_seconds`+`rate_human`; RunningJobRow.tsx already renders `ETA {formatEta(job.eta_seconds)}`. Remaining F1.6 delta is a site-drain header line (deferred; cosmetic). (3) **F1.5 pre-download history-match dedup -- the genuinely-new, shipped piece:** NEW db.db_find_url_in_history(url, exclude_site=None) -- exact-URL match against a 'done' history row on the indexed `url` column, fail-soft to None (a lookup error never blocks a download). NEW SiteRunner._dedup_preflight(url, job) called at the top of _process_one (after the retry_after check, before any work): exact-URL match is default-ON (config dedup_exact_url) and the fuzzy filename+size match is opt-in (config dedup_fuzzy default off, reusing db_find_filename_duplicate); on a hit the job is set to status `skipped_duplicate` with a message linking the prior history row id, and the download is skipped. An explicit force_download (Approve) bypasses dedup entirely so a deliberate re-download is never skipped; HEAD content-length probe is a future opt-in (intentionally not wired). Distinct from the pre-existing post-download cross_site_dedup (which only logs). No new route (ENDPOINT_CATALOG / gui_parity / G12 unchanged); FUNCTION_INDEX regenerated (runner.py line shift from the new method + hook); DEPENDENCY_GRAPH unchanged (db_find_url_in_history imports nothing internal; runner->db edge pre-existed). ## v3.66.218 -- Track F Wave 2 F1-B: F1.4 predictive relogin. NEW bulk_downloader/relogin_predict.py (NOT a guard): pure, fail-safe decision predictive_relogin_due(age_sec, observations, fraction=0.8, min_observations=3) -> True|False|None. Returns None (no opinion) when there are fewer than 3 observed session lifetimes or on any malformed input, so a data-thin site is unchanged; never raises. Refreshes at a FRACTION (default 0.8) of the learned median(lifetime), clamped to [0.1, 1.0]. Composes with -- does not duplicate -- session_keeper.predict_next_expiry (same median idea; keeper untouched this cut) and admission.next_eligible_retry (window snapping stays the caller's job; a proactive relogin is not a retry backoff). WIRED into runner.py::maybe_preemptive_relogin behind opt-in predictive_relogin_enabled (default OFF -> path byte-identical to the pre-F1.4 fixed cookie_max_age_hours heuristic). When ON and >=3 observations exist, the prediction is authoritative (overrides the fixed threshold both ways); with too little data it returns None and the runner falls back to the fixed threshold; any predictor/db error is caught and falls through fail-open to the fixed path (logged as a preemptive_relogin diagnostic event). New optional config keys: predictive_relogin_enabled (bool, default False), predictive_relogin_fraction (float, default 0.8). No routes/endpoints added (ENDPOINT_CATALOG/gui_parity unchanged); FUNCTION_INDEX regenerated (runner.py line shift); DEPENDENCY_GRAPH regenerated (one new edge runner->relogin_predict, 729->730; relogin_predict.py imports nothing internal, so it has no outgoing edge -- the session_lifetime_observations read happens in runner, whose runner->db edge already existed). Guards 7/7 byte-identical (no guard touched; relogin_predict.py is a new non-guard module). Tests: tests/test_v3_66_218_predictive_relogin.py (21: 0.8*median math, MIN_OBSERVATIONS gate, fraction clamping, fail-safe inputs, + full runner-hook integration incl. opt-out / predictive-override / not-yet-due-blocks-fixed / thin-data-fallback / fail-open / no-cookie-age).

## v3.66.217 -- Track F Phase F1-A: admission trio on a shared seam. NEW bulk_downloader/admission.py consolidates the signals that should HOLD a site from admitting new work, plus a retry-scheduling helper. F1.3 cookie-expiry admission (NEW runtime behaviour): opt-in via cookie_admission_enabled; when a site's auth jar is fully lapsed (every dated cookie past expiry, >=1 dated cookie; session cookies never trigger a hold), runner.start() lands the site in a self-resolving "cookies_expired" state and spawns no workers -- killing the auth-burst mass-fail where a wave of pickups all redirect-to-login. F1.1 bad-hours retry (NEW): next_eligible_retry() snaps a computed backoff timestamp forward to the next active download-window OPEN when it would otherwise fire while the window is CLOSED; wired at both backoff sites (the main retry-policy schedule + the 60s re-login backoff); inert unless window_enabled with a valid spec. F1.2 disk-aware admission: admission_hold() is now the single reusable source of the low-disk signal (default 2.0GB threshold) shared by the cookie gate and tests -- the inline runner.start() low_disk block (which owns the fire_event hook) remains the runtime actor, so this cut adds NO new disk behaviour, only consolidation. WHOLE module is fail-open by contract: admission_hold returns None (admit) and next_eligible_retry returns its input unchanged on ANY internal error -- admission is a convenience gate, never a safety gate. No routes/endpoints/functions added (ENDPOINT_CATALOG/FUNCTION_INDEX/gui_parity unchanged); DEPENDENCY_GRAPH regenerated (new module edge runner->admission). Guards 7/7 byte-identical (no guard touched). Tests: tests/test_v3_66_217_admission_f1a.py (24: disk/cookie/retry pins on synthetic stubs + 2 start() integration paths). RIDE-ALONG (read-only measurement, not part of the F1-A runtime): NEW tools/baselines_snapshot.py — pre-F1 baselines (hourly_stats/site, 7-day auth-fail/site, 7-day dup-URL fetch; idle-tab request rate is an explicit not-instrumented stub, no DB persistence). stdlib-only, opens the live DB READ-ONLY via the package's own path resolution; run BEFORE deploy/restart to capture the before-state. ## v3.66.216 -- Track F Phase F2.6: DOM Analyzer Workbench (post-hoc capture inspection; replay half of the dev-tools loop, F2.7 is the live half). NEW bulk_downloader/dom_analyzer.py (server core) + bulk_downloader/dom_serialize.py (package-owned rrweb-node->HTML serializer; no tools/ inversion; build_template_from_wacz left byte-identical). LOAD-BEARING F2 GATE (fail-closed): a capture's DOM is layered-redacted before any of it is shown -- redact_dom_node (class-PII subtrees + input values) -> _propagate_mask (sink-side: honors a mask class over DESCENDANT text nodes, closing the gap where rrweb-serialized child text under bd-mask survives redact_dom_node) -> redact_artifact (value-content secrets in attrs/hrefs/text) -> scan_artifact_secrets; ANY residual withholds the tree+html and returns counts-by-kind only (never a value/path). release guards byte-identical to the 181 baseline), no engine reimplemented.

  release gate asserting no operator-facing endpoint echoes a stored secret VALUE
  and no shipped template/SPA interpolates a secret-named field unmasked. Boots
  the in-process Flask test client, seeds a site whose persisted credential carries
  a unique sentinel, scans every arg-free / single-`<sid>` operator-facing GET
  endpoint (≈529 in-sandbox; asserts a >50 floor for host-portability), and fails
  if the sentinel surfaces. A planted-leak probe proves the substring detector is
  value-agnostic. The secret-name rule is single-sourced from

## v3.66.165 — 2026-06-08 (DOM-recorder fix: arm-after-load + buffer-drain; closes the Capture Navigation Blocker)

Promotes `__version__` to `3.66.165`. Rewrites the rrweb DOM-capture transport in
`bulk_downloader/dom_recorder.py` and adds a drain pump to `tools/capture_session.py`. The network (CDP)
recorder, `cloak.py`, `extraction_core.py`, `capture_workbench.py`, the `decision_confidence`/`CP_*`
locations, the Settings Center routes, install-path, requirements, and `capture_session.py`'s `wait_until`
default (`"load"`) are unchanged. The vendored `rrweb`/`snapdom` JS is byte-unchanged. Changed runtime:
`bulk_downloader/dom_recorder.py`, `tools/capture_session.py`. New tests: `tests/test_v3_66_165_dom_drain.py`,
`tests/test_capture_session_nav_resilience.py` (D2(a)). Updated tests: `tests/test_dom_recorder_asi.py`
(behavioral tier → arm/drain), `tests/test_v3_66_139_dom_recorder.py` (transport assertion). Plus
`bulk_downloader/__init__.py`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `tests/test_settings_center_slice4.py` (version pin).

Closes the Capture Navigation Blocker (real captures crashed the renderer and/or returned
`dom_log_count=0`).

- **Root cause (two independent defects, one redesign).** (1) `rrweb.record()` armed at document-start (via
  `add_init_script`) over a not-yet-built heavy-SPA DOM crashed the renderer (Chromium "Aw, Snap"/SIGTRAP);
  the `goto`/`load` timeout previously attributed to a navigation-layer fault was a consequence of the dead
  renderer. (2) Even when recording started, rrweb's `emit` closure could not call the Playwright-exposed
  binding (`TypeError: this._global[this._globalBindingName] is not a function`), so every event was dropped
  and `dom_log` stayed empty.
- **Fix.** Arm rrweb **after load** via `page.add_script_tag` (never document-start), have it emit into an
  in-page buffer `window.__bd_dom_buf` (bounded; drop-and-count safety cap), and have Python **drain** that
  buffer over `page.evaluate` on a one-second interval (both the TTY and noVNC waits) and once at finish. All
  Playwright calls stay on the main capture thread; no exposed binding. The drain re-arms after navigation
  (which resets the in-page buffer), so events are not lost across redirects/new tabs. The v3.66.164 ASI
  separator (`rrweb_js() + "\n;\n" + _BOOTSTRAP`) is preserved; the D2(a) capture-navigation helper remains as
  the load-timeout safety net.
- **Validation.** Affected test band 74 passed / 1 skipped; broad regression band 151 passed; in-sandbox
  behavioral arm/drain produced a type-2 full snapshot. Validated on a real capture: `dom_log_count=1625`
  (was 0), `network_log_count=635`, two type-2 full snapshots across a login redirect (re-arm-after-navigation
  proven), no SIGTRAP, no ASI page error.
- **Known limitations.** Arming after load does not record DOM mutations in the first load window;
  `add_script_tag` is subject to a page's CSP (`arm_dom_recorder` fails closed and retries). A separate,
  unaddressed item: rrweb masks `type=password` inputs but not `email`/hidden inputs in the DOM capture.

new `tests/test_dom_recorder_asi.py`.

- **Root cause (backend-independent ASI concatenation bug).** `dom_recorder.recorder_script()` joined the
  vendored rrweb UMD bundle and the record bootstrap with a bare newline (`rrweb_js() + "\n" + _BOOTSTRAP`).
  The bundle's final statement is `...}))` with no terminating semicolon and `_BOOTSTRAP` begins with an IIFE
  `(function(){...})()`, so JavaScript ASI parsed the boundary as `}))(function(){...})()` — calling the
  bundle's trailing value as a function and throwing `"(intermediate value)(...) is not a function"`. The
  bootstrap never ran, `rrweb.record()` never started, and `dom_log` stayed empty on every backend.
- **Fix.** A single explicit statement separator: `recorder_script()` now returns
  `rrweb_js() + "\n;\n" + _BOOTSTRAP`, terminating the bundle's final statement before the bootstrap IIFE.
- **Tests.** New `tests/test_dom_recorder_asi.py`: 5 static guards (separator present; not the bare-newline
  join; bundle tail lacks `;`; no CDN/runtime network; vendored assets from disk) + a behavioral tier
  (skips cleanly without a healthy browser). Verified: static 5/5; adjacent DOM/capture band 201 pass /
  0 fail / 3 expected skips; byte-compile + import-walk clean; Node A/B mechanism proof against the real
  vendored bundle (OLD join throws the ASI error, NEW join starts recording). Full browser
  `dom_log_count` proof is tracked separately under the Capture Navigation Blocker finding (a stash
  browser navigation/`load` condition, independent of this fix).

## v3.66.163 — 2026-06-07 (install-path patch: CloakBrowser + rrweb/snapdom provisioned by the normal stash install path)

Promotes `__version__` to `3.66.163`. An **install-path / dependency** patch only — **no runtime
behavior change**. `bulk_downloader/cloak.py`, `dom_recorder.py`, `tools/capture_session.py`,
`extraction_core.py`, `capture_workbench.py`, `tools/cockpit_core.py`, `tools/cockpit_console.py`,
the `decision_confidence`/`CP_*` locations, the 11 Settings Center routes, the PUT numeric-range
backstop, VPN/global-AI/write surfaces, template promotion, and download/acquisition behavior are
all unchanged. The vendored `rrweb`/`snapdom` runtime JS is byte-unchanged. Changed files:
`install_linux.sh`, `bulk_downloader/__init__.py`, `CHANGELOG.md`,
`tests/test_settings_center_slice4.py` (version pin); new `requirements-cloak.txt` and
`tests/test_cloak_install_path.py`.

Closes Finding C (v3.66.162 live census): a from-scratch / rebuilt stash venv had no `cloakbrowser`,
so every browser flow silently fell back to Playwright.

- **CloakBrowser is now installed and verified by the normal stash install path.** `install_linux.sh`
  gains a non-fatal, offline-first install ladder run after the Playwright Chromium step: (a) a
  repo-local `wheels/` wheelhouse, then (b) a `bd_cloak` offline pack's `pip-wheels/` (via
  `BD_CLOAK_PACK` or conventional locations) — both `pip install --no-index --find-links … "cloakbrowser[geoip]"`
  — then (c) an online `pip install -U "cloakbrowser[geoip]"` fallback. It pre-downloads the stealth
  Chromium (`python -m cloakbrowser install`), reports status (`python -m cloakbrowser info`), runs an
  `import cloakbrowser` availability check, and prints an explicit verdict (`CloakBrowser available: …`
  or `CloakBrowser unavailable; browser flows will fall back to Playwright.`). The Playwright install
  step is unchanged; cloak.py still owns all backend selection — **no launch args / fingerprint /
  proxy flags added**. `cloakbrowser[geoip]>=0.3.31` is declared in a new posture-isolated
  `requirements-cloak.txt`.
- **rrweb/snapdom vendored assets are auto-restored if missing.** The installer now restores
  `bulk_downloader/vendor/rrweb/rrweb.min.js` (rrweb 2.0.1 `umd/rrweb.min.js`) and
  `bulk_downloader/vendor/snapdom/snapdom.js` (@zumer/snapdom 2.12.8 `dist/snapdom.js`) per
  `vendor/VENDOR.md`. Present + non-empty files are left untouched (idempotent); only a missing file
  is restored, offline-first (local/offline sources) with an **install-time-only** npm fallback that
  builds in a throwaway temp dir, copies only the runtime JS, and removes the temp dir — **no
  node_modules in the deploy tree, no runtime npm dependency, no CDN runtime loading**. On failure it
  warns clearly that DOM capture will be unavailable rather than silently continuing. `dom_recorder.py`
  is unchanged and still loads the local vendored files from disk.
- **No runtime browser launch behavior changed.** This release only provisions/verifies
  dependencies; it adds no evasion/fingerprint logic and changes no capture runtime path.

## v3.66.162 — 2026-06-07 (capture/cockpit patch: Cloak display-error narrowing + cockpit capture options parity)

Promotes `__version__` to `3.66.162`. A small, contained capture/cockpit patch. No change to
`extraction_core`, the `decision_confidence`/`CP_*` locations, the 11 Settings Center routes
(only `validate` non-GET), the PUT numeric-range backstop, secret handling, template promotion,
download/acquisition behavior, or the read-only/filtered VPN summary. Three source files changed:
`bulk_downloader/cloak.py`, `tools/cockpit_core.py`, `tools/cockpit_console.py`.

- **Cloak display-error marker narrowing.** The persistent-context fallback launch now classifies
  failures using a narrowed set of six display-specific markers, so a missing/blocked X display
  raises a clear, front-loaded message (start Xvfb/noVNC or run headless) chaining the original
  cause. Generic `browser closed unexpectedly`-style crashes are **no longer misclassified** as
  display/display-missing failures. Headless launches are never reclassified; success and fallback
  paths and the launch args are otherwise unchanged.
- **Cockpit `profile_dir`/`autofill` form-presence coverage.** Adds a source-level test pinning the
  already-shipped persistent-profile and native-autofill capture fields (no runtime change).
- **Cockpit capture numeric options parity.** Exposes three existing, backend-supported
  `capture_session` options in the cockpit Capture form, each validated and passed through only when
  supplied (blank reproduces the prior command exactly):
  - `body_cap_mib` → `--body-cap-mib` (int 1–64; default 1)
  - `chunk_events` → `--chunk-events` (int 1000–1,000,000; default 10000)
  - `max_seconds` → `--max-seconds` (int 1–1700; default 1500, kept below the cockpit runner's
    1800s kill so the capture auto-saves gracefully)
- **Withheld (not exposed), by design:** `--system-chrome` (TLS-fingerprint/anti-detection-adjacent),
  `--finish-file` (cockpit-managed sentinel), `--url-memory-file` (internal/path surface), and
  `browser_backend`/`use_cloakbrowser` and DOM/rrweb/snapdom/noVNC toggles (not `capture_session`
  flags — exposing them would invent backend behavior). No bot-detection/evasion logic added.

## v3.66.158.3 — 2026-06-06 (live-capture fixes: multi-tab recorder + fMP4/DASH segment recognition)

Point release on top of 3.66.158.2. `__version__` deliberately **stays `3.66.158`**
(strict `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` contract; 158.3 is the deploy label for this additive
slice). **No runtime / acquisition / auth / promotion change.** Both fixes came out of
the first live authenticated Reptyle capture and are additive: one to the capture tool,
one to the read-only diagnostic.

- **Multi-tab capture recorder attachment** (`tools/capture_session.py`) — both
  recorders (network CDP + rrweb DOM) now attach to **every page the context opens**,
  not just the first, via a new `_attach_recorders()` helper that wires the initial
  page and a `context.on("page", ...)` listener (per-page, de-duplicated, best-effort).
  Fixes captures that recorded an abandoned login page (0 dom / 0 segments) when an SPA
  oauth redirect or popped playback tab moved the real session off the initial page.
  Single-tab captures are unchanged. New `tests/test_capture_multitab.py` (7/7);
  `test_storage_capture` unaffected (9/9).
- **fMP4 / DASH segment recognition in the readiness gate** (`tools/workflow_diagnostic.py`)
  — the gate counted only HLS `.ts` as segments, so Cloudflare Stream fMP4/DASH
  (`seg_N.mp4`, `init.mp4`, `.m4s`) scored 0 and a fully-streamed capture read as
  `incomplete`. Added `_fmp4_dash_segments()` + a precise regex, folded (deduped) into
  both the phases and template-diff segment counts. **Diagnostic-only — the production
  `netlog_classify` kind logic is deliberately untouched** (changing it could shift
  acquisition-candidate behavior). Regex is specific enough that analytics/direct-download
  URLs don't match. `tests/test_workflow_diagnostic.py` extended to 15/15 (+3).

Known, out of scope: the player runs in a Cloudflare Stream **iframe**, so DOM capture
is still 0 for Reptyle (`context.on("page")` doesn't reach frames). This does **not**
block the api-driven Reptyle template — its download is the API/cachefly call, not a DOM
click. Iframe-level DOM binding remains a separate future change if a selector-driven
site ever needs it.

into the cockpit end to end and closes out the standing backlog (items 1–5).

`cc.finish_capture(task_id, discard=)` + `POST /cockpit/api/captures/finish`
write that sentinel, and the Captures task row now shows **finish** / **discard**

## v3.66.157 — 2026-06-05 (Surface the observed API host as a review hint)

A promotable template needs an `api{base}` block for the runtime's
`build_api_url`, but v151 deliberately keeps the API host out of the normalized
candidate unless the builder states it outright (the page is app.reptyle.com,
the API is api2.reptyle.com, and signed URLs are scrubbed). That left the
reviewer to find the host by hand. This makes it easy without weakening the
rule: the builder records the host that actually served the download-resolution
call as `network_discovery.observed_api_hosts` (a diagnostic, like `top_hosts`),
and the normalizer names it in the existing "set api{base}" warning — e.g.
"…download-resolution calls were observed on: api2.reptyle.com; set api{base}
accordingly."

Strictly a hint. It is stored under `observed_api_hosts`, **not** the `api_host`
key that `_api_host` consumes, so: the API patterns stay relative, no `api`
block is auto-created, and a human still makes the call. The change is additive
— tests assert the host appears in the warning *and* that behaviour is
unchanged (`_api_host` still returns "", patterns stay relative, no `api`
block). Builder/normalizer/pipeline suites 151/152/154/155 green.
(`tests/test_v3_66_157_observed_api_host_hint.py`, 7 tests.)

## v3.66.156 — 2026-06-05 (selector_lint: don't flag player controls as chrome)

The nav-words rule in `selector_lint` matches `settings`, `menu-bar`, `account`,
`search`, etc. to catch selectors aimed at account/nav chrome instead of a real
download control. But a video player's own quality opener —
`[aria-label="Open the video quality settings menu"]` — tripped it on
"settings", so every reviewed template with a quality menu got a spurious
"targets nav/account/search chrome" warning (surfaced by the v155 round-trip).

Fix: a playback-context guard. A nav word is ignored when the selector clearly
targets a player control (`quality`, `resolution`, `playback`, `bitrate`,
`subtitle`, `caption`, `theoplayer`, `vjs`, `video player`). The generic-root
checks are untouched, and genuine chrome still flags — `[aria-label="Account
settings"]`, `.navbar a`, `[aria-label="Search"]`, `[aria-label="Open
preferences"]` all still warn; scoped selectors stay safe. Verified the
normalizer candidate for a reptyle-shaped capture no longer carries the
false-positive warning. (`tests/test_v3_66_156_lint_player_control.py`, 11
tests; lint-dependent suites 151/152/155 green.)

## v3.66.155 — 2026-06-05 (Pipeline round-trip regression guard)

Test-only. No behaviour change — locks in that the four template-pipeline
stages stay shape-compatible end to end: a DOM-bearing capture builds a rich
draft, the normalizer turns it into a runtime-shaped review candidate,
`promote_template.py --enable` writes an enabled reviewed template, and the
**runtime** (`template_registry.find_template_for_url` +
`template_assist.template_to_learned_download` / `preferred_resolutions` /
`build_api_url`) loads and consumes it. If the normalizer's output shape or
promote's writer ever drifts from what the runtime expects, this fails in CI
instead of in a live capture session.

Verified on a fabricated reptyle-shaped capture (synthetic, no browser/network;
promote runs as a subprocess into a temp dir, never the repo's
`templates/reviewed/`, so the gold template is never touched):
- build → selectors {login, player, quality, download} + ladder [2160..240],
  confidence `high`;
- normalize → `review_ready`, `download.button_hint`→`trigger`, quality mapped,
  resolutions and host intact;
- promote `--enable` → `status: enabled`, loadable by the registry;
- runtime → working `trigger_selectors` (incl. the download trigger) and
  `preferred_resolutions` == the full ladder.

It also encodes the one intended manual-review step: the first-party API host is
scrubbed from the page capture (v151 no-host-guessing rule), so `build_api_url`
returns None on a freshly promoted template and begins working only once a
reviewer adds the `api{base}` block — the test asserts both halves.
(`tests/test_v3_66_155_pipeline_roundtrip.py`, 5 tests.)

## v3.66.154 — 2026-06-05 (Rich builder recovers the full resolution ladder)

On capA the rich builder reported `resolutions_seen:[2160]` even though the
stream offered 240–2160. Two gaps in `tools/build_template_from_wacz.py`:

- `RES_RE` keys on a trailing `p` (`2160p`), but the media segments are bare
  numbers (`AVC_2160.mp4`, `VP9_1080.mp4`). Those matches fed `media_patterns`
  but their resolution digits were thrown away. Now each `AVC_<h>.mp4` /
  `VP9_<h>.mp4` adds its height to `resolutions_seen`.
- Manifest **bodies were never parsed.** Network entries carry `response_body`,
  and an HLS master (`#EXT-X-STREAM-INF:…,RESOLUTION=WxH`) or DASH MPD
  (`height="H"`) enumerates the entire rendition ladder even when the player
  only streamed one rung. New `_manifest_resolutions()` parses both, tolerant of
  bytes/str bodies, truncation, and manifests served without the extension
  (sniffs `#EXTM3U` / `<MPD`); heights filtered to 100..8640.

Resolutions now merge from four sources — the `download-resolution` API call,
segment URLs, and the HLS/MPD manifest bodies — so `resolution_priority` comes
out as the full ladder a reviewer expects. This was the under-count flagged
after the v152 chain run; the normalizer already passes whatever the draft
carries, so no normalizer change was needed.

Faithfulness preserved: a capture with no manifest body and no segments (the
capA shape) still reports exactly the rung(s) actually seen — the ladder is
recovered only when the manifest is in the capture, never invented. So
re-running an *old* network-only capture only gains the full ladder if its
manifest body was captured; a fresh DOM capture (which fetches the master
manifest) is the reliable path. Synthetic-only tests
(`tests/test_v3_66_154_builder_resolution_ladder.py`, 11 incl. an end-to-end
build from a fabricated `.wacz`).

## v3.66.153 — 2026-06-05 (Capture through noVNC: sentinel finish, no terminal)

To build a DOM-bearing reptyle template we need an interactive capture, and
that has to run on stash through the cockpit's headless noVNC pane (the authed
profile, VPN, and cloak config all live there — a plain SSH shell has no display
and the headed browser dies with TargetClosedError). The cockpit already opens
the browser in a virtual display; the only break was the **save trigger**.

`capture_session.py` stopped on a terminal `input()` (press ENTER to save). As
a cockpit subprocess it has no controlling terminal, so `input()` got EOF and
saved instantly — the browser flashed open and closed before the operator could
log in. Fix: branch on whether stdin is a TTY.

- **TTY (operator terminal): unchanged.** Still prints the prompt and waits for
  ENTER. Terminal capture keeps working exactly as before.
- **No TTY (cockpit / noVNC): keep the browser open and wait for a sentinel.**
  The process stays alive — so the browser stays up in noVNC and the operator
  can actually log in, press play, and open the download menu. When done, from a
  second SSH shell: `touch <out_dir>/FINISH` to save, or `touch <out_dir>/CANCEL`
  to discard (no WACZ written). The exact `touch` commands are printed to the
  task log. Bounded by `--max-seconds` (default 1500, kept below the cockpit
  runner's 1800s subprocess kill) so an abandoned capture still saves gracefully
  instead of being SIGKILLed mid-write. SIGTERM/SIGINT also finish gracefully.

New flags (non-interactive only, posture-clean — they change *when* capture
stops and *whether* the WACZ is written, never what is captured or redacted):
`--max-seconds` and `--finish-file` (explicit sentinel path; default
`<out_dir>/FINISH` next to `--out`).

No cockpit blueprint changes ship in this release: the operator drops the
sentinel from a shell, so `tools/cockpit_console.py` is untouched (a cockpit
"Finish capture" button is a possible later polish). The browser leg stays
unverifiable in the sandbox; the finish logic is pure/poll-based and unit-tested
(`tests/test_v3_66_153_capture_finish_sentinel.py`, 10 tests).

## v3.66.152 — 2026-06-05 (Ship the rich builder + harden the flat-draft path)

Real-capture testing on stash exposed two things: stash was still running the
old flat WACZ builder (it dumps every captured URL verbatim), and the normalizer
mishandled the flat-draft shape. Fixes both.

- **`tools/build_template_from_wacz.py` → the rich (network_discovery) builder.**
  Replaces the old flat builder so drafts are clean by construction: query
  strings stripped, media emitted as host-less suffix patterns
  (`.../VP9_{resolution}.mp4`), sha256 provenance. Signed Cloudflare/cachefly
  URLs and PII never survive capture.
- **`bulk_downloader/pattern_hygiene.py` — signed-blob, PII, and noise rejection.**
  Now also drops: JWTs (`eyJ…` in path or as `?p=<jwt>&s=<sig>`), long opaque
  base64/base64url token segments (cachefly `dirmatch=…/expiretime=…` blobs),
  `email` (and getbeamer) tracker URLs carrying PII, and non-media first-party
  noise (`/exclusive-offers`, `/active-subscriptions`, `/experiments`,
  `/banners`, `/event-log`, `/comments`, `/votes`, `/tags`). The
  `download-resolution` and `watch` endpoints are preserved; a 32-char hex id
  stays under the 40-char opaque threshold and is kept.
- **`bulk_downloader/template_normalize.py` — resolutions fix.** Now reads a
  flat draft's top-level `resolutions` key (was dropping `[2160…240]` to `[]`).
- **`tools/cockpit_console.py` — missing-newline fix** (separate from the
  pipeline): `api_tasks` had its `return` fused to the next route's `@bp.get`
  decorator via the `@` operator, 500-ing `/cockpit/api/tasks` and silently
  unregistering `/cockpit/api/task/<id>`. ENDPOINT_CATALOG.md regenerated to
  include the now-registered route.
- Tests: `test_v3_66_152_signed_url_and_noise_hardening.py` (9). Regression-clean
  across 147, 148, 150, 151, contracts, function-index, endpoint-catalog.

## v3.66.151 — 2026-06-04 (Automate the review-middle: rich-draft → runtime-shape normalizer)

Bridges the WACZ builder to the runtime without changing either. The
sophisticated builder stays rich; the runtime keeps consuming reviewed
templates; a new normalizer converts a rich draft into a runtime-shape **review
candidate** that a human reviews and promotes. Nothing is ever auto-enabled.

Pipeline: WACZ → `build_template_from_wacz.py` (rich draft) →
`normalize_template_draft.py` (runtime-shape review candidate) → lint/safety
review → `promote_template.py` (manual promote) → runtime reviewed template.

- **`bulk_downloader/template_normalize.py` (new) + `tools/normalize_template_draft.py` (new CLI).**
  `normalize_draft()` converts a rich builder draft into the runtime reviewed
  shape: `network_discovery.api_patterns`/`media_patterns` → flat
  `network_patterns` — relative API paths stay **relative** unless the draft
  carries an explicit API host (no host guessing; the API may live on a
  different subdomain), media suffixes kept as-is, and everything host-bearing
  is run through `pattern_hygiene` so trackers and signed/credential URLs land
  in `rejected_patterns`. `resolution_priority`/`resolutions_seen` →
  `resolutions`; `selectors.download.button_hint` (and an old draft's
  `selectors.download.button`) → `selectors.download.trigger`, never
  `row_selectors`; `row_selectors` emitted only when pre-existing,
  non-blocking-lint AND modal-scoped. Provenance/source preserved; `warnings`
  emitted; status `review_ready` or `draft_review_required`, **never `enabled`**.
- **`bulk_downloader/pattern_hygiene.py` (extended).** Now also rejects
  signed/credential URLs: AWS SigV4 (`X-Amz-*`), CloudFront (`Policy` /
  `Signature` / `Key-Pair-Id` / `Expires`), and `token` / `auth` / `bearer` /
  `sig` / `credential` query keys. Query keys are matched as keys, so legit path
  segments like `/auth/login` survive. The rich builder strips query strings,
  but old flat drafts can carry a full signed media URL — this keeps those out
  of templates.
- **`tools/promote_template.py` (updated).** Now validates and promotes the
  normalized runtime candidate shape and **refuses raw builder drafts** (run the
  normalizer first). Keeps the BAD_TERMS safety scan, adds a `selector_lint`
  blocking gate, and drops the site-specific required-pattern hardcoding so it
  works for any normalized candidate. `--enable` is still required to enable.
- Runtime, the executable reviewed-template format, and the builder are all
  unchanged. Tests: `test_v3_66_151_normalizer.py` (17). Regression-clean across
  cockpit no-auto-promote suites (110/112/113), 147, 148, 150, user_templates,
  contracts; no route or function-index changes.

## v3.66.150 — 2026-06-04 (Lint enforced at creation + network-pattern hygiene)

Closes the loop on reviewed-template safety: selector lint now blocks at the
*creation* points (not just on display), and tracker/telemetry noise is stripped
before a draft becomes an enabled reviewed template. Recognition-only; no stored
values are read or written.

- **Network-pattern hygiene (#2).** New `pattern_hygiene.scrub_network_patterns`
  drops analytics / ad / error-telemetry beacons (Sentry, GTM, Google Analytics,
  Clarity, tsyndicate, …) and non-URL junk (inlined HTML/JS/JSON blobs that a
  capture mistook for patterns), keeping real asset/media/relative patterns.
  `template_manager.promote_draft` now scrubs `network_patterns` on the way to
  the enabled reviewed template and reports `dropped_patterns`. (The existing
  reptyle draft's Sentry/tsyndicate/GTM lines are removed on promotion.)
- **Lint at the teach→save create flow (#1).** `user_templates.save_user_template`
  now runs `selector_lint.lint_learned` and refuses a learned block whose row
  selectors are generic/nav (`a`, `[href]`, `nav a`, …) — these would over-match
  at runtime. `promote_draft` already refused blocking-lint drafts; this extends
  the same gate to the other create path.
- **Lint surfaced in status (#1).** `GET /api/sites/<sid>/template_status` now
  returns `lint` + `has_blocking_lint` for the active reviewed template, and the
  site page's Template card shows a warning when an enabled template carries an
  unsafe selector. Frontend bundle rebuilt.
- Tests: `test_v3_66_150_lint_and_hygiene.py` (8). Regression-clean across
  user_templates (24), 148 backend group (14), 144 template endpoints (6).
  FUNCTION_INDEX regenerated (line-number sync). No route changes.

`profile_sync.profile_storage_status` + `GET /api/sites/<sid>/profile/status`:
for the manual / main / worker / keeper profiles, reports each storage item

**Risk fixes.** (1) Verified the debug/diagnostics bundle never carries

## v3.66.147 — 2026-06-04 (Dry-run diagnostics: Candidate Inspector + Static Template Test Runner)

First slice of the backend group. Two read-only, no-download diagnostics built
on the hardened `candidate_filter` (so the 146 nav rejection is reflected in
both), plus a new `bulk_downloader/dry_run.py`.

**Candidate Inspector / Dry-Run Classifier (#1).** `dry_run.inspect_candidates(html, page_url)`
walks every detection candidate in pasted/captured page source and classifies
each — selector, text, `href`/`data-href`/`data-url`/`data-src`, score, size,
host, positive signals, verdict (`download`/`trigger`/`rejected`) and rejection
reason — then reports the **winner** that would be selected (highest-scored
*accepted* candidate; a homepage/nav/rejected candidate is never the winner,
mirroring the runtime gate). A nav-only page yields no winner. Endpoint:
`POST /api/sites/<sid>/candidates/inspect` (body `{html, url?}`). Never fetches,
never downloads.

**Static Template Test Runner (#5).** `dry_run.template_dry_run(url, html="")`
reports whether a reviewed template matches the URL, its selector groups,
resolutions, **redacted** network patterns (query strings + token-ish segments
stripped), `selector_lint` warnings, static selector hit-counts against any
supplied HTML (Playwright-only selectors report `n/a` rather than failing — exact
live counts need a browser), the candidate classification, and whether a final
safe candidate would be selected. Endpoint:
`POST /api/sites/<sid>/template/dry_run` (body `{html?, url?}`). Never fetches,
never downloads, never reads stored values.

**Tests.** `test_v3_66_147_dry_run.py` (11 — inspector winner is an accepted
download, nav/homepage flagged with reasons, nav-only page has no winner;
template_dry_run matches reptyle / rejects unknown host / classifies + counts /
redacts tokens; both endpoints via the fresh_app client). FUNCTION INDEX +
ENDPOINT CATALOG regenerated for the two new endpoints. Superset of 146.

## v3.66.146 — 2026-06-04 (Navigation-URL rejection enforced in the live download path)

Closes the highest-risk gap behind bad `download.bin` files: the homepage / a
nav link being selected as the download. The `candidate_filter` classifier was
already used when *building* templates, but the live picker
(`detect.find_best_download` → `runner._do_download`) never consulted it, so a
learned/curated selector resolving to `/` or `/movies` could be extracted as a
direct URL and saved as `download.bin`. This release enforces the classifier in
the runtime path.

**Navigation URL rejection engine (`candidate_filter`).** Added an explicit
nav-path matcher (`_NAV_PATH_RE` / `_is_nav_path`) covering plural listings and
account/search/commerce paths — `/movies`, `/models`, `/series`, `/search`,
`/settings`, `/logout`, `/categories`, `/deals`, `/account`, `/browse`, … — and
a new `"navigation URL"` rejection in `classify()`. A strong media/download
signal (media extension, manifest, download path, API pattern) still overrides
it, and singular content paths like `/movie/<id>/…` are deliberately *not*
matched, so reptyle's real `/movie/<id>/download-resolution/<res>` is
unaffected.

**Runtime gate (`runner.gate_candidate_url` + `_do_download`).** A new pure
helper resolves a candidate's URL from `href` / `data-href` / `data-url` /
`data-src` (learned `url_attribute` first), resolves relative hrefs against the
page URL, and classifies it. `_do_download` now calls this **before** any
direct-URL extraction or click: a homepage / nav / account / search /
unrelated-host URL is refused with a logged reason and routed to
`needs_review` ("Rejected navigation URL (…) — not a download…") instead of
reaching filename generation. URL-less click-targets are **not** gated (they
fall through to `expect_download`, so unknown-site fallback keeps working), and
the gate is fail-open — any classifier/parse error yields no rejection so a bug
can never cost a real download.

**Selector safety linter (`selector_lint`).** New pure module flagging unsafe
generic selectors (`a[href]`, `[href]`, `a`, `*`, `button`, `.btn`, nav/account
selectors) as errors for row roles and warnings for triggers; scoped clauses
(dialog/modal/download) pass. `lint_template` / `lint_learned` / `lint_selector`
/ `has_blocking_issues`. A regression confirms the shipped reptyle reviewed
template carries no blocking row-selector issues.

**Tests.** `test_v3_66_146_runtime_gate.py` (11 — exercises the actual runtime
gate, incl. `href="/"` refused and a valid download-resolution URL accepted,
plus `_do_download` routing a nav URL to `needs_review`) and
`test_v3_66_146_detection_safety.py` (12 — nav-path rejection + linter). FUNCTION
INDEX regenerated for the new `gate_candidate_url`. Superset of 145.

## v3.66.144 — 2026-06-04 (Reviewed-template subsystem: in-source + wired)

The reviewed-template subsystem (`template_assist`, `template_registry`,
`tools/onboard_site_template`) and its reptyle tests previously lived only on
the deployed host, outside the release source. An unzip-over-the-top update of
the shared files reverted the one `runner.py` line that wired it in, orphaning
the modules and dropping reptyle back to generic detection (which is what
produces a bad `download.bin`). This release folds the whole subsystem **into
source** so an overlay can't orphan it again, and restores + hardens the
wiring.

**Subsystem folded into source.** `bulk_downloader/template_assist.py`,
`bulk_downloader/template_registry.py`, `tools/onboard_site_template.py`, and
`templates/reviewed|drafts/` now ship in the package. The three reptyle tests
moved under `tests/` so the standard runner discovers them (they were at the
repo root and silently never run).

**Runtime wiring restored (Goal 3).** `runner.py` calls
`merge_template_download_hints(page, learned_dl)` before the trigger scan again
(soft import; degrades gracefully if the subsystem is absent), so an enabled
reviewed template's selectors reach the download path.

**Reviewed download shape consumed (Goal 3).** `template_to_learned_download`
now reads the reviewed `download.trigger` (e.g. "Download Full Movie", which
opens a modal) and modal-scoped `download.row_selectors`, in addition to the
legacy `download.button`. The reptyle template was authored with this shape but
the consumer ignored it. Result: the trigger is clicked first, then the
dialog's `download-resolution`/resolution rows are scraped — real media/API
URLs, never the homepage. `candidate_filter` already rejects
`https://app.reptyle.com/` (homepage) and generic `a[href]`.

**Reviewed-template visibility API (Goal 2, backend).** New
`GET /api/sites/<sid>/template_status` (read-only: enabled template summary +
onboarding state + a "Reviewed Template: <host> enabled" label) and
`POST /api/sites/<sid>/template_onboard` (runs the onboarding planner, persists
`template_onboarding` / `auto_teach_first_run` / `template_auto_detect_mode`;
launches the capture flow when a capture is required and `run` is set —
approved sites never launch). The React site-page badge/button lands in a
follow-up (frontend rebuild).

**Manual-login handoff (Goal 1).** Already shipped in 140/141 and unchanged —
`profile_sync` syncs Cookies + Local/Session Storage + IndexedDB + WebStorage
into `main` + every `w*` + every `keepalive_*`, skips the leveldb `LOCK`, backs
up replaced items, and keepers are paused (no locks) and auto-relaunched.

**Tests.** `test_v3_66_144_template_subsystem.py` (10) and
`test_v3_66_144_template_endpoints.py` (6) cover all four goals: onboarding
detects approved templates, `auto_teach_first_run` off when approved,
SiteRunner compat wrappers, homepage URL rejected / real download URL accepted,
safe profile-storage sync, the merge integration, and both endpoints. The
reptyle trio (registry 3 / assist 4 / runner wiring 1) now runs in-suite.

per-block guarding, System Status GUI wiring, `handoff_status` (empty-safe +
detects manual/session), offline asset locality + no-CDN, backend downgrade to
playwright when CloakBrowser is absent, and end-to-end bad selector / bad URL
rejection through the extractor (empty draft now also flags `review_required`).

**Route-count tripwire** — the new GET route takes the cockpit rule count
155→156→**157** (POST count unchanged at 23); the `len(rules)` assertion was
bumped across the 31 `TestWiring` files. The shared/dynamic-count follow-up
(noted in v3.66.142) still stands — this is the second consecutive release to
hand-bump it.



Three areas, shipped together: the manual-login → runtime profile handoff is
hardened, the site-template flow stops mistaking ordinary page links for the
download control, and a new multi-capture builder compares several approved
captures instead of trusting one. DOM capture is confirmed fully offline.

**profile_sync hardening** (the v3.66.140 manual-login → runtime handoff).
Five fixes to `bulk_downloader/profile_sync.py`:
- *Timestamped backups* — before an existing auth/session item is replaced in a
  target profile, the old copy is moved into `<profile>/.sync_backups/<ts>/`
  (at the profile root, outside `Default/` so Chromium ignores it). A bad sync
  is now recoverable. No backup dir is created when the destination is fresh.
- *No LOCK files* — `Local Storage` / `Session Storage` / `IndexedDB` /
  `WebStorage` are copied with the leveldb `LOCK` file skipped at every level
  (a stale LOCK confuses the Chromium that later opens the profile).
- *Honest "synced"* — a profile is reported under `synced` only if ≥1 item was
  actually copied; otherwise it's recorded under the new `skipped` key with a
  reason. `finish_manual_login`'s "synced N profiles" message is now accurate.
- *Keepalive guard* — keepalive targets are synced while holding the same
  `session_keeper.get_takeover_lock(site, idx)` the keeper acquires before it
  launches, so the keeper can't relaunch/reopen the profile mid-copy. If the
  keeper already holds the lock (mid-launch), that target is skipped rather
  than clobbering a live profile.
- *Logging* — each target logs the copied item names + target profile name.

**Safer template candidates** — new `bulk_downloader/candidate_filter.py` gates
download candidates so the flow no longer resolves a generic `a[href]` to the
homepage or a nav link and produces a bad `download.bin`. A URL-bearing
candidate is accepted only with a positive site signal (media extension /
manifest URL / download path / resolution label / known API pattern) and no
hard rejection: generic href-only selector, homepage link, nav/header/footer,
search/settings/login/logout, share/favorite/comment/vote, or unrelated
external-service link. It is kind-aware — URL-less quality/download **menu**
buttons survive as triggers (not rejected for lacking a URL), and an external
media CDN serving real media is allowed. `template_extractor` now requires a
URL-based media/download signal for **row** selectors; when none qualify it
falls back to the best-scored rows but flags `review_required`, and the
filtered-out links are surfaced as `rejected_candidates`.

**Multi-capture template builder** — new `bulk_downloader/template_multi.py`
(`build_multi_capture_draft`) compares several APPROVED captures of one site
(`login` / `player` / `quality_menu` / `download_menu` / `download_result`)
into a **review-required** draft: selector **support counts** (how many
captures/roles each passing selector appears in), **rejected** candidates with
reason + role, **reusable network patterns** (request URL templates with
`{id}` / `{hex}` / `{res}` collapsed, media/API only, with role coverage), and
**resolution priority** (tiers high→low). Exposed at
`POST /cockpit/api/captures/build-multi-template` (inline capture dicts or
filenames under the captures root, path-traversal guarded), alongside the
existing two-capture `build-template` route. Recognition-only — no replay, no
network, no rule writes.

**Offline DOM capture, no CDN** — confirmed the whole capture path injects the
vendored rrweb 2.0.1 + snapdom 2.12.8 from `bulk_downloader/vendor` with no
remote-CDN fallback (the asset readers raise if a bundle is missing). Added
`dom_recorder.using_local_assets()` and a one-time log in `attach_dom_recorder`
making the offline guarantee explicit.

**Route-count tripwire maintenance** — the new POST route shifts two hardcoded
cockpit-blueprint counts in the `TestWiring` tests: `len(rules)` 155 → 156 (31
files) and `len(posts)` 21 → 23 (11 files). Note: the POST tripwire was already
stale by one before this change (v3.66.139's `build-template` POST updated the
total-rules assertion but not the POST one); this release adds the second and
sets both to the correct live values. These 42 magic numbers re-break on every
route addition and should be replaced with a shared/dynamic count (follow-up).



Every browser launch in the app now goes through the **same shared wrapper**
(`bulk_downloader/cloak.py`), backend-selectable as **`cloakbrowser`** or
**`playwright`**. Previously only session keeper used the wrapper; runner
workers, login, manual login, manual download, and capture each launched
Playwright directly — so the backend choice (and stealth behaviour) was
inconsistent between flows.

**Single source of truth.** New `cloak.resolve_backend(config)` returns
`"cloakbrowser"` or `"playwright"`, resolved with precedence: per-call config →
env → global Settings → default (cloakbrowser when importable, else
playwright). A request for `cloakbrowser` downgrades to `playwright` when the
package isn't installed. Configure via the `browser_backend` key (config /
`BD_BROWSER_BACKEND` env / Settings); the legacy `use_cloak` /
`session_keeper_use_cloakbrowser` booleans are still honoured. `use_cloak()` is
now a thin shim over `resolve_backend()`.

**Wrapper owns the Playwright lifecycle.** The wrapper starts and (on the
playwright backend) returns the `sync_playwright` instance for the caller to
stop; on the cloakbrowser backend it returns `pw=None` and the context/browser
stops its own. Callers no longer start their own `sync_playwright` — this is the
same thread-bound pattern session keeper already used. New helpers:
`launch_browser()` (non-persistent), `persistent_context()` (context-manager
form with the channel→bundled retry), and `log_choice(flow, backend, detail)`.

**Flows routed:** runner workers + manual download (`runner._launch_browser`,
now a 4-tuple `(browser, ctx, pw, backend)`), automated login + manual login +
login verify (`login.py`), capture session and DOM capture (`capture_session`).

**Clear per-flow logs.** Each flow emits one line —
`  [browser] <flow>: <backend> — <detail>` — e.g. `worker[site/0]`,
`manual download[site]`, `manual login`, `login`, `login verify`,
`keepalive[site/0]`, `capture`, `DOM capture`. DOM capture shares the capture
session's browser, so it reports that backend.

`browser_backend=playwright` reproduces the exact pre-3.66.141 launch behaviour
(an escape hatch if a cloak launch misbehaves). Existing channel→bundled-Chromium
and per-site/VPN-proxy fallbacks are preserved on every path.

Tests: `tests/test_v3_66_141_browser_backend.py` (8). Regressions green across
worker pipeline, keeper, login, teach, capture, and DOM suites.

## v3.66.140 — 2026-06-04 (manual-login → runtime profile session handoff)

Fixes a login-handoff bug: a successful **manual login** persisted only to its
own Chromium profile (`profiles/<sid>/manual`), but downloads and keepalive run
in separate profiles (`profiles/<sid>/main`, `.../w<N>`, `.../keepalive_<N>`),
so they kept their own logged-out session — manual login "worked" but wasn't
reused when downloads started.

New module `bulk_downloader/profile_sync.py` propagates the login-continuity
browser state from the manual profile into the runtime profiles.
`runner.finish_manual_login` (the `/api/sites/<sid>/login_manual_done` "Done"
handler) calls it after the manual browser is closed by `finalize_manual_login`
— so the source profile is flushed to disk — and while the session keepers are
paused (so no process holds a runtime profile open). It syncs into every
existing runtime profile and seeds `main` (plus `keepalive_0` when the keeper is
enabled) even if absent, so the first download after a fresh manual login is
logged in.

Only the state needed for login continuity is copied — never the whole profile
(caches, GPU state, History, etc. are large and worker-specific):
`Cookies`, `Cookies-journal`, `Local Storage`, `Session Storage`, `IndexedDB`,
`WebStorage`. The source's `Default/`-subdir layout is mirrored into each
destination. The copy is best-effort per target (one profile failing doesn't
abort the rest) and gated on a successful login.

Verified: `tests/test_v3_66_140_profile_sync.py` 4/4 (seeds main + keepalive_0 +
existing workers; excludes non-continuity state; flat-layout + no-manual cases);
no regression in the manual-login path (teach-credentials 11, teach-urls 13,
keeper-collision 9, worker pipeline 35, login fallback 4). `FUNCTION_INDEX.md`
regenerated; both drift gates green. The live-browser write path (real Chromium
flushing the manual profile) is not exercised offline.

Known limitation: an *extra* download worker (`w<N>`, N≥1) created fresh for the
first time *after* a manual login won't have existed at sync time, so it starts
unseeded until the next manual login; the common single-worker (`main`) and
keepalive cases are covered. A follow-up could seed a new worker profile from
`main` at creation.
