## v3.66.139 — 2026-06-04 (cloak keep-alive toggle in Settings; rrweb/snapdom capture wiring; multi-capture template build route + cockpit action)

Three features, built A → B → C.

**A. CloakBrowser keep-alive toggle surfaced in Settings.** `cloak.use_cloak()` now
consults a global app-config value as a layer, so the CloakBrowser-vs-Playwright choice
for keep-alive launches is controllable from the Settings UI rather than only via env or
per-site config. Precedence is unchanged in spirit and now explicit: per-call/per-site
config → `BD_USE_CLOAK` / `BD_SESSION_KEEPER_USE_CLOAKBROWSER` env → global Settings value
(`session_keeper_use_cloakbrowser`, read lazily from `app_config.json`) → default (prefer
cloak). The `/api/global_config` POST whitelists the new key; GET already returns the whole
config so it flows to the UI automatically. The SPA gains a "Use CloakBrowser for keep-alive"
switch in the Session keep-alive section (`Settings.tsx`, with `GlobalConfigSubset` extended
in `api-types.ts`).

**B. rrweb + snapdom wired into the capture path.** `DomCapture` defined an rrweb-style
DOM-event ingest (`record_dom_event`) but nothing produced those events — a capture session
recorded network (via `capture_via_cdp`) and left `dom_log` empty. New module
`bulk_downloader/dom_recorder.py` closes the gap: it injects the vendored rrweb bundle into
the capture page (`page.add_init_script`), starts `rrweb.record` with the project's PII
redaction classes (`bd-mask`/`rr-mask`, `bd-block`/`rr-block`, `bd-ignore`/`rr-ignore`), and
forwards each emitted event into `record_dom_event` (full snapshot → `is_full_snapshot`,
incremental → `data.source`); serialized-node redaction in `DomCapture` is a second layer.
`tools/capture_session.py` now attaches the recorder right after `capture_via_cdp`, before
the first navigation. rrweb 2.0.1 and @zumer/snapdom 2.12.8 are vendored under
`bulk_downloader/vendor/` (see `vendor/VENDOR.md`) as self-contained global-attaching bundles.
snapdom support adds an opt-in `snapshot_dom(page)` helper and a `DomCapture.record_dom_snapshot`
sink — opt-in and never auto-taken on a logged-in capture, because a rendered raster can
contain visible PII that the class-based text redaction does not cover.

Caveat: the live browser injection round-trip (rrweb emitting through the Playwright binding
in a real capture) is not exercised offline — the same verification boundary the project
already documents for `capture_via_cdp`. The pure mapping, ingest/redaction, snapshot sink,
and asset/JS integrity are unit-tested (`tests/test_v3_66_139_dom_recorder.py`), and all
injected JS validates under `node --check`.

**C. Multi-capture template build exposed as a route + cockpit action.** The
synth → workbench → (optional freeze) pipeline (`capture_synth.synthesize` →
`capture_workbench.build_workbench` → `capture_template.build_template`) was reachable from
no route or GUI. New cockpit endpoint `POST /cockpit/api/captures/build-template` runs it
in-process — recognition-only (no replay, no network, no rule-table writes), matching the
cockpit's read/compute posture. It accepts two capture filenames under `BD_CAPTURES_ROOT`
(`.json`/`.wacz`, loaded via `capture_ingest.load_capture`, path-checked against the root) or
inline capture dicts for testing, with an optional `freeze` flag. The cockpit Captures page
gains a "Build template from two captures" card (two inputs + freeze selector + result panel),
mirroring the offline-analyze card. Tested via the blueprint test client
(`tests/test_v3_66_139_build_template_route.py`); the cockpit UI itself is not browser-runtime-tested.

`ENDPOINT_CATALOG.md` and `FUNCTION_INDEX.md` regenerated for the new route and functions
(both drift tests green).

## v3.66.138 — 2026-06-04 (CloakBrowser made canonical; session-keeper launch hardened)

CloakBrowser is now the canonical, default browser backend for automated persistent-profile
launches, with vanilla Playwright as an automatic fallback. New module `bulk_downloader/cloak.py`
wraps the optional `cloakbrowser` package the same way `stealth.py` wraps `playwright-stealth`: one
lazy, cached availability probe (`is_available`), one backend decision (`use_cloak`, default = prefer
cloak), and `open_persistent_context(...)` which launches via CloakBrowser and falls back to
Playwright on missing import, explicit disable, OR a launch-time failure (e.g. the stealth Chromium
binary can't be fetched on a network-restricted host). It returns `(context, pw, backend)` so callers
don't have to juggle the pw-vs-cloak lifecycle.

`session_keeper.py` now routes its keep-alive browser launch through `cloak.open_persistent_context`
instead of calling `sync_playwright()` directly; the launch log reports the chosen backend.

Two cloak bugs from the experimental variant trees (cockpit_cloak / clurable / urable_fixed) are
fixed by construction — the base never had cloak, so these only affected those branches:
  - The unconditional module-level `from cloakbrowser import launch_persistent_context` — which
    crashed `import bulk_downloader.session_keeper` (and therefore `app.py`) on hosts without
    cloakbrowser, even when the feature was toggled off — is gone. The probe is lazy and the disable
    flag is honored before any import or launch. `import bulk_downloader.session_keeper` now succeeds
    with cloakbrowser absent.
  - The `use_cloak` NameError (referenced-but-never-assigned in one variant's `_launch_browser`,
    silently degrading to httpx) is structurally impossible: the decision lives in `cloak.use_cloak()`.

Toggle: cloak is on by default; disable per-call via config `use_cloak` / `session_keeper_use_cloakbrowser`,
or env `BD_USE_CLOAK` / `BD_SESSION_KEEPER_USE_CLOAKBROWSER=0`.

Scope: the headed manual-login path (`login.py`, `channel="chrome"` plus the user's real Chrome and
password manager) and the runner's ephemeral launches are intentionally left on Playwright — `channel`
is mutually exclusive with CloakBrowser's bundled stealth Chromium. The runner worker-scrape launch
can adopt `cloak.open_persistent_context` as a follow-up.

Verified: toggle matrix; import-without-cloakbrowser; runtime cloak→fallback→Playwright on a
network-restricted host; session-keeper tests 33/33 and 19/19 cloak/keeper-related test files clean in
isolation.

## v3.66.137 — 2026-06-02 (Autonomy — Phase K: held-out designation assist; the last code phase)

`tools/autonomy_held_out_assist.py` (assist) + `tools/autonomy_designate.py` (human-only CLI). This
is the reflexive phase — it concerns the **held-out evidence that feeds the tier-3 gate authorizing
`live_site_config` autonomy** — so it is deliberately **NOT an apply-kind**: not grantable, no
autonomous write, no reverser. Designating held-out evidence is a `corpus_writes` action and stays in
`PERMANENTLY_INELIGIBLE` (permanently human). Automating it would let the system manufacture its own
tier-3 and self-expand authority, which the architecture forbids.

The assist is read/compute/propose only. For a candidate capture it reports, reusing the oracle's OWN
logic (never a parallel reimplementation): the integrity verdict — REJECT on overlap with training
evidence or on any raw signing value (descriptors are names/shapes only — posture) — and the tier-delta,
computed by running the real `oracle_verdict` with the candidate appended to the held-out descriptors. A
parity test pins this projection to the verdict produced after the candidate is actually designated, so
the assist can never propose something the gate would reject (no permissive drift). It also surfaces
held-out evidence staleness (`held_out_designated_at`) for re-confirmation.

`autonomy_designate.py` mirrors the grant CLI: human-invoked, not wired into the Class-C cycle, not
grantable. It appends a capture name to `capture_provenance.json` held-out + stamps
`held_out_designated_at` — and only after the assist verdict passes (it refuses a rejected candidate).
The assist module writes nothing under any path. No new routes, no POST (cockpit stays 155 / 21);
`PERMANENTLY_INELIGIBLE` unchanged. After K, only **L** remains, which is not code (the human decision
to raise Class C to `auto_with_guardrails`).



`tools/autonomy_library_reconcile.py` registers kind **`library_reconcile`** (per-site) on the
generic harness — the second operational kind after `queue_housekeeping`. It removes `library`
rows whose file went away (`file_exists=0`) and was last seen present more than
`BD_LIB_RECONCILE_MISSING_DAYS` ago (default 30). The media file is **never** touched
(`also_delete_file=False`, always) — only the stale index row is removed, and the removal is fully
reversible.

Notable design points:

- **Debounce off `last_scanned`, no migration.** The scanner flips `file_exists` 1→0 when a path is
  gone but leaves `last_scanned` (last time the file was seen present) intact, so a transient mount
  blip — which reappears on the next scan and refreshes `last_scanned` — never accumulates
  missing-age. No schema or scanner change was needed.
- **Exact reversal of a child-FK row.** A `library` row's autoincrement `id` is an FK target
  (`library_tags ON DELETE CASCADE`, `history.library_id` back-ref). New `library_snapshot(id)` /
  `library_restore(snapshot)` helpers (in `library.py`, generic over columns) snapshot the row + its
  tags and restore all three on rollback **preserving the original `id`**, so tag links and the
  history back-ref line up again.
- **Operational gate, no oracle tier-3.** Gate = active per-`(site, library_reconcile)` grant + the
  aged-missing predicate. Dark by default. Four safety layers on a removal: grant required, 30-day
  debounce, file never touched, exact-reversible. `dry_run(site)` reports the plan without writing.
- **Scope boundary.** Per-site (rows carry `site_id`). Orphan IMPORT (on-disk files with no row) is
  deliberately **not** here — imported rows are unattributed (`site_id=''`) and need the not-yet-built
  global grant scope. File MOVES stay with `storage_tier`; NFO/sidecar regen is unverified, out of scope.

Surfaces read-only through the existing Authority aggregation — **no new routes, no new POST** (cockpit
stays 155 paths / 21 POST). Grants remain CLI-only / human-only (`--kind library_reconcile`). Authority
now lists four kinds.



The first `register_apply_kind(...)` after consolidation, and the first operational target:
`tools/autonomy_queue_hk.py` registers kind **`queue_housekeeping`** (per-site) on the generic
harness. Two operations, two risk tiers:

- **I-A — terminal-row GC (live once granted):** deletes queue rows whose status is terminal
  (done/error/failed) and untouched for `BD_QUEUE_HK_GC_AGE_DAYS` (default 7). Zero live-work
  impact; fully reversible (deleted rows are snapshotted and re-inserted on rollback).
- **I-B — abandon retry-exhausted/stuck rows (OFF by default):** transitions pending/running rows
  with `retries >= BD_QUEUE_HK_MAX_RETRIES` and no update in `BD_QUEUE_HK_STALE_HOURS` to `failed`.
  Gated behind `BD_QUEUE_HK_ABANDON` (default off) for a dry-run observation week before activation.
  Reversible (restores prior row state = re-queues the job).

Architecture notes: operational kinds do **not** use the oracle tier-3 gate — `queue_housekeeping`'s
gate is an active per-`(site, queue_housekeeping)` grant plus an objective per-row predicate, so it
is dark by default (no grant ⇒ nothing runs). DB access goes through injectable wrappers so tests
need no database. Reuses the harness's record_change → register_pending (fail-closed review) →
validator (revert on miss) → rollback chain unchanged. Surfaces read-only through the existing
Authority aggregation — **no new routes, no new POST** (cockpit stays 155 paths / 21 POST). Grants
remain CLI-only / human-only; `tools/autonomy_grant.py` already supports `--kind queue_housekeeping`.
A `dry_run(site)` helper reports the plan without writing (for the pre-activation week).



Folds the Class-C sprawl into one model. A new generic harness, `tools/autonomy_apply.py`,
turns "an apply kind" into a **registration** rather than a module: `register_apply_kind(kind,
gate, current, proposer, applier, reverser, …)` records the hooks and registers the reverser;
`apply_for_kind(site, kind)` runs the single shared orchestration (gate → propose →
corroborate → before/after → backup → record_change → apply → register_pending → validate →
revert-on-miss → transition). H (`live_site_config`) and v1 (`staging_json`) are **refactored
onto it** with no behavior change — registration hooks are late-binding wrappers so existing
monkeypatch tests still hold.

**Authority model (D0 = compute the gate now).** `class_c_site_eligible(site, kind)` is no
longer a hardcoded `False` stub — it is **computed**: eligible iff an active per-(site, kind)
grant ∧ Class C at `auto_with_guardrails` ∧ oracle tier ≥ 3. It stays **dark by default**:
with no grant, or Class C at approve-each, or no tier-3 evidence, it is `False`. Grants are now
**per-(site, kind)**: granting `(site, live_site_config)` never grants any other kind. Old
single-kind grants `{site: {granted: …}}` migrate to `{site: {live_site_config: …}}`
(normalize-on-read, persist-on-write). `reconcile_grants` sweeps every (site, kind) and may
only **auto-suspend** (contraction); it never creates or un-suspends (expansion is human-only,
via the CLI). No kind can apply without a registered reverser.

**Cockpit.** New **Authority** view (site × kind grant matrix, pending across all kinds,
registered kinds) replaces the Live Config page, backed by 5 read-only routes
`/api/authority/{status,grants,pending,kinds,change}`. The legacy
`/api/live/{status,grants,pending,change}` routes **remain as compatibility aliases**
returning the same data filtered to `live_site_config` (equivalence is by construction — one
reader). No new POST routes (accept/reject still reuse `/api/review/decide`; grants are
CLI-only). Cockpit unique paths **150 → 155**; POST count unchanged at **21**.

After this, I/J/K are thin `register_apply_kind(…)` registrations (a kind + four functions),
inheriting the grant store, CLI, reconcile, fail-closed window, rollback, audit, and Authority
view. More autonomy = register more reversers + grant more (site, kind) pairs; never remove a
gate.



The first **production write**. For a site the operator has explicitly **granted**, and only
when human-designated held-out evidence corroborates the change (oracle tier 3), the system
can autonomously apply a `learned`/`scoring` change to live `sites_config.json` — and only
that — under a fail-closed window that reverts on silence and a **pure** post-apply
validation that reverts on failure. Full chain reused: `record_change("live_site_config", …)`
→ `register_pending` → fail-closed 24h window → rollback → audit. **Build dark**: with no
grant or no tier-3 evidence, nothing applies.

Deliberately NOT in scope: no login-field change, no credential read/write, no corpus, no
debt retirement, no finding confirm/falsify, no policy change, no release approval, no
capture execution, no third-party interaction, no second site in one in-flight window. H
**never authors selectors** — it forwards the synthesis subsystem's proposal.

- `tools/autonomy_live.py` — NEW. `maintain_live_config(site)` / `maintain_all_live()`
  (host-scheduled; never a cockpit button). Applies ONLY the target site's `learned`+
  `scoring`, leaving every other key (credentials, login selectors, …) and every other site
  byte-identical; atomic `.tmp`+`os.replace` (the `_save_sites_config` contract).
  * `_restore_live_block` reverser, registered on import — coupling the apply path to a
    registered reverser (nothing applies that can't be rolled back).
  * `_post_apply_validation` — PURE descriptor match: derives the proposed descriptor from
    the block's `_expectations` and requires the oracle's identity/rendition/template-shape
    agreement with held-out. NO network, NO browser, NO re-download, NO byte comparison;
    fail-closed.
  * `_backup_sites_config` — timestamped, **credential-redacted** snapshot before each write;
    keeps the last 10.
  * Read-only views `live_status` / `live_grants` / `live_pending` / `live_change`.
- `tools/autonomy_grant.py` — NEW. Per-site grants. **Creating / revoking / un-suspending a
  grant is HUMAN-ONLY (CLI/host).** `reconcile_grants()` is a host job that AUTO-SUSPENDS
  only (trust < floor, oracle tier < 3, frozen, expired) — it never creates a grant and never
  un-suspends. Authority contracts automatically, never expands. Writes the store the oracle
  already reads (`governance/oracle/site_auto_grants.json`) + `grants_log.jsonl`.
- `tools/autonomy_eligibility.py` — `apply_path_exists()` rewired from hardcoded `False` to
  `agr.has_reverser("live_site_config")`. `participation_eligible` (unchanged formula) now
  becomes True only when ALL hold: active grant, Class C allowed, apply path (reverser),
  tier-3 corroborated evidence, trust ≥ floor, not frozen, blast OK.
- `tools/autonomy_guardrails.py` — `has_reverser(kind)` helper.
- `tools/cockpit_console.py` — +4 **GET** endpoints (`/api/live/status|grants|pending|change`)
  + nav "Live Config" + `PAGES.liveconfig` / `PAGES.liveconfigchange`. Accept/reject reuse
  `/api/review/decide`; **no new POST**; grant status is read-only (no grant button).
- Acceptance: accept blesses + stops the clock; reject rolls back now; silence rolls back at
  the deadline; validation failure rolls back now.
- Tests: `tests/test_v3_66_133_live_config_apply.py` — only learned+scoring change; all other
  keys + other sites byte-identical; credentials never in records or backups; no/suspended/
  expired grant ⇒ no apply; rollback restores; validation-fail/reject/silence revert; accept
  keeps; freeze blocks; route count 150; no new POST; views read-only; build-dark applies
  nothing; reconcile never grants/un-suspends; apply-path tracks the registry.
- Cockpit route count 146 → 150 (tripwire bumped). ENDPOINT_CATALOG 881 → 885. FUNCTION_INDEX
  unchanged (1057).

## v3.66.132 — 2026-06-02 (Autonomy — v1: first bounded apply wire, staged config candidates)

The first real autonomy wire. The system can now autonomously maintain a confined,
reversible, per-site **staged config candidate**, exercising the full chain — oracle/trust
gates → staged candidate apply → `record_change("staging_json", …)` → `register_pending`
→ fail-closed 24h window → auto-revert if not accepted → transition/audit log — on the
lowest-risk write target in the system. It writes **no production config**, promotes
**nothing** to live, changes **no behavioral fields**, and handles **no credentials**.

- `tools/autonomy_staging.py` — NEW module (no module-level I/O; host-scheduled apply +
  read-only views):
  * `maintain_staged_candidate(site)` / `maintain_all()` — host-scheduled (cron/CLI, beside
    `decay_all_trust` + `scan_and_record`); never a cockpit button. Stages a candidate IFF
    `staging_eligible`. Idempotent. Writes only the `staging_json`-kind candidate file via
    `agr._atomic_write_json`; never `sites_config.json`.
  * `staging_eligible(site)` — the v1 gate (oracle tier 3 + trust ≥ floor + reversible +
    blast-ok + single-site + not pinned), via `impact_report`. A **separate, strictly
    weaker** authority than `participation_eligible`, which is NOT consulted and stays
    `False`.
  * Candidate carries a **credential-redacted** copy of the live block's behavioral fields
    (secrets/PII never embedded) plus a system-authored `evidence` annotation. Behavioral
    fields are verbatim — v1 proposes no behavioral change.
  * `staged_candidates()`, `staged_candidate(site)`, `staging_status()` — read-only views.
- `tools/cockpit_console.py` — +3 GET endpoints (`/api/staging/status|candidates|candidate`)
  + a "Staged Candidates" page and a "Staged Candidate" detail page (evidence delta,
  behavioral-unchanged confirmation, redacted-keys, rollback-preview, deadline), in the
  Governance nav. Cockpit routes 143 → 146. **No new POST.**
- `tools/cockpit_core.py` — `review_decide` extended with a **narrow delegation**: when the
  item is a pending guardrails `change_id`, accept/reject is routed through the audited
  `agr.mark_reviewed` (reject reverts immediately; accept stops the fail-closed clock
  **without promoting**). Reuses the existing `/api/review/decide` POST — no new route. For
  any non-change-id item it behaves exactly as before.
- `tests/test_v3_66_132_staged_candidate_autonomy.py` — NEW: no production config writes
  (byte-identical + source grep); behavioral byte-identical to redacted live; no credential
  leak (sentinels absent from candidate, staged file, change record); no policy/corpus/debt/
  finding/credential/capture constructs; fail-closed auto-revert; reject reverts immediately
  via the delegation; accept does not promote; `participation_eligible` stays False;
  `staging_eligible` is separate and weaker; audit trail (change record + pending +
  transition); wiring (146 routes, no new POST). Route-count tripwire bumped 143 → 146.

Build-dark: against empty oracle/trust stores nothing qualifies and no candidate is staged.
This is expected until real held-out captures + a week of `decay_all_trust`/`scan_and_record`
accrue. v2 would add a live-config apply path with its own reverser + a per-site grant;
higher autonomy comes from registering more reversers, never from removing gates.

Sixth and final Phase-G deliverable. Adds an append-only audit log of governance-state
**transitions** that ties G1–G5 together: as a site gains or loses evidence-qualification
(G1), its trust crosses the floor (G3), or its evidence goes overdue (G4), the movement is
recorded for audit. It records movement; it never causes it. Because there is no Class C
apply path, `participation_eligible` never transitions to True — the log shows
evidence/trust/validation movement with participation pinned False. No automation, no new
POST.

- `tools/autonomy_promotion.py` — NEW module (read-mostly; no module-level I/O; no apply/
  promotion of a real change; no corpus/policy/credential writes):
  * `record_transition(site, field, before, after, by, reason)` — append one transition to
    the append-only log (`governance/promotion/activity.jsonl`, matching the guardrail
    alerts log).
  * `scan_and_record(by)` — diff each site's current governance state (composed from G1/G3/
    G4) against the last snapshot and append a transition for each changed field; save the
    snapshot atomically (`.tmp` + replace). Host-scheduled (cron/CLI), never a button. The
    first scan establishes a baseline and records nothing.
  * `activity_log()`, `site_activity()`, `promotion_overview()`, `promotion_status()` —
    read-only views. `TRACKED_FIELDS` spans evidence_qualified, participation_eligible,
    trust_eligible, oracle_tier, validation_status.
- `tools/cockpit_console.py` — +3 GET endpoints (`/api/promotion/status|activity|site`) +
  a "Promotion Activity" page (the transition log) and a "Site Activity" detail page, in
  the Governance nav. Cockpit routes 140 → 143. No new POST (the scan is host-scheduled).
- `tests/test_v3_66_131_promotion_activity.py` — NEW: record appends; scan baselines then
  records a real `trust_eligible` True->False transition; append-only (log only grows,
  prior entries preserved, no truncate/unlink/clear); participation never transitions True;
  ties-chain (tracked fields span the phases); store atomicity (snapshot .tmp+replace,
  activity append); views; wiring (143 routes, no new POST). Route-count tripwire bumped
  140 → 143.

**Phase G complete (G1–G6, v3.66.126–131).** The governance INFRASTRUCTURE for tightly
controlled Class C experimentation now exists end to end — eligibility, rollback,
trust, validation, impact, and a transition audit — without Class C being enabled:
Approve-each remains the default, there is no apply path, and `participation_eligible` is
False everywhere. Recommended next step is the telemetry pause (deploy to `stash`, wire
`decay_all_trust` + `scan_and_record` into cron, collect ~1 week of real signal) before
relying on the trust and transition data.

Third Phase-G deliverable. Adds per-site trust scoring with automatic DECAY and wires it
into eligibility. The load-bearing invariant — the one Phase H is built on — is that
**trust may only ever DECREASE automatically**: adverse signals lower a site's trust;
favourable signals never raise it on their own. The only path that raises trust is an
explicit human restore (a governance action), with no automatic caller. Authority
therefore never expands automatically; it only contracts as risk rises. No automation is
enabled and no new POST is added.

- `tools/autonomy_trust.py` — NEW module (no module-level I/O; not read-only — decay/reset
  write the trust store atomically, but it performs no forbidden mutation):
  * `signal_trust(site)` — a pure [0,1] score from real signals (oracle tier, evidence
    freshness, global rollback + review-expiry rates, oracle hard-failures, freeze).
  * `effective_trust(site)` — the stored, ratcheted value (BASELINE = 1.0 for an unseen
    site). Read-only.
  * `decay_trust(site, by)` — the auto-decay mutator: `stored := min(stored, signal)`. Can
    only LOWER trust (an improved signal leaves the floor untouched). Host-scheduled
    (cron/CLI), never a cockpit button. `decay_all_trust(by)` decays every site.
  * `reset_trust(site, value, by, reason)` — the ONLY raise; requires a human identity;
    logged; no automatic caller.
  * `trust_eligible(site)` (`effective_trust >= MIN_TRUST = 0.5`), `trust_site`,
    `trust_overview`, `trust_status` (read-only rollups).
- `tools/autonomy_eligibility.py` — G3 wire: `evaluate_site` reads `effective_trust(site)`;
  a site below `MIN_TRUST` is not evidence-qualified (new decay reason) — even if its
  current evidence looks good — until a human restores trust. Undecayed sites are at
  BASELINE and unaffected. New verdict key: `trust`.
- `tools/cockpit_console.py` — +3 GET endpoints (`/api/trust/status|overview|site`) + a
  "Trust Decay" page (per-site trust, signal, eligibility, last restore) and a "Site
  Trust" detail page, in the Governance nav. Cockpit routes 131 → 134. No new POST.
- `tests/test_v3_66_128_trust_decay.py` — NEW: trust only decreases automatically (decay
  lowers, a good signal does not raise; monotonic non-increasing); human restore is the
  only raise (requires identity); the signal score is bounded and frozen-caps low; trust
  gates eligibility (a decayed site is ineligible even with good evidence; a human restore
  requalifies); read-only views; store atomicity/UTF-8/UTC + no forbidden mutation;
  wiring (134 routes, no new POST). Route-count tripwire bumped 131 → 134.

NOTE (honest scope): this phase does NOT add an oracle-disagreement rate to the guardrail
throttle metrics. That metric requires applied-change-vs-oracle outcomes, which do not
exist without a Class C apply path; trust uses only the signals that are real today.

Second Phase-G deliverable. Surfaces the guardrail rollback engine as a read-only
Rollback Center and wires "a change is eligible only if it can be reverted" back into the
G1 eligibility layer. No automation is enabled and no new mutation is added: reverting a
change remains an audited guardrail function (host cycle / operator), never a cockpit
button. The engine's load-bearing properties (revert restores before-state + is
idempotent; review rejection triggers a revert; expired Class C auto-reverts fail-closed;
a reverser error freezes all automation) are unchanged and re-anchored by this phase's
tests.

- `tools/autonomy_rollback.py` — NEW module (read-only; no module-level I/O):
  * `rollback_capability(target_kind)` — whether a reverser is registered for a target
    kind (with `None`, reports engine readiness). The precondition the eligibility layer
    consults.
  * `reverser_registry()`, `rollback_history()`, `reversibility_report()`,
    `pending_windows()` (flags expired-unreviewed Class C windows the next sweep would
    auto-revert — does not sweep here), and the `rollback_center()` dashboard. All
    read-only; it never reverts or writes.
- `tools/autonomy_eligibility.py` — G2 wire: `evaluate_site` now consults
  `rollback_capability` for a candidate's `target_kind`. A candidate whose target kind
  has no registered reverser is irreversible, so it is not evidence-qualified (a new
  decay reason). The no-candidate path is unchanged (engine-operational → reversible).
  New verdict keys: `rollback_target_kind`, `rollback_capable`.
- `tools/cockpit_console.py` — +4 GET endpoints (`/api/rollback/center|history|
  reversibility|reversers`) + a "Rollback Center" page (dashboard + reverser registry +
  recent history) and a "Reversibility" sub-page, in the Governance nav. Cockpit routes
  124 → 131. No new POST.
- `tests/test_v3_66_127_rollback_center.py` — NEW: rollback always works (round-trip +
  idempotent + reflected in history); review rejection triggers rollback; expired Class C
  flagged then swept; eligibility requires a registered reverser (reversible target
  qualifies, irreversible does not); Rollback Center views; read-only/posture (grep bans
  the CONSTRUCT); wiring (131 routes, no new POST). Route-count tripwire bumped 127 → 131
  across all test files.

Phase G builds the INFRASTRUCTURE for tightly-controlled Class C experimentation
without broadly enabling it. G1 is the eligibility layer. Building it does NOT enable
autonomy: Class C stays Approve-each by default, no per-site grant can be issued, and no
Class C apply path exists — so `participation_eligible` is 0 for every site. The new,
load-bearing safety property is DECAY: qualification is withdrawn automatically as
held-out evidence goes stale. Trust may only ever decrease here.

- `tools/autonomy_eligibility.py` — NEW module (read-only; no module-level I/O), a
  participation-eligibility layer ABOVE the oracle:
  * `evaluate_site(site, ...)` returns two dimensions. `evidence_qualified` = oracle
    Tier ≥ 3 AND held-out evidence ≤ 30d AND not frozen AND no oracle hard-failure AND
    the candidate (if any) is not a permanently-ineligible target — this is what DECAYS.
    `participation_eligible` = `evidence_qualified` AND the per-site Class C gate open
    (grant + level) AND a Class C apply path exists AND no other site in flight — False
    for EVERY site in this build.
  * `apply_path_exists()` → False (first-class; participation is gated on it).
    `can_participate(site)` is the single chokepoint any future apply path must consult.
  * `eligibility_overview()` caps the evidence-qualified "considered" set at 3 ("a small
    number of Tier-3 sites"); `eligibility_status()` for the cockpit header. Descriptors
    by NAME only (inherited from the oracle); no fetch / browser / re-download /
    byte-compare / signed-URL reconstruction / capture-login execution.
- `tools/cockpit_console.py` — +3 GET endpoints (`/api/eligibility/status|overview|
  site`) + an "Eligibility Governance" page (per-site table + decay reasons + a per-site
  detail drilldown) in the Governance nav section. Cockpit routes 124 → 127. No new POST
  (eligibility is evaluation only; the state-change surface is unchanged).
- `tests/test_v3_66_126_eligibility_governance.py` — NEW: stale/unknown-freshness/frozen
  evidence removes qualification (decay); ineligible sites can't participate AND no site
  is participation-eligible even with Class C flipped to auto + fresh Tier-3 evidence;
  every permanently-ineligible action blocks regardless of tier; the considered set is
  capped; the module is read-only and posture-safe (grep bans the CONSTRUCT — `def
  apply(`, `def rollback(`, `hashlib`, `mark_reviewed(` — never a docstring word); wiring
  (127 routes, no new POST, GET 200s). Route-count tripwire bumped 124 → 127 across all
  test files.

## v3.66.124 — 2026-06-02 (Autonomy — Phase E: tiered correctness oracle & eligibility engine)

The final step of AUTONOMY_POLICY_v2: a TIERED descriptor oracle (Tier 0–3) + an
eligibility engine. Determines ELIGIBILITY ONLY — performs no automation. Completing
the oracle does NOT enable Class C auto: C defaults to Approve-each, the per-site
eligibility gate is empty by design (no grant mechanism), and there is no Class C apply
path. Descriptors only — no fetch, no download, no byte-compare; signing by name only.

- `tools/autonomy_oracle.py` — NEW module (no module-level I/O):
  * `oracle_verdict(site, candidate=None, held_out=None)` — tiered verdict (0–3) from
    descriptor availability + cross-capture agreement; `automation_eligible` ALWAYS
    False. Hard failures: no held-out / training-held_out overlap / raw signing value /
    candidate affecting permanently-ineligible targets.
  * `eligibility_matrix()` (per-site tiers; 0 automation-eligible), `class_c_site_eligible`
    (the per-site gate — False for every site; no grant mechanism), `oracle_status`,
    `held_out_evidence_report`, `ineligible_sites_report`, `oracle_reports`.
  * `generate_oracle_reports(by)` — explicitly writes the six artifacts (oracle_verdict
    .json, eligibility_matrix.{json,md}, oracle_report.md, held_out_evidence_report.md,
    ineligible_sites_report.md); operator-invoked, never automatic.
  * Posture: descriptors only; `_has_raw_signing_value` hard-fails value-like tokens;
    PERMANENTLY_INELIGIBLE = pinned actions + credential handling.
- `tools/autonomy_policy.py` — built-guardrails manifest now includes correctness_oracle
  (guardrail set complete). Documented: completeness does NOT enable automation.
- `tools/cockpit_console.py` — +6 GET endpoints (`/api/oracle/status|eligibility|verdict|
  held-out|ineligible|reports`) + an Oracle & Eligibility page (+ verdict, held-out,
  ineligible, reports sub-views) in the Governance nav. Cockpit routes 112 → 118. No
  new POST.
- `tests/test_v3_66_124_oracle_eligibility.py` — NEW: every spec requirement — Tier 0
  blocks; Tier 1 no automation; Tier 2 requires independent held-out; Tier 3 requires
  multiple agreeing held-out; overlap rejected; raw signing values blocked; no network/
  browser/re-download/byte-compare/reconstruction constructs; pinned + credentials
  permanently ineligible; per-site gate False for all (incl. after flipping C to auto);
  no per-site grant mechanism; report generation explicit; no apply/approve/rollback/
  write; Class C auto not enabled by default; wiring (+6 GET = 118; no POST).
- Cross-phase tests (A–D) updated: as of Phase E the guardrail set is complete, so
  set("C","auto") succeeds — the assertions now re-anchor on the durable safety facts
  (default Approve-each; `can_autonomously("C")` False by default; nothing autonomous).
- Route-count tripwires bumped 112 → 118.
- Docs: `docs/oracle_eligibility.md`.

AUTONOMY A–E BUILD COMPLETE: A governance foundation (v3.66.120), B Class B automation
(v3.66.121), C guardrail infrastructure (v3.66.122), D human review experience
(v3.66.123), E tiered oracle & eligibility (v3.66.124). Class C auto remains OFF;
enabling any per-site autonomy is a separate, deliberate, per-site governance decision —
never family-wide, never for the pinned actions.

## v3.66.122 — 2026-06-02 (Autonomy — Phase C: guardrail infrastructure)

Builds the safety apparatus Class C autonomy would require — WITHOUT enabling it.
Headline property: after Phase C the only unbuilt guardrail is the correctness oracle
(Phase E), so Class C auto stays impossible to opt into, and Class C remains at
Approve-each by default. The brakes, rollback, caps, fail-closed review windows, and
self-throttle for a capability that stays off.

- `tools/autonomy_guardrails.py` — NEW module (no module-level I/O):
  * Rollback engine — `record_change` (before/after/diff), `rollback` (via registered
    reverser; restores before-state), `change_record`, `list_changes`,
    `register_reverser`. Fully exercised on a CONFINED staging target
    (`staging_json`); never writes live config or corpus.
  * Backlog + blast-radius caps — `backlog_ok` (BACKLOG_CAP), `blast_radius_ok`
    (one site at a time, MAX_INFLIGHT_SITES=1), `outstanding_unreviewed`,
    `inflight_sites`.
  * FAIL-CLOSED review windows — `register_pending` (Class C gets a deadline),
    `mark_reviewed` (reject ⇒ immediate rollback), `sweep_review_windows`
    (expired-unreviewed Class C auto-reverts; Class B stays provisional).
  * Self-throttle — `throttle_metrics` (rollback/review-expiry rates; oracle-
    disagreement null until Phase E), `self_throttle_check` (breach ⇒ demote C to
    Approve-each, LOWER-ONLY, distinct audit + alert).
  * Guardrail-failure branch — `guardrail_failure` (freeze-and-alert, never proceed);
    rollback/sweep route their own errors through it. In-GUI alerts only (no push).
- `tools/autonomy_policy.py` — `safety_demote` added (authorized automatic
  de-escalation; can ONLY lower a level, never raise; distinct `safety_demote` audit
  action, separate from the human governance edit path the pin guards). Built-

## v3.66.121 — 2026-06-02 (Autonomy — Phase B: Class B automation)

correctness-critical. DEFAULT-OFF — Class B stays at "suggest"; nothing runs
autonomously until the operator opts in, and the kill switch gates every action.

  * Four Class B actions, each kill-switch-checked, with suggest/apply modes, logged,
    and reversible: `reorder_queue` (orders the PLAN queue by readiness/priority),
    `generate_notifications` (in-GUI alerts from current state — NO external push),
    `refresh_dashboard_cache` (regenerable snapshot), `generate_review_packet`
    (read-only pending-review artifact).

    generated notifications, packet, or dashboard cache; idempotent.
  * append-only action log (`housekeeping_log`; the action_logging guardrail);
    `run_housekeeping` dispatcher (no background scheduler in this phase);
    `housekeeping_status`; readers (`list_notifications`, `dashboard_cache`,
    `list_review_packets`). `_guard` checks the kill switch before any action;
    `_auto_or_manual` records whether Class B is opted into auto.

  `action_logging` + `reversibility`, so Class B Level 3 becomes selectable (opt-in).

## v3.66.120 — 2026-06-02 (Autonomy Governance — Phase A foundation)

First implementation step of the approved AUTONOMY_POLICY_v2 design: the governance
MODEL and the safety apparatus, built before any engine. Read-only / record-only —
NO autonomous execution, no Class B automation, no Class C anything. Nothing in this
phase orders queues, mutates templates/selectors/profiles, writes the corpus, retires
debt, launches captures, or runs logins.

- `tools/autonomy_policy.py` — NEW module (no module-level I/O; safe to import on app
  load):
  * 2-D policy MODEL — action classes by **write-target** (A/B/C/D) × involvement
    levels (observe/suggest/approve_each/auto_with_guardrails). `ACTION_CLASSES`,
    `LEVELS`, `CLASS_LEVEL3_GUARDRAILS`, `PINNED_APPROVE_EACH`, `DEFAULT_LEVELS`.
  * Versioned policy STORAGE (computed-on-read safe default; atomic .tmp+replace; runtime
    store root, never shipped) + stable `policy_hash` over levels+thresholds+model.
  * `set_policy_level()` — audited, atomic, versioned; the **code-level hard gate**
    that refuses Level 3 when guardrails are absent / for read-only A / for
    irreversible D; requires an operator identity.
  * Independent **kill switch** (`freeze`/`unfreeze`/`is_frozen`/`freeze_status`) in a
    SEPARATE file from the policy; fails safe when unreadable.
  * Immutable **decision-snapshot** recorder (`record_decision_snapshot` /
    `list_decision_snapshots` / `get_decision_snapshot`) capturing inputs + the policy
    version + hash in effect; id derived from content (identical decisions collide;
    never overwritten).
  * Guardrail **registry** (`guardrail_registry`; Phase A = kill_switch +
    decision_snapshot built) + the enforcement primitive `can_autonomously` (False for
    every class in Phase A; False whenever frozen) + `governance_status`,
    `policy_report`, append-only audit (`read_audit`).
- `tools/cockpit_console.py` — +4 GET endpoints (`/api/policy/matrix|status|audit|

    dropped) and `redact()` reuse on every echoed string.

## v3.66.109 — 2026-06-01 (Band F closed out — Forecasting & Trends, data-gated)

Closes out the last band of the 130-feature cockpit roadmap. Band F is the
data-blocked tail — forecasting / trend / velocity / calibration / sustainability /
correlation — every one of which needs a real time-series to be honest. With only
a few distinct corpus days, projecting would be a slope from a handful of points
(confident-looking, zero predictive validity), which the posture forbids. So Band F
ships as **honest, data-gated scaffolding** rather than fake dashboards:

- `tools/cockpit_core.py` — Band F block: `_distinct_days`, `_history_gate`,
  `_series_by_day`, `_linear_projection` (naive least-squares baseline, no RNG),
  `_gated` envelope, and six panel functions (`forecast_panel`, `trend_panel`,
  `velocity_panel`, `calibration_panel`, `sustainability_panel`,
  `correlation_panel`) + `forecasting_overview`. 25 metrics, mapping every
  data-blocked roadmap feature id. Each COMPUTES its structure but WITHHOLDS output
  (status `insufficient_history`, value `None`) until the corpus crosses the
  threshold (≥14 distinct days for trends/forecasts, ≥21 for cross-site
  correlation, ≥20 logged forecast→outcome pairs for calibration). They populate
  automatically as history accrues. Read-only; NO model or network call anywhere.
- `tools/cockpit_console.py` — one new GET endpoint `/api/forecasting` + a single
  "Forecasting & Trends" page (`PAGES.forecasting`) + nav entry. Follows the v107
  consolidation pattern: one honest page closes the whole band rather than ~25 fake
  pages. Cockpit routes 80 → 81. No new POST surface (read-only).
- `tests/test_v3_66_109_band_f.py` — NEW: gate fires, nothing fabricated while
  gated, every Band F id has a home, six panels, calibration gates on records not
  days, posture-clean (no model/network/writes/RNG), page wired + serves, +1 route.
- Route-count tripwires (v104/v107/v108) bumped 80 → 81 (deliberate).

The 130-feature roadmap is now fully accounted for: Bands A–E shipped/validated,
Band F scaffolded-and-gated. No remaining roadmap work is effort-blocked — only
data-blocked, and now visibly so.

## v3.66.108

Three operator-facing cockpit additions: a top-bar layout option, a read-only
debug log console, and an OPT-IN interactive shell.

- **Layout toggle** — the nav can now sit as a horizontal bar across the top
  instead of the left sidebar; the choice persists (localStorage). Pure
  front-end; collapsible sections work in both layouts.
- **Debug Log Console** (`debug_log`, GET /api/debug-log) — a read-only,
  redacted tail of the application log. Every line passes through redact(); any
  line that still trips posture_scan is withheld entirely. The page has no input
  and runs nothing. Set BD_LOG_FILE to point at the running log.
- **Interactive Shell** (`tools/cockpit_shell.py`, GET/POST /api/shell/*) — an
  opt-in web terminal to the operator's own machine, enabled by explicit operator
  decision. **This is a deliberate departure from the recognition-only posture,
  and it is hard-gated and isolated:**
    * OFF by default. Every entry point refuses (403 / ShellError) unless
      BD_COCKPIT_SHELL=1. Its presence in the route table grants no capability
      while gated off.
    * Lives in its own module that cockpit_core.py NEVER imports — so the
      recognition cockpit's allowlist guarantee (test_v3_66_98) is untouched and
      still proven: the recognition surface still cannot execute arbitrary
      commands and has no shell=True anywhere.
    * PTY-backed real bash; line-mode console (handles cd/pipes/env/git; not
      full-screen TUI). Output is ANSI-stripped for display.
    * Every command is recorded to shell_audit.log.
    * SECURITY: it runs commands as the cockpit OS user. The cockpit MUST be
      bound to localhost/LAN and behind authentication before enabling this — the
      Shell page says so prominently, and refuses to pretend otherwise.
- Cockpit routes 73 -> 80 (debug-log + 6 shell endpoints; shell endpoints refuse
  when gated off). The v98 POST route-shape tripwire now enumerates a third,
  explicitly-labeled "gated_shell" POST category so the recognition contract
  (actions vs inert-state) stays explicit and any other unexpected POST still
  trips it.
- Tests: `test_v3_66_108_console_shell.py` prove the shell is off by default
  (every entry point refuses; endpoint 403), is isolated from core (core never
  imports it, no shell=True in core), runs+audits real commands when enabled, and
  the debug log redacts/withholds leaky lines and cannot execute.

## v3.66.101

Cockpit Wave 3 — composition + ops, completing the 20-feature plan. Seven pages,
all read-only over existing data except the health-checks refresh (which writes
ONLY a snapshot and runs no tool). Recognition-only and human-gated, unchanged.

- **Release Center** — a read-only ready/not-ready preview: debt status, risk
  summary, and a posture scan of recent artifacts, with a conservative verdict.
  It does NOT build and does NOT bump the version; the authoritative regression +
  drift gate remains tools/build_release.py on the host.
- **Executive Summary** — daily / weekly / release / validation / all summaries
  generated from the corpus + CHANGELOG: recent activity by outcome, debt,
  drift, recent releases, and a one-line headline. Generated, never written.
- **Evidence Coverage Heatmap** — a category × outcome grid plus support buckets
  (well-supported = confirmed, weak = partial, untested, open-debt). Read-only
  over the corpus.
- **Resource Utilization** — CPU/RAM/disk via psutil (with a /proc fallback),
  plus active-captures / queue-depth / completed from the cockpit's OWN task
  state — not a system process scan. Read-only: no process is controlled.
- **Knowledge Graph** — the corpus's own resolves-relationship graph (nodes
  typed assumption/finding/validation/drift/debt; edges = resolves), rendered as
  a clickable SVG. Nothing inferred or written.
- **Evidence Diff** — compare two captures or two sites. Capture diff compares
  rendition descriptor SETS and signing-marker NAMES only — raw signing values
  are never compared or shown (posture-safe; paths confined to the captures
  root). Site diff compares corpus-entry sets.
- **Scheduled Health Checks** — read-only refreshes (debt / coverage / risk /
  mission) that recompute dashboards and write a timestamped snapshot atomically.
  No browser, no capture, no corpus/selector/profile change. There is
  intentionally NO always-on in-app scheduler (it would add background work at
  import); to schedule, call it from host cron — the snapshot is the durable
  output.
- New endpoints under `/cockpit/api`: readiness, exec, coverage, resources,
  graph, diff, health-checks (+ health-checks/run POST). Total cockpit routes
  now 39 unique; the only tool-running POSTs remain the three allowlisted
  actions plus queue/launch — the new health-checks/run POST writes a snapshot
  and runs no tool.
- Tests: `test_v3_66_101_cockpit_wave3.py` (23 checks) prove readiness neither
  builds nor bumps, the diff never shows raw signing values (posture-clean),
  resource stats contain no process-control calls, the graph edges are the
  corpus's real resolves pointers, and health-checks/run writes only a snapshot
  (corpus unchanged). The v98 route-shape tripwire was updated for the deliberate
  new refresh POST.

This completes the operator cockpit: 33 features across the plan were requested;

## v3.66.100

Cockpit Wave 2 — the operator-state layer. Adds campaigns, a capture queue, an
operator notebook, a review workbench, and a one-click review packet builder,
backed by a small local JSON state store. The crucial property: **stored state
is inert data — nothing executes from it.** Recognition-only and human-gated,
unchanged.

- **Capture Campaigns** — group captures toward a validation goal
  (n3_validation / player_config / workflow / cross_title_specificity /
  general). Tracks evidence collected, what's still needed, and a recommended
  next capture — advisory only; runs nothing.
- **Capture Queue Manager** — a visual queue (pending / running / completed /
  failed / requires_review) with drag-to-reorder. A queue item is a PLAN:
  adding one runs nothing; launching one routes through the SAME validated,
  allowlisted capture path (start_task → capture_session) one at a time.
- **Operator Notebook** — per-site notes (observation / hypothesis / followup /
  capture_plan), separate from the corpus and never feeding it.
- **Review Workbench** — surfaces corpus-candidate suggestions on disk and queue
  items flagged for review; records an accept/reject/defer decision as data. It
  NEVER applies a decision — writing the corpus, promoting a selector, updating a
  profile remain deliberate, separate human steps outside the cockpit.
- **One-Click Review Packet** — assembles a site's timeline, corpus entries,
  drift history, candidates, and recommended actions from existing artifacts.
  Read-only; packages, does not generate or write.
- **Local state store** — `cockpit_tasks/operator_state.json`, written
  atomically (.tmp + replace) per the project's state-file invariant; degrades
  to empty state on a corrupt load. Every state-write validates its inputs, so
  injection is rejected on the way in.
- New endpoints under `/cockpit/api` (GET to view, POST to write local state):
  campaigns, queue, queue/reorder, queue/state, queue/launch, notes,
  notes/<site>, review, review/decide, packet/<site>. Total cockpit routes now
  33; the only tool-running POSTs remain the three allowlisted actions plus
  queue/launch (which reuses the validated capture path).
- Tests: `test_v3_66_100_cockpit_wave2.py` (24 checks) prove queue items are
  inert (add runs nothing, starts pending), launch routes through the validated
  path, review records-but-never-applies, notes/packets never write the corpus,
  every state-write validates inputs, and the store is atomic. The two earlier
  route-shape tripwires (v98/v99) were updated for the deliberate new state
  POSTs while keeping their guard against any UNEXPECTED future POST.

## v3.66.93

Bug fix (recognition-only drift detection) + test reconciliation. No corpus or
debt change.

- **Fix: v1 template migration masked rendition drift.** `migrate_template`
  recovered each slot's recorded value from `goal["url_template"]`, but that
  field stores the *templated* path (".../{content_id}/{rendition}"), so it
  recorded the placeholder tokens ("{content_id}") as if they were real values
  and, because the role classifier saw a placeholder, mis-roled every slot to
  identity. A migrated v1 template therefore reported `identity_change`/clean on
  a capture the full template correctly flagged as `RENDITION_DRIFT` — i.e. it
  MASKED drift, the exact failure mode `test_v3_66_69 ::
  test_migrated_v1_detects_rendition_drift` guards. Migration now recovers the
  recorded path from the concrete `request_key` (method + query stripped; only
  the PATH read, recognition-only preserved), restoring correct recorded values
  and slot roles. All 16 tests in the rendition-drift file pass.
- **Test reconciliation (stale snapshots, not defects):** two `TestLiveCorpusDebt`
  assertions in `test_v3_66_78_corpus_debt.py` were pinned to the .78-era debt
  shape. The HLS capability gap (VC-0014) has since been resolved by VC-0029
  (verified resolves-pointer), so `test_capability_debt_items_are_capability_gaps`
  now confirms that resolution instead of requiring the closed gap; and
  validation debt has been worked down to exactly the two still-untested axes
  (VC-0017, VC-0018), so `test_validation_debt_is_untested_assertions` asserts
  that exact deliberate state.

## v3.66.89 — offline capture-ingestion tool

A real tool, not documentation: ingest local capture artifacts into the framework's
existing analysis pipeline, fully offline, and emit reviewable reports. It reuses the
existing analysis modules rather than duplicating them, and it never writes the corpus.

- **New `bulk_downloader/capture_ingest` module**: the reusable core. `load_capture`
  reads a `.json` export or a `.wacz` archive (the same loader pattern the other tools
  use); `discover_captures` expands a directory; `normalize_capture` produces a common
  internal model (requests, masked URLs, response/header/initiator presence flags,
  timestamps/seq, redaction state, signing markers by name/type only); `analyze_captures`
  and `analyze_perturbation` dispatch to the existing `goal_skeleton`, `drift_series`, and
  `perturbation_run`. A same-identity series of two or more captures auto-runs the temporal
  harness; a real baseline/perturbed pair runs the perturbation harness on its real path
  (verdict left to the data, never pre-forced).
- **New `tools/offline_capture_analyze.py` CLI**: produces `capture_inventory.md`,
  `offline_analysis.md`, `drift_report.md` (when applicable), `validation_readiness.md`,
  and `corpus_candidate_entry.json` (when applicable). The readiness report labels every
  result as confirmed, possible, unsupported, validation-ready, insufficient, or
  required-next-capture.
- **Posture enforced, not promised**: recognition-only — no fetch, replay, reconstruction,
  or signing computation. Every displayed goal is a masked path template (query dropped,
  path templated), signing is named by marker only, and the temporal harness's boolean
  drift verdicts are surfaced without fingerprints. A runtime `posture_scan` re-checks
  every generated report for an escaped signing value and fails the run closed before
  writing anything. The tool contains neither the forbidden filename nor the
  pass-through-redactor class, so the build posture gate passes.
- **Corpus boundary enforced**: the tool never writes `validation_corpus.jsonl`. A
  suggested entry is emitted only as a reviewable `corpus_candidate_entry.json`, carries no
  `resolves` pointer, has an `untested` or `partial` outcome, and therefore cannot retire
  debt. A dry compatibility check confirms it is schema-shaped and debt-neutral.
- 16 tests covering loading, normalization, analysis reuse, the posture boundary, the
  corpus boundary, and report production. Recognition-only; corpus unchanged at 34 entries.

## v3.66.88 — perturbation-capture harness (VC-0017 / VC-0018 infrastructure)

Fourth and final roadmap item. The fragility map predicts how each assumption
responds to a player_config or workflow perturbation, and those two columns have
never been exercised (VC-0017, VC-0018). This release builds the harness to test
them — and, critically, enforces in code that synthetic perturbations cannot retire
validation debt.

- **New `perturbation_harness`**: `perturbation_run(baseline, perturbed, axis,
  evidence=...)` re-derives the goal skeleton for each capture and checks, per
  fragility kind, whether the observed change matches the predicted response
  (neutral / may_invalidate / likely_invalidates).
- **Enforced synthetic/real boundary**: when `evidence == "synthetic"`,
  `resolves_debt` and `affects_{confidence,sensitivity,corpus_conclusion}` are
  forced `False`; only `evidence == "real"` leaves them pending a genuine outcome.
  A synthetic perturbation is a fabricated what-if and cannot move debt, confidence,
  sensitivity, or any corpus conclusion.
- **Machinery validated, not predictions**: `validate_machinery` runs both synthetic
  perturbations and confirms the harness re-derives, detects per-kind change, maps to
  the prediction, and faithfully reports TENSION when a fabricated change disagrees
  with a prediction (a harness that only ever agreed with itself would be the broken
  one). The tensions are quarantined as synthetic and update nothing.
- **VC-0017 / VC-0018 remain UNTESTED**: the corpus entry carries no `resolves`
  pointer. Missing evidence is named explicitly — a real same-title capture with a
  different player configuration (VC-0017), and a real same-title capture reached by a
  different workflow (VC-0018). Correction and capability debt remain zero; validation
  debt stays at VC-0017 and VC-0018.
- 9 harness tests pass. Corpus 34 entries. Recognition-only.

## v3.66.87 — temporal validation harness; VC-0019 retired on real N=3 data

Third roadmap item: the infrastructure that converts the framework's standing
predictions into tested outcomes over time. This is the evidence engine the
recognition releases were sequenced to enable.

- **New `temporal_harness.drift_series`**: given an ordered same-title capture
  series (N>=2), measures drift on four axes — identity, rendition, signing,
  structural — and checks each standing prediction (identity invariant; renditions
  vary by download choice, not identity; signing per-session; structure stable),
  emitting `confirmed | falsified | untested` per axis. For N>=3 it tests VC-0019
  (does a third same-title session resolve the N=2 "may be coincidental" hedge).
  Builds on the existing `temporal_benchmark` primitives.
- **Recognition-only**: signing values are compared by one-way fingerprint in
  memory for drift detection and never stored, returned, or echoed — only a boolean
  `drifted` per marker leaves the module.
- **Honest measurement**: signing drift is reported `untested` (not falsified) when
  the values were scrubbed at capture time, since drift is then undeterminable. On
  the real ultrafilms N=3 series, identity/rendition/structural drift are confirmed
  and signing is untested-by-redaction; signing drift is separately confirmed on
  nubile, whose `e`/`st` values were present and differed between sessions.
- **VC-0019 retired on real data**: the ultrafilms title1 N=3 series (identity
  `53eb2252` across three independent sessions/renditions) empirically falsifies the
  two-capture-fluke hypothesis, so the floor lifts. Scope recorded precisely: this
  confirms STABILITY (the invariant is reliably constant for this title), NOT
  title-SPECIFICITY (which needs cross-title captures and is a separate question).
- **`debt_report` fix**: `validation_debt` now honors `resolves` the same way
  correction and capability debt do. The corpus is append-only, so a tested
  prediction keeps its original `untested` entry and is retired by a later entry
  that resolves it; without this, a retired validation item lingered as debt
  forever and the report misstated the truth. Surfaced when VC-0019 was retired.
- **Corpus**: VC-0033 records the harness evidence and `resolves` VC-0019 with real
  N=3 data. Correction and capability debt remain zero; validation debt drops to
  VC-0017 and VC-0018. 9 new harness tests + a broad regression pass. Corpus 33
  entries.

## v3.66.86 — short-signing recognition by value shape (VC-0021)

Second item of the signing-recognition sequence; with it, capability debt reaches
zero. Some sites sign with short or unconventional QUERY names (nubile:
`e=<token>&st=<expiry>`) that the name-based marker list does not match. Rather than
enumerate brittle short names, this release recognizes signing by **value-shape
corroboration**: a param whose value VARIES across same-title captures AND is shaped
like signing material (token / jwt / unix_ts) is a candidate signing param,
regardless of name. The two corroborating facts together catch the short names and
structurally exclude content identities, which are invariant across same-title
captures and so never vary.

- **`capture_synth`**: `_value_shape_is_signing` + a `value_shape` branch in
  `_classify_slot` (type `signing_value`, `basis=value_shape`, value masked). Only
  consulted after the name- and value-URL checks, so it never reclassifies what they
  already own.
- **Result**: nubile surfaces `e`/`st` as signing (masked). The rule also incidentally
  recovered bros's `validto` — an unconventional expiry name the marker list missed —
  which a name-based nubile fix would not have, demonstrating the generalization that
  motivated the value-shape choice. Identities and benign short ids (`3`, `12`) are
  correctly not flagged.
- **Corpus**: the fix `resolves` VC-0021. **Capability debt is now zero**; correction
  debt remains zero; validation debt stands at three (VC-0017/18/19), unchanged
  because this release produced no validation evidence. 131 regression tests pass +
  a new discriminator suite. Corpus 32 entries.

---

## v3.66.85 — signing-in-path recognition (VC-0026)

First item of the signing-recognition sequence, the prerequisite for the temporal
harness's signing-drift axis. Signing detection previously inspected query
parameters only; some CDNs sign in the path (site `t`: a
`key=…,s=,end=<expiry>,ip=<addr>` path segment). The candidate-generation change
correctly demoted that segment below the identity floor, but it landed in
`literal_segments` verbatim — a real token and client IP sitting unlabeled. This
release recognizes path-embedded signing, surfaces the markers by name and type,
and masks every value. Recognition-only: nothing is reconstructed, replayed, or
computed.

- **`capture_workbench`**: `_mask_path_signing` + `_kv_pairs` + `_PATH_SIGN_TYPE`.
  Reuses the shared `_SIGN_MARKER` vocabulary (the same regex the netlog classifier
  uses), which already anchors tokens on path boundaries, rather than restating it.
  Once a segment is known-signing, all its `key=value` siblings are named — so
  `s=`/`ip=` are surfaced without adding brittle single-letter markers to the global
  vocabulary (the VC-0021 lesson).
- **Masking and posture**: every value is masked in `literal_segments`, and
  `url_template` is reconstructed from the masked path parts (query-stripped), so no
  signing value survives in any returned field. A `key=value` segment with no
  recognized marker is masked but not asserted to be signing (conservative).
- **Explainability**: a `path_signing` record surfaces each marker as `{name, type}`,
  parallel to the candidate-scoring and goal-selection records.
- **Result**: t surfaces `key`(token)/`s`(opaque)/`end`(expiry)/`ip`(ip-binding) with
  zero raw values anywhere; sites without path-signing are unchanged.
- **Corpus**: the fix `resolves` VC-0026. Capability debt drops to VC-0021 only;
  correction debt remains zero. 8 new tests + 123 regression pass
  (`tests/test_v3_66_85_signing_in_path.py`). Corpus 31 entries.

Closes the last candidate-side residual. `_RENDITION_SIGNAL` now matches a bare
resolution width/height suffix (nubile: `_3840`) from the **known resolution set**
after a `_`/`-`/`x` delimiter, so nubile's resolution-suffixed filename classifies
as a RENDITION rather than a second identity. The known-set gate keeps ids, segment
indices, and years from false-matching.

- **`capture_workbench._RENDITION_SIGNAL`**: adds a delimiter-anchored bare-suffix
  alternative over `{144…7680}`. Precise by construction — `493498581`, `53eb2252`,
  uuids, `segment_00249`, `part_12345`, `clip_2024` all do **not** match.
- **Result:** nubile is now fully correct — one identity (the slug) + one rendition
  (the `_3840` filename). The original VC-0020 is fully closed.
- **Corpus:** the fix `resolves` VC-0028. **Correction debt is now ZERO**; remaining
  debt is capability (VC-0021, VC-0026) and validation (VC-0017/18/19) only. 107
  existing tests pass + 6 new (`tests/test_v3_66_84_rendition_suffix.py`). Corpus 30

First capability item off the clean candidate-generation baseline. Goal-selection
now prefers an HLS/DASH manifest over its segments, so the existing
`classify_url` hls_manifest recognition fires. Recognition-only — the signed
manifest is surfaced, never reassembled.

- **`capture_synth` goal-selection**: `_media_kind` distinguishes manifest
  (.m3u8/.mpd) / segment (.ts/.m4s) / progressive; goal = highest-seq manifest if
  any, else highest-seq media, else last request. Segments stream continuously, so
  the old highest-seq-media rule picked a late segment (→ unknown); the manifest is
  the recognized target.
- **Goal-selection explainability**: a `goal_selection` record (manifest_candidates,
  segment_candidates, n_segment_candidates, selected, reason) — the same visibility
  candidate generation now provides. Candidate URLs are query-stripped (no signing
  values).
- **Result:** bros (manifest captured) → `hls_manifest`, 4 manifest candidates over
  36 segments. Progressive sites (ultrafilms/nubile) unchanged. filthy/evil/df
  captured **no** manifest, so they fall back to highest-seq media — transparently,
  via `goal_selection.manifest_candidates == []`; recovering session-specific signed
  manifests is a separate, larger item.
- **Corpus:** the manifest-preference `resolves` VC-0014; capability debt drops to
  VC-0021 (nubile `e`/`st`) and VC-0026 (signing-in-path). 119 existing tests pass +
  9 new (`tests/test_v3_66_83_hls_manifest_preference.py`). Corpus 29 entries.

The first framework-level candidate-generation change, scoped to the smallest one
that proves the architecture. Replaces the binary admission gate with a confidence
score; retires the candidate_loss and candidate_over_generation classes with one
change. Recognition-only; no downstream changes.

- **`capture_workbench.goal_skeleton`**: the binary `_segment_is_addressable` gate is
  replaced by `_candidate_signals` + `_admit_candidate`. Positive signals (id_shape,
  hex_with_digit, has_digit, **filename_echo**) raise identity confidence; negative
  signals (**signing/`key=value` form**, tiny_numeric, storage_hint) lower it; admit
  above an audit-derived floor (`_CANDIDATE_FLOOR`). The grouping pass
  (`_sharded_run_map`) is retained and now gated on admission. Every promoted slot
  carries `score`, `positive_signals`, `negative_signals` — the same visibility the
  downstream confidence/sensitivity layers provide.
- **Corpus acceptance, no regressions:** nubile slug now admitted via filename_echo
  (**loss retired**); t's six bogus identities → one real id + rendition, signing/
  routing demoted below the floor (**over-generation retired**); bros still collapses
  to one sharded identity; ultrafilms/filthy/evil opaque ids unchanged; all 9 audited
  scaffolding segments stay literal. 145 existing tests pass + 14 new.
- **Corpus:** VC-0027 records the correction and `resolves` VC-0020 (loss) and VC-0025
  (t over-generation) — the candidate-generation classes are closed. VC-0028 tracks
  the remaining nubile rendition-signal residual (`_3840` → bad_candidate_selection,
  tactical). Posture pairing: t's demoted signing now sits in `literal_segments`
  verbatim — VC-0026 (recognize/surface path-signing by name) should mask it.
- Tests: `tests/test_v3_66_82_confidence_admission.py` (14 — scoring unit tests +
  the corpus acceptance criteria as regression tests). Corpus 28 entries.

Single-capture analysis of three new sites. Recognition-only; no model change —
findings recorded, signing surfaced by name (token/IP values never stored).

- **nook** (`nookies.com`): clean. Readable-slug identity `Harper-Hill-MYLK2` promoted
  correctly (it carries a digit, so it passes the addressability gate — the case
  nubile's digitless slug failed).
- **df** (`gammacdn`): clean; third site on the filthy/evil ecosystem, structurally
  consistent (uuid identity, CloudFront signing, `576p` recognized).
- **t** (`ahcdn`): **candidate over-generation (VC-0025) — the third
  candidate-generation failure**, crossing the VC-0024 threshold. Path-embedded
  signing (`key=/s=/end=/ip=` prefix) plus routing/storage segments are promoted as
  six identity slots; only the numeric id is the real content key. Over-generation
  now has TWO mechanisms — hash-sharding (bros, fixed by VC-0016) and
  signing/routing-as-identity (t, new) — so the per-case sharding fix does not
  generalize. Same opaque-token bias as nubile, opposite direction.
- **New capability gap (VC-0026):** signing-in-path is not recognized (signing
  detection is query-only) and is mislabeled as identity — more severe than VC-0021.
- **Recommendation:** the architectural trigger has fired; candidate generation moves
  from recommended to active framework-level work (demote non-identity opaque
  segments on the over-generation side; emit corroborated discards on the loss side;
  shape becomes a confidence input). See THREE_SITE_FINDINGS.md.
- Corpus 26 entries. `by_failure_class`: candidate_over_generation 3, candidate_loss
  1, capability_boundary 3, bad_candidate_selection 3, insufficient_evidence 3.

Turns the corpus from a list of findings into a taxonomy of failure modes — a more
durable planning artifact. Recognition-only; no model behavior changed.

- **`failure_class` axis** (`validation_corpus.py`), five classes:
  `candidate_loss`, `candidate_over_generation`, `bad_candidate_selection`,
  `capability_boundary`, `insufficient_evidence`. `failure_class(entry)` resolves
  explicit-field → id-keyed backfill → None (a confirmation is not a failure).
  id-keyed because VC-0005 (falsified) and VC-0006 (confirmed) share a subject. A
  correction is tagged with the class of failure it addresses, so a finding and its
  fix share a class. Validated against `FAILURE_CLASSES`; added to `_OPTIONAL`.
- **Every correction/anomaly/gap mapped:** bad_candidate_selection (VC-0002/0005/
  0015), candidate_over_generation (VC-0012/0016), capability_boundary (VC-0014/
  0021), insufficient_evidence (VC-0017/0018/0019), candidate_loss (VC-0020).
  `summarize` gains `by_failure_class` + `unclassified_failures` (empty — every
  failure-bearing entry is classified); `debt_report` items now carry
  `failure_class`.
- **Framework-level finding recorded (VC-0024):** *candidate generation is a lossy
  filter upstream of the uncertainty machinery, and candidate loss bypasses every
  downstream safeguard.* Candidate generation has now failed in both directions —
  over-generation (bros) and loss (nubile) — while role/fragility errors sit on the
  visible-candidate side. The durable lesson: a loss defeats the safeguards; a bad
  selection trips them. See FAILURE_TAXONOMY.md.
- Corpus 24 entries. Tests: `tests/test_v3_66_80_failure_taxonomy.py` (13 —
  resolution precedence, id-keyed backfill, shared-subject disambiguation,
  validation, distribution, both-directions finding, framework entry).

Real-data validation across 5 sites / 4 distinct ecosystems (added `evil` and
`nubile`). Recognition-only; no model behavior changed this release — the corpus
records the outcomes and the new debt, leaving the fixes to prioritization.

- **Framework-level held on 5 sites** (VC-0023, strengthens VC-0009/0010/0011):
  `goal_selection` robust on all 5; reusable classes reproduce; signing-opacity
  surfaced across 4 distinct schemes; none reconstructed.
- **`evil` confirms intra-ecosystem consistency** (VC-0022): `evil` and `filthy`
  (both gammacdn) produced structurally identical workbench output.
- **`nubile` reopened correction debt** (VC-0020, falsified/anomaly): its
  readable-slug identity was treated as a path literal (real identity missed) and
  its bare-resolution-suffix filename (`_3840`) was mislabeled as identity
  because `_RENDITION_SIGNAL` matches only `WxH`/`p`. The framework is wrong about
  nubile's roles. Two facets — rendition-suffix (fixable heuristic) and
  readable-slug identity (needs a second title or a slug heuristic).
- **`nubile` signing-name capability gap** (VC-0021): short param names `e`/`st`
  not recognized as signing markers, so no signing scheme was reported for
  nubile. Conservatively incomplete, not a misclassification.
- **Debt now (23 entries):** correction = VC-0020 (reopened); capability =
  VC-0014 (HLS) + VC-0021 (signing names); validation = VC-0017/0018/0019.
  `at_clean_correction_checkpoint: false`. See MULTI_SITE_5_RESULTS.md.

Makes the corpus the primary planning artifact: it now separates the three KINDS
of debt, which are different work. Marks the checkpoint where the framework
transitions from learning-by-correction to evidence-driven capability expansion.
No model behavior changed; this is corpus tooling + the checkpoint.

- **`validation_corpus.debt_report`** + **CLI `validation_corpus.py debt`**.
  - **correction debt** — known WRONG: unresolved falsifications/anomalies. A
    problem is addressed if a later entry `resolves` it OR it carries a shipped
    (non-pending) fix — so VC-0002 (filename, fixed in .69 before the resolves
    mechanism) correctly counts as addressed.
  - **capability debt** — conservatively INCOMPLETE: open capability gaps.
  - **validation debt** — NOT YET CHALLENGED: `untested` assertions.
  Answers the five planning questions and reports
  `at_clean_correction_checkpoint`.
- **`untested` outcome** added (validation debt). Three known-untested assertions
  registered: VC-0017 (player_config perturbation axis), VC-0018 (workflow axis),
  VC-0019 (`n2_floor` more_sessions→resolves) — the fragility axes no capture has
  exercised.
- **Checkpoint reached (corpus = 19 entries):** correction debt NONE (all three
  falsifications/anomalies addressed), capability debt ONE (HLS, VC-0014),
  validation debt THREE, no orphaned evidence — `at_clean_correction_checkpoint:
  true`. See CORPUS_DEBT_REPORT.md. HLS manifest-preference is now framed as the
  first capability expansion driven by accumulated evidence, not the next
  correction.
- Tests: `tests/test_v3_66_78_corpus_debt.py` (12 — categorization, addressed
  logic incl. shipped-fix and resolver-pointer, orphaned-evidence detection,

The second validation→correction loop, and the first applied to a larger
STRUCTURAL error rather than a single rule: the bros over-split (11 identity
slots for one logical id). Recognition-only; posture unchanged.

- **Model change** (`capture_workbench.py`): new `_sharded_run_map` detects CDN
  path-sharding — a run of ≥3 contiguous short (≤4 char) opaque identity-role
  segments — and `goal_skeleton` collapses such a run into ONE sharded-identity
  slot (sample preserves the run, regex matches it, `sharded_segment_count`
  recorded). Keys on the SHAPE of sharding, so it is general, not bros-specific.
- **Observed effect (matched prediction exactly):** bros 11 → 1 identity slot;
  `framework_level` 13 → 3; `path_template` clean
  (`…/hls/{content_id}/video/{rendition}/{path15}`). ultrafilms (8-char id) and
  filthy (36-char uuid) skeletons byte-identical — no regression.
- **Generalized beyond bros:** collapses two synthetic shard schemes (5×3-char,
  5×2-char) sharing no values with bros; does NOT fire on single ids
  (8/16/36-char); respects the ≥3 run floor (a 2-segment run stays split).
- **Corpus.** VC-0016 records the correction with the richer fields — original
  anomaly, root_cause, minimal correction, expected_effect, observed_effect,
  downstream_layers, prediction_matched, generalized — and `resolves` VC-0012.
  New optional correction fields (`root_cause`, `expected_effect`,
  `prediction_matched`, `generalized`) are now part of the schema for every
  future correction. Corpus 16 entries; **pending corrections: none** (both
  corrections resolved; the HLS item remains a tracked capability gap, not a
  correction).
- Tests: `tests/test_v3_66_77_sharded_collapse.py` (9 — collapse, boundaries,
  generalization, real bros, corpus entry/resolution).

The first model change driven by accumulated corpus evidence. The second-title
validation both falsified the rendition perturbation rule (VC-0005) and confirmed
the identity one (VC-0006); this release acts on that, splitting the skeleton
fragility by role. Recognition-only; posture unchanged.

- **Model change** (`capture_workbench.py`): `_assumption_kind` and `_FRAGILITY`
  split the single `skeleton` kind into `skeleton_identity`
  (`different_title → validates`, now validated) and `skeleton_rendition`
  (`different_title → may_invalidate`, corrected — filename is resolution-keyed,
  not title-keyed). `title_invariant`'s survival note updated (its
  `different_title → validates` is now validated by the second title; its
  player_config/workflow axes remain untested). `modeling_dependencies` no longer
  flags the rendition slot's validates rule (it was corrected away).
- **Observed effect** (real ultrafilms drafts): `assume:skeleton:rendition` now
  perturbs `may_invalidate`; `assume:skeleton:content_id` keeps `validates`;
  `modeling_dependencies` flags only `title_invariant` + content_id; goal
  classification still `direct_file`; ultrafilms/filthy output otherwise
  unchanged (no regression).
- **Corpus correction record.** New optional `correction` sub-object with six
  fields — old_assumption / falsifying_evidence / corrected_assumption /
  validation_evidence / downstream_layers / observed_effect — and a `resolves`
  list. VC-0015 records this correction in full and `resolves` VC-0005. Append-only
  preserved: the falsified entry is never edited; resolution is a new entry
  pointing back. `summarize` drops resolved ids from `pending_corrections` and
  surfaces `resolved_corrections`. Corpus now 15 entries; pending corrections
  drop from two to one (only the bros over-split remains — the next item).
- Tests: updated `test_v3_66_60`/`test_v3_66_71` to assert the role-split (the
  old uniform-rule assertions now guard the correction); new
  `tests/test_v3_66_76_fragility_correction.py` (15 — split values, no dead key,
  correction-record schema, resolution mechanics, seed).

Matures the corpus into the primary artifact before any new layer. The two
multi-site findings (bros over-split, HLS classification gap) are evaluated as
validation outcomes and recorded with an explicit conclusion class; neither is
fixed here. A second classification axis lets the corpus report where the
framework was correct, conservative, and wrong. No new model behavior; posture
unchanged.

- **`conclusion_class` axis** on `validation_corpus.py`: framework_level /
  site_specific / anomaly / capability_gap (the four the operator tracks),
  plus model_correction / method_validation so every entry classifies.
  `summarize` adds `confirmed_framework_level`, `confirmed_site_specific`,
  `confirmed_anomalies`, `confirmed_capability_gaps`, and `by_conclusion_class`.
- **Append-only preserved.** `conclusion_class` is an explicit field on new
  entries; the 13 pre-field entries are classified by an explicit, auditable
  backfill map, leaving their JSONL lines immutable. The append-only regression
  test still passes.
- **bros over-split → confirmed anomaly** (VC-0012, `anomaly`, partial). The
  ROLE axis worked (segments correctly called identity); the SEGMENTATION
  granularity is wrong (one CDN-sharded id read as eleven). CDN path-sharding is
  general, so the corrective generalises — a model-granularity issue, not a site
  patch. In `pending_corrections`; owed a fix.
- **HLS classification → confirmed capability gap** (VC-0014, `capability_gap`,
  confirmed). The classifier returned `unknown` on every HLS goal across two
  unrelated ecosystems — never misclassified — confirming `direct_file` is
  correctly site-specific. The repeated `unknown` justifies a recognition-only
  `hls_manifest` classification (recognise, not resolve). Tracked as a capability
  gap, NOT a wrongness — distinct from a correction.
- **Corpus: 14 entries** — 3 framework-level, 1 site-specific, 1 anomaly, 1
  capability gap, 6 method validations, 2 model corrections. Two pending
  corrections (`_FRAGILITY` role-split; bros over-split) and one pending
  capability (HLS recognition) remain tracked, none built. See
  VALIDATION_OUTCOMES_EVALUATION.md.
- Tests: `tests/test_v3_66_75_conclusion_class.py` (11 — backfill, explicit
  field, validation, the four buckets, capability-gap-not-a-correction, seed).
