Mechanizes the multi-site test specified in v3.66.72 (MULTI_SITE_BENCHMARK_SPEC),
now that captures from unrelated ecosystems exist. It builds a workbench per site
and compares the generalization layer's LABELS head-to-head — a test of the
labels the layer already committed to, not a fresh claim. Also lands a small
corpus fix and the accumulated multi-site/temporal outcomes. Recognition-only;
posture unchanged. (`bulk_downloader.multi_site_benchmark` is standalone — not
imported by `app.py`.)

- **`bulk_downloader/multi_site_benchmark.py`** + **`tools/multi_site_benchmark.py`**
  CLI. `site_profile` extracts the comparison fields from one workbench;
  `compare_sites` produces the confusion-style readout — reusable classes
  reproduced on ≥2 sites (confirmed reusable), method properties robust on ALL
  sites (confirmed framework-level), goal-classification outcomes that vary
  (confirmed site-specific, no over-reach), and anomalies (a rule that reproduced
  with wrong granularity). `multi_site_run` builds + compares.
- **Validated on three genuinely unrelated ecosystems** (recognition-only):
  ultrafilms (wowgirls CDN, JWPlayer, expires/token, progressive mp4), filthy
  (gammacdn, CloudFront Key-Pair-Id/Policy/Signature, HLS), bros
  (project1content, videojs, hash/ip/validto, HLS). Result: reusable + framework
  labels HELD across all three; signing-opacity confirmed across 3 distinct
  signing schemes (none reconstructed); `assume:goal_selection` robust on all
  three. Two findings surfaced — bros' CDN-sharded path over-splits into 11
  identity slots (the segment-role rule reproduced but with wrong granularity),
  and no recognition-only HLS-manifest classifier exists (HLS goals classify
  `unknown`). See MULTI_SITE_VALIDATION_RESULTS.md.
- **Corpus:** `validation_corpus.jsonl` grows to 13 entries (VC-0008…VC-0013
  record the multi-site + first real rendition-drift outcomes — 10 confirmed /
  2 falsified / 1 partial). `summarize` fix: `pending_corrections` now includes
  PARTIAL outcomes with a pending model change (a rule that only half-held is
  still owed a fix), not just falsified ones.
- **Posture:** recognition-only; reads recognition-only workbench output, never

- Tests: `tests/test_v3_66_74_multi_site_benchmark.py` (9). Verified end-to-end:

Pivots from validating the framework to ACCUMULATING its validation history. The
workbench has now produced several real validation outcomes (content_id
promotion confirmed, filename promotion falsified → the .69 split, a sensitivity
flag that preceded a real finding); this release makes those accumulate into a
permanent, append-only ledger so the framework's error history and model
improvements are measurable rather than anecdotal. Recognition-only; the corpus
stores prose metadata, never capture bytes or signing values.

- **`bulk_downloader/validation_corpus.py`** + **`tools/validation_corpus.py`** CLI.
- **`validation_corpus.jsonl`** — the ledger (JSONL, append-only, git-diffable),
  seeded with the 7 real events to date and shipped in the zip so it accumulates
  as the tree is carried forward. It is DATA, not consolidated-KB wisdom:
  appending an event is part of doing validation and is allowed in any session,
  distinct from the override-gated KB merge.
- **Schema** per entry: id, date, version, subject, category (assumption /
  confidence_cap / sensitivity_flag / perturbation_rule / drift_verdict),
  basis_kind, prediction, observation, outcome (confirmed / falsified /
  partial), evidence, model_change, notes. `validate_entry` gates every append.
- **`summarize`** answers the failure-accumulation questions directly: what the
  framework has been wrong about, falsification rate by basis_kind, predictive
  confidence caps and sensitivity flags, a perturbation-rule ledger (the SAME
  rule can be confirmed in one role and falsified in another — kept as both),
  shipped model changes, and pending corrections.
- **Immediate findings from the seed:** both falsifications so far are
  `shape_heuristic` (the empirically weakest basis kind); the
  `skeleton different_title→validates` rule reads confirmed=1 (identity) /
  falsified=1 (rendition); and a concrete PENDING correction is surfaced — the
  `_FRAGILITY` skeleton perturbation map still applies `validates` to both roles
  but reality returned `may_invalidate` for rendition (the .69 split fixed the
  slot role, not the perturbation map).
- Tests: `tests/test_v3_66_73_validation_corpus.py` (15 — schema, append-only,
  query, summary semantics, seed integrity/consistency, posture).

Adds the harness for validating the model across DATES (the second-title work
validated it across titles). Same title, same workflow, captured later: it
measures whether the drift verdict taxonomy stays meaningful over time and
whether the confidence/sensitivity conclusions themselves hold up. The harness
is built and tested now so a real later same-title capture becomes a measurement
immediately, not another build session. Recognition-only; posture unchanged.
(`bulk_downloader.temporal_benchmark` is standalone — not imported by `app.py`.)

- **`bulk_downloader/temporal_benchmark.py`** + **`tools/temporal_benchmark.py`** CLI.
- **Churn classification** (`classify_churn`, needs only template + later capture):
  maps the v3.66.69 five-way diff verdict plus a cross-host probe onto the churn
  taxonomy — `signing_churn` (markers changed, shape holds), `rendition_churn`
  (RENDITION_DRIFT: recorded member gone), `cdn_churn` (goal host moved but the
  same path shape exists on another host — re-hosted, not broken),
  `structural_drift` (shape changed), `breakage` (goal host absent and no
  same-shape request anywhere). A same-title run that returns an identity change
  is flagged `identity_change_unexpected` ("verify it's the same title").
- **Second-order transition** (`build_transition`, needs the original pair + the
  later capture): re-runs the workbench on the later capture and reports, per
  assumption, whether it stayed STABLE / WEAKENED / STRENGTHENED / CHANGED_CATEGORY,
  whether each decision's weakest-link confidence moved, and whether a
  weight-contingent ordering became robust (or vice versa) — turning sensitivity
  from a snapshot into a longitudinal claim.
- **Graceful degradation:** diff + churn always run; the transition reports
  PENDING and names the missing baseline (original pair or stored snapshot) when
  it isn't available. A `snapshot` mode dumps the before workbench so a future
  run needs no original captures.
- **Posture:** recognition-only; signing reported by marker NAME only, every
  echoed URL query-stripped, `network_log` read for path SHAPE only.
- Tests: `tests/test_v3_66_72_temporal_benchmark.py` (11 — one per churn
  category, the transition report, graceful degradation, posture). Verified on
  the real title2 WACZ: the harness correctly flags it `identity_change_unexpected`
  (it is a different title, not a temporal recapture).

---

Adds a robustness test over the hand-authored constants and perturbation rules
already in the workbench's dependency graph. The graph STRUCTURE is fixed; the
weights (`_NODE_WEIGHT`, `_STAB` multipliers) and the `_FRAGILITY` perturbation
rules are authored. This layer holds the structure constant, sweeps the authored
choices over it, and reports which orderings survive and which are artifacts.
Built against the filename/rendition case: a conclusion that ranks where it does
only because of a constant — or rests on a perturbation rule reality already
disproved — is flagged plainly. Recognition-only; posture unchanged.
(`capture_workbench`, not imported by `app.py`.)

- **`_sensitivity(draft)`** — recomputes the graph-derived rankings (the flow's
  downstream-weight ordering, which also drives blast radius, and the stability
  verify-first ordering) under the approved sweep, classifying each assumption
  ROBUST (rank unchanged across every regime) or CONTINGENT (a modeling choice
  moves it), naming the regime that flips it.
- **Approved sweep**, over one fixed structural closure: ±1 on each integer node
  weight (independent jitter), all-equal node weighting, rank-reversal/
  adversarial node weighting, and fragility-band reordering on the `_STAB`
  multipliers. No fine magnitude sweep — the all-equal and reversal regimes
  expose contingency more legibly than tuning constants would.
- **Hand-authored-rule flags.** `modeling_dependencies` names conclusions whose
  standing rests on an authored `_FRAGILITY` perturbation prediction
  (`validates`/`resolves`) on an inferred assumption — not an observation — so
  the report says plainly where a conclusion survives only because a rule says
  so.
- **Grounding result:** on the pre-second-title draft, only `assume:goal_selection`
  is robust (rank 1 across all regimes — a structural fact); the skeleton-slot
  orderings (including the rendition slot that fed the half-wrong recommendation)
  are contingent under `±1` node-weight regimes; and the rendition slot's
  `different_title -> validates` rule is flagged as hand-authored — the exact
  rule the second-title capture returned `may_invalidate` for. Sensitivity would
  have flagged that ordering and that rule as untrustworthy before a capture
  disproved them.
- Tests: `tests/test_v3_66_71_sensitivity.py` (8 — sweep coverage, robust vs
  contingent classification, the hand-authored-rule flag, posture).

---

Adds a traceable confidence readout for the decisions the workbench asserts,
derived purely from the stability of the assumptions each decision rests on —
never a standalone number. Built against the filename falsification: a decision
that rests on an inferred shape-heuristic assumption must read CAPPED and
FRAGILE before a capture proves it wrong, not look settled until reality
intervenes. Recognition-only; posture unchanged. (`capture_workbench`, not
imported by `app.py`, so the broad suite is unaffected.)

- **`_decision_confidence(draft, flow, stability)`** — for each decision, walks
  the uncertainty-flow depends-on edges back to the `assume:*` nodes it rests
  on, indexes each into the stability profiles for band + basis + perturbation,
  and reports a band plus the full supporting-assumption trace.
- **Weakest-link aggregation.** A decision's confidence is the stability band of
  its LEAST stable load-bearing assumption — averaging is rejected because it
  hides exactly the kind of fragile dependency the filename case exposed.
- **Band-plus-trace, never the band alone.** Every confidence label ships with
  its supporting assumptions, their stability bands, inferred-vs-observed basis,
  and the `would_invalidate` perturbation, so the derivation is auditable.
- **Decisions scored:** `goal_classification` and `new_provider_required` (via
  the flow graph) and each change-plan recommendation (via an explicit,
  auditable category→assumption map).
- **Grounding result:** on the pre-second-title draft, the
  `additional_capture_recommended` recommendation reads `low-medium`, capped by
  `assume:title_invariant`, with both skeleton slots flagged `inferred` — i.e.
  the layer would have shown that (half-wrong) recommendation as not-settled
  before the capture. Decisions resting on the unverified goal pick cap `low`.
- Tests: `tests/test_v3_66_70_decision_confidence.py` (9 — weakest-link
  semantics, band+trace invariant, goal-selection capping, the grounding case,
  posture).

Hardens the template/capture drift loop after a real second-title capture
falsified a workbench prediction. The second-title validation (content_id
`53eb2252` → `ba7f0af0` while the served rendition silently changed) read
**CLEAN** under v3.66.68 because a permissive filename regex let "the goal
family still exists" pass as "the same goal still holds." The fix corrects the
model and makes the verdict discriminate along the axes the temporal drift
benchmark measures. Recognition-only; posture unchanged.

- **Workbench: addressable segments now split into two roles.** The pre-.69
  model had a single "addressable id" concept and assumed every addressable
  path segment was the per-title identity key. `capture_workbench._segment_role`
  now classifies a segment as `identity` (opaque content key, co-varies with
  title — the detector target) or `rendition` (resolution/quality/fps
  descriptor, constant per title, a download choice). `goal_skeleton` tags each
  slot with its `role`; the uncertainty-flow assume-node, `_impact` capture
  recommendation, and `_uncertainty_plan` weighting are all role-aware, so a
  rendition slot is no longer presented as a per-title identity claim and a
  second title is no longer credited with promoting it.
- **`build_template` freezes role + recorded value per slot.** Each slot now
  carries `role` and the `recorded` path value, so the diff compares
  observed-vs-recorded rather than observed-vs-regex. Recorded values are path
  identifiers, never signing material.
- **`_match_goal` collects the whole matched set.** It no longer returns the
  first shape-matching request (which masked the member change); it reports
  per-slot observed value sets and whether the recorded member is present.
- **Five-way `diff_template` verdict.** `HELD` / `IDENTITY_CHANGE` (different
  title, structure holds — informational, NOT counted as drift) /
  `RENDITION_DRIFT` (same family, recorded member absent — drift) /
  `IDENTITY_AND_RENDITION_CHANGE` (both moved; title informational, rendition
  mismatch called out — drift) / `STRUCTURAL_DRIFT` (host present, shape
  changed) / `MISSING` (host absent). Maps 1:1 onto the churn taxonomy the
  temporal benchmark needs to separate.
- **`migrate_template` upgrades v1 templates with no recapture.** A pre-.69
  template's `role`/`recorded` are re-derived from its own recorded goal URL;
  `diff_template` auto-migrates on read. Existing deployed templates get the
  new discrimination immediately.
- Tests: `tests/test_v3_66_69_rendition_drift.py` (16 — role classifier, slot
  freezing, all five verdicts, matched-set, migration, posture). `.60` workbench
  and `.68` template suites updated to the two-role model and still green.

## v3.66.68 — 2026-05-30 (capture/template loop: template-vs-capture drift mode)

The symbiotic other half of `capture_synth`. Where synth diffs two captures to
find what varies, this diffs ONE fresh capture against a stored *template* — a
frozen set of predictions distilled from a confirmed draft — and reports which
predictions still HELD and which DRIFTED. A template stops being static and
becomes something captures continuously re-validate; a site change (new CDN
host, added path segment, new signing) surfaces as drift before a download
silently breaks. It also closes goal-selection by accumulation: a template can
store a human-confirmed goal pick that future diffs inherit instead of
re-guessing.

- New `bulk_downloader/capture_template.py`:
  - `build_template(draft)` distils the durable predictions (goal
    classification, URL skeleton, slot patterns, signing expectation) plus the
    human-confirmable goal selection (ships `unconfirmed`).
  - `diff_template(template, capture)` runs a fresh capture against the
    template via a structural goal matcher (`_match_goal`) + the real
    `deep_detect.classify_url`, emitting per-prediction HELD/DRIFTED/MISSING, a
    drift verdict, decayed list, and the goal-selection accumulation check.
- New `tools/template.py` CLI: `build CAP_A CAP_B [--out]` and
  `diff TMPL CAP [--json]`.
- POSTURE: recognition-only — classification, URL-shape match, signing-marker
  PRESENCE. Never reconstructs/computes/replays signed material. A leak found
  in testing (the echoed matched URL carried live `expires`/`token` values) was
  fixed: `_safe_url` strips the query from every echoed URL, signing is
  reported by param name only, and the internal query (used for the name check)
  is dropped before the result is returned. Static-guard + no-signing-values
  tests enforce this.
- `tests/test_v3_66_68_capture_template.py`: 11 tests (build distils durable
  predictions, signing recorded as markers-not-values, goal_selection starts
  unconfirmed; clean diff on a source capture; drift on host change / added
  segment / new signing param / slot-pattern change; recognition-only static
  guard; no signing values in diff output).

On the real `ultrafilms.com` pair: a template builds cleanly
(`dd-video.wowgirls.com/{content_id}/{filename}`, direct_file, signing markers
recorded without values), and diffing a source capture against it reports CLEAN
across all five checks with goal selection flagged heuristic-until-confirmed.

## v3.66.67 — 2026-05-30 (workbench: blast radius, generalization, contradiction pass)

Three maintainer-facing dimensions, each pure structure over what the draft
already computes (the first of two planned passes — decision-confidence and
sensitivity analysis are deferred pending a design decision on whether they may
be anything other than transparent functions of stability/weights).

- **Failure blast radius** (`_blast_radius`): the flow graph's downstream
  closure re-presented as cost-of-being-wrong. Per assumption: which findings
  become invalid, which impact conclusions collapse, which recommendations
  change, the node count, and the fraction of the draft to reconsider. Ranked
  by blast weight. On `ultrafilms.com`, `goal_selection` has the largest blast
  (~9% of the draft; collapses three impact nodes and two plan items) —
  pairing with its low stability, that is the real exposure.
- **Generalization risk** (`_generalization`): partitions conclusions into
  directly-reusable (the N=2 fact, the pattern shapes), reusable rule-classes
  whose instances are local (telemetry-is-unrecoverable, signing-marker policy,
  the classify_url rule — recorded once with an instance count), and
  site-specific conclusions (the goal pick, the id values, each telemetry
  param). Classification is by assumption basis kind, not substring matching —
  the honest split is that most conclusions rest on a general method but are
  themselves local.
- **Contradiction detection** (`_contradictions`): a cross-layer consistency
  pass with five concrete checks (stale capture recommendation; ranking
  recommends already-attempted evidence; a param both addressable and
  unrecoverable; classifier-sufficient vs new-provider-required; provider-type
  vs no-provider-change). Reports clean when the layers agree.
- Threading fix: `bodies_state` now flows into `_impact` and `_change_plan`, so
  a body re-capture is no longer recommended when bodies were already retained
  — a real latent inconsistency the contradiction pass would otherwise flag.
  On `ultrafilms.com` the consistency pass now reports no contradictions.
- `tests/test_v3_66_60_capture_workbench.py`: +10 tests across the three
  layers (blast sorted + goal_selection largest + bounded fraction;
  generalization partition + signing-as-class + telemetry-not-inflating-
  framework; contradictions clean-when-consistent + detects both injected
  contradiction classes). 50 total.

## v3.66.66 — 2026-05-30 (workbench: assumption stability)

The last translation-layer dimension: how much to TRUST each assumption,
independent of how much rests on it. Where uncertainty flow gives downstream
weight, stability gives fragility — and crossing the two separates
load-bearing from trustworthy.

- New `capture_workbench._assumption_stability(draft, flow, n_captures)`: a
  per-assumption trust profile with the assumption's basis (`heuristic` /
  `shape_heuristic` / `assumption_untested` / `negative_observation` /
  `structural_limitation`), a stability band, survival across the captures
  examined (with a strength note — e.g. a same-title content-id "held" only
  weakly), a perturbation map (what a different title / more sessions /
  player config / workflow would do: validates / resolves / may_invalidate /
  likely_invalidates / neutral), and local-vs-generalizes scope.
- `verify_first`: ranks assumptions by downstream weight × fragility, so the
  top item is both load-bearing AND fragile. Homogeneous families (e.g. dozens
  of source-unknown telemetry params with an identical profile) collapse into a
  single grouped "triage as a block" row so they do not bury the real risks —
  a fix prompted by the real capture, where 38 telemetry params otherwise
  flooded the list.
- Exposed as `assumption_stability` in `--json` and an "ASSUMPTION STABILITY"
  section in the report (per-assumption detail also collapses large families).
- `tests/test_v3_66_60_capture_workbench.py`: +6 tests (profile per assumption,
  goal_selection low-stability heuristic, source-unknown high-stability
  observation, verify-first crosses weight × fragility, skeleton validated by a
  different title, large family collapsed). 40 total.

On the real `ultrafilms.com` pair: `goal_selection` tops verify-first at risk
36 (weight 12 × heuristic/low-stability) — both the heaviest carrier and the
least trustworthy, fragile to player-config and workflow changes;
`content_id`/`filename` at risk 8 each show `title=validates` (the second-title
capture hardens them); and the 38 telemetry params collapse to one
high-stability block. This completes the layer set: evidence, impact, change
plan, uncertainty ranking, uncertainty flow, and assumption stability.

## v3.66.65 — 2026-05-30 (workbench: uncertainty flow / dependency graph)

Uncertainty as a first-class artifact alongside evidence, impact, change plan,
and ranking: an explicit dependency graph over the workbench's own conclusions,
so a maintainer can point at one assumption and see everything downstream that
rests on it — and which inferred assumption carries the most uncertainty into
findings, impact, and recommendations.

- New `capture_workbench._uncertainty_flow(draft)`: builds typed nodes
  (assumptions, findings, skeleton patterns, impact conclusions, change-plan
  items) and `depends_on` edges, then computes per-node transitive downstream
  closure and a ranking of which inferred assumptions carry the most downstream
  weight (plan=3, impact=2, pattern/finding=1). Each high-carry assumption is
  flagged `capture_resolvable` or not — a high-carry assumption that no capture
  candidate addresses is one to verify by hand, which the evidence ranking
  alone cannot surface. Includes a `what_if` for provenance edges appearing
  (which nodes would change). Exposed as `uncertainty_flow` in `--json` and an
  "UNCERTAINTY FLOW" section in the report; the full graph is queryable per
  node.
- `tests/test_v3_66_60_capture_workbench.py`: +6 tests (graph well-formed,
  goal-selection is a top carrier, carriers sorted, transitive closure reaches
  plan nodes, hand-check flag, provenance what-if). 34 total.

On the real `ultrafilms.com` pair the top uncertainty carrier is
`assume:goal_selection` (downstream weight 12, flagged verify-by-hand): the
entire impact + plan chain rests on the highest-seq-media goal heuristic, and
more captures won't resolve it. The capture-resolvable assumptions
(`content_id`, `filename`, `title_invariant`) sit lower at weight 4 each —
decomposing exactly which nodes made up the second-title capture's ~73%
uncertainty reduction.

## v3.66.64 — 2026-05-30 (workbench: uncertainty-reduction ranking)

The layer on top of the change plan: given that a maintainer can only collect
a little more evidence, which capture buys the most confidence across the whole
draft. Pure derivation over already-computed fields, plus one new honest input
— whether response bodies were ALREADY retained in the captures.

- New `capture_workbench._uncertainty_plan(draft, bodies_state)`: enumerates the
  draft's *uncertain* conclusions (the N=2 confidence floor, shape-inferred
  skeleton slots, the title-invariance assumption, N=2 provenance edges, and —
  only when bodies were not already retained — source-unknown slots), weights
  them by how much each gates the draft's value, and ranks candidate evidence
  collections by the weighted share they would resolve. Each candidate reports
  an estimated reduction %, which conclusions move to observed, which slots
  change category, and which detector-impact conclusions depend on it.
- `build_workbench(synth, *, captures=None)`: optional `captures` lets the
  ranker see body-retention (`_bodies_retained`). When bodies were already on
  and resolved nothing, the "re-capture with bodies" candidate is honestly
  ranked at ~0% with the reason stated — rather than parroted as a generic
  recommendation. Backward compatible (no captures → body state "unknown",
  still ranks). The CLI passes the loaded captures.
- Rendered as "WHERE THE NEXT HOUR PAYS OFF" in the report and `uncertainty`
  in `--json`. The reduction % is documented as a transparent weighted count,
  not a probability.
- `tests/test_v3_66_60_capture_workbench.py`: +5 tests (ranked + sorted,
  bodies-already-on zeroes that candidate, 2nd title outranks bodies when
  bodies on, candidates carry justification, body-state unknown without
  captures). 28 total.

On the real `ultrafilms.com` pair the ranking is: second different title ~73%
(promotes the content-id + filename skeleton slots and the title-invariance to
observed), third session ~27% (lifts the N=2 floor), retained bodies ~0%
(already retained in these captures, resolved nothing — the source-unknown
values are confirmed client-computed). That quantifies and justifies the
intuition that a second title is the highest-leverage next capture.

## v3.66.63 — 2026-05-30 (workbench: prioritized maintainer change plan)

The executive-summary layer on top of evidence + impact: aggregates the
report's findings into a prioritized, maintainer-facing triage answering "what
does this report imply I should do?" — a summary, not code generation.

- New `capture_workbench._change_plan(draft)`: derived purely from
  already-computed fields (impact / skeleton / slots / unrecoverable), it emits
  a priority-sorted list of recommendations, each tagged with one category:
    * `existing_classifier_already_sufficient` — the work-saving negative (no
      new URL rule needed);
    * `detector_configuration_change_likely` — new provider plumbing, or
      extend a known provider's id patterns;
    * `selector_chain_or_workflow_investigation_likely` — reach/login work +
      the live session supplying opaque signing inputs;
    * `additional_capture_recommended` — the specific captures that promote
      inferred conclusions to observed (2nd title / `BD_CAPTURE_BODIES=1` /
      3rd session);
    * `unrecoverable_from_observer_side_evidence` — the scope boundary (do not
      pattern these);
    * `no_action_required` — terminal when nothing actionable surfaces.
  Each rec carries an `action`, a `why` (its evidence basis), and `refs` to the
  real components involved. Rendered as the LEAD section of the CLI report
  ("read this first") and in `--json` as `change_plan`.
- `tests/test_v3_66_60_capture_workbench.py`: +4 tests (category set for a
  generic-bucket goal, priority-sorted invariant, new-provider plan leads with
  the config-change category, plan never empty). 23 total.

On the real `ultrafilms.com` pair the plan reads: (1) selector/workflow
investigation — login/nav + live session for the 11 signing inputs; (2)
additional capture — 2nd title / bodies / 3rd session; (3) existing classifier
sufficient — goal is `direct_file`, no provider rule needed; (4) 38 params
unrecoverable, do not pattern. That is the manual triage the maintainer would
otherwise do by hand.

## v3.66.62 — 2026-05-30 (workbench: evidence trail + detector-impact map)

Extends the workbench from "what it found" toward "what detector change it
implies" — reducing the manual translation between understanding a capture and
understanding the code edit.

- Per-slot **evidence + basis**: every typed slot now carries the concrete
  observations behind its verdict (value differs across captures A/B, matches
  a named shape rule, located in / absent from observable sources) and a
  `basis` of `observed` vs `inferred`. Signing slots NEVER echo the value —
  their evidence is the policy match ("matches signing policy — value
  withheld").
- Per-slot **strengthen** + **affects**: each slot states what additional
  capture would raise its confidence (e.g. `BD_CAPTURE_BODIES=1` may resolve a
  source-unknown value to a provenance edge; a 3rd session confirms an N=2
  edge) and which detector component it maps to (signing → live-session
  workflow, not a rule; provenance → resolver layer; client-computed →
  unrecoverable by any component).
- New **detector-impact map** (`capture_workbench._impact`): calls the REAL
  `deep_detect.classify_url` on the goal URL (lazy import) so the verdict is
  authoritative, then reports whether a new provider is required and which
  components are likely affected, grounded in this tree's actual symbols
  (`SOURCE_TYPES` / `PROVIDERS` / `_PROVIDER_ID_PATTERNS` / `classify_url` /
  `selector_chains`). Key behaviour: a goal that classifies as `direct_file` /
  `*_manifest` / `extensionless_file` is reported as needing **no** new
  provider plumbing — the effort is workflow-reach (login/navigation
  selector_chains + sites_config) plus the live session supplying opaque
  signing params. A provider-like host that is neither a known provider nor a
  bare media file flags the 3-place provider plumbing. Rendered in the CLI
  report and `--json`.
- `tests/test_v3_66_60_capture_workbench.py`: +5 tests (evidence present,
  signing evidence withholds the value, impact grounded + no-new-provider for a
  manifest goal, confidence-capture recommendations, unknown-provider host
  flags new plumbing). 19 total.

Validated on the real `ultrafilms.com` pair: goal correctly classified
`direct_file` (.mp4) → no new provider; effort mapped to selector_chains +
sites_config + live-session signing; the 38 telemetry params shown with
evidence (e.g. a `vb` counter observed as `0`→`1`), confirming they are
client-side and unrecoverable.

## v3.66.61 — 2026-05-30 (workbench: goal URL skeleton; validated on real captures)

Follow-up to v3.66.60's detector workbench, driven by running it against real
drift-heavy `ultrafilms.com` captures.

- New `capture_workbench.goal_skeleton(synth)`: derives the **goal URL
  skeleton** — the actual detector target — from the goal request's
  `url_template`. It splits the PATH into structural literals vs *addressable
  content-identifier* segments and templates the latter (e.g.
  `dd-video.wowgirls.com/{content_id}/{filename}`), emitting a shape-derived
  extraction regex per addressable segment. Signing params stay opaque (they
  live in the query and are already `{slot}` in the template — never
  patterned). This closes the gap the live run exposed: when both captures are
  of the *same title*, the content id is invariant and so never appears as a
  varying slot, leaving the v3.66.60 draft with zero patterns even though the
  id is right there in the URL. The skeleton surfaces it. Rendered in the CLI
  report and the `--json` draft.
- Rationale-accuracy fix: the `rotating_opaque` verdict's explanation no
  longer claims "no identifier shape" — the live data showed many such slots
  DO have id/filename/unix_ts shapes; they are rotating because they are
  source-unknown (telemetry/client-derived), which the text now says
  correctly.
- `tests/test_v3_66_60_capture_workbench.py`: +5 `TestGoalSkeleton` tests
  (addressable-segment templating, signing never patterned, regex+rationale
  present, no-goal -> None, structural words stay literal). 14 total.

Live validation (real `ultrafilms.com` A/B pair, both .57 flag-ON, body
capture on): the workbench correctly classified all 49 varying/credential
slots — 11 signing (opaque, zero patterned), 12 client-computed, 26
rotating/telemetry — and independently reproduced the known 38-unresolved
finding, refusing a pattern for every one. Zero provenance edges (the retained
bodies all arrive after the goal request in sequence — the forward-flow timing
wall, confirmed). The goal skeleton produced the actionable target
`dd-video.wowgirls.com/{content_id}/{filename}` with `expires`/`token` held
opaque. Methodology note for the operator: capture two DIFFERENT titles to
turn the content id into a confirmed varying slot.

## v3.66.60 — 2026-05-30 (detector workbench: synth output → reviewable draft)

Shortens the manual translation between *observing* a site's workflow and
*expressing* it as project-native detector logic. This is the expensive step
when sites drift faster than detector updates: finding the workflow isn't the
bottleneck anymore — hand-converting a capture into a detector is.

- New `bulk_downloader/capture_workbench.py`: a recognition layer on top of
  `capture_synth`. `build_workbench(synth) -> DetectorDraft` promotes synth's
  per-parameter output into a reviewable draft that explains, per slot, a
  *stability verdict* and *why*:
    * `signing` — credential/short-lived; left opaque, supplied by the live
      session, NEVER given an extraction pattern;
    * `provenance_linked` — value carried from an earlier captured response;
      the value rotates but the dependency EDGE is stable (the useful thing
      for a drift-heavy site);
    * `client_computed_suspected` / `rotating_opaque` — no observable source;
      surfaced as unrecoverable-by-observation (must be produced by the live
      session), never patterned;
  plus provenance edges, candidate `deep_detect`-style extraction patterns for
  path-addressable / id-shaped identifiers, per-conclusion confidence, and a
  known-vs-inferred marker with a one-line rationale on every slot.
- New `tools/workbench.py`: CLI that runs synth over two captures of the same
  action (`.json` or `.wacz`), then the workbench, and prints the draft (also
  `--json`). Recognition only — it reads captures and emits a draft detector;
  it never fetches, replays, or reconstructs, and signing material is left
  opaque.
- Posture: the workbench is on the detect-and-surface side of the line. Its
  output terminates at *recognition* ("here is the stable shape, here is a
  candidate detector, here is what's known vs inferred"), never at bytes. A
  static guard test asserts the module contains no HTTP-client/replay/synthesis
  capability, and that draft patterns only ever target identifier shapes.
- Declared out of scope for this increment (deferred): selector-chain emission
  (network synth carries no DOM context — needs an A-T2 DOM capture as input);
  enriching provenance by passing the raw captures in (prefer a response-body
  edge over a weaker page-URL edge); and auto-install of any draft (drafts are
  review material; nothing writes into `deep_detect`).
- `tests/test_v3_66_60_capture_workbench.py`: nine tests on a controlled,
  drift-heavy A/B fixture (rotating id/session/signing-token/expiry/cache-
  buster) exercising every verdict, plus the posture/static guards. Live
  validation against real `ultrafilms.com` captures is the next step.

## v3.66.59 — 2026-05-30 (redactor seam + dev-only raw capture inspection)

Adds a local-troubleshooting affordance to *see* an unredacted capture — and,
in the same change, removes the in-release path that already shipped one,
so the raw capability becomes dev-only.

- New `bulk_downloader/capture_redactor.py`: a redactor *seam*.
  `SessionCapture.record_network` / `set_cookies` now route their scrubbing
  through `active_redactor()`. The release ships exactly one redactor — the
  real `Redactor`, always on — and never swaps it (nothing in the release
  reads any env/config that changes it), so this is byte-for-byte the prior
  redaction behaviour for production. `to_capture_dict` stamps `_UNREDACTED`
  + a warning iff the active redactor is a pass-through (never in the
  release).
- New `bd_dev_inspect.py` — DEV-ONLY, **excluded from every release zip**.
  It is the *only* place the unredacted-capture capability exists. With
  `BD_CAPTURE_RAW=1`, `enable_raw_capture()` installs a pass-through redactor
  into the seam so a capture is stored raw (real URLs/headers/bodies/cookies)
  for local inspection and hand-fixing, with a loud stderr banner and the
  `_UNREDACTED` stamp. It is an inspection view, NOT a reconstruction engine:
  no replay, no stream reassembly, no signed-URL synthesis (those remain out
  of scope, separate decision).
- `tools/capture_session.py`: the `--no-redact` flag is **removed**. It
  previously wrote an unredacted WACZ straight from the release — i.e. the
  raw capability already shipped — which defeats capture-time redaction as a
  guarantee. The CLI now always redacts; raw capture is available only when
  `bd_dev_inspect` is installed alongside (soft-import, inert without it) and
  `BD_CAPTURE_RAW` is set. (The `redact=False` *constructor* arg on
  SessionCapture/DomCapture is unchanged — it remains the ephemeral in-memory
  affordance used by the unit suite, never persisted.)
- Hard guarantees that the capability never ships: `bd_dev_inspect.py` is in
  `dev_suite._MANIFEST_EXCLUDE_NAMES`, and `build_release` now runs a posture
  gate that opens the built zip and fails the build if the forbidden filename
  OR a content marker (`_PassThroughRedactor`, `BD_CAPTURE_RAW`) appears in
  any shipped `.py`. Belt and suspenders.
- `tests/test_v3_66_59_redactor_seam.py`: seam defaults to redacting; raw mode
  (with the dev module) is unredacted + stamped; disable restores redaction;
  the dev module is manifest-excluded while the inert seam ships.
  `test_v3_66_50_at2_dom_capture.py` updated: `--no-redact` is gone and the
  parser rejects it.

Operator note: raw capture ships separately as `bd_dev_inspect_v3_66_59.zip`
(drop `bd_dev_inspect.py` next to `bulk_downloader/`, then
`BD_CAPTURE_RAW=1 python tools/capture_session.py …`). A raw capture contains
your live session credentials — never share, upload, or commit it as a
fixture; strip your own cookies before sending one anywhere.

## v3.66.58 — 2026-05-30 (C-T2: preserve signed-URL provenance in bodies)

Fixes the redactor defect a real ultrafilms capture exposed: when a JSON
response body held a signed media URL (e.g. `streamSources[].file`,
`downloads.4K`), `_redact_json` masked the *entire value* `<scrubbed>` —
taking the non-secret content id, path and `filename=` down with the
signature. Those are exactly the provenance C-T2 traces, and they only ever
live inside such URLs, so wholesale masking guaranteed bodies could never
resolve them.

- New `capture_bodies._redact_signed_or_mask(value)`: a signed media URL now
  keeps its host/path + benign query and has only its signing params
  scrubbed — identical to how a signed URL nested in a query VALUE is already
  handled (`capture_redact.redact_query` / `_redact_nested_value`, v3.66.52).
  The path is not the secret; the signature is, and it is still removed. Used
  in both `_redact_json` branches (dict value, bare string in array).
- Posture guards, applied before keeping anything: a JWT/bare token (no URL
  structure) → full mask; signing markers in the PATH itself → full mask
  (keeping the path would leak them); an HLS segment (`.ts`/`.m4s`, or the
  `key=` + `end=`/`limit=` triple) → full mask even with query-signing, since
  that is the canonical short-lived signed stream the posture never keeps.
  CloudFront / S3 / generic expiring direct-media URLs keep path, scrub
  signing. The stored URL is non-functional (signature gone) and reveals no
  structure not already present elsewhere in the capture.
- `_redact_text` (free-text body path) is deliberately left as full-mask —
  text bodies are unstructured and lower-value, so the conservative choice
  stands there.
- `tests/test_ct2_capture_bodies.py`: all existing `TestNoSigningMaterial
  Survives` adversarial cases still pass (secrets absent); new
  `TestSignedUrlProvenanceSurvives` (4 tests) pins that the id/path/filename
  now SURVIVE for a non-HLS signed media URL while signing is scrubbed, and
  that HLS + path-signed URLs stay fully masked.

Scope note: this broadens what body-tracing can resolve on sites where an
early "sources/config/playlist" JSON carries signed CDN URLs whose path id is
reused by later requests. It does NOT help where the body arrives after its
consumers (the ultrafilms timing wall — every retained body there is after
the analytics/goal requests), where values are client-computed, or for HLS.
Per-site benefit is empirical and needs a real capture to confirm.

## v3.66.57 — 2026-05-30 (C-T2 source half: CDP response-body fetching)

Closes the gap a real ultrafilms capture exposed: the `.55`/`.56` body work
(retain+redact in `record_network`, body search in `_trace_source`) operated
on `response_body`, but the live CDP capture driver never populated it —
`capture_via_cdp` recorded request/response *metadata* from `Network.*`
events and never issued `Network.getResponseBody`, so `response_body` was
`None` on every live capture and `BD_CAPTURE_BODIES` was moot. This adds the
missing *source* half.

- `capture_via_cdp` now builds a CDP body fetcher (`Network.getResponseBody`)
  and threads it through `feed_cdp_event` → `_finalize`. On a normal
  `loadingFinished` (not a redirect/error leg) the body is fetched and passed
  to `record_network`, which redacts it at capture time via the existing
  `redact_body` path.
- Gated by `capture_bodies.should_capture_body(content_type)` =
  `bodies_enabled() AND text/JSON`. The fetch only happens with
  `BD_CAPTURE_BODIES` on AND for a text/JSON content-type, so binary bodies —
  video/font/image, and crucially the signed media streams — are never
  pulled into memory. That is both the perf guard and the posture line: we
  fetch the JSON API responses the operator's own authenticated session
  received, never stream bytes. A signed URL appearing inside a fetched JSON
  body is still scrubbed by `redact_body`'s signing detectors.
- Failure-safe: a fetch that raises (body evicted, CDP error) or returns a
  base64 (binary) body degrades to `None` — the entry is still recorded; a
  capture never crashes because one body couldn't be fetched.
- Default-off / no-fetcher paths are byte-for-byte the prior metadata-only
  capture. `feed_cdp_event` and `_finalize` gained an optional
  `body_fetcher=None`; existing callers and the unit suite are unaffected.
- `tests/test_v3_66_50_at1_session_capture.py`: new `TestCdpResponseBodyFetch`
  (5 tests) drives the finalize path with a mock fetcher and pins flag-on
  fetch+redact, flag-off no-fetch, binary-skip (posture), fetch-failure
  degradation, and the no-fetcher metadata-only path. Live end-to-end fetch
  still needs a stash capture to validate (no real browser in the sandbox).

Note: with this, a fresh capture taken with `BD_CAPTURE_BODIES=1` will
actually retain text/JSON bodies, so `_trace_source` can resolve params whose
values originate in (non-signed) JSON fields. Signed/credential params
(`expires`, `token`, `mu`) stay unresolved by design — their values are
scrubbed in any stored body.

## v3.66.56 — 2026-05-30 (C-T2 body provenance + E-T1 capture-time surfacing)

Completes the value half of the two .54/.55 capture-side features. v3.66.55
made the synthesizer *retain* response bodies; this release makes it *read*
them, and makes the fingerprint risk visible the moment a capture finishes
rather than only inside the stored WACZ. No default behaviour changes — body
provenance is inert unless `BD_CAPTURE_BODIES` is on, and the surfacing only
prints when fingerprinting is actually detected.

### C-T2 body provenance (`capture_synth.py`)

- `_trace_source` now searches prior retained response bodies as a final
  provenance source, after page-context and header sources. A parameter
  value that first appeared in an earlier response body (e.g. an id or
  reference a later media URL embeds) now resolves to
  `response_body:<METHOD host/path>` instead of `source_unknown` — closing
  the ~94 `source_unknown` params C-T1's live validation left open. Without
  this, the bodies v3.66.55 retains had no consumer.
- Bodies are searched only from `prior` entries (the requests preceding the
  one under analysis), so provenance flows forward in time — a value can
  only originate in a response that came before the request using it. The
  new `_body_haystack` helper skips length markers and `<scrubbed>` blobs,
  so the search is a no-op when body capture is off (default) and a
  credential redacted at capture time can never be traced to a body
  (credentials remain surfaced as credential params, never given a benign
  source).
- The `source_unknown` reason string now reflects body-capture state
  honestly (points the operator at `BD_CAPTURE_BODIES`).
- `tests/test_ct1_capture_synth.py`: new `TestBodyProvenance` pins the three
  properties — value resolves to the right prior response with bodies on;
  stays `source_unknown` with bodies off (default path inert); a redacted
  credential in a body is never traceable.

### E-T1 capture-time surfacing (`tools/capture_session.py`)

- After a capture finishes, the operator CLI now prints a one-line
  `WARNING: ...` to stderr when `fingerprint_detection` reports anti-bot /
  fingerprinting presence — so "this site runs DataDome; expect challenges"
  is heard at capture time, not only when the WACZ is later inspected. This
  is the surface half of E-T1's detect-and-surface mandate. ASCII only
  (project no-emoji hygiene); prints nothing when no fingerprinting is
  detected. Exercised end-to-end by the live capture harness on stash.

## v3.66.55 — 2026-05-30 (SigV4 detector widening + E-T1/C-T2 live-path wiring)

Follow-ups to v3.66.54: closes the AWS-SigV4 detector gap that release
surfaced, and wires both capture-side modules into the live capture path
so they are actually reached. No default behaviour changes — body capture
stays opt-in and off by default; fingerprint detection is additive and
read-only.

### SigV4 detector widening (`netlog_classify.py`, `capture_bodies.py`)

- `netlog_classify._SIGN_MARKER` gains a dedicated `x-amz-[a-z-]+=` branch
  so AWS SigV4's hyphenated query params (`X-Amz-Signature=`,
  `X-Amz-Credential=`, `X-Amz-Date=`, …) are detected as signed. The
  general marker branch anchored each token on a boundary char + trailing
  `=`, which the hyphenated form defeats (token preceded by `-`; `x-amz-`
  followed by a word, not `=`) — so every SigV4-signed URL previously read
  as UNSIGNED, i.e. as a pass-through download candidate. That was the
  v3.66.54 finding from the C-T2 adversarial body test.
- The new branch does NOT loosen the general boundary class, so it adds no
  false positives on unrelated hyphenated params (e.g. `cache-bust=`).
- Removed the local `_SIGV4_RE` workaround added to `capture_bodies.py` in
  v3.66.54 — the widened shared detector is now the single source of
  truth, consistent with the no-duplication rule.
- `tests/test_v3_66_34_netlog_classify.py`: 3 SigV4 regression guards
  (full param set signed; signature-param-alone signed; hyphenated non-AWS
  param NOT falsely signed).

### E-T1 / C-T2 live-path wiring (`session_capture.py`)

- C-T2: `record_network` now routes the RESPONSE body through
  `capture_bodies.redact_body` (content-type pulled from the response
  headers via the new `capture_bodies.content_type_of`) instead of always
  marking it. With `BD_CAPTURE_BODIES` unset (default) `redact_body`
  returns the identical length marker, so the live capture path is
  byte-for-byte unchanged unless the operator opts in. Request bodies are
  still always marked (they carry POST credentials; never retained).
- E-T1: `to_capture_dict` now attaches a `fingerprint_detection` field —
  the presence-only anti-bot/fingerprinting risk assessment computed from
  the capture's own response data — so the risk picture travels with every
  capture (and into the WACZ export). Additive; the capture-dict shape
  checks are membership (`k in d`), so the new key is safe. Detect-and-
  surface only — reads what the site returned, emits nothing runnable.
- No import cycle (capture_bodies / fp_detect import nothing from
  session_capture). Verified against all capture-dict consumers (synth,
  recon corpus, dom_capture subclass, wacz export): 296 tests green.

## v3.66.54 — 2026-05-30 (capture-side detection: E-T1 fingerprint detect + C-T2 body slice + P5-2b watch)

Two posture-clean capture-side modules and one diagnostic. All are
detect/record-redact only — no evasion, no replay, no stream reassembly.
Both new modules ship present but NOT yet wired into the live capture
path (same pattern as `honeypot_threshold` at v3.66.36: available,
gated/opt-in, pending a dedicated wiring change). Live-path wiring is a
follow-up so the capture path .52 just fixed is not disturbed here.

### E-T1 — TLS / anti-bot fingerprinting detection (`fp_detect.py`, new)

- Presence-only detector: scans a capture dict's `network_log` for the
  response-side tells an anti-bot vendor leaves behind, and surfaces a
  one-line operator risk note. Reads only what the site already returned
  (vendor cookies/headers, echoed JA3/JA4 hashes, challenge responses);
  it does not sniff handshakes, compute a fingerprint to present, or
  feed any replay path.
- Vendors detected: Cloudflare, Akamai, DataDome, PerimeterX, Imperva
  Incapsula, Kasada, AWS WAF. Matches on header names, Set-Cookie name
  prefixes (so detection survives value redaction), and Server
  substrings. Carries the matched tells as evidence, not just a verdict.
- Confirmed scope: detect-and-surface only; the curl_cffi replay half
  (B-T3 / E-T2) stays posture-declined. A test asserts the summary names
  the risk and contains no evasion verbs (rotate/impersonate/bypass/…).
- `tests/test_et1_fp_detect.py`: 12 tests (both header shapes, cookie
  prefix vs. value redaction, fp-echo headers, challenge detection,
  clean-capture negative, malformed-input robustness, posture guard).

### C-T2 — opt-in response-body slice (`capture_bodies.py`, new)

- Closes the ~94 `source_unknown` params from C-T1's live validation by
  letting the operator opt in to retaining text/JSON response bodies
  (redacted at capture time) so `capture_synth._trace_source` can trace
  a later URL's values back to the body that first carried them.
- Record-redact-export, strictly bounded: gated on `BD_CAPTURE_BODIES`
  (default OFF → byte-for-byte the prior length-marker path); only
  `text/*` and `*json*` content types are ever retained; redaction
  happens at store time, never deferred to export.
- Body redactor reuses the shipped signing detectors
  (`capture_redact.SENSITIVE_QS_KEY` for keys, `netlog_classify._is_signed`
  for signed-URL values, JWT/long-token shape rules for value shapes). A
  value is masked when its key looks sensitive OR its value looks
  signed — the two-sided rule is the point, since bodies hide signing
  material under benign key names.
- Found + locally handled a real gap: `netlog_classify._is_signed`'s
  regex anchors each marker on a boundary char + trailing `=`, so AWS
  SigV4's hyphenated `X-Amz-Signature=` reads as UNSIGNED to it. The body
  redactor carries a narrow local SigV4 check; widening the shared
  detector (touches netlog + synth) is a tracked follow-up, not folded
  into this feature.
- HLS playlists (`mpegurl`) are deliberately treated as ineligible and
  reduced to a length marker — a manifest of signed segment URLs is
  exactly what should not sit on disk. Known, intentional limitation.
- `tests/test_ct2_capture_bodies.py`: 16 tests led by an ADVERSARIAL
  "no signing material survives" suite that buries JWTs, signed
  CloudFront/S3 URLs, and HLS key/end/limit segments under innocent
  field names. Flag handled per-test (not via an autouse env fixture —
  a known-fragile custom-runner shim corner, per the .52 lesson).

### P5-2b — accuracy-watch diagnostic (`tools/p5_2b_accuracy_watch.py`, new)

- Read-only watch: compares the per-site learned honeypot drop threshold
  against the global rule on real `history.honeypot_score` data, reusing
  the shipped `honeypot_threshold` functions (no reimplementation, so it
  can't drift from the runner). Buckets sites FIRED / ABSTAINED / NO-DATA
  so an abstention is never misread as agreement, and for FIRED sites
  counts whether the learned threshold would change any real decisions.
- Runs on stash (needs the live DB); degrades cleanly to an INCONCLUSIVE
  verdict on an empty/un-migrated DB rather than throwing.

## v3.66.53 — 2026-05-30 (test-infra: live-capture lifecycle + two skip removals)

Test-infrastructure only — no product code changed. Takes the full
custom-runner suite on Linux to 0 failed / 0 skipped.

- `test_extension_live.py` (live Playwright MV3 extension E2E): replaced
  the `_setup_done`/`_teardown_done` two-flag scheme with a single
  `_live` flag — set in `setup_method`, cleared in `teardown_method`. The
  project's `run_tests.py` reuses ONE instance per class and calls
  setup/teardown once per test; the old scheme set the session up before
  the first test but tore it down after it, so tests 2+ ran against a
  stopped Playwright session ("Event loop is closed") and a closed
  harness ("Connection refused"). The `_live` flag restores the file's
  intended per-test boot under the shared-instance runner while still
  absorbing pytest's setup_method+setUp / teardown_method+tearDown
  double-fire. Reproduced both failures in-sandbox with the old file and
  confirmed the fix clears them (7/7). No product code involved.
- `test_v3_43_78_static_analysis_fixes.py`: `test_v3_43_71_emoji_free`
  could only ever skip in a release tree — its subject moved to the
  KB-only `CHANGELOG_archive.md` (v3.66.30 packaging policy). Re-scoped to
  `test_current_release_emoji_free`, which asserts the topmost (current)
  CHANGELOG entry is emoji-free — the rule applied to the entry that
  actually ships. The historical range stays covered by
  `test_post_roadmap_releases_emoji_free`.
- `test_v3_66_14_phase3_p7_confidence.py`:
  `test_confidence_ordering_matches_score_ordering` skipped on a
  single-candidate input. Switched to the HLS master input (two variants,
  distinct bandwidths → distinct scores) and made `≥2 candidates` a hard
  assertion, so the score/confidence rank-equivalence is actually
  exercised.

## v3.66.52 — 2026-05-30 (C-T1 validated; live-capture-leg + installer fixes)

Capture-synthesis C-T1 (static 2-capture → minimal recipe) extended and
validated end-to-end on real authenticated traffic. Detect-and-surface-risk
posture unchanged: redact + diff + classify only, no replay/reconstruction.

Capture-synthesis (`capture_synth.py`):
- Path-segment id recovery: requests whose per-item id sits in the URL path
  (different request keys across captures) are re-paired when their paths
  match modulo exactly one non-empty segment (`_single_path_seg_diff`
  guards against false pairings).
- Wider static dataflow: a non-credential param value is now traced to the
  referrer, meta tags, player-element attributes, inline script config, and
  `js_globals` — not only the entry URL. Credential fields excluded.
- Credential-by-key hardening: a query param whose key matches the signing
  set (token/sig/signature/policy/expires/key-pair-id/…) is slotted as a
  masked credential even when an under-scrubbed capture left its value in
  cleartext.

Redaction (`capture_redact.py`):
- `redact_query` recurses into a URL-encoded signed URL nested inside a
  param value (keeps host/path, redacts inner signing params; depth-capped).
- `scrub_headers` redacts URL-shaped values of non-sensitive headers.
- Re-scrubbed the six `recon_corpus` fixtures (removed cleartext CloudFront
  signing material that had been committed).

Live-capture leg (fixes — were silently breaking ALL live capture):
- `session_capture.capture_via_cdp` registered CDP listeners under the
  prefix-stripped event name (`requestWillBeSent`) instead of the full
  `Network.requestWillBeSent` Playwright emits, so no events were recorded
  and captures wrote an empty `network_log`. Now registers under the full
  names; added `TestCdpLiveWiring` (fake CDP client driving a request
  end-to-end into `network_log`).
- `tools/capture_session.py` gained the repo-root `sys.path` bootstrap it
  was missing (`ModuleNotFoundError` when run from the repo root).

Installers / frontend:
- TS2688 (`Cannot find type definition file for testing-library__jest-dom`):
  `frontend/tsconfig.json` sets `"types": []` and `tsconfig.node.json`
  `"types": ["node"]`, constraining the `@types` auto-scan;
  `install_linux.sh` clears a stale `tsbuildinfo` + the deprecated DT stub
  before `npm run build`.
- `install_service.sh` / `install_ai_ollama.sh`: fixed-path `/tmp/*.err`
  redirects replaced with `mktemp` (kills the root-owned-stale-file EACCES
  class).
- `install_ai_ollama.sh`: Ollama install verified by binary presence rather
  than the official installer's exit code (non-zero on the benign "group
  ollama exists"); writes `ollama.service` itself when the official
  installer skipped it.

Test runner (`run_tests.py`):
- The pytest-shim `raises(...)` context manager now exposes
  `.value`/`.type`/`.traceback` like pytest's `ExceptionInfo`, so tests that
  inspect the raised exception (`str(excinfo.value)`) pass under the shim
  instead of raising `AttributeError: 'Ctx' object has no attribute 'value'`.
- `_MonkeyPatch` gained `setitem`/`delitem` (dict-item set with restore/pop
  on undo), fixing `AttributeError: '_MonkeyPatch' object has no attribute
  'setitem'`. Together these close 17 harness-only failures surfaced by the
  full custom-runner suite on Linux (phase-4 SSRF-hardening/rebinding + pwmgr
  remainder); the underlying product code was already correct.

Capture-synthesis track, NOW tier. Detect-and-surface-risk posture:

## v3.66.50 — 2026-05-29 (F3 DOM-visibility full + F11 duplicate-field module)

Detect-side, posture-clean. Closes the last Tier-1 detect item (F3) and
the Tier-5 extraction (F11). Survey-before-spec (L18) confirmed F5 / F6 /
F8 / F12 already shipped in v3.66.44 — not rebuilt.

- **F3** — DOM-visibility honeypot filter, full version (extends the
  v3.66.28 P5-3 base):

    `transform:translatex/y(-9999px|-10000px)`, `transform:scale(0)`,
    `clip-path:circle(0)` (whitespace-stripped/lowercased to match the

## v3.66.49 — 2026-05-29 (F1 codec scoring + F2 challenge/trap-URL vocab)

### Added
- F1: codec-quality tie-breaker scoring. New `CODEC_TIERS` +
  `detect_codec_tier()` in heuristic_scoring, and parallel
  `codec_score()` / `codec_label()` + `_CODEC_PATTERNS` in detect.
  Ranking: remux/source = AV1 (4) > HEVC (3) > VP9 (2) > H.264 (1).
  Wired into `score_text_signals` as a small additive bonus. The max
  bonus (4) is strictly below the smallest resolution-tier gap among
  real download tiers (720p+, gap 5), so codec breaks ties WITHIN a
  resolution but can never override the resolution ranking — the
  load-bearing F1 caveat. The 8K/6K/5K resolution vocab was already
  complete in RESOLUTION_TIERS / _RES_LABEL_PATTERNS (INV-005); F1's
  resolution half required no change, only the codec table.
- F2 (R-P5-2 vocab extension): two new honeypot_score pre-fetch rules.
  - `trap_url_term` (0.70): a candidate path routing through a
    redirect/interstitial term (TRAP_URL_TERMS: /click, /clk, /go,
    /out, /redirect, /tracking, /interstitial, /popup). Scored below
    the drop threshold so a lone match downscores, never drops.
  - `brand_trap_term` (0.55): brand-workflow terms (BRAND_TRAP_TERMS:
    affiliate, sponsor, offer, survey, verify, captcha, subscribe,
    premium, checkout). WEAK signal — sits in the downscore band only,
    so a legitimate "Subscribe to get download" / membership flow is
    kept (deprioritised), never dropped. This is the load-bearing F2
    caveat.
- New exported frozensets `TRAP_URL_TERMS` and `BRAND_TRAP_TERMS` in
  honeypot_score.

### Changed
- deep_detect `SUSPICIOUS_URL_PATTERNS` gains the redirect infixes
  `/clk?` and `/tracking?` (existing terms intact). Challenge-vendor
  vocab (DataDome / PerimeterX / Kasada / Akamai / Imperva / Incapsula
  / Cloudflare) was already complete in `BOT_DEFENSE_MARKERS`; F2's
  challenge half required no change — verified by test.

### Tests
- `tests/test_v3_66_49_f1_codec_res.py` (22): codec ranking in both
  modules, high-res vocab guard, and the codec-never-overrides-
  resolution caveat via the full score_text_signals path.
- `tests/test_v3_66_49_f2_trap_vocab.py` (22): trap_url_term +
  brand_trap_term firing, the downscore-not-drop caveat, MAX-combine
  with a real drop-tier rule, deep_detect vocab presence, no tier
  overlap.

### Notes
- Detect-side only; posture-clean (no evade/replay/fingerprint).
- No INV-005-tagged line modified; codec scoring is a separate additive
  signal, not part of the resolution parallel-table invariant.
- Ad-network domains (revcontent, mgid, outbrain, taboola) were already
  present in `KNOWN_TRACKER_HOSTS` — F2 "verify" item confirmed, no add.

## v3.66.48 — 2026-05-29 (C4-B player-js cipher + C2 signing_callback + P5-2b wire)

### Added
- C4-B: in-process player-JS YouTube signatureCipher decipher backend
  (BD_YOUTUBE_CIPHER=player-js). Functionally equivalent to the yt-dlp
  backend but requires no external binary; solves signature obfuscation
  only (no DRM/paywall/age-gate), distinct source_type
  youtube_resolved_cipher_playerjs, fails loud on cipher rotation.
  Built under an explicit operator posture-override (non-precedent).
- C2: per-site JWPlayer signing_callback wiring via
  provider_resolve.build_signing_callback(config) + signing_callback param
  on deep_detect/deep_detect_live, attached to jwplayer embeds at resolve
  time. Reachable in production when a site sets resolve_providers=True
  (see Changed); off by default.

### Changed
- P5-2b: resolve-time honeypot score is now stamped onto the completion
  history row (resolve->runner->db_log), so honeypot_threshold per-site
  learning has real data to read. Only populated via the deep_detect
  fallback path; the common find_best_download path is unchanged.
- Provider resolution is now operator-controllable per site via the
  `resolve_providers` config flag (default OFF). When enabled, the
  runner's live deep_detect fallback resolves provider embeds — which
  is what activates C4-B (YouTube signatureCipher decipher), C2
  (JWPlayer signing_callback, built from the same per-site config), and
  the P5-2b honeypot-score wire. The runner builds the `(url) ->
  (status, headers, body)` http_get adapter the resolvers require and
  emits a one-time stderr WARNING on enable (outbound third-party
  requests + the cipher decipher; signature obfuscation only, no
  DRM/paywall/age-gate bypass). Default OFF preserves pre-v3.66.48
  behaviour exactly.

## v3.66.47 — 2026-05-29 (debug-session fixes — cross-platform encoding + atomic write)

A systematic audit of the v3.66.46 tree. Honest result: a 6400-test-green,
linted codebase yielded **5 real defects** (not the thousands a naive count
would manufacture). All fixed; most are cross-platform (Linux-default UTF-8
hid them; they bite on the still-shipped Windows path).

- push.py: `read_text()` of the VAPID JSON without `encoding=` (non-ASCII → crash
  on non-UTF8 default platform). Fixed; added encoding to the sibling write too.
- app.py `_save_global_notify_settings`: now writes via tmp + `os.replace` so a
  crash mid-write can't corrupt the apprise settings file (atomic-write rule).
- Subprocess `text=True` without `encoding=` on the unicode-bearing call sites —
  runner.py (yt-dlp filename parse), enrichment.py, thumbnail_gen.py ×3 (ffmpeg).
  Linux works today; Windows cp1252 would mangle non-ASCII filenames. Pinned to utf-8.
- Removed a dead line introduced in v3.66.46's fingerprint observer.

Sweeps that came back clean (recorded for the audit trail): bare except,
mutable defaults, `==None`, module-level import work, SQLite time mixing,
open() leaks, lock+DB pattern, f-string prefixes, flat-key migration residue.

## v3.66.46 — 2026-05-29 (F9 detect-side bot-defense detector + mid-process session resilience)

Two detect-side features. Posture unchanged — both report/recover, neither evades.

- **Bot-defense / fingerprinting detector (F9 detect-side).** scan_blockers
  now emits `bot_defense_systems` (named vendors — Cloudflare, DataDome,
  PerimeterX/HUMAN, Akamai Bot Manager, Kasada, Imperva/Incapsula, Arkose,
  reCAPTCHA, hCaptcha) grouped from the raw markers, and `fingerprinting`
  (canvas/webgl/webdriver_probe/audio signals from inline scripts), with an
  operator warning. A live, config-gated (`detect_fingerprinting`, off by
  default) observer records which fingerprinting APIs the page actually
  INVOKES at runtime and logs `fingerprint_observed`. Record-only: it wraps
  the getters to set a flag and calls through to the original — return
  values are unchanged. No spoofing, no evadability scoring.
- **Mid-process session resilience.** Broadened `_check_redirect` auth
  detection: wider login-path hints (/account/login, /users/sign_in,
  /log-in, …) plus an in-place login-wall body check (`AUTH_BODY_RE` —
  password-input / "session expired" / "log in to continue", tuned to
  ignore logged-in nav). A session that dies mid-process now routes through
  the existing relogin + re-queue + re-press path instead of failing as
  "no download button found". No new re-drive code — reuses
  `_handle_auth_required`'s capped retry accounting.

Known-open bundle items (re-derived against v3.66.42 source):

- **B5** `secrets_store.migrate_from_plaintext`: roll back the backend
  `set()` when the roundtrip-verify fails, so a password is never left
  in BOTH the encrypted backend and plaintext config (was doubling the
  attack surface the migration meant to halve).
- **B6** `secrets_store.MasterPasswordBackend.unlock`: clear `self._key`
  on a failed verify so a wrong password after a good unlock actually
  leaves the backend locked (was leaving it unlocked under the prior key).

  row access through a `{lowercased: original}` header map so Title-cased

  instead of `uris[0]` (mobile-first entries lead with androidapp://).
- **B9** `extension_vault.revoke_by_prefix`: reject prefixes < 4 chars
  (`startswith("")` matched any token).
- **B10** `extension_vault.validate_vault_token`: coalesce the

  on every authenticated request.
- **B11** `secrets_store.find_plaintext_passwords` / `migrate_from_plaintext`:
  walk `accounts[]` so multi-account sites don't report
  `remaining_plaintext: 0` while per-account passwords sit in the clear.
  Adds `account_password_key`, `make_account_password_reference`,
  `_split_account_scope`.
- **B14** `app.api_secrets_import_apply`: slug standalone imports by
  name+username with a per-batch counter (two same-named entries no

- **B15** `app.api_secrets_change_password`: probe the old password

  on `site_id` delete (narrow: only when the value exactly equals the

- **B19** `vpn_config._validate_tunnel_dict`: reject empty or `:`-bearing

to 0600, but the more sensitive files were written at the umask default

## v3.66.41 — 2026-05-28 (SECURITY — pwmgr/vault audit follow-ups AF1–AF4)

Source-audit findings on the pwmgr/vault/auth surface, in the same defect
families as the LIVE v3.65.2 bundle (these are audit findings, not the
bundle's B-numbers — the B6–B19 spec isn't in the KB). Pinned by
`tests/test_v3_66_41_pwmgr_audit_followups.py`.

- **AF1 — non-constant-time auth-token comparison (app.py).** The
  BD_AUTH_TOKEN bearer and X-BD-Token were compared with `==`, leaking
  length/prefix via timing on the primary auth secret (the CSRF check
  already used `secrets.compare_digest`). New `_token_eq` helper does a
  constant-time compare and treats non-ASCII input as a non-match.
- **AF2 — malformed secrets.json silently wiped (secrets_store).**
  `_load_or_init` reinitialized to an empty vault on a parse error; the
  next `set()` then overwrote the file, destroying recoverable data. Now
  moves the unparseable file aside to `secrets.json.corrupt-<hex>` before
  reinit.
- **AF3 — phantom revocation (extension_vault).** `_save_tokens` swallowed
  write failures, so `revoke_vault_token` / `revoke_by_prefix` could return
  True while the deletion never persisted (a "revoked" token still valid
  after restart). `_save_tokens` now returns `bool`; revoke reports False
  when the save didn't stick.
- **AF4 — malformed vault_tokens.json silently wiped (extension_vault).**
  Same class as AF2 for the token store (would drop every paired
  extension). Now backs the file up to `vault_tokens.json.corrupt-<ts>`
  before reinit.

## v3.66.40 — 2026-05-28 (SECURITY — B3 audit-log redaction + B20 IDN normalization)

- **B3 — audit-log sanitization (audit.py).** `_redact`'s secret set
  predated the password manager and missed `vault_token` / `pairing_token`
  / `csrf_token` / `cookies` / `master_password` etc., so those landed in
  the audit `before`/`after` columns in plaintext. Redaction now also
  matches by key-name SUBSTRING (`_SECRET_KEY_MARKERS`: password, secret,
  token, api_key, cookie, credential, private_key, vault), so any
  sensitive field is stripped even if not explicitly enumerated.
  Over-redaction is the safe direction for a security log.
- **B20 — IDN/Punycode normalization (extension_vault.get_hostname).**
  Hostnames are now normalized to their ASCII punycode form before
  autofill matching, so a homograph host (e.g. a Cyrillic-"a"
  "exаmple.com") can't be confused with or impersonate an ASCII host and
  harvest its saved password. All-ASCII hosts are byte-identical; malformed
  IDN falls back to the raw host without raising. Sits in front of the B1
  `_host_suffixes` matcher.

Pinned by `tests/test_v3_66_40_audit_idn_hardening.py`. Remaining pwmgr
bundle items still open in OPEN_THREADS 0 (no recorded fix shapes in the
KB — need the v3.65.2 handoff): B6–B11 / B14–B16 / B19.

## v3.66.38 — 2026-05-28 (SECURITY — pwmgr hardening: B1/B12/B4/B13/B17/B18)

Re-derived against v3.66.34+ source from the never-shipped v3.65.2
password-manager hardening bundle. Closes the five LIVE-exploitable bugs;
each fix carries a content-level attack/failure pinning test
(`tests/test_v3_66_38_pwmgr_hardening.py`).

- **B1 — autofill phishing (extension_vault.entries_matching_origin).**
  Patterns were matched with `re.search` over the full URL, so an attacker
  page whose URL merely *contained* a saved host as a substring
  (`https://attacker.com/?next=login.example.com`) was offered the saved
  password. Now matches each pattern via `re.fullmatch` against the
  dot-bounded suffixes of the request hostname (new `_host_suffixes`
  helper). `fullmatch` (not `match`) also rejects `example.com.attacker.com`.
  Subdomain/parent-domain matches preserved.
- **B12 — vault-token privilege amplification (app.py).** The global auth
  gate opened the entire `/api/secrets/extension/*` prefix to any Bearer,
  so a leaked vault token could reach `pair_issue` / `list_paired` /
  `revoke`. Narrowed the gate to an explicit read-only data-route
  allowlist (`_EXT_VAULT_DATA_ROUTES`: list_for_origin, fetch_one, ping);
  added a defense-in-depth `_reject_if_vault_token()` guard on the three
  management handlers (403 if authenticated by a vault token, regardless of
  global-auth config). Legit session+CSRF / BD_AUTH_TOKEN callers unaffected.
- **B4/B17 — silent password loss (secrets_store.MasterPasswordBackend).**
  `_save()` now returns `bool` and cleans up its `.tmp` on failure;
  `set()` / `delete()` roll back the in-memory mutation and raise
  `SecretsPersistError` on a failed persist instead of reporting success.
- **B13 — migration phantom success.** Because `set()` now raises on a
  failed persist, `migrate_from_plaintext` records a real error and keeps
  the plaintext instead of replacing it with a `@cred:` reference that the
  next restart would resolve to nothing.
- **B17/B18 — change_password atomicity.** Rotation is now all-or-nothing:
  any undecryptable entry aborts before mutation (no silent drop); the new
  key is derived from a fresh salt without pre-mutating state; the swap is
  rolled back fully and raises on persist failure. All mutations + the
  in-memory reads they race with run under a per-instance `RLock`
  (`is_unlocked()` stays lock-free).

Still unshipped from the bundle (correctness, not LIVE-exploitable): B2
manifest excludes for secrets.json/vault_tokens.json/secrets_meta.json, B3
audit-log sanitization, B20 IDN/Punycode normalization, and the
B5–B11/B14–B16/B19 set. Tracked in OPEN_THREADS item 0.

## v3.66.36 — 2026-05-28 (P5-2b per-site honeypot threshold learning)

**Feature core + ready persistence (opt-in, default off).** Follow-up to
R-P5-2. Lets the honeypot drop threshold be learned per-site from the
site's own confirmed traps instead of one global number.

New module `bulk_downloader/honeypot_threshold.py`:

- `learn_threshold(trap_scores, *, default, …)` — the one knob. Returns
  the `default` (unchanged) below `min_samples=5` confirmed traps;
  otherwise the 10th-percentile of trap scores, clamped to `[0.5, 0.95]`.
  No model file, no training pipeline.
- `trap_scores_for_site()` — collects persisted `honeypot_score` values
  for a site's confirmed traps (`find_tinies` semantics + non-NULL score).
  Degrades to `[]` on a missing column / no DB, so it can never break or
  tighten anything without real data.
- `learned_drop_threshold(site_id, *, default)` — collector → learner.

Persistence (additive, byte-compatible):

- `history.honeypot_score REAL DEFAULT NULL` added to the base CREATE and
  via migration **v7** (`add_history_honeypot_score`, idempotent
  PRAGMA-checked ALTER for existing DBs).
- `db.db_log()` gains a trailing optional `honeypot_score=None` kwarg.
  Existing callers are unaffected; the column stays NULL until stamped.

Seam (`provider_resolve`):

- `_honeypot_drop_threshold(site_id=None)` and an additive
  `resolve_provider_embed(..., site_id=None)` kwarg. When
  `BD_HONEYPOT_PER_SITE=1` **and** the global threshold is active **and** a
  site_id is supplied, the global value is replaced by the per-site
  learned value; otherwise behaviour is identical to v3.66.35.

Scope note: the learner, collector, additive schema and seam are complete
and tested. The remaining hop to make the loop self-feeding — stamping the
resolve-time `_honeypot_score` onto the completion-time history row
(runner → `db_log`) — is intentionally deferred (it's cross-module
pipeline threading, and §P5-2b's gate is precisely about not building
speculative surface before the global rules show inadequacy). Until that
wire lands the column stays NULL and the feature is inert. 25 tests in
`tests/test_v3_66_36_honeypot_threshold.py`.

## v3.66.35 — 2026-05-28 (P5-1b cross-site selector reuse)

**Feature (opt-in, default off).** Closes P5-1b. A high-confidence login
selector proven on one site can now be consulted as a low-priority tail
for a structurally-similar sister site (e.g. Aylo-family forms that share
input/button structure but rotate CSS-module class names and live on
different hosts).

New module `bulk_downloader/cross_site_selectors.py`:

- `selector_shape()` normalizes a selector to a structural fingerprint —
  strips rotated hash classes (`form.joHetV` → `form`) and numeric id
  suffixes (`#user_12345` → `#user`), keeps stable attributes
  (type/name/autocomplete/…) and `:has-text(...)`.
- `form_signature()` hashes the shapes of each role's top selector;
  structurally-identical forms collide regardless of host. Returns None
  when there's no user/pass anchor, so empty sites never collide.
- A flat JSON store (`$BD_HOME/cross_site_selectors.json`) keyed by
  signature, written atomically (`.tmp` + `os.replace`, utf-8). Only
  selectors with `_per_selector` hits ≥ 2 and zero misses are shared.
- `sync_and_augment()` is the single façade login.py calls: records this
  site's proven selectors, then appends a deduped, own-source-excluded,
  capped tail of cross-site matches. Wrapped so a corrupt store / missing
  BD_HOME / odd config can never break a login.

Wiring: both chain-assembly points in `login.py` (interactive + headless)
gate on `BD_CROSS_SITE_SELECTORS=1`. Unset → nothing read or written,
identical behaviour to v3.66.34. The store shape is intentionally generic
so capture-synthesis C-T1 anti-unification output can later write under
the same signature key (the §P5-1b coordination note). 30 tests in
`tests/test_v3_66_35_cross_site_selectors.py`.

## v3.66.34 — 2026-05-28 (network-log media classifier)

**Diagnostic-extraction release.** A classifier that reads a bd-recon
capture's `network_log` and reports the media it contains — manifests,
segments, direct files — with each item's signing status, expiry, and
DRM flag. Passes through ONLY genuinely unsigned direct media as
download candidates.

### What it does, and the line it holds

New module `bulk_downloader/netlog_classify.py`. The corpus showed that
on member sites the playable media in a network log is overwhelmingly
**signed and short-lived** — segment/manifest URLs carrying `key=`,
`end=<expiry>`, `limit=`, `policy=` tokens that exist specifically so
the stream can't be replayed outside the authenticated player. This
module **describes** those streams (kind, signed=true, expiry surfaced)
but never emits them as fetch-ready candidates — reassembling a signed
stream from its captured segments is defeating the signing, and that's
the declined path. Only unsigned direct media (e.g. an openly-served
trailer/preview `.mp4` with no signing markers) passes through as an
actual candidate; unsigned lone segments and all DRM-marked items are
reported but never candidates.

### API

`classify_network_log(capture, *, host=None) -> CaptureReport`. The
report exposes `hls_manifests` / `dash_manifests` / `segments` /
`signed_items` / `unsigned_media` tallies, a `summary()` string, a
JSON-serializable `as_dict()`, and `candidates()` — which returns only
the unsigned-direct-media URLs. Operates purely on already-captured
data; no network access.

### The invariant (pinned by tests)

A signed or DRM-marked URL is NEVER returned by `candidates()`. The
test suite asserts this on synthetic mixed logs AND across the whole
committed recon corpus — if a future change leaked a signed URL into
candidates, the corpus test fails.

### Tests

`tests/test_v3_66_34_netlog_classify.py` (21 tests): kind
classification (HLS/DASH/segment/direct), signing detection (key
markers, scrub-placeholder-means-signed, expiry extraction incl.
ms→s normalization), DRM flagging, the candidate invariant across
synthetic + corpus inputs, and report serialization. Regression: the
v3.66.33 corpus-extraction suite still passes.

### Files changed

- `bulk_downloader/__init__.py` (version → 3.66.34)
- `bulk_downloader/netlog_classify.py` (new)
- `tests/test_v3_66_34_netlog_classify.py` (new, 21 tests)
- `CHANGELOG.md` (this entry)

### Scope note

This is the offline/diagnostic half of the network-log work. Live
interception wired into the runner, and reassembly of signed streams
from captured segments, were deliberately NOT built — they cross the
detect-vs-evade line the posture doc draws (signed segment URLs are an
access control; reassembling them defeats it). This module reports what
a capture holds and surfaces only the genuinely open media. Product
backlog otherwise unchanged: P5-1b, C2, C4-B, P5-2b.
