## v3.66.33 — 2026-05-28 (JSON-LD Movie-type + real recon-corpus validation)

**Extraction-coverage release.** Validated the existing JSON-LD
extractor against a corpus of real member-site recon captures, fixed
the one concrete gap the real data exposed, and committed a scrubbed
held-out fixture set so the finding can't silently regress.

### The finding

A 40-file `bd-recon` capture corpus (AdultTime, dfxtra, Vixen,
NaughtyAmerica, Nubiles family, Brazzers, etc.) was run through
`extract_jsonld_media`. Of 8 JSON-LD blocks across the corpus, only 1
produced a candidate. Diagnosis: the sites ship video metadata under
schema.org `Movie` (AdultTime, dfxtra) — not in `JSONLD_MEDIA_TYPES` —
and those `Movie` nodes carry only metadata, no playable `contentUrl`.
The one hit was Vixen's genuine `VideoObject` with an `embedUrl`.

The honest takeaway: **on these sites JSON-LD is SEO metadata, not a
source of playable URLs** — the playable media lives in the network log
/ player config for blob:-based players (matches the FUTURE_FEATURES
prediction for blob players). A synthetic fixture would have hidden
this by carrying a fake `contentUrl`.

### The fix

`JSONLD_MEDIA_TYPES` gains `Movie`, `TVEpisode`, `Clip`, `Episode`. The
existing `_walk` already recurses nested `trailer`/`video`/`hasPart`
properties, so a Movie that DID nest a VideoObject would already have
been found; the gap was purely the top-level type allowlist. After the
fix all 8 corpus blocks produce a candidate — and `_emit` does NOT
fabricate a `content_url`/`embed_url` when none is present, so the 7
metadata-only Movie blocks are captured as labelled candidates
(name/description/thumbnail/duration) without inventing a source.

### Scrubbed corpus fixture + scrubber tool

  * `tools/scrub_recon.py` (new) — strips every credential-bearing
    field from a bd-recon capture: top-level cookies/local_storage/
    session_storage, per-network-entry auth/cookie headers,
    request/response bodies (→ length markers), and token-like query
    params (token/key/sig/sid/expires/policy/jwt/…) in every URL.
    Keeps the structural data extractors need.
  * `tests/fixtures/recon_corpus/` (new) — 6 representative SCRUBBED
    captures. Verified: zero live session tokens, cookies/storage
    replaced with `<scrubbed>`. Real session data was NOT committed.

### Tests

`tests/test_v3_66_33_recon_corpus_extraction.py` (7 tests): fixtures
present + provably scrubbed (asserts no `SID=`/cookie strings survive),
Movie-type recognized, Movie block → metadata candidate with no
fabricated URL, VideoObject+embedUrl still extracts, and the
corpus-wide "every block produces a candidate / playable URLs are
elsewhere" characterization. Regression: 408 deep_detect/JSON-LD tests
pass unchanged.

### Files changed

- `bulk_downloader/__init__.py` (version → 3.66.33)
- `bulk_downloader/deep_detect.py` (`JSONLD_MEDIA_TYPES` += Movie/TVEpisode/Clip/Episode)
- `tools/scrub_recon.py` (new — credential scrubber)
- `tests/test_v3_66_33_recon_corpus_extraction.py` (new, 7 tests)
- `tests/fixtures/recon_corpus/*.json` (new, 6 scrubbed captures)
- `CHANGELOG.md` (this entry)

### Still open / notes

This validated JSON-LD. The corpus also has rich `player_elements`
(video.js/Kosmos configs) and `network_log` data that the existing
`extract_player_configs` and media-harvest paths could be validated
against next — the blob:-based players confirm the playable source is
in the network log, so a future pass wiring network-log harvest into
the candidate set is the natural follow-up (Roadmap-F4/F6). Product
backlog otherwise unchanged: P5-1b, C2, C4-B, P5-2b.

## v3.66.32 — 2026-05-28 (Phase 5 P5-1: selector synthesis with fallback chains)

**Feature release.** Closes `OPEN_THREADS.md` item P5-1 (acceptance
criteria A1–A4). Adds structured fallback-chain support for learned
selectors — per-step timeout, post-condition, and advance/abort rules —
without changing the persisted JSON for the common case.

### What ships

New module `bulk_downloader/selector_chains.py`:

  * **`SelectorStep`** — a step carrying `selector`, `timeout_ms`
    (default 3000), `post_condition` (`locator_exists` (default) |
    `input_held` | `navigation_occurred` | `text_appeared:<pattern>`),
    `advance_on` (failure modes that advance to the next step), and a
    per-step `on_unlisted_failure` policy (`advance` | `abort`).
  * **Backward-compatibility shim (A1).** A plain string parses to a
    default `SelectorStep`; a default step serializes back to the plain
    string. So a `learned.{login,download}.*` list that only ever held
    bare strings round-trips to exactly itself — zero schema churn on
    existing site configs. Only steps that actually use the richer
    fields persist as dicts.
  * **`try_step` dispatcher (A2).** Single helper consumers call per
    step; returns `("ok" | "advance" | "abort", detail)`. `abort` is
    new — when a step's post-condition fails in a mode NOT in
    `advance_on`, the per-step policy decides whether to fall through
    or stop the chain. Per the operator decision this session,
    `on_unlisted_failure` is **per-step configurable**, defaulting to
    `abort` for `navigation_occurred` steps (blindly trying the next
    submit selector could submit the form blind) and `advance`
    everywhere else (matches the legacy lenient behavior).

### Consumers wired (A2/A3)

`login.py::_attempt_headless_fill_submit` now dispatches its three
fill/submit loops through `try_step` via an inline `_run_chain` helper.
For bare-string chains (the common case) the behavior is byte-for-byte
the legacy "advance on missing-or-threw". An optional `runner` kwarg
(default `None`, same fail-open pattern as v3.66.29's P5-3b) routes
each step decision through `runner.log_event("selector_step", ...)`
with a structured `extra` payload — the persistence A3 asked for. A
None runner is silent and the logging is wrapped so it can never break
the login path. The blind-Enter last resort is now suppressed when a
submit step *aborted* (the abort was the safety signal).

### Promote/demote unchanged (A4)

The runner's `_bump_per_selector` / `_maybe_demote_selectors`
promote-on-hit / demote-on-miss machinery operates on the persisted
`list[str]`. Because default steps persist as bare strings, that
machinery is untouched for the common case — front-promotion still
removes-and-reinserts the winning string, hits/misses still accumulate.
A4 falls out of keeping the persisted list as the source of truth and
putting the richness only at consumption time.

### Fixture

`tests/fixtures/selector_chains/legacy_learned_blocks.json` — three
realistic `learned.{login,download}` blocks in the legacy `list[str]`
shape, with selectors that are the **exact output of
`synthesize_selectors()`** for representative recorded events (not
hand-invented). The shim tests round-trip every block unchanged. Real
stash blocks can be swapped in later without changing the tests (they're
shape-driven). A5 (cross-site selector reuse) remains explicitly out of
scope; if pursued it's a separate item P5-1b.

### Tests

`tests/test_v3_66_32_phase5_selector_chains.py` — 29 tests across the
shim round-trip (bare/dict/mixed, blank-drop, unknown-mode-drop),
`try_step` for every post-condition, each advance/abort path, the
default-policy derivation, the fixture round-trip, and the A4
promote/demote invariant. Regression: existing login suites
(`test_v3_62_2_login_fallback`, `test_login_submit_robustness`,
`test_t6_login_security`, others — 82 tests) all pass unchanged.

### Files changed

- `bulk_downloader/__init__.py` (version → 3.66.32)
- `bulk_downloader/selector_chains.py` (new — SelectorStep, shim, try_step)
- `bulk_downloader/login.py` (`_attempt_headless_fill_submit` → chain dispatch + optional runner logging)
- `tests/test_v3_66_32_phase5_selector_chains.py` (new, 29 tests)
- `tests/fixtures/selector_chains/legacy_learned_blocks.json` (new fixture)
- `CHANGELOG.md` (this entry), `FUNCTION_INDEX.md` (no change — nested fn + new module aren't indexed)

### Still open

P5-1b (cross-site selector reuse) — deferred, A5 was out of scope.
Product backlog otherwise unchanged: C2 (frozen), C4-B (deferred),
P5-2b (deferred). The capture-synthesis track (separate roadmap) is
parallel; C-T1 there overlaps this work and should reuse `SelectorStep`.

## v3.66.31 — 2026-05-28 (F1–F3 bug-fix unit)

**Bug-fix release.** Clears the three follow-ups filed in v3.66.30.
All three are test-harness / installer robustness fixes; no
product-runtime behavior change.

### F1 — `run_tests.py` serial-retry unpack ValueError

`discover_and_run`'s import-error path returned a 3-tuple
`(name, err, ok)` while every other row it emits is a 4-tuple
`(name, err, ok, duration)`. When a file failed to import during the
**serial retry** phase, `_retry_failures_serial` crashed unpacking
`n, _, ok, _` with `ValueError: not enough values to unpack (expected
4, got 3)`, taking down the whole suite run after the parallel pass.
Surfaced on the stash full-suite run in the v3.66.30 session.

Fix: the import-error return is now a 4-tuple
`(name, "IMPORT ERROR: ...", False, 0.0)`. Added a defensive
row-normalizer at the retry boundary so any future shape drift
degrades gracefully (short rows padded to 4) instead of crashing the
classifier. Verified: a deliberately broken-import test file now
yields a 4-tuple and the classifier survives.

### F2 — stale `test_v3_43_71_emoji_free`

`TestF3NoEmojiInRecentChangelog::test_v3_43_71_emoji_free` asserted
v3.43.71 appears in `CHANGELOG.md`, but that entry has been moved to
`CHANGELOG_archive.md` — which is KB-only and absent from release-zip
extracts (v3.66.30 policy). The test hard-failed with "couldn't find
v3.43.71 in CHANGELOG". A second latent bug: the archive heading omits
the leading `v` (`## 3.43.71`) while the active log uses `## v3.43.71`,
so the section regex only matched one form.

Fix: `_read_section` now tries both `v<ver>` and `<ver>` heading forms,
and `test_v3_43_71_emoji_free` **skips** (rather than fails) when the
section can't be located because the archive isn't present. When the
archive IS present, the emoji check runs and passes. Verified both
ways: archive-absent → 1 pass + 1 skip; archive-present → 2 pass.

### F3 — `install_service.sh` root-owned version stamp under sudo

When run under `sudo`, the install-time `write_deployed_version.sh`
invocation ran as root, so `tools/deployed_version.txt` became
root-owned. The systemd unit's `ExecStartPre` then re-runs the same
helper as `User=${RUN_USER}` (the non-root operator), which can't
overwrite the root-owned file → `ExecStartPre` exits 1/FAILURE on
every start (non-fatal, but noisy and confusing).

Fix: when the installer is running as root and `RUN_USER` is non-root,
the install-time helper now runs via `sudo -u "$RUN_USER"`, so the
stamp is created owned by the same user the service runs as. A
belt-and-suspenders `chown "$RUN_USER"` reclaims any pre-existing
root-owned stamp from an earlier install. Also cleaned the four
pre-existing non-ASCII em-dashes in the PT11 comment block to restore
the installer's ASCII-only invariant. Verified: `bash -n` clean,
0 non-ASCII, both root and non-root branches select the correct
invocation.

### Files changed

- `bulk_downloader/__init__.py` (version → 3.66.31)
- `run_tests.py` (F1: 4-tuple import-error row + retry normalizer)
- `tests/test_v3_43_78_static_analysis_fixes.py` (F2: dual heading
  form + skip-not-fail on absent archive)
- `install_service.sh` (F3: `sudo -u RUN_USER` helper invocation +
  chown reclaim + ASCII cleanup)
- `CHANGELOG.md` (this entry), `FUNCTION_INDEX.md` (regenerated)

### Still open after this unit

Product backlog unchanged: C2 (frozen), C4-B (deferred), P5-1
(needs fixture), P5-2b (deferred). No operator-side items remain.

## v3.66.30 — 2026-05-28 (Fresh-install hardening + operator-side close-out)

**Bug-fix + ops release.** Born from a full fresh-host deploy to stash
that surfaced three install-blocking defects, plus closes all four
operator-side backlog items (A1–A4). No new features; this is
robustness and backlog cleanup.

### Bug fixes

- **`app.py` startup self-test crash on bare-list `sites_config.json`.**
  The selftest pre-loader at module import called
  `_cfg_for_st.get("sites")` unconditionally, assuming the config is a
  dict shaped `{"sites": [...]}`. But the historical (and the shipped
  `sites_config.example.json`) format is a **bare list of site dicts**,
  on which `.get` raises `AttributeError` — and the surrounding
  `except` only caught `FileNotFoundError / JSONDecodeError / OSError`,
  so a valid-but-old-shape config killed the import and the service
  never started. Now tolerates both shapes (dict-with-`sites` and bare
  list), skips non-dict entries defensively, and widens the `except` to
  include `AttributeError, TypeError`. A malformed config degrades to
  "no sites configured" in the selftest rather than crashing boot.

- **Frontend `tsc -b` build failure: implicit `testing-library__jest-dom`
  type.** `vitest` in devDependencies pulls `@testing-library/jest-dom`
  into TypeScript's implicit ambient-type scan. With no explicit `types`
  field, `tsc -b` tried to load a `testing-library__jest-dom` type
  library entry point and failed with TS2688, blocking the `/m2` SPA
  build (503 until the build succeeds). Fixed by scoping
  `compilerOptions.types` explicitly: `["node", "vite/client"]` in
  `frontend/tsconfig.json` and `["node"]` in `frontend/tsconfig.node.json`.
  Test files can still `import "@testing-library/jest-dom"` explicitly;
  they're just no longer force-loaded into the production build.

- **`install_service.sh` ExecStartPre permission failure.** When
  `install_service.sh` was run under `sudo`, `write_deployed_version.sh`
  wrote `tools/deployed_version.txt` as root, so subsequent service
  starts (running as the operator user) hit `Permission denied` on the
  ExecStartPre stamp (status=1/FAILURE; non-fatal but noisy). Documented
  the `chown` remediation; the script change to write as `$SUDO_USER` is
  deferred to a follow-up (the running deploy is fixed in place).

### Operator-side backlog — all closed

- **A1 — remote-teach scripts validated on stash.** Full fresh-install
  procedure exercised end-to-end on real hardware (Ubuntu 24.04, Tesla
  T4): venv + Playwright Chromium, frontend SPA build, systemd service,
  all four `bd-*` remote-teach units RUNNING, noVNC reachable from a
  phone, manual-teach Chromium visible and interactive inside the noVNC
  view.
- **A2 — deployed to stash.** v3.66.30 (was planned as v3.63.8; deployed
  current instead). Service active + enabled on boot. LAN routes: `/`
  (desktop) 200, `/m` → `/m2/` 200, `/m2` SPA 200.
- **A3 — bd-install kit patches fold-in.** Verify-and-close: the
  BDKIT_FIXES.md Bug 1 (double-wrapped kit auto-unwrap) and Bug 2
  (`bd → bdu` rename + `|| true` chmod) are already inline in
  `install_bulkdl_kits.sh`; v3.66.17 §E content-aware source-zip
  selection is inline in `bd-install`. No external patch layer remained.
- **A4 — 10-phase polluter audit.** Ran against the v3.66.30 source:
  6063 passed, 0 new polluters. Sixth consecutive release with an empty
  cross-phase cluster. Two pre-existing non-pollution test issues noted
  for follow-up (stale `test_v3_43_71_emoji_free`; audit-mode tests that
  hard-fail when CHANGELOG/FUNCTION_INDEX are absent from a release-zip
  extract).

### Packaging policy change

- **`CHANGELOG.md` and `FUNCTION_INDEX.md` now ship in the release zip.**
  Previously KB-only per the KB_VS_ZIP split. Twice now, audit-mode and
  drift tests (`test_function_index_in_sync`, `test_contracts`,
  `test_t51_regenerate_goldens`, `test_v3_43_78` emoji check) have

### Post-deploy verification

Live-test suite against the running v3.66.30 service: **17 pass / 10
warn / 0 fail (27 run), exit 0.** All warns are expected-state (no sites

concurrency under load).

- `test_v3_43_78_static_analysis_fixes::test_v3_43_71_emoji_free` —

## v3.66.29 — 2026-05-27 (Phase 5 P5-3b: runner.log_event routing for honeypot_filtered)

**Follow-up release.** Closes `OPEN_THREADS.md` item P5-3b. Routes the
v3.66.28 `honeypot_filtered` filter-summary through
`runner.log_event(...)` when a Runner handle is available, so the
emission participates in the structured event log alongside every
other runner event — site_id tagged, persisted in the bounded
event-log deque, broadcast via SSE — instead of going to bare
stderr. Falls back fail-open to the v3.66.28 stderr behavior when
no runner is wired (the `auto_detect.py` call path) or when
`log_event` itself raises.

### What ships

`find_best_download` grows a `runner=None` keyword argument. When
set, the existing emission helper builds the same summary string
the v3.66.28 stderr line carried and invokes
`runner.log_event("honeypot_filtered", message, extra=...)` instead
of `sys.stderr.write`. The `extra` payload exposes a structured
`{count, mode, reasons, all_dropped}` dict so future learning
pipelines (P5-2b's per-site threshold tuning is the obvious
consumer) can read the data without re-parsing the message string.

### Plumbing

Four call sites in `runner.py` now pass `runner=self`:

  * Line 736 — main worker's verify-picks path
  * Line 800 — main worker's commit-picks path
  * Line 5793 — main download path (the hot one)
  * Line 6344 — deep-detect retry path

`auto_detect.py:271` deliberately keeps the default `runner=None` —
that path has no Runner handle to pass, and the v3.66.28 stderr
emission is the right behavior there.

### Fail-open at every layer

Mirrors the R-P5-3 / R-P5-2 pattern:

  * `runner` is `None` → stderr (the v3.66.28 contract)
  * `runner.log_event(...)` raises → fall through to stderr
  * Filter itself raises → caught upstream by the v3.66.28
    fail-open block in `add()`; no emission either way

A bug in the logging layer must not silence the operator signal.

### Tests

27 tests in `tests/test_v3_66_29_phase5_honeypot_log_event.py`
across eight buckets:

  * `TestRunnerNonePreservesStderr` (3) — v3.66.28 back-compat
  * `TestRunnerLogEventRouting` (6) — message shape, extra-dict
    schema, count consistency, strict-mode passthrough
  * `TestAllDroppedWithRunner` (4) — empty-result path still
    emits, `extra.all_dropped=True`, marker preserved
  * `TestLogEventFailureFallback` (2) — fail-open both flows
  * `TestSilentWhenNothingFiltered` (3) — no spurious emission
    when filter is off or no decoys found
  * `TestReasonsTruncation` (2) — list capped at 10, count
    reflects the full total
  * `TestSignatureBackCompat` (5) — every existing call shape
    still works (positional, keyword, mixed)
  * `TestModuleLoad` (2) — `runner` kwarg present, default
    `None`, positioned last

## v3.66.28 — 2026-05-27 (Phase 5 P5-3: DOM-visibility honeypot filter)

**Feature release.** Closes `OPEN_THREADS.md` item P5-3. Ships a
DOM-visibility honeypot filter that drops invisible decoy `<a>` tags
and buttons during the wide-scan in `detect.find_best_download` —
catching anti-bot honeypots that R-P5-2's post-resolution URL scorer
can't see (the decoy never makes it into the provider-resolved
candidate list in the first place; it's just an off-screen `<a>` in
the page DOM that looks like a download link).

### What ships

A new module `bulk_downloader/dom_honeypot.py` (~340 lines) with
two parallel entrypoints — one for BeautifulSoup elements, one for
Playwright locators — sharing the same TRAP_URL_TERMS and
TRAP_TEXT_TERMS vocabularies. Plus `find_duplicate_field_decoys`
for paired hidden/visible inputs sharing a name (anti-bot form
honeypot). Wired into `detect.find_best_download`'s `add()` closure
so invisible candidates never enter the scoring list.

### Opt-in mechanism

`BD_DOM_HONEYPOT_FILTER` env var. Values:
  * unset / `off` / any unrecognized value → no filtering (default;
    v3.66.27 behavior byte-for-byte preserved)
  * `cheap` → Playwright `is_visible(timeout=300)` + URL/text vocab
    on every candidate
  * `strict` → same as `cheap` for now (reserved for future BS-level
    confirmation pass)

Read at call time, not module load — mirrors `_honeypot_drop_threshold`
and `_yt_cipher_backend` conventions so `monkeypatch.setenv` works
in tests.

### Detection rules

**Visibility signals** (each fires standalone):

  * `inline_style_hidden` — `display:none`, `visibility:hidden`,
    `opacity:0`, `left:-9999px`, etc. (reuses
    `deep_detect.HONEYPOT_CSS_HIDDEN` — one source of truth)
  * `hidden_attribute` — bare HTML `hidden` attr
  * `aria_hidden` — `aria-hidden="true"`
  * `css_class_hidden` — class-based hiding via `<style>` block
    consultation (same simple selector match as
    `_is_visible_input` for BeautifulSoup path)
  * `not_visible` — Playwright `is_visible(timeout=300)` returns
    False (only on the locator path; layout-aware, catches external
    stylesheets that BS can't see)

**Vocabulary signals** (each fires standalone):

  * `trap_url_term` — URL/data-href/data-url/data-src contains a
    redirect/tracking token (`/click?`, `/clk?`, `/go?`, `/out?`,
    `/redirect?`, `/sponsor`, `affiliate`, `popup`, `interstitial`,
    etc.). All terms ≥3 chars to avoid random-path collisions
    (pinned by `test_no_overly_short_url_terms`).
  * `trap_text_term` — visible text or `title`/`aria-label`/`alt`
    contains `sponsored`, `advertisement`, `promoted`, `popup`,
    `interstitial`, etc. Bare `"ad"` deliberately excluded — too
    noisy (matches `addon`, `add to cart`, etc.).

**tabindex=-1 semantics:** for LINKS/BUTTONS, `tabindex="-1"` alone
is NOT a decoy trigger — modal close buttons and JS focus-managed
widgets legitimately use it. For form INPUTS, `tabindex="-1"` IS
standalone — handled inside `find_duplicate_field_decoys`'s
`_input_is_hidden` helper, matching the proven `deep_detect._is_visible_input`
form-field rules.

### Duplicate-field decoys

`find_duplicate_field_decoys(form_inputs, css_text="")` returns a
list of `{"name": str, "reason": "duplicate_field_hidden_decoy"}`
for any input name that has BOTH a visible and a hidden instance.
All-hidden duplicates (e.g. dual CSRF mirrors from a framework
template) and all-visible duplicates (multi-step form chunking)
are NOT reported — those aren't the honeypot pattern.

### Failure semantics

Fail-open at every level (mirrors R-P5-2):

  * If `is_link_decoy_playwright` raises, the candidate is KEPT.
    Pinned by `TestFindBestDownloadIntegration::test_dom_filter_exception_fails_open`.
  * If Playwright's `is_visible()` raises, treat as "can't tell,
    assume visible" — don't drop. Pinned by `test_is_visible_exception_fails_open`.
  * If `get_attribute` raises, the corresponding signal is skipped
    (other signals still checked). Pinned by
    `test_get_attribute_exception_fails_open`.

A bug in honeypot detection must not cost the operator a real
download.

### Operator log

Single stderr summary line emitted per scan when any candidate was
filtered: `honeypot_filtered: count=N mode=cheap reasons=[...]`.
Mirrors P5-2's stderr pattern. Runner-level `log_event` integration
deferred — stderr is consistent with the rest of `provider_resolve`
and visible in the runner log.

### Tests

`tests/test_v3_66_28_phase5_dom_honeypot.py` — 60 tests:
  * 5 cases for inline-style hidden (display:none, visibility:hidden,
    opacity:0, off-screen positioning, negative-control no-style)
  * 4 cases for `hidden` HTML attribute (bare, empty, value, button)
  * 4 cases for aria-hidden (true, false, absent, button)
  * 5 cases for CSS-class hidden (class display:none, class
    visibility:hidden, id selector, unrelated-CSS negative,
    no-CSS negative)
  * 4 cases for tabindex=-1 semantics (alone on link, plus hidden
    combo, plus aria-hidden combo, alone on button)
  * 8 cases for TRAP_URL_TERMS (5 positive + 3 negative including
    `/sports`, `/clarification`, legit `/video/file.mp4`)
  * 4 cases for TRAP_TEXT_TERMS
  * 2 reason-precedence cases (visibility signals beat vocab)
  * 7 cases for Playwright locator path (5 positive paths + 2
    fail-open paths)
  * 7 cases for `find_duplicate_field_decoys` (real duplicate, no
    duplicate, all-hidden, all-visible, tabindex=-1 input, multi
    duplicate, nameless input)
  * 6 integration cases for `find_best_download` with mock
    Playwright page (off / cheap / strict / unrecognized / all
    filtered / exception fail-open)
  * 4 module-constant sanity cases

  * `bulk_downloader/detect.py` (+38 lines: env-var reader,
    `add()` closure filter, log emission)

## v3.66.27 — 2026-05-27 (Phase 5 P5-2: candidate-URL honeypot scoring)

**Feature release.** Closes B1–B3 of `OPEN_THREADS.md` item P5-2.
Ships a deterministic, opt-in honeypot scorer that filters resolved
provider candidates before they reach the download queue. Catches
URLs that look like real content (right extension, right path shape)
but resolve to tracking pixels, paywall stubs, or 200-OK HTML decoys.

### What ships

A new module `bulk_downloader/honeypot_score.py` (pure function, no
network, no imports of other BD modules) plus a wiring hook in
`provider_resolve.resolve_provider_embed`. Opt-in via the env var
`BD_HONEYPOT_SCORE_THRESHOLD` (a float in (0, 1]). Default unset →
no behavior change; the release is byte-for-byte compatible with
v3.66.26 for any operator who doesn't set the env var.

### Rules (combine by max, not sum)

Pre-fetch (URL inspection only, no HTTP):

  * `tracker_host` (0.95) — URL host or parent domain is on the
    `KNOWN_TRACKER_HOSTS` list (doubleclick.net, taboola.com,
    adnxs.com, etc.). Subdomain-aware: `ads.doubleclick.net`
    matches; `mydoubleclick.net` does not (substring attack
    rejected).
  * `pixel_path` (0.85) — URL path contains a known pixel route
    token like `/pixel`, `/track`, `/beacon`, `/imp.gif`, `/p.gif`.
    Path-rooted match — tokens must start with `/`, so the rule
    doesn't fire on filenames that happen to contain the substring
    (`soundtrack.mp4` is safe).
  * `empty_path_only_qs` (0.70) — URL has no path component
    (`/` or empty) but a query string with at least one
    cache-buster-style key (`v=`, `cb=`, `utm_*`). The classic
    `https://t.example.com/?v=abc123` tracker shape.

Post-fetch (require operator to supply a HEAD probe result):

  * `media_but_html` (0.90) — URL extension says media (`.mp4`,
    `.webm`, etc.) but probe Content-Type is `text/html`. Manifest
    extensions (`.m3u8`, `.mpd`) are exempt because they're
    inherently text.
  * `tiny_media_body` (0.80) — URL extension says media but probe
    Content-Length is under 1 KB. Manifest extensions exempt.
  * `cookie_on_media` (0.40) — probe sets cookies on a media URL.
    Weak signal alone (real CDNs occasionally do this for
    CORS-adjacent reasons); strong when stacked with anything else.
  * `host_class_redirect` (0.75) — media URL redirects to a
    DIFFERENT host that's itself on `KNOWN_TRACKER_HOSTS`. Same-host
    redirects (token refresh) and cross-CDN failover don't fire.

Rules combine by `max`, not sum — a URL that's both tracker-hosted
AND has a tiny body doesn't score 1.75; it scores 0.95 (the
strongest signal wins). Avoids the "many weak signals add up to a
false positive" failure mode.

### Threshold zones

`BD_HONEYPOT_SCORE_THRESHOLD` is the drop threshold:

  * `score >= drop_threshold` (default 0.8) → **drop** the
    candidate; emit `honeypot_drop:` line to stderr with the
    provider, URL, score, and reason.
  * `0.5 <= score < drop_threshold` → **downscore**: multiply the
    candidate's `score` by 0.5, append a `honeypot signal (...)`
    warning, keep the candidate. Ranks below cleaner alternatives
    but still available if it's the only candidate.
  * `score < 0.5` → keep unchanged.

If every candidate from a resolver is dropped, the dispatcher
surfaces an error string `all <provider> candidates filtered out by
honeypot score (threshold=X.XX)` so the caller can distinguish "we
found candidates but they were all traps" from "the resolver found
nothing."

### What's deliberately conservative

  * **Default off.** The release ships zero behavior change unless
    an operator sets `BD_HONEYPOT_SCORE_THRESHOLD`. We do not pick
    a "safe" default threshold for them.
  * **CDN hostnames are NOT on the tracker list.** Cloudfront,
    Akamai, fastly, etc. carry real content; we will not blanket-
    flag them. The tracker list is unambiguously-not-content
    domains only.
  * **`0` and `1.5` and other "weird" thresholds are treated as
    off**, not as "drop everything" or "drop nothing." A
    misconfiguration must not silently kill all candidates.
  * **Fail-open on scorer crash.** If a future rule mishandles a
    weird input and `score_candidate` raises, the candidate is
    kept (not dropped). Bug in scoring must not cost the operator
    a download.

### Why "ML" isn't shipped (B4 deferred)

The spec's B4 (per-site threshold learning) is explicitly out of
scope for this first cut. Get deterministic rules into operators'
hands first; revisit only if accuracy isn't enough. The data the
learning loop would need (operator's "no, that wasn't what I
wanted" labels) is already partially available via the
`cleanup_helpers.find_tinies` flow; B4 can hook there when it
ships.

### Files changed

  * `bulk_downloader/honeypot_score.py` (new, ~320 lines)
  * `bulk_downloader/provider_resolve.py` (+~110 lines: env-var
    reader, filter function, integration hook between resolver
    return and cache write)
  * `bulk_downloader/__init__.py` (version → 3.66.27)
  * `tests/test_v3_66_27_phase5_honeypot_score.py` (new, 82 tests)
  * `CHANGELOG.md` (this entry)
  * `OUTSTANDING_WORK.md` / `handoff/OPEN_THREADS.md` (P5-2 →
    R-P5-2)

## v3.66.26 — 2026-05-27 (Phase 4 C4 A3: YouTube signatureCipher hybrid dispatch)

**Feature release.** Closes the A1 leg of `OPEN_THREADS.md` item C4
(YouTube `signatureCipher` decipher) — the largest known Phase 4 gap
since v3.66.20 — and wires the dispatch site for the future A2 leg
(in-process player-JS decipher). v3.66.20 promoted `resolve_youtube`
out of stub status but left signed-only formats producing an empty
candidate list with a counted error; this release lets operators
opt into deciphering them.

### What ships

A single env var `BD_YOUTUBE_CIPHER` selects one of three backends:

  * `off` (default) — preserves v3.66.20 behavior verbatim. Signed-only
    responses produce no candidates; the error string still contains
    "signed" + the count, satisfying the v3.66.20 contract pinned by
    `test_v3_66_20_phase4_youtube.py::test_signed_format_skipped_with_clear_error`.
    Zero behavior change for anyone who doesn't opt in.
  * `yt-dlp` — A1 leg of the hybrid. Shells out to
    `yt-dlp --dump-single-json --no-warnings --no-playlist --skip-download
    <watch_url>` when signed-only candidates need to be produced. Hard
    30s wall-clock timeout. Argv list, never `shell=True`. `video_id`
    is sanitized against `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{11}$` before being inserted
    into the URL (belt-and-suspenders; argv is already shell-safe).
    `shutil.which("yt-dlp")` is memoized at module level so the PATH
    lookup runs at most once per process.
  * `player-js` — A2 leg, stub. Returns "not yet implemented" with a
    hint to fall back to `yt-dlp` or `off`. Pins the dispatch site so
    the A2 swap (when it lands) is a one-function replacement with no
    public-surface change.

### Hot-path optimization

The decipher dispatch is gated behind the existing skip condition in
`resolve_youtube`: it only fires when `candidates` is empty AND
`signed_skipped > 0`. If `hlsManifestUrl` or any unsigned format is
present, no subprocess is launched — we already have what we need.
yt-dlp fork is on the order of 100ms even when it succeeds; on a
typical YouTube watch page HLS is present and that cost would be
pure waste.

### Distinct `source_type` for deciphered candidates

Deciphered URLs carry `source_type="youtube_resolved_cipher_ytdlp"`
(and, when A2 lands, `youtube_resolved_cipher_playerjs`). Distinct
from `youtube_resolved` / `youtube_resolved_adaptive` because
deciphered URLs have a short undocumented TTL that downstream cache
code should respect — anything that hashes on `source_type` (the
candidate dedupe in the ranker, future per-source-type cache policy)
will treat them as different cache keys, which is what we want.
Each deciphered candidate also carries a `warnings` entry
flagging the short TTL.

### Failure modes

Every dispatch error returns a string, never raises:

  * `BD_YOUTUBE_CIPHER=off` with signed-only formats →
    "youtube has N signed format(s) but BD_YOUTUBE_CIPHER=off; set to
    yt-dlp or player-js to decipher"
  * yt-dlp not on PATH → "yt-dlp not on PATH; install yt-dlp or set
    BD_YOUTUBE_CIPHER=off"
  * Subprocess timeout → "yt-dlp subprocess timed out after 30s on
    video_id=<id>"
  * Non-zero exit → "yt-dlp subprocess failed with exit code N:
    <stderr first line>" (only the first line of stderr is included —
    yt-dlp often emits secondary diagnostics that pollute the message)
  * Empty/malformed output → "yt-dlp returned no formats with direct
    URLs for video_id=<id>" / "yt-dlp output not parseable" / "yt-dlp
    output is not a JSON object"
  * `BD_YOUTUBE_CIPHER=player-js` → "player-js decipher not yet
    implemented in v3.66.26; set BD_YOUTUBE_CIPHER=yt-dlp ... or
    BD_YOUTUBE_CIPHER=off"

Unknown values for `BD_YOUTUBE_CIPHER` fail closed — they normalize
to `off`. A typo in the env var doesn't silently enable a different
backend.

### What stays out

  * **No app.py wiring.** The env var is read inside `provider_resolve`;
    no config-file plumbing this release. Per-site override stays
    YAGNI until a fixture motivates it (mirrors the C2 stance on
    `signing_callback`).
  * **No subprocess for other resolvers.** The "deep_detect is pure
    HTML → report" contract continues to hold for Vimeo, Wistia,
    Brightcove, JWPlayer. Only YouTube punches through it, only
    behind an opt-in flag, only when no in-process path produced
    candidates.
  * **No caching of yt-dlp output.** TTL on deciphered URLs is short
    and undocumented; caching the JSON blob risks serving expired
    URLs. The existing per-resolution candidate cache handles
    repeat-call dedup at a coarser grain.

### Files modified

```
bulk_downloader/provider_resolve.py            # +~280 lines (cipher dispatch + 3 backend fns + wiring)
bulk_downloader/__init__.py                    # version → 3.66.26
tests/test_v3_66_26_phase4_youtube_cipher.py   # new, 37 tests
CHANGELOG.md                                   # v3.66.26 entry at top
handoff/OPEN_THREADS.md                        # C4 → R-C4 (partial), new C4-B item for A2 leg
OUTSTANDING_WORK.md                            # C4 → R-C4 (partial), new C4-B item
v3_66_26_release_notes.md                      # new
v3_66_26_handoff.md                            # new
```

tests/test_v3_66_26_phase4_youtube_cipher.py alone           37/37  PASS  (0.13s)
v3.66.25 tight-proof + v3.66.20 youtube + new (8 files)     298/298 PASS  (5.13s)
v3.66.22 broader sweep + v3.66.20 youtube + new (17 files)  485/485 PASS  (24.75s)
Cross-phase polluter check (phases 02 + 03 + 07 + 09)      2468/2468 PASS  (132s)

The cross-phase check confirms no new polluter introduced. The known
pre-existing polluter clusters from v3.66.19 (`test_u27/28/29` +
`test_v3_62_2_login_fallback`) are in phase_02 and pass clean in the
combo above — same dormant-in-this-combo state as v3.66.25.

### Test seam note (operator-relevant)

`_decipher_signed_formats_ytdlp` accepts an optional `_run` parameter
(default `None`, lazy-resolves to `subprocess.run` at call time).
This is a test seam: tests can either pass `_run=stub` directly, or
`monkeypatch.setattr(subprocess, "run", stub)` and have it flow
through the dispatcher path. The original draft used a default-arg
seam (`_run: Callable = subprocess.run`) but that captures the
reference at function-definition time and breaks
module-level-monkeypatch tests — the lazy lookup pattern is the
right one for this kind of seam. Documented here so future edits
preserve the contract.

## v3.66.25 — 2026-05-27 (Phase 4 P6: DNS rebinding close on the SSRF guard)

**Security/hardening release.** Closes `OPEN_THREADS.md` item C3,
the DNS-rebinding TOCTOU left open by v3.66.24's pre-fetch guard.

v3.66.24's `_is_safe_public_host` resolves a hostname via
`socket.getaddrinfo` and checks the resulting IPs, but httpx
re-resolves the hostname at connection time. An attacker who
controls authoritative DNS for their own domain can return public
IPs to our resolution and private IPs to httpx's, hopping the
guard. v3.66.25 closes that gap at the httpx transport layer.

### What landed

  * **`_SSRFGuardedTransport`** — a subclass of `httpx.HTTPTransport`.
    Lazy-imported (matching the discipline of `_make_default_http_get`)
    and memoized at module level so repeated factory calls return
    the same class object — important for `isinstance` checks in
    tests. For each outgoing request:
      1. If `allow_private_hosts=True`, pure pass-through.
      2. If the URL's host is already an IP literal (v4 or v6), the
         event hook already classified it pre-fetch — pass through.
      3. Otherwise the transport does ITS OWN `socket.getaddrinfo`,
         classifies every returned IP via the existing
         `_classify_ip`. Any private IP in the resolution set
         raises `SSRFBlocked` immediately (same fail-closed policy
         as the predicate — one bad IP poisons the set). DNS
         failures and empty resolution results also fail closed.
      4. On success, rewrites `request.url` to the IP literal we
         just vetted. httpx's `URL.copy_with(host=...)` handles
         IPv6 bracketing. The `Host` header was populated from the
         ORIGINAL URL when the `httpx.Request` was constructed and
         is preserved across the URL mutation — virtual-hosting
         servers continue to route correctly.
      5. Sets `request.extensions["sni_hostname"]` to the original
         hostname. httpcore reads this when calling
         `stream.start_tls(server_hostname=...)`, so TLS
         certificate verification continues to validate against the
         original hostname even though the URL now carries an IP
         literal.
      6. Delegates to the base transport. Because httpcore now sees
         an IP-literal URL, it does NOT re-resolve — the rebinding
         window is closed.
  * **`_SSRFGuardedTransport_factory()`** — module-level factory
    that constructs and memoizes the transport class. Underscore-
    prefixed; not in `__all__`.
  * **`_make_default_http_get` rewired.** The `httpx.Client(...)`
    construction now passes the guarded transport via the
    `transport=` kwarg. The `allow_private_hosts` flag is threaded
    through to the transport so opt-out behaviour is consistent
    across both layers.
  * **Defense in depth, not replacement.** The pre-fetch / redirect
    event hook from v3.66.24 stays put. The hook fires at the
    hostname level once per outgoing request (initial + every
    redirect target); the transport fires once per connect, at the
    IP level. A regression test explicitly verifies the event hook
    is still installed alongside the transport — a future refactor
    that drops the hook "because the transport catches everything
    now" would fail the test.
  * **Docstring update on `_is_safe_public_host`** — replaces the
    "TOCTOU caveat" paragraph with a note that v3.66.25's transport
    layer closes the gap.

### Files changed

  * `bulk_downloader/provider_resolve.py`
    * Added `_SSRF_GUARDED_TRANSPORT_CLS` module-level memo binding.
    * Added `_SSRFGuardedTransport_factory()` factory function.
    * Inside the factory: `_SSRFGuardedTransport` class with
      `__init__`, `handle_request`, and the testable
      `_prepare_request` helper.
    * `_make_default_http_get` now constructs and passes the
      guarded transport into `httpx.Client(transport=...)`.
    * Docstring on `_is_safe_public_host` updated to point at the
      transport-layer close.
  * `bulk_downloader/__init__.py` — version → 3.66.25.
  * `tests/test_v3_66_25_phase4_ssrf_rebinding.py` — new, 35 tests
    across 7 classes plus a module-level export check.

### Test status

```
tests/test_v3_66_25_phase4_ssrf_rebinding.py alone        35/35   PASS
v3.66.24 Phase 4 tight-proof + new (6 files)             229/229  PASS
v3.66.22 broader sweep + new (15 files)                  416/416  PASS  (30.9s)
```

No transient flakes observed this release.

### Test coverage

The new test file's seven classes mirror the threat model:

  * `TestTransportClassShape` (4) — subclass, factory memoization,
    `allow_private_hosts` flag stored, `_prepare_request` exists.
  * `TestPrepareRequestPassThroughCases` (4) — opt-out short-circuit,
    IPv4 / IPv6 literal short-circuit, empty-host short-circuit. Each
    verified by bombing `socket.getaddrinfo` and confirming it isn't
    called.
  * `TestPrepareRequestBlocking` (9) — loopback v4 / v6, RFC1918,
    AWS metadata (169.254.169.254), multicast, mixed-set poisoning
    (both orderings), DNS failure (fail-closed), empty resolution.
  * `TestPrepareRequestRewriting` (6) — URL host rewritten to IP
    literal, Host header preserved as original hostname, SNI
    extension set, IPv6 rewrite with brackets, deterministic
    first-IP-chosen behaviour, non-default port preserved.
  * `TestDNSRebindingCaught` (3) — the canonical test: a stateful
    `getaddrinfo` fake returns a public IP on the first call
    (consumed by `_is_safe_public_host`) and a private IP on the
    second (consumed by the transport). The transport refuses. Plus
    a loopback-rebind variant and a consistent-resolution negative
    control.
  * `TestTransportWiredIntoFactory` (4) — fake `httpx.Client`
    intercepts construction and verifies the `transport=` kwarg is
    a `_SSRFGuardedTransport` instance with the right
    `allow_private_hosts` value, plus a defense-in-depth regression
    guard that the event-hook layer is still installed.
  * `TestEndToEndComposition` (2) — even when
    `_is_safe_public_host` is monkeypatched to allow a hostname,
    the transport still refuses if it resolves private. Also: an
    obvious literal like `127.0.0.1` is refused by the event-hook
    layer FIRST, so the transport's `_prepare_request` is never
    invoked.
  * `TestOptOutShortcircuit` (2) — real `http.server` fixture plus
    `allow_private_hosts=True`. End-to-end localhost fetches
    succeed via both IP-literal and hostname (`localhost`) paths.

Plus a module-level test that `__all__` is unchanged — the new
transport surface is private (underscore-prefixed).

### What is NOT mitigated (intentional / known)

  * **Resolvers that inject their own `http_get`.** The transport
    is on `_default_http_get` only. Resolvers that pass their own
    `http_get=` (e.g. Brightcove's BCOV-Policy header injection)
    bypass both layers. Currently safe because Brightcove templates
    against a hardcoded host; future resolvers that both inject a
    custom `http_get` AND follow attacker URLs would need to compose
    with the factory or guard themselves. Unchanged from v3.66.24.
  * **httpx connection pool reuse across requests.** The transport
    re-resolves on every `handle_request` call, so a long-lived
    client with multiple requests to the same hostname will
    re-vet each time. That's correct behaviour, not a gap.
  * **IPv6 zone IDs.** Same caveat as v3.66.24 — `fe80::1%eth0`
    notations rely on `_classify_ip`'s link-local rejection, not on
    specific zone-ID handling.

### What's NOT shipped (still deferred)

  * **YouTube `signatureCipher` decipher** — unchanged from v3.66.24.
    The largest remaining Phase 4 backlog item. Design fork between
    yt-dlp subprocess and in-process player-JS decipher.

## v3.66.24 — 2026-05-27 (Phase 4 P6: SSRF hardening on _default_http_get)

**Security/hardening release.** Closes the SSRF gap flagged as the
next-session recommendation in the v3.66.23 handoff and as
`OPEN_THREADS.md` item C1.

Before this release, `provider_resolve._default_http_get` called
`httpx.Client(...).get(url)` with no host validation. Until v3.66.22,
that was safe by construction — every resolver templated URLs against
a hardcoded provider host (e.g. `cdn.jwplayer.com/v2/media/<id>`), so
the attacker controlled the id but not the host. v3.66.23's JWPlayer
self-hosted path was the first to follow an attacker-controlled URL
from page HTML. Match-existing-behavior was the explicit decision at
the time; this release adds the guard.

### What landed

  * **`SSRFBlocked` exception class** — exported in `__all__`.
    Distinct from network errors so resolver call sites can tell
    a guard refusal apart from a real connection failure. Existing
    resolver code catches `Exception` broadly, so the message
    surfaces through to the operator without per-resolver changes.
  * **`_is_safe_public_host(host)`** — predicate. Resolves hostnames
    to IPs via `socket.getaddrinfo`, classifies each result against
    `ipaddress.ip_address(...)` properties. Returns
    `(True, "")` for public unicast, `(False, reason)` otherwise.
    Rejects loopback, RFC1918 private, link-local (incl. AWS
    metadata 169.254.169.254), IPv6 ULA, multicast, reserved, and
    unspecified ranges. Hostname → IP failures fail closed.
    Multi-record DNS responses must ALL resolve to public IPs;
    one private record in a set blocks the host.
  * **`_classify_ip(addr, host_repr)`** — per-IP classifier. Splits
    out from the hostname predicate so literal-IP hosts share the
    same logic. Returns `(False, reason)` with a reason string that
    includes both the original host repr and the offending IP, for
    operator diagnostics.
  * **`_make_default_http_get(*, allow_private_hosts=False)`** —
    factory. The default produces a guarded fetcher; an explicit
    `allow_private_hosts=True` produces an unguarded one for dev /
    mock use. Per the OPEN_THREADS C1 spec, the opt-out is
    constructor-only — there is no env var, no module switch, no
    class attribute. A test explicitly verifies that env vars named
    things like `BD_ALLOW_PRIVATE_HOSTS` / `DISABLE_SSRF_GUARD`
    have NO effect.
  * **Redirect-time guard via httpx `event_hooks`.** The factory
    installs a `request` event hook that re-runs the predicate on
    every outgoing request — including redirect follow-ups. A
    public host that 302s to `http://localhost/admin` is blocked
    at the redirect target. This closes the
    `follow_redirects=True` bypass.
  * **`_default_http_get` is now a module-level binding produced by
    `_make_default_http_get()`** — keeps the existing
    `pr._default_http_get = ...` monkeypatch pattern working (one
    test in `test_v3_66_16_phase4_p4_provider_resolve.py` uses
    this).

### Files changed

  * `bulk_downloader/provider_resolve.py`
    * Added `SSRFBlocked` exception class.
    * Added `_is_safe_public_host`, `_classify_ip` helpers.
    * Added `_make_default_http_get` factory.
    * `_default_http_get` is now produced by the factory.
    * `SSRFBlocked` added to `__all__`.
  * `bulk_downloader/__init__.py` — version → 3.66.24.
  * `tests/test_v3_66_24_phase4_ssrf_hardening.py` — new, 47 tests.

### Test status

```
tests/test_v3_66_24_phase4_ssrf_hardening.py alone           47/47   PASS
tests/test_v3_66_16_phase4_p4_provider_resolve.py (regr.)     8/8    PASS
tests/test_v3_66_18_phase4_jwplayer.py (regr.)               64/64   PASS
tests/test_v3_66_20_phase4_jwplayer_feeds.py (regr.)         22/22   PASS
tests/test_v3_66_23_phase4_jwplayer_selfhosted.py (regr.)    53/53   PASS
v3.66.22 tight-proof + JWPlayer regression + new SSRF        381/381 PASS
```

One transient session_keeper failure was observed mid-run on the
first sweep and did not reproduce on the second. Same
`lock.acquire(timeout=0.5)` sandbox-CPU-contention transient
flagged in v3.66.22 §A.

### What is NOT mitigated (intentional / known)

  * **DNS rebinding TOCTOU.** Our `_is_safe_public_host` resolves
    the hostname, but httpx re-resolves at connection time. An
    attacker who controls authoritative DNS for their own domain
    could rebind between our resolution and httpx's. Closing this
    fully requires a custom httpx transport that pins the
    connection to the IP we resolved. The realistic threat model
    is "untrusted HTML points us at a private IP literal or a
    public name that simply resolves to one" — both of which ARE
    mitigated. The rebinding case is now `OPEN_THREADS.md` C3.
  * **IPv6 zone IDs / scope IDs.** The predicate strips bare
    brackets but doesn't handle `fe80::1%eth0`-style zone notations
    specifically. `getaddrinfo` may still resolve them; the
    classification on the resulting address will still reject as
    link-local, so behavior is safe-by-default. Not perfect though.

### What's NOT shipped (still deferred)

  * **YouTube `signatureCipher` decipher** — unchanged from v3.66.23.
  * **Full DNS-rebinding TOCTOU close** (new OPEN_THREADS C3).
  * **JWPlayer signing_callback wiring in app.py** — unchanged from
    v3.66.23.

## v3.66.23 — 2026-05-27 (Phase 4 P5: JWPlayer self-hosted)

**Feature release.** Picks up the JWPlayer self-hosted item from the
v3.66.20+ deferred list. The handoff said "different config endpoint
and signature scheme from cloud-hosted" — after reading JWPlayer's
public docs, the actual gap is narrower and more tractable: self-hosted
pages load their feed JSON from a customer-controlled URL (not on
`cdn.jwplayer.com` or `feeds.jwplayer.com`), and the feed shape is
identical to the cdn feeds endpoint. Once you've fetched the JSON, the
same per-source classifier we use for the cdn paths handles it.

The "signature scheme" piece is real but only for DRM and signed-URL
deployments — categorically out of scope for an unauthenticated
scraper (see signing posture below).

**Approach (the "B-prime" design discussed in the planning session):**

  * Resolve unsigned self-hosted feeds on ANY host.
  * **Detect** DRM and signed-URL markers in the feed JSON and return
    a structured `scheme=...` error WITHOUT attempting to bypass.
  * **Hook** for operators with legitimate credentials: a
    `signing_callback` parameter that the resolver uses instead of
    the default `http_get` when supplied. The callback's contract
    matches `http_get`: `(url) -> (status, headers, body_bytes)`.

The rationale was discussed at length in the session — Option A (no
signing support) leaves operators with their own credentials no
clean integration point; Option C (full DRM) is out of scope for
legal and engineering reasons that are documented in
`handoff/OPEN_THREADS.md`. B-prime is the middle path: legitimate
credentialed access is wireable, but the resolver itself doesn't
attempt bypass.

### Files changed

  * `bulk_downloader/provider_resolve.py`
    * Added `_resolve_jwplayer_selfhosted` helper.
    * Added `_jwplayer_check_drm_markers` helper (case-insensitive
      lookup of `drm.<scheme>` per-entry blocks and top-level
      `signedUrls` / `signingKey` flags).
    * Added module-level constants
      `_JWPLAYER_ALLOWED_SCHEMES`,
      `_JWPLAYER_DRM_MARKER_KEYS`,
      `_JWPLAYER_SIGNED_URL_MARKER_KEYS`.
    * Extended `resolve_jwplayer` dispatch to add the
      `ids["config_url"]` branch. Priority order is
      `media_id` → `feed_id` → `config_url` so cdn-hosted patterns
      still win when both are present.
    * Updated the "missing" error string from `"missing media_id
      or feed_id"` to `"missing media_id, feed_id, or config_url"`.
    * `urlparse` added to the urllib imports for scheme-validation.
  * `bulk_downloader/deep_detect.py`
    * Added `config_url_attr` pattern to
      `_PROVIDER_ID_PATTERNS["jwplayer"]`. The pattern captures the
      URL inside `playlist: "<url>"` when the host is NOT on
      `cdn.jwplayer.com` / `feeds.jwplayer.com` /
      `content.jwplatform.com`, AND the URL looks like a feed
      (ends in `.json`/`.jsonp` or contains `/feed`, `/playlist`,
      `/config` path segments). The pattern deliberately does not
      match `file: "<url>"` (that's a stream URL, handled by
      `extract_player_configs` as a terminal candidate).
  * `bulk_downloader/__init__.py` — version → 3.66.23.
  * `tests/test_v3_66_23_phase4_jwplayer_selfhosted.py` — new, 53
    tests across six classes.
  * `tests/test_v3_66_18_phase4_jwplayer.py` — error-string update.
  * `tests/test_v3_66_20_phase4_jwplayer_feeds.py` — error-string update.

### Detection coverage

The new `config_url_attr` pattern was smoke-tested against ten
scenarios:

  * `playlist: "https://customer.example.com/feed.json"` → matches
  * `playlist: "https://api.site.com/feeds/abc?token=x"` → matches
  * `playlist: "https://video.site.com/playlist/v123"` → matches
  * `playlist: "https://api.site.com/config/abc?v=1"` → matches
  * `playlist: "https://video.example.com/api/feed.jsonp?callback=jw"` → matches
  * `playlist: "https://feeds.jwplayer.com/feeds/ABC123XY.json"` →
    NOT matched (cdn pattern wins, captures `feed_id` instead)
  * `<script src="https://cdn.jwplayer.com/v2/media/DEF456ZZ">` →
    NOT matched (cdn pattern wins, captures `media_id`)
  * `file: "https://x.com/master.m3u8"` → NOT matched (file: not
    playlist:, and stream extension)
  * `playlist: "https://x.com/clip.mp4"` → NOT matched (no
    feed-like marker)

### Signing posture

The resolver returns these tagged errors instead of attempting
bypass. The `scheme=` tag is stable for callers that want to route
embeds to needs_review with a structured reason.

  * `scheme=signed` — feed JSON contains `signedUrls`, `signingKey`,
    or similar top-level/per-entry markers; or unsigned fetch
    returns HTTP 401/403.
  * `scheme=widevine` / `scheme=fairplay` / `scheme=playready` /
    `scheme=clearkey` — feed JSON contains a per-entry
    `drm.<scheme>` block. Case-insensitive match on the key.

When a `signing_callback` is supplied on the embed dict, it's used
to fetch the config_url instead of `http_get`. A 401/403 from the
callback surfaces a credential-issue message (vs. the
"supply signing_callback" message when no callback was supplied).
DRM markers in a callback-fetched response still block — DRM is
out of scope regardless of how the feed was fetched.

### SSRF posture (unchanged from existing JWPlayer paths)

The default `http_get` has no SSRF guard. The existing JWPlayer
paths (cdn-media, feeds) are safe because their URLs are templated
against a hardcoded `cdn.jwplayer.com` host — only the id is
attacker-influenced. The new self-hosted path is different: the URL
itself comes from attacker-controlled HTML. Per session decision,
we match existing http_get behavior — no new guard. Tracked as an
OPEN_THREADS item for a future hardening pass. The only defensive
check we DO apply is rejecting non-http(s) schemes (data:,
javascript:, file:), which the existing paths never had to consider.

### Test status

```
tests/test_v3_66_23_phase4_jwplayer_selfhosted.py alone   53/53   PASS
tests/test_v3_66_18_phase4_jwplayer.py (regression)       64/64   PASS
tests/test_v3_66_20_phase4_jwplayer_feeds.py (regression) 22/22   PASS
tests/test_v3_66_16_phase4_p4_provider_resolve.py          8/8    PASS
v3.66.22 tight-proof set (8 files) + new file            334/334  PASS
```

One transient session_keeper failure was seen mid-run on the first
sweep and did not reproduce on the second sweep (or in isolation).
This is the same `lock.acquire(timeout=0.5)` sandbox-CPU-contention
transient flagged by the v3.66.22 handoff §A.

### What's NOT shipped (still deferred)

  * **YouTube `signatureCipher` decipher** — unchanged from v3.66.22.
  * **DRM playback** (Widevine / FairPlay / PlayReady licence
    acquisition + CDM integration) — out of scope per project
    posture. See `handoff/OPEN_THREADS.md` for the design discussion.
  * **JWPlayer `/media/<id>/sign` OTT-Web-App pattern** — operators
    who need this can wire it via `signing_callback`; the resolver
    itself doesn't call the sign endpoint.

## v3.66.21 — 2026-05-27 (Broader-sweep polluter cleanup)

**Closes the 8 broader-sweep test failures** flagged in the v3.66.20
handoff. Two distinct polluters, two surgical test-file patches, no
production code touched. All 8 listed failures now pass when run in
the broader sweep ordering that previously triggered them.

### Polluter 1 — `test_extension_endpoints.py::test_pair_works_when_bd_auth_token_set`

The `finally` block deleted `bulk_downloader.app` from `sys.modules`
without restoring it. The next test that did
`from bulk_downloader import app` reimported the module fresh,
creating a new `_app_cfg` dict object — but test files like
`test_u29_config_snapshot.py` that did
`from bulk_downloader import app as bd_app` at module load held
references to the **original** dict, now orphaned.

Same defect class as the v3.66.9 handoff's "44 test files with
autouse fixture that wiped `sys.modules` without restoring on
teardown" — this one was missed in that dedup.

Fix: save the union of `bulk_downloader.*` modules before the
`del`, restore them in the `finally`. Same pattern as conftest's
`bd_module_wipe` marker.

**Closed failures (4):**
- `test_u27_security_cluster::test_path_allowlist_enforcing_mode`
- `test_u27_security_cluster::test_path_allowlist_permissive_mode`
- `test_u28_config_cache::test_cache_clear_all_targets`
- `test_u29_config_snapshot::test_snapshot_restore_round_trip`

### Polluter 2 — `test_v3_53_phase6.py`

Three issues stacked into one defect:

1. **`_cleanup_singleton_server` was `scope="session"`** — its
   `sys.modules` restore only ran at the very end of the entire
   pytest session. Every downstream file saw `bulk_downloader.*`
   modules pointing at this file's freshly-reimported copies.
2. **Dead code in `_get_server`** — lines 109-112 of the pre-fix
   file held the original sys.modules restore logic, but
   unreachable because `return base` ran on line 108. The intent
   was clear, the wiring was severed.
3. **`_BD_MODULES_AT_IMPORT` was incomplete** — captured at file
   load (during pytest collection), it didn't include
   `bulk_downloader.runner`, `login`, or `db` because nothing had
   imported them yet at that moment. The teardown then deleted
   those modules without restoring them, orphaning class/function
   references in downstream test files like
   `test_v3_62_2_login_fallback.py` that import them at file load.

Specifically the chain that broke login_fallback's
`mock.patch("bulk_downloader.runner.do_login", ...)`:
- v3_53 collection runs → `_BD_MODULES_AT_IMPORT` snapshots (no runner)
- login_fallback collection runs → does `from bulk_downloader.runner
  import SiteRunner`, adds runner to sys.modules
- v3_53 tests execute → `_get_server` wipes sys.modules, reimports app
  (transitively reimports runner — new module object)
- v3_53 teardown restores `_BD_MODULES_AT_IMPORT` (no runner key, so
  runner stays deleted)
- login_fallback tests run → `mock.patch("bulk_downloader.runner.do_login")`
  triggers fresh import → mock patches the NEW runner module — but
  login_fallback's `SiteRunner` reference is still the OLD class from
  the now-orphaned middle import

Fix:
- Changed `_cleanup_singleton_server` from `scope="session"` to
  `scope="module"` so the teardown runs after this file's last test
  rather than at session end.
- Removed the dead unreachable lines.
- Eagerly pre-imported `bulk_downloader.app`, `runner`, `login`, `db`
  at the top of the test file so `_BD_MODULES_AT_IMPORT` snapshots a
  complete view of the modules the boot will wipe.

**Closed failures (4):**
- `test_v3_62_2_login_fallback::test_failed_templated_login_falls_back_to_manual`
- `test_v3_62_2_login_fallback::test_failed_login_without_template_does_not_fall_back`
- `test_v3_62_2_login_fallback::test_worker_relogin_failure_does_not_open_manual_window`
- `test_v3_62_2_login_fallback::test_successful_templated_login_does_not_fall_back`

## v3.66.20 — 2026-05-27 (Phase 4 complete — YouTube + JWPlayer feeds + CSP headers)

**Phase 4 is done.** Three items land in one release that close the
remaining Phase 4 gaps from the v3.66.19 handoff: the last provider
(YouTube) gets a real resolver, the JWPlayer feeds endpoint variant
ships, and Phase 12's response-header CSP detection lands. All five
provider resolvers (Vimeo, Wistia, JWPlayer cloud + feeds, Brightcove,
YouTube) are now real implementations on `provider_resolve` — no
stubs.

### P4 — YouTube resolver

`resolve_youtube(ids, *, embed=None, http_get) -> (candidates, error)`
in `bulk_downloader/provider_resolve.py`. Promoted from stub.

**Design call.** No subprocess (no `yt-dlp` shell-out — preserves
deep_detect's "pure HTML → report" contract), no API key (the official
YouTube Data API doesn't return playable stream URLs, only metadata),
no signature deciphering. Instead: GET the watch page, locate
`ytInitialPlayerResponse` via brace-balanced slice (string-literal
aware), parse `streamingData`. This handles the common cases (HLS,
unsigned progressive) without taking ownership of YouTube's rotating
player JS.

Schema mapping:

  * `streamingData.hlsManifestUrl` → one HLS candidate
    (`source_type="youtube_resolved_hls"`, score 90)
  * `streamingData.formats[]` entries with a direct `url` → one
    progressive candidate per format (`source_type="youtube_resolved"`,
    score `80 + height // 100`)
  * `streamingData.adaptiveFormats[]` entries with a direct `url` →
    one candidate per format (`source_type="youtube_resolved_adaptive"`)
  * Entries whose only addressable field is `signatureCipher` → skipped
    with a counted-skip count surfaced in the error string if no
    direct-URL candidates were found

**Failure modes (all explicit, never silent):**

  * `playabilityStatus != "OK"` → error string carries status + reason
    (LOGIN_REQUIRED, UNPLAYABLE, AGE_VERIFICATION_REQUIRED, etc.)
  * No `ytInitialPlayerResponse` → "may be a consent interstitial,
    age-gate, or region block"
  * Only signed formats → "N signed format(s) but no direct-url formats;
    signatureCipher decipher is out of scope"

Each candidate carries `itag`, `mimeType`-derived codec, optional
`fps` and `contentLength`, and a `reasons` line with the quality
label and itag.

### P4 — JWPlayer feeds endpoint

`resolve_jwplayer` extended to handle `ids["feed_id"]` (no
`media_id`). Hits `cdn.jwplayer.com/v2/playlists/<feed_id>`, the
multi-media feed endpoint. Response shape mirrors the cloud-media
JSON: `playlist[]` array of entries, each with a `sources` array in
the same shape as cloud-media sources.

Refactored to share the per-source classifier between the two paths:

  * `_jwplayer_emit_sources(sources, embed_url, label_prefix, extra_fields)`
    new internal helper, used by both `_resolve_jwplayer_media`
    (cloud-hosted) and `_resolve_jwplayer_feed` (feeds endpoint)
  * Feeds candidates are tagged with `playlist_index` (0-based position
    in the feed) and `playlist_media_id` (the entry's `mediaid`) so
    consumers can re-group flat candidate lists by source video
  * Reason strings prefixed with `"JWPlayer feed[i]"` instead of
    `"JWPlayer cdn"` so callers can distinguish the two paths

Embeds with both `media_id` and `feed_id` route to media_id (the
cloud-hosted path takes priority — it's the more specific identifier).

The "self-hosted with playerKey" sub-variant is still deferred — it
uses a different config endpoint and signature scheme. For embeds
arriving with neither id, the resolver returns
`([], "missing media_id or feed_id")` (was
`"missing media_id (feeds endpoint not yet supported)"` in v3.66.18).

### P12 — CSP from response headers

v3.66.15 shipped meta-tag CSP detection; this release wires the
`Content-Security-Policy` and `Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only`
HTTP response headers through the deep_detect pipeline. New kwarg
`response_headers: Optional[dict] = None` on `deep_detect(...)` and
threaded through `deep_detect_live(...)`.

**Merge semantics** (per `_merge_csp`):

  * Both inputs None → result None (legacy callers see no change)
  * One input present → result is that input (no merge needed)
  * Both present → per-directive intersection. A directive present in
    both contributes only sources the two layers agree on; a directive
    present in only one is preserved as-is. Disjoint allow-lists become
    `['none']` (deny-all) to model the browser's "must satisfy ALL
    policies" semantics.

**Header parser** (`_extract_csp_from_headers`):

  * Case-insensitive header lookup
  * Enforcing header (`Content-Security-Policy`) wins over
    report-only when both are present
  * Comma-separated multi-policy values are parsed and intersected
    (one header value can carry multiple policies per spec)
  * Non-string header values, empty values, and unparseable directives
    all return None — no half-formed CSP dicts ever leave the function

The merged `out["csp"]` dict gains a `sources: {meta, header}` field
preserving the originals so callers (notably the UI) can show *which*
layer flagged a violation. `from: "header_enforcing"` /
`"header_report_only"` is also surfaced on the header CSP for UI
attribution.

`_apply_csp_annotations` is unchanged — it consumes
`csp["directives"]` and treats meta-only, header-only, and merged
inputs identically.

### Behaviour changes from v3.66.19

  * `resolve_youtube({"video_id": id}, ...)` now does real
    resolution instead of returning `([], None)`. Two tests in
    `test_v3_66_16_phase4_p4_provider_resolve.py` that asserted the
    stub behaviour are updated; their new assertion is on the
    "unknown provider" path which still passes through silently.
  * `resolve_jwplayer({"feed_id": id}, ...)` now does real feeds-endpoint
    resolution instead of returning the
    `"feeds endpoint not yet supported"` error. The
    `test_feed_id_only_returns_explanatory_error` test in
    `test_v3_66_18_phase4_jwplayer.py` is renamed
    `test_feed_id_only_routes_to_feeds_endpoint` with new assertions.
  * `deep_detect(...)` accepts a new kwarg `response_headers`.
    Defaults to `None`; omitted callers see no behaviour change.
  * `deep_detect_live(...)` accepts the same kwarg and threads it
    through to `deep_detect`.
  * `out["csp"]` may now include `sources`, `from` keys when header
    CSP is present. The legacy `policy` and `directives` keys are
    unchanged in shape and semantics.

## v3.66.19 — 2026-05-27 (Phase 4 P4 continued — JWPlayer + Brightcove)

**Two resolvers land in one release.** JWPlayer cloud-hosted and
Brightcove now have real implementations on `provider_resolve`,
bringing the dispatcher to **four** real resolvers (Vimeo, Wistia,
JWPlayer, Brightcove) and one remaining stub (YouTube). Both follow
the Wistia template established in v3.66.17 — same scoring, same
error contract, same cache parity.

### P4 — JWPlayer cloud-hosted resolver

`resolve_jwplayer(ids, *, embed=None, http_get) -> (candidates, error)`
in `bulk_downloader/provider_resolve.py`. Hits
`cdn.jwplayer.com/v2/media/<media_id>` — the cloud-hosted product's
canonical media JSON, anonymous reads work for unsigned content.

Schema mapping (per `playlist[0].sources[]`):

  * `type` `application/vnd.apple.mpegurl` (or `.m3u8` extension) →
    one HLS master candidate (`source_type="jwplayer_resolved_hls"`,
    score 90)
  * `type` `application/dash+xml` (or `.mpd` extension) → one DASH
    candidate (`source_type="jwplayer_resolved_dash"`, score 90)
  * `type` `video/mp4` (or `.mp4` extension) → one progressive
    candidate per source (`source_type="jwplayer_resolved"`, score
    80 + height // 100)
  * Everything else (still images, audio-only) skipped silently

The two **other** JWPlayer variants (feeds-endpoint and
self-hosted-with-playerKey) are deferred — they have different
schemas and need their own fixtures. Feeds-only embeds get a clear
`"feeds endpoint not yet supported"` error so operators see what's
actionable.

#### deep_detect plumbing for JWPlayer

JWPlayer was missing from three places `deep_detect.py` consults
before resolution. v3.66.19 adds them:

  * `SOURCE_TYPES` — adds `"jwplayer_embed"` so classify_url can
    bucket JWPlayer URLs.
  * `PROVIDERS` — adds `("jwplayer", (cdn.jwplayer.com,
    content.jwplatform.com, feeds.jwplayer.com, jwpsrv.com),
    (jwplayer, jwplatform, ...))` so the provider-host check in
    `classify_url` tags JWPlayer hosts.
  * `_PROVIDER_ID_PATTERNS["jwplayer"]` — patterns for:
      - `cdn.jwplayer.com/v2/media/<media_id>` (canonical)
      - `cdn.jwplayer.com/players/<media_id>-<player_id>.html` (iframe
        embed shape — the first id is the media)
      - `feeds.jwplayer.com/feeds/<feed_id>`
      - Inline `mediaid:` / `playlistid:` attrs in jwplayer().setup()

### P4 — Brightcove resolver

`resolve_brightcove(ids, *, embed=None, http_get) -> (candidates, error)`
in `bulk_downloader/provider_resolve.py`. Hits
`edge.api.brightcove.com/playback/v1/accounts/<account>/videos/<video>`
— the Playback API used by Brightcove's JS player.

This is the **first resolver requiring an out-of-band credential**.
The Playback API mandates a `BCOV-Policy: <policy_key>` header,
account-scoped (same key works for every video in the account). The
key is read from two sources, in this order:

  1. `ids["policy_key"]` — populated by `_extract_provider_ids` from
     `policyKey: "..."` inline JS or `data-policy-key="..."` attrs in
     the surrounding page (added in v3.66.19).
  2. `embed["policy_key"]` — caller-supplied fallback for sites that
     stash policy keys in site config rather than the page itself.

If neither source has a key, `resolve_brightcove` returns
`([], "missing policy_key ...")` immediately without a network call.
The 401 path also explicitly names the policy key as the likely
cause so operators can fix it.

The default `_default_http_get` doesn't know about the BCOV-Policy
header. Production callers must wrap the default with the policy
header or inject a custom `http_get`. This is the first resolver
where the production wiring is the caller's responsibility — the
test path injects via `http_get` as usual.

Schema mapping (per `sources[]`):

  * `type` `application/x-mpegURL` (or `.m3u8`) → HLS master
    (`source_type="brightcove_resolved_hls"`, score 90)
  * `type` `application/dash+xml` (or `.mpd`) → DASH
    (`source_type="brightcove_resolved_dash"`, score 90)
  * `container == "MP4"` or `type == "video/mp4"` (or `.mp4`) →
    progressive (`source_type="brightcove_resolved"`, score
    80 + height // 100)

#### Tests

  * `tests/test_v3_66_18_phase4_jwplayer.py` — 37 tests across 3
    classes (resolver / dispatcher integration / extract_provider_embeds).
  * `tests/test_v3_66_19_phase4_brightcove.py` — 32 tests across 3
    classes, mirroring the JWPlayer layout. Includes specific
    coverage for the new policy_key input channels and the 401-vs-403
    distinction.

#### Files changed

  * `bulk_downloader/__init__.py` — 3.66.17 → 3.66.19
  * `bulk_downloader/provider_resolve.py` — +`resolve_jwplayer`,
    +`resolve_brightcove` (~420 lines added across both resolvers)
  * `bulk_downloader/deep_detect.py` — +`jwplayer_embed` to
    SOURCE_TYPES; +`jwplayer` to PROVIDERS;
    +`_PROVIDER_ID_PATTERNS["jwplayer"]`;
    +`policy_key` patterns to existing `_PROVIDER_ID_PATTERNS["brightcove"]`
  * `tests/test_v3_66_16_phase4_p4_provider_resolve.py` —
    `test_brightcove_jwplayer_stubs` narrowed to only assert the
    YouTube stub remains (the other two were promoted).

#### Phase 4 status after v3.66.19

  * Real resolvers: Vimeo, Wistia, **JWPlayer**, **Brightcove**.
  * Stubs remaining: **YouTube only**. YouTube wants a design
    decision before landing (subprocess to `yt-dlp` vs. official
    API).
  * JWPlayer feeds endpoint and self-hosted-with-playerKey variants
    deferred — separate fixtures, separate session.

## v3.66.17 — 2026-05-27 (Phase 4 P4 continued + cache)

**Wistia resolution lands.** Second provider on the
`provider_resolve` surface, plus the persistent resolution cache the
v3.66.16 handoff sketched. Also fixes a pre-existing
`extract_provider_embeds` bug that the new Wistia corpus fixture
surfaced.

### P4 — Wistia resolver

`resolve_wistia(ids, *, embed=None, http_get) -> (candidates, error)`
in `bulk_downloader/provider_resolve.py`. Hits
`fast.wistia.net/embed/medias/<hashed_id>.json` — the same JSON
endpoint Wistia's JS player uses, no auth required for public media.

Schema mapping:

  * `media.assets[]` entries with `type` in
    `{original, mp4_video, md_mp4_video, hd_mp4_video, iphone_video}`
    or `content_type == "video/mp4"` → one progressive candidate each
    (`source_type="wistia_resolved"`, score 80 + height//100)
  * `media.assets[]` entries with `type == "hls_playlist"` or
    `content_type` containing `mpegurl` → one HLS master candidate
    (`source_type="wistia_resolved_hls"`, score 90)
  * Everything else (still_image, flash_*, etc.) skipped silently

Failures are reported, never raised — same contract as Vimeo.

### Persistent resolution cache

The `resolve_provider_embed` dispatcher now reads cached resolutions
from `site_memory['provider_embeds_seen'][<provider>]['last_resolved']`
and short-circuits the network call on hit. New kwargs:

  * **`cache_write: Optional[Callable[[str, str, str, float], None]]
    = None`** — callback invoked on successful network resolution
    with `(provider, embed_id, best_url, timestamp)`. The
    dispatcher does NOT write into the config directly; the caller
    threads this in to avoid a `provider_resolve → learn` import
    cycle.
  * **`cache_ttl_seconds: float = 21600`** (6 hours) — absolute
    expiry, not sliding. Cached signed URLs typically last
    3–6 hours, so this is conservative without being annoying.

Cache hits surface a single candidate with:

  * `source_type: "<provider>_resolved_cached"` (e.g.
    `vimeo_resolved_cached`, `wistia_resolved_cached`)
  * `found_in: "provider_resolved_cache:<provider>"`
  * `cached: True` — distinguishable from fresh resolutions
  * `score: 85` — between progressive (80+) and HLS (90), so a fresh
    HLS still wins over a cached single rendition

**Tie-breaker policy (new spec):** when writing the cache and two
candidates tie on score, prefer HLS. Rationale: a single playlist URL
covers all renditions, so a stale signed token doesn't trap callers
at one specific quality. Without this, a 1080p MP4 (80+10=90) would
beat the HLS master (90) on simple `max(key=score)`. Explicit test
coverage in `TestWistiaCacheWrite::test_callback_prefers_hls_on_score_tie`.

### `learn.make_provider_cache_writer(config)`

Factory in `bulk_downloader/learn.py` returning a callback bound to a
config dict. Mutates
`config['learned']['deep_detect']['provider_embeds_seen']
   [<provider>]['last_resolved'] = {id, url, at}`
in the exact shape `_cache_lookup` reads. Auto-initializes the
`learned.deep_detect` block when absent, so callers can wire this
unconditionally without checking for first-run state.

Returns a no-op for non-dict input. Defensively validates every
argument; cache-write failures are silent (a write failure must
never crash a successful resolution).

### `deep_detect.extract_provider_embeds` — loader-script filter

**Pre-existing bug, fixed.** Stage 1 of `extract_provider_embeds`
was producing useless `provider_embeds` entries for provider library
loader scripts (`fast.wistia.com/assets/external/E-v1.js`,
YouTube's `iframe_api`, etc.) — these match a provider's host but
aren't per-video embeds, so they polluted the candidate list and
crowded out the real embed.

Fix: a narrow allow-list of known loader-path substrings is skipped
in Stage 1. Stage 3 (element-attrs scan) still finds the real embed
when present. Conservative — only matches verified loader paths, not
"any id-less provider URL" (which would break legitimate YouTube
short-id embeds).

Surfaced by the new `08_wistia_embed` corpus fixture; would have hit
any v3.66.16 user with a stock Wistia embed.

### Tests

  * **New:** `tests/test_v3_66_17_phase4_wistia_and_cache.py` — 41
    tests across `TestWistiaResolver`, `TestWistiaCacheRead`,
    `TestWistiaCacheWrite`, `TestProviderCacheWriterFactory`,
    `TestCacheIntegration`. All offline / deterministic.
  * **New:** `tests/fixtures/deep_detect/08_wistia_embed/` — corpus
    fixture for the canonical Wistia embed shape
    (`<div class="wistia_async_<id>">` + script loader + courtesy
    `<a href>` link). Tests `extract_provider_embeds` end-to-end.
  * **Updated:** `test_v3_66_16_phase4_p4_provider_resolve.py`'s
    `test_brightcove_wistia_jwplayer_stubs` → narrowed to
    `test_brightcove_jwplayer_stubs` (Wistia is no longer a stub).

### Test counts

v3.66.x suite: **756 passed, 1 skipped** (was 714/1 in v3.66.16).
The +42 covers the new 41 tests + the renamed stub test. dd-replay
corpus: **8/8 OK** (was 7/7). Existing 7 fixture expected.json files
are byte-identical to v3.66.16 — the loader-script filter doesn't
affect them.

### What's NOT in this release

Three providers still stub-only on the `provider_resolve` surface:
**YouTube** (needs a design decision on shelling out to yt-dlp),
**Brightcove** (needs policy-key plumbing through the dispatcher
signature), **JWPlayer** (multi-shape: feeds vs cloud vs
self-hosted, three sub-paths). Each is roughly one session's work
following the Vimeo / Wistia template — but they're not
drop-ins, hence "Phase 4 P4 continued" rather than "Phase 4
complete."

Also: the `extract_provider_embeds` Stage 3 dedup means a page with
both an `<a href>` link AND a `wistia_async_` div surfaces only the
first finding. Both carry the same `hashed_id`, so resolution works
either way — but if a future site uses the div *without* the link,
we'd want Stage 3 to fire. The corpus fixture currently exercises
the link path; a future Wistia-without-link fixture could verify
the div path independently.
