### Bonus: full-suite green at cut

End-of-session full-suite run on the cut tree turned up 3 failures
in `tests/test_v3_43_55_csrf_bootstrap.py`. Diagnosis traced to
`tests/test_u28_config_cache.py::test_cache_clear_single_target`,
which sets `bulk_downloader.app._INDEX_HTML_CACHE = "<cached>"`
(a module-level global) without restoring it. Downstream tests that
hit `GET /` then see the poisoned cache, the index handler's
`html.replace("<!--CSRF_META-->", csrf_meta, 1)` becomes a no-op,
and the response body is the literal string `"<cached>"` with no
meta tag — exactly what the failing assertions reported.

Bug was latent in environments where the harness ran each test file
in its own subprocess (parallel mode, nproc>=2). The sandbox is
nproc=1, so `--workers` resolves to 1, the harness falls back to
in-process serial, and every poisoned global leaks across files.
Same defect class would also bite anyone running the suite with
`--workers=1` on any host.

Fix: wrap both `test_u28_config_cache.py::test_cache_clear_all_targets`
and `test_cache_clear_single_target` in try/finally that saves and
restores `_INDEX_HTML_CACHE`, `_FFMPEG_CACHE`, and
`api_status._disk_cache`. Final full-suite run after the fix:
**5080/5080 passing, 0 failures, 0 skipped.**

### Follow-on fixes after suite run

**v3.66.5 backlog #6 — extension_live flaky test.** Applied the
two-line fix from `handoff/v3_66_5_flaky_test_diagnosis.md`:
`_BDServerThread` no longer pre-allocates a port via the
TOCTOU-prone `_free_port()` helper. Instead it passes `port=0`
directly to `werkzeug.serving.make_server`, letting the kernel
atomically assign an ephemeral port at bind time, and reads
`self._server.server_port` afterward. No window during which a
sibling worker can grab the same port and intercept the test's
HTTP traffic. The `_free_port()` helper is retained for back-compat
but is no longer called from `_BDServerThread`. After fix, all 7
tests in `tests/test_extension_live.py` pass — including the
previously-flaky `test_lookup_url_surfaces_blocked_state`, which
also ran (rather than skipped) because the sandbox has
Chromium-for-Testing installed.

**Audit follow-up on the u28 fix.** Grepped the test tree for the
same module-global-poison pattern. Most hits were already correctly
wrapped in save/restore (the `_app_cfg["path_allowlist"]` family
in test_t10/t11/t15/t17/u27) or run under autouse fixtures that
purge `sys.modules` between tests (the v3_66_3/4/5 family). One
real leaker found: `tests/test_u29_config_snapshot.py::test_snapshot_restore_round_trip`
mutates `_app_cfg["log_level"]` and `_app_cfg["global_max_concurrent"]`
without restoration. Applied the same try/finally pattern as the
u28 fix.

**Second audit pass — sys.modules purgers.** Grep'd for tests that
do `del sys.modules['bulk_downloader.X']` without a matching
autouse / setup_method that re-isolates. Found 4 high-concern
suspects: test_v3_43_80_modules.py, test_v3_43_80_runner_hooks.py,
test_v3_53_phase6.py, test_v3_60_phase12.py. Fixed the first two
by adding an autouse fixture that saves env (`BD_INSTALL_DIR`,
`BD_DISABLE_KEEPALIVE`) and the `bulk_downloader.*` module snapshot
at test entry, then restores both at teardown. The latter two were
left alone — they spin up daemon-thread Flask singletons whose
lifecycle is tightly coupled to env state, so the safe fix is
non-trivial. Listed as remaining work in the v3.66.7 backlog.

### Implementation notes worth remembering

- **`patch.dict(sys.modules, ...)` does NOT affect `from package import name`.**
  Once `bulk_downloader.deep_detect` is imported, the parent package
  gets a `.deep_detect` attribute. `from . import deep_detect` reads
  that attribute, bypassing sys.modules. Use
  `patch("bulk_downloader.deep_detect", ...)` (attribute patching)
  instead. This bit the v3.66.6 test suite for one cycle before the
  diagnosis landed.
- The runner's `_try_deep_detect_fallback` deliberately uses the
  OFFLINE `deep_detect()` analyzer rather than `deep_detect_live()`.
  The runner already owns a live browser; spawning another HTTP
  client for probe HEAD requests on every failed scrape would
  multiply traffic. The offline analyzer covers the common case
  (HTML has the info we need) and is much cheaper.

### Deferred (still network-blocked)

- **Backlog #2 — `frontend/` `npm install`.** The new node kit
  (v20.18.0) and the new SPA kit closed the `spa/` gap. But
  `frontend/package.json` (the legacy D3 tree, 32 deps, distinct
  from `spa/`) still has an empty `node_modules`. A networked host
  needs to `cd frontend && ./node/bin/node ./node/lib/node_modules/npm/bin/npm-cli.js install`
  to populate it. Sandbox cannot.
- **Backlog #3 — `bdctl deep-detect` real-URL smoke testing.**
  Subcommand code-complete and unit-tested. End-to-end smoke
  against 3 sample sites needs network access.

## v3.66.5 — 2026-05-25

**The deep_detect feature: a 4180-line module that handles every
detection surface a single page might need — login forms, multi-
resolution download cards, HLS/DASH manifests, provider embeds,
state blobs, JSON-LD media, two-step POST workflows, trap links,
honeypots, DRM/CAPTCHA markers — and ranks the results into one
report. Wired into the runtime auto-pick path as a fourth mode
alongside the existing three.**

### What landed across v3.66.0 → v3.66.5

- **v3.66.0 — `auto_detect.detect_site_config`**: lightweight
  template-free selector discovery. Three input modes (live Page,
  pasted HTML, URL+fetch). Returns `{ok, source, learned: {login,
  download}, warnings, error}` in the same shape `_auto_pick_templates`
  already consumes. New global flag `template_auto_detect_mode` with
  three values (`static` default, `detect`, `detect_then_static`).
- **v3.66.1 — `deep_detect` core**: resolution-card extractor (the
  8K/4K/1080p picker pattern), URL classifier covering 50 source
  types, helpers for parsing dimensions, codec, fps, size, base64,
  URL normalization with `<base href>` support, JSON unicode escapes,
  percent-encoded URLs, protocol-relative.
- **v3.66.2 — manifest + provider + login parsers**: HLS master
  playlist parser (variants + alt audio + subtitles + encryption
  flags + low-latency markers), DASH MPD parser (per-Period
  Representation extraction, ContentProtection detection),
  state-blob extractor for Next.js / Nuxt / Apollo / Relay / Remix
  / SvelteKit / Redux / preloaded-state, provider embed extractor
  for 12 providers (Kaltura, Brightcove, Wistia, Vimeo, YouTube,
  Mux, Cloudflare Stream, Bunny Stream, Panopto, Vidyard,
  Dailymotion, SproutVideo), player-config extractor for Video.js,
  JWPlayer, Plyr, plus generic `sources: [...]` for Shaka /
  Bitmovin / THEOplayer / React Player / HLS.js / DASH.js, login
  scorer with 0-100 confidence + raw_score for distinguishing
  tied-at-ceiling forms, classifications for `form_password` /
  `passwordless` / `mfa` / `sso_oauth` / `saml` / `webauthn` /
  `device_code`, honeypot detector with duplicate-field detection
  and fake-submit-button detection.
- **v3.66.3 — orchestrator + Flask route**: `deep_detect()` master
  function that combines every detector into one ranked report
  with cross-cutting deduplication, `prefer_resolution` parameter
  ("highest" / "1080p" / "4k" / "8k" / ...) that boosts matches
  by +500 and penalizes overshoots by -300, blocker scanner
  (`scan_blockers`) for bot defenses + DRM + CAPTCHA + honeypots,
  trap-link penalizer rejecting ad/tracker hosts and off-screen
  decoys, two-step POST reveal detector for "Generate download
  link" workflows, JSON-LD media extractor with per-object detail,
  new `/api/dev/deep_detect` Flask route (POST body `{html,
  base_url, prefer_resolution}`; 4 MiB cap; honors `_dev_mode_guard`
  + `_check_csrf`).
- **v3.66.4 — Tier 2 runtime probes**: `deep_detect_live` layered
  on top of `deep_detect` with HEAD probing (Content-Disposition +
  Content-Type sniffing, promotes `unknown` URLs to
  `header_attachment` / `hls_manifest` / `dash_manifest` /
  `extensionless_file`), meta-refresh follow, async-export workflow
  polling (redirects, JSON `url` body, status-URL polling with
  bounded attempts and interval), filename hint capture from
  Content-Disposition (including RFC 5987 percent-decoded names),
  HEAD 405 → GET Range:0-0 retry, injectable HTTP client for
  testability.
- **v3.66.5 — runtime wiring + UI toggle + Tier 1 disclaimer**:
  Hard probe gate on DRM markers removed; instead a `disclaimer`
  field is emitted in `report["probes"]` carrying a human-readable
  advisory the UI can render as a banner — detection is heuristic
  and a user who knows their content is rights-cleared shouldn't
  be paternalistically blocked. The disclaimer copy explicitly
  acknowledges the heuristic nature of the markers. `'deep'` added
  as a fourth `template_auto_detect_mode` value with a `<deep-detect>`
  tag on applied templates so logs distinguish provenance.
  `to_site_config_block(report)` adapter translates a deep_detect
  report to the existing `{learned: {login, download}}` runtime
  schema. `snapshot_via_playwright(url)` helper added to
  `auto_detect`. Settings modal in `static/app.js` gained a
  Template auto-detect section with a four-option Mode dropdown
  and explanatory copy. `/api/global_config` validates the new
  field server-side (rejects unknown modes with 400 + a
  naming-the-valid-set error). `bdctl deep-detect` CLI command
  with `--url` / `--html FILE` / `--html -` (stdin) input modes,
  `--prefer-resolution`, `--live`, `--poll`, `--max-probes`,
  `--probe-timeout`, `--json` flags. Auto-JSON when stdout is
  piped, human table when interactive.

### Tests

240 new tests across six new files
(`test_v3_66_0_auto_detect.py` through
`test_v3_66_5_settings_ui.py`). Full suite at cut: 5044/5044 passing
across 248 test files.

## v3.65.1 — 2026-05-24

**Four delivery units: WCAG AA fix for amber-on-amber-soft text (A1),
D4 retirement of the legacy `/m` mobile route per D3_OPT_IN.md's
v3.65.0 schedule (slipped one release into v3.65.1), B4 manifest-
verifier self-reference fix, and B5 runtime-artifact exclusion
expansion — the latter includes a security finding (vapid_keys.json
was leaking into release zips built after suite execution).**

Counter at cut: 2 named candidate units (A1, D4) accumulated under
v3.65.0, plus 2 incidental units (B4, B5) caught while building this
release.

### Security note for v3.65.0 and earlier

If you built a release zip locally after running the suite (and
deployed that zip), **check whether vapid_keys.json is present in
the zip**:

```
unzip -l BulkDownloader_v<X_Y_Z>.zip | grep vapid_keys.json
```

If present, the zip contains a private key. Rotate the VAPID keypair
on any operator that received that build, and rebuild from clean.
Releases distributed through the canonical `/mnt/user-data/outputs/`
flow are likely unaffected — that flow built in a fresh tree before
suite execution — but local rebuilds may have leaked. B5 prevents
recurrence.

---

### Bug-fix track (4 units)

**A1 — amber-soft + amber text WCAG AA fix.** The `bg-amber-soft +
text-amber` pairing used across the SPA contrasted at 1.97:1 in light
mode, well below WCAG AA's 4.5:1 threshold. Dark mode was already
passing at 8.16:1. The finding was pre-existing — JobErrorModal,
CommandPalette, LogDiff, and the warning badge variant had been on
this pattern before v3.65.0 — but V1–V6 expanded the usage materially
(StatusPill amber tone, AttentionBanner hero card, SiteRow issue tint,
AddSiteWizard amber callouts).

Fix: a new `--amber-dim` token (`#92400e` in light mode, mirrors the
legacy `app.css` `--adim` value used in the pre-SPA UI) was added to
`frontend/src/index.css` `:root`, lifting contrast to 6.52:1. Dark
mode `--amber-dim` is `#fbbf24` (= `--amber`) — dark mode already
passed, but the token is provided symmetrically so consumers don't
have to mode-branch. Exposed as Tailwind utility `text-amber-dim` via
`frontend/tailwind.config.js`.

13 swap points across 10 SPA files: `StatusPill.tsx`, `ui/badge.tsx`,
`JobErrorModal.tsx`, `CommandPalette.tsx`, `AddSiteWizard.tsx`,
`AttentionBanner.tsx` (x3 — icon, h2, count badge), `LogDiff.tsx`
(x3 — alert Card, B-side labelColor, needs_review pill), `Advanced.tsx`,
`SiteDetail.tsx` (not-found eyebrow). The 9 standalone `text-amber`
sites that sit on regular surfaces (KPICard valueKind=warn,
ActivityRow Review label, TodayStatsCard Running stat, BySiteList
queued count, Queue Counter, LogDiff event-list warning labels x2,
Advanced status indicators x2, JobErrorModal event-list warnings)
were correctly NOT swapped — `--amber` on regular surface already
passes AA.

**D4 — /m legacy route retirement.** Per D3_OPT_IN.md's retirement
schedule (originally targeting v3.65.0; the v3.65.0 release-cut
shipped the visual track only, so D4 slipped to v3.65.1).

- `/m` and `/m/` now return an unconditional `302 → /m2/`. The U9
  opt-in branching is gone. The `_m2_opt_state` helper is no longer
  consulted in this handler.
- `/m/ops` and `/m/ops/` retire on the same schedule, also 302 to
  `/m2/`. The SPA covers per-site stop via its API (POST
  `/api/sites/<id>/stop`) — there's no admin workflow on the mobile
  UI that the SPA doesn't already cover.
- `/m2?ui=v1` no longer redirects back to `/m` — that would have
  looped with the new unconditional `/m`. The branch was removed
  entirely. Effect: a stale `bd_ui=v1` cookie on the SPA is now
  harmless (was already true on `/m2` per the U9 contract; the same
  is now true on `/m` since both routes terminate at the SPA).
- The legacy `mobile.html` and `m_ops.html` templates stay on disk
  for emergency rollback until v3.66.0 per the doc.
- The `_m2_opt_state`, `_m2_apply_opt_cookie`, `_M2_COOKIE_NAME`,
  `_M2_COOKIE_TTL` helpers are kept in `app.py` — the `?ui=v2` path
  on `/m2` still sets the cookie for back-compat. They may retire
  in v3.66.0 alongside the template removal.

Use 302 (Found), not 301 (Permanent). The route is permanent in
practice, but 301 caches aggressively in browsers — if a future
release ever needs to flip behaviour for hotfix reasons, 302 leaves
that door open.

The U9 contract tests in `tests/test_d3_u9_opt_in.py` were rewritten
to pin the v3.65.1 routing (23 tests, up from 19 in v3.65.0). New
pins: unconditional 302 on all `/m` variants including stale-v1-cookie,
`/m/ops` retirement, `/m2?ui=v1` no-loop, cookie attributes via
direct helper call, legacy templates still on disk.

**B4 — `tools/build_release.py` zip self-reference fix.** Latent
defect in the verifier flow surfaced when v3.65.1 was built in a tree
where the output dir IS the repo root. The builder writes the release
zip, then calls `zip_manifest_check(zip_path)` which walks
`root.rglob('*')` — by then the just-written zip is on disk and gets
reported as "in tree, missing from zip" (because a zip can't contain
itself). Fix: add `.zip` to `_MANIFEST_EXCLUDE_SUFFIXES` in
`bulk_downloader/dev_suite.py`. Any `*.zip` in the tree is either the
artifact we just wrote or a stray from a prior build — neither is
source. Pinned with 4 new tests in
`tests/test_v3_64_3_release_zip_excludes_runtime_sentinels.py`
(`TestReleaseZipsExcludedFromManifest`).

**B5 — runtime-artifact exclusion expansion (security).** v3.65.1's
first successful build (post-B4) shipped three runtime artifacts that
should never have been in the zip:

- `vapid_keys.json` — a PEM private key generated by the push-
  subscription module on first import of `bulk_downloader`. SHIPPING
  THIS IS A SECURITY ISSUE: any operator deploying a zip containing
  someone else's `vapid_keys.json` would have their web-push origin
  compromised. Same defect class as v3.64.3's `.integrity_last_run`
  finding; worse blast radius. Now in `_MANIFEST_EXCLUDE_NAMES`.
- `state/heartbeat.json` — written by `_heartbeat_to_disk_loop` in
  `app.py` (state dir is `mkdir(exist_ok=True)`'d at runtime, never
  source). Excluded via `state` in `_MANIFEST_EXCLUDE_DIRS` so any
  future state files are also caught.
- `test_singleton.db` — created by `test_v3_43_72_dedup.py` via
  `get_default_registry("test_singleton.db")` in cwd. Test artifact.
  Now in `_MANIFEST_EXCLUDE_NAMES`.

The pattern: any release zip built AFTER the suite has executed in
the same tree would have included these. Releases built in fresh
extractions (the canonical `/mnt/user-data/outputs/` flow) are likely
unaffected. v3.65.0 zip confirmed clean.

Pinned with 8 new tests in
`TestB5RuntimeArtifactsExcluded`. Two tests specifically verify the
exclusions are not substring-based — `tests/test_state_machine.py`
and `docs/vapid_keys_design.md` (hypothetical) must NOT be excluded.

### Documentation

- `D3_OPT_IN.md` rewritten to reflect "v3.65.1 — retirement landed"
  state. "How it works" table updated; original v3.64.x opt-in
  behaviour moved into a historical section. Emergency-rollback
  section added pointing to `bulk_downloader/templates/mobile.html`.

### Counter at session close

0 bug fixes toward next release. 0 feature units. v3.65.1 = 4 bug-fix
units total (A1, D4, B4, B5).

The threshold counter resets to 0/0 for v3.65.2.

fix: `tests/test_v3_64_3_d5a_prebuild_spa.py` was writing a Posix
`#!/bin/bash` stub at `<tmp>/npm` (no extension) and prepending
to PATH; on Windows, `shutil.which("npm")` honors PATHEXT and
skips bare-name files, walking on to find the real `npm.CMD` in
nodejs. The real npm ran against `{"name":"test"}` package.json
with no `build` script → fail. Fix: `os.name == "nt"` branch
writes `npm.cmd` with three cmd-batch behaviors
(`succeed_with_dist`, `succeed_no_dist`, `fail_install`)
mirroring the bash versions. Posix path unchanged.

**B2 — L33 `_orphans()` Linux fix (2a) + L20/L21 `_resolve_bd_home`
(2b).** Bundled as one delivery unit. L33 ("no-leaked-chromium")
sampled `/api/dev/leak_scan` looking for `orphan_chromium` /
`orphan_browsers` keys top-level and nested under `processes`.
The endpoint actually emits `processes.chromium` /
`processes.ffmpeg`; none of L33's candidate keys matched, so
`_orphans()` returned None on every sample and L33 WARN'd "could
not sample orphan-process count from /api/dev/leak_scan" on
every deploy since L33 was introduced. Fix: one-line extension
in `live_tests/checks.py::_orphans()` to recognize
`processes.chromium`, with `orphan_chromium`-named keys keeping
priority for future endpoint variants. L20/L21 (WAL invariants)
WARN'd on Windows with the tempdir DB-path message because
`live_tests/run.py:32` defaulted `--bd-home` to
`os.environ.get("BD_HOME") or os.getcwd()`. On Windows the
runner was invoked from a tempdir cwd without BD_HOME set, so
live tests looked for the DB at
`<tempdir>\downloader_history.db`. Fix: new
`_resolve_bd_home(cli_arg, base_url)` with explicit
first-hit-wins chain (CLI arg → BD_HOME env → `/api/dev/env` →
`/api/dev/proc` → `os.getcwd()` with WARN print). Each step
prints which one matched.

**B3 — L33 Windows-shape fallback.** Single delivery. B2's L33
extension assumed `processes.chromium` would be present on
Windows; in practice the upstream `_child_process_count()` in
`perf_lab.py` walks `/proc` which doesn't exist on Windows, so
its except branch returns `{}` — no `chromium` key at all. B2
couldn't handle that case; L33 WARN'd on Windows with "could
not sample orphan-process count" even though the endpoint
reported a clean `verdict: "no leak signals"` with empty
`findings`. Fix in `live_tests/checks.py::_orphans()`: when
`processes` is `{}` AND `verdict == "no leak signals"` AND
`findings == []`, trust the endpoint's self-verdict and return
0 (clean). On Linux nothing changes — the `chromium` key path
matches first. Two new contract tests in
`tests/test_u42_resource_live_tests.py`:
`test_l33_passes_on_windows_shape_empty_procs_with_no_leak_verdict`
(pins the new PASS path) and
`test_l33_does_not_pass_on_empty_procs_with_actual_findings`
(pins that empty procs + real findings still WARNs honestly —
the verdict-trust path doesn't mask actual leaks).

**Uninstaller maintenance (NOT a delivery unit, but in this
release).** `uninstall_windows.bat` and `uninstall_linux.sh`
rewritten to cover the full install surface: regular + dev
install dirs, Desktop shortcut, Start Menu, Playwright cache,
pip cache, Ollama runtime + models, AppData / `~/.config` dirs.
Operator confirmed the Windows uninstall worked on the live VM.

### Feature track — D3 visual redesign (V1–V7)

SPA-only; no legacy `/` UI changes; one Python touch for a
structurally honest worker-count display.

**V1 — Token foundation.** New `StatusPill` primitive (5 tones, 3
sizes, `asToggle` with `aria-pressed` semantics). `PageHeader`
extended with `variant: "compact" | "display"` + `statusLine` +
`belowStatus`. `AppShell` accepts and forwards header-variant props.
`BottomTabBar` floating-pill restyle. No new dependencies.

**V2 + V2.1 — Home redesign + workers_total backend extension.**
Hero `AttentionBanner` with amber-soft surface and full-width
dark-ink "Resolve →" button. `TodayStatsCard` tri-stat layout with
ACTIVITY eyebrow and `opacity-40` for zero values. `KPICard` polish
(`font-bold tracking-tighter`, opacity-40 empty state).
`ThroughputSparkline` eyebrow polish. New default mobile and desktop
layouts in `useDashboardLayout`. `DEFAULT_WIDGET_IDS` adds
`disk_free` (4→5 widgets). `Home.tsx` flips to
`headerVariant="display"` with a 3-pill status row. Backend:
extracted `compute_worker_counts(runners) -> dict` helper in
`app_widgets_api.py`. `/api/dashboard/v2` now emits `workers_active`
+ `workers_total` alongside back-compat `active_workers`. The
"workers_total is None on empty fleet — never the magic 16"
invariant now applies to BOTH `/api/widgets/data` and
`/api/dashboard/v2` via the shared helper. `DashboardV2` type
extended; status line reads new fields, falls back to
`"{N} workers active"` when `workers_total` is null/undefined.
Two new contract tests in `test_d3_u2_v2_endpoints.py`.

**V3 — Sites + AddSiteWizard.** `Sites.tsx` filter strip swaps the
Tabs primitive (role=tablist, paired tabpanels expected) for a
StatusPill toggle row (button + aria-pressed) — Tabs without
tabpanels was a minor a11y lie; filter UI maps cleanly to toggle
buttons. Four filters: All/Active/Paused/Issues. Amber-soft tint
on `SiteRow` when `captcha_pending || auth_state === "expired"`.
Dashed "Add another site" footer card with 3-word subtitle.
`AddSiteWizard` gains a 3-segment decorative stepper (NOT gated —
the debounced full-draft POST to `/api/sites/validate` is FROZEN
by `test_d3_u4_add_site_wizard_calls_validate`), "Use a template
instead" callout, glass-blur footer.
`test_d3_u4_sites_uses_filter_state` updated to enforce the
docstring's *intent* (four filter labels + Filter union +
StatusPill + asToggle) rather than the Tabs primitive name —
brittle primitive-name pins are an anti-pattern.

**V4 — Queue typography polish.** Counter restyle (`text-3xl
font-bold tabular tracking-tighter` numbers, `opacity-40` for zero).
Section eyebrows `tracking-wider`. Percentage `font-semibold` in
one line. `WaitingJobRow` padding `p-2.5 → p-3`, filename
`font-semibold`. All pointer events, `onOpen`, `onToggleSelect`,
and no-swipe-library contracts preserved across both selection-mode
and swipe-mode variants.

**V5 — Activity polish; Settings audited.** `Activity.tsx` window
strip swaps Tabs primitive for StatusPill toggle row (24h/7d/30d/
All — same swap rationale as V3). Headline card typography polish.
`ActivityRow` filename `font-medium → font-semibold text-ink`.
Settings was reviewed and NOT edited: `SettingSection` already
uses the V2/V4 patterns (`tracking-wider` eyebrows, `font-medium`
labels); the Count/Percent toggle uses `role="radiogroup"` +
`role="radio"` + `aria-checked` and stays that way — radiogroup
(mutex from a fixed set) is semantically distinct from StatusPill
asToggle (independently togglable button + aria-pressed); visual
similarity is not a license to weaken semantics.

**V6 — DesktopShell display variant + SiteDetail not-found polish.**
`DesktopShell` extended with `variant: "compact" | "display"` +
`statusLine` + `belowStatus` props matching PageHeader. Renders
`text-2xl font-bold` heading + status line + pills row in display
mode; compact preserved as default. `AppShell` now forwards
`headerVariant` / `headerStatusLine` / `headerBelowStatus` to BOTH
PageHeader AND DesktopShell — pre-V6, these props were dropped on
desktop, silently downgrading display-variant Home to compact at
the lg breakpoint, and a mobile-only test sweep would not have
caught it. `SiteDetail` "Site not found" card polished to match
the V2 AttentionBanner pattern. All four b3 e2e contracts
preserved (`Site not found`, `Back to sites`, `Delete {name}`
aria-label, `Open widget library for this site` aria-label).

**v3.65.0 sequencing — Path B.** D4's `/m` unconditional 302
redirect was considered for this cut and rejected. v3.65.0 ships
visual-only; the legacy `/m` redirect arc ships separately as
v3.65.1. Cleaner rollback story; one risk surface at a time.

**Process notes.** The five-unit full-suite gate was deferred to
unit 10 by an explicit one-time operator directive in the V5
session. This release-cut runs `tools/build_release.py`'s release
gate (full suite from the extracted zip) which satisfies the
deferred gate at the same moment the release ships. The directive
was one-time and does NOT establish precedent.

**Frozen contracts preserved (verification log).** All audited via
per-unit affected-test sweeps and a static re-audit at release
cut: WIDGET_IDS = `attention/today/throughput/now-running/by-site`;
POST `/api/dashboard/v2/resolve` + `role="alert"` on AttentionBanner;
`aria-label="Open {site.name}"` exact regex on SiteRow (b3 e2e);
`onToggleSelect` + `selected?: boolean` on SiteRow + WaitingJobRow;
pointer events + `onOpen` + no swipe library on WaitingJobRow;
`pctOverride` on RunningJobRow; `useQueueStream` + `onMutate` in
Queue; POST `/api/sites/validate` + `useDebouncedValue` +
`role="alert"` in AddSiteWizard; `workers_total === null` on empty
fleet (now extended to `/api/dashboard/v2`); all Activity contracts
(export.csv, debouncer, 4 window strings, sparkline prop); all four
SiteDetail b3 e2e pins; `bd-dashboard-layout-${siteId}` per-site
namespace; `compute_worker_counts` shared helper between two
endpoints.

**Known pre-existing finding (deferred to v3.65.1).** The
amber-soft surface + amber text pattern (`bg-amber-soft text-amber`)
contrasts at 1.97:1 in light mode — fails WCAG AA. This is a
pre-existing condition: the pattern is also used by `JobErrorModal`,
`CommandPalette`, `LogDiff`, and the warning badge variant, all of
which predate V1–V6. V1–V6 did expand its use (StatusPill amber
tone, hero AttentionBanner, SiteRow issue tint). Dark mode passes
AA at 8.16:1. Fix in v3.65.1: add an `--amber-dim` token in
`frontend/src/index.css` (the legacy `app.css` already has one) and
swap amber-soft text instances to `text-amber-dim`. The `opacity-40`
zero-state pattern also falls below AA Large in light mode by
design — empty values are intentionally subordinate, not a defect.

**Suite baseline at v3.65.0:** **4797 / 4797 pass / 0 fail /
0 skip** expected on stash (was 4793 at v3.64.5; +2 from V2.1's
new dashboard_v2 worker contract tests in
`test_d3_u2_v2_endpoints.py`, +2 from B3's L33 Windows-shape
contract tests in `test_u42_resource_live_tests.py`). Per-unit
affected-test sweeps live-verified during each unit (297 cases
across V2–V6).

v3.64.2, v3.64.3, v3.64.4). The standing process note continues to

What landed.

* **A.1 restore (KB optimization inline `# INV-NNN` tags).**
  Originally produced 2026-05-22 alongside the A.2 compaction;
  verified absent across v3.63.10 / v3.64.0 / v3.64.1 / v3.64.2 /
  v3.64.3 zips. The handoff state never integrated into the
  release line. Restored as of this cut: 19 inline tags + 8
  file-top markers + 2 INV-003 explanatory comments + 4
  pre-existing dev_suite.py tags = **33 total `# INV-` lines**
  across 10 source files (`session_keeper.py`, `runner.py`,
  `dev_suite.py`, `db.py`, `heuristic_scoring.py`, `detect.py`,
  `secrets_store.py`, `vpn_config.py`, `extractors.py`,

  `tests/test_inv_tags_not_regressed.py` with `INV_TAG_FLOOR=33`
  asserts the count never silently decreases. Custom-runner
  compatible (uses `assert False, msg`, not `pytest.fail`).

* **B-3 e2e test spec.** `frontend/e2e/b3_site_detail.spec.ts` —
  six tests across four describe blocks covering the per-site
  widget dashboard route at `/sites/:siteId`. Surfaces under test:
  Sites row tap navigation, deep link rendering, not-found state,
  edit-mode toggle, WidgetPicker scoping to siteId, scope-key
  isolation (per-site layout writes don't touch the global
  `bd-dashboard-layout` key), and the Delete-site affordance.
  Skip-clean on environments with no sites configured (fresh
  install runs green). Counts under the existing
  `playwright.config.ts` glob; no config changes.

* **`frontend/src/lib/polling.ts` — TS strict-mode fix
  (bug, latent in v3.64.3) + unused-import sweep.**
  `AdaptiveOpts<T>` declared its `query` field as
  `Query<T, unknown, T>`, hardcoding `TError` to `unknown`. But
  `useQuery<SitesV2>(...)` (single type arg) lets TanStack infer
  `TError = Error` by default, and `Error` is not assignable to
  `unknown` in the contravariant `TError` position on TanStack's
  `Query` type. Result: every `adaptiveInterval()` call site
  (Sites, Home, Queue, Activity, NowRunningList,
  ThroughputSparkline, useWidgetData — 7 sites) failed to
  type-check under strict-mode TypeScript when built fresh on a
  machine that hadn't cached the pre-bug compile output.

  Fix: `AdaptiveOpts<T>.query` now uses a structural minimum
  type `{ state: { data: T | undefined } }` instead of TanStack's
  `Query<T, ..., T>`. The helper only reads `query.state.data`;
  it doesn't need to know about TError, the query key, the retry
  function, or any other TanStack internal. Decoupling from the
  full `Query` type also makes the helper resilient against
  future TanStack type-shape changes. All 7 existing call sites
  type-check unchanged; no call-site edits needed.

  (False start: a first attempt added a second generic
  parameter `E = unknown` to `AdaptiveOpts<T, E = unknown>`. That
  didn't actually fix anything because explicit single-generic
  call sites like `adaptiveInterval<QueueV2>(...)` cause TS to
  use the default for `E` instead of inferring from the argument
  — `AdaptiveOpts<QueueV2, unknown>` ends up structurally
  identical to the original. The structural-type approach
  bypasses the inference question entirely.)

  Also dropped one unused `X` import from
  `components/SortableQueueGroup.tsx` (TS6133, latent in v3.64.3
  alongside the polling.ts errors).

  This bug class was latent in v3.64.3 because the v3.64.3
  sandbox build apparently went through some path (cached output,
  or a TS version with looser strictness) that didn't surface it.
  The stash build of v3.64.3 hit it on first compile.

## v3.64.3 — 2026-05-23

**Five operator-driven units — opt-in sound sync, the 7 unbuilt
live_tests, per-site widget hooks, the prebuild-SPA release flag, and
a latent test fix.** Counters were 1 bug / 4 feature when cut.
Below-threshold under the 10-bug / 20-feature gate; cut on operator
request to consolidate the unreleased work into a single drop-in for
fresh-PC installs. This is the third consecutive threshold-bypass cut
(v3.63.10, v3.64.1, v3.64.2, v3.64.3 = four in a row); per the
OPEN_THREADS process note, bypasses do not establish precedent and the
cadence rule remains in force.

### Features

**Opt-in cross-device completion-sound sync (D5b).** The completion
sound preference (Web Audio ping when the queue drains) was per-device
in v3.64.2 by design — silencing one device shouldn't silence the
others. v3.64.3 keeps per-device as the **default** and adds a Settings
toggle ("Sync sound across devices") that opts a device into reading
the value from `global_config.sound_on_complete` instead. Two new
`/api/global_config` keys (`sound_sync_enabled`, `sound_on_complete`)
plus a new `useSyncedSoundPref` hook that handles the dual-source
logic. The sync toggle is itself per-device — otherwise you couldn't
opt out from a single device. Flipping sync ON adopts the current
localStorage value (so a sound-on user sees no behavior change);
flipping OFF preserves localStorage. 7 backend tests cover the
allowlist + paired-adoption + default-unset contract.

**Catalog backfill — 7 live_tests checks (L4, L8, L9, L19, L28, L30,
L36).** The `live_tests` package shipped 30 of 37 checks; this lands
the remaining 7. The IDs are the original numeric assignments; names
were re-derived from neighbouring subsystems:

- **L4 `playwright-browsers-installed`** — verifies Chromium binary
  on disk; WARN if Firefox/WebKit missing (BD doesn't use them but
  the install is incomplete); FAIL if Chromium absent.
- **L8 `cookie-jar-not-empty-on-active-sites`** — for every site with
  `auth_state=ok`, the configured `cookie_file` must exist and be
  non-empty on disk. Catches the silent "logged in but cookies were
  nuked" mismatch.
- **L9 `cookie-files-readable-and-fresh`** — non-empty cookie files
  parse as JSON or Netscape; files >30d old WARN; corrupt parse FAIL.
- **L19 `ai-text-call-roundtrip`** — counterpart to L18 (vision). POSTs
  to `/api/ai/classify` and verifies structured response. WARN on AI
  disabled/unreachable; FAIL if the text-call path itself errors.
- **L28 `service-restart-preserves-queue`** — the only disruptive new
  check. Snapshots queue counts, `systemctl restart`, waits for
  `/api/health`, verifies total preserved. WARN without systemd unit.
- **L30 `vpn-tunnel-inventory-consistent`** — reads `/api/dev/vpn_config`
  (dev-mode gated). FAIL on duplicate IDs / all-missing IDs; WARN
  with dev mode off (the production default).
- **L36 `m2-spa-bundle-served`** — `/m2/` returns 200 HTML with no
  `X-BD-M2-Status: not-built`, and at least one referenced asset
  also returns 200. Distinguishes whole-service-down (WARN) from
  /m2-specifically-broken (FAIL) via an `/api/health` precheck.

The full catalog is now 37/37. Stale top-of-file docstring (claimed
"only L22 + L26 implemented" since the file shipped) fixed at the
same time.

**Per-site widget configuration (B-2).** The backend `/api/widgets/<sid>`
endpoints have existed since v3.43.60; the v3.64.2 SPA only wired the
global path. `useWidgetSelection(siteId?: string)` and
`useWidgetData(siteId?: string)` now optionally accept a site_id —
when undefined, behavior is identical to v3.64.2 (localStorage
selection + global data, zero behavior change); when provided, both
hooks route through the per-site backend with proper TanStack Query
cache isolation. `apiPut` and `apiDelete` added to `api-client.ts`
to support the PUT/DELETE verbs the widgets endpoints require. 10
backend tests cover the GET/PUT/DELETE round-trip. NB: the SPA does
not yet have a per-site detail route, so the hooks are wired but not
yet consumed; a future B-3 unit will add the UI.

**Release-builder `--prebuild-spa` flag (D5a).** `tools/build_release.py`
gains an opt-in flag that runs `npm install && npm run build` in
`frontend/` before zipping, so the resulting release zip ships with
`frontend/dist/` and the operator can skip the build step at deploy
time. Default off preserves the v3.64.2 contract (build on deploy
target — OPEN_THREADS 1b). Useful for fresh-PC installs where Node
may not be available on the target. Helper handles all the failure
modes — no frontend dir, no `package.json`, no npm on PATH, npm
install/build non-zero exit, silent build break where npm reports
success but `dist/index.html` is missing. 9 tests cover the flag
plumbing + helper exit codes via stubbed npm.

### Bug fixes

**`test_d3_u1_m2_route_503_when_dist_missing` is now environment-
independent.** The test claimed to verify "503 when dist missing" but
actually only verified "dist doesn't exist on the dev's machine" —
`_M2_DIST_ROOT` is computed at module import time from `__file__`,
so the test's cwd-change fixture didn't actually hide dist. After
1b ran on stash and produced a real `frontend/dist/`, the test
started failing for environmental reasons. Now uses
`monkeypatch.setattr(a, "_M2_DIST_ROOT", fake_dist)` to point at a
guaranteed-absent path, so the missing-dist code path is exercised
regardless of the host's file layout.

### Notes

- `# INV-` tag count unchanged.
- `FUNCTION_INDEX.md` regenerated (line numbers shifted by docstring
  expansion in `api_global_config`).
- `ENDPOINT_CATALOG.md` unchanged (no new routes).
- Full-suite gate at unit #5: 6 foreground batches, all `Failed: 0`.
- Owed at next merge: DANGER_MAP entry on per-device sound needs
  rewrite (opt-in sync exists now); OPEN_THREADS line on "30 of 37
  checks" → "37 of 37"; LESSONS_LEARNED entry on filesystem-
  assumption test bugs.

## v3.64.2 — 2026-05-23

**Three operator-driven SPA fixes — keep-alive persistence, desktop
shell + themes restoration, and widget catalog restoration.** All three
units shipped together. Counters were 0 bug / 3 feature when cut.
Below-threshold under the 10-bug / 20-feature gate; operator requested
the release explicitly to consolidate the patches before further work.

What landed.

* **Unit 1 — Persistent Chromium for the session keeper +
  user-assignable refresh intervals.** A bug latent since v3.43.15:
  `session_keeper._launch_browser` called `launch()` + `new_context()`
  even though the module docstring claimed `profiles/<sid>/keepalive_<idx>`
  was used. The ephemeral context meant cookies the site set between
  heartbeats (rotated session tokens, refreshed CSRF cookies) were lost
  every 24h (browser-age restart), on crash, and on takeover release.
  Fix: switched to `launch_persistent_context(user_data_dir=…)`, with
  first-launch-only DB-cookie seeding so existing installs inherit
  their last-known-good session state. The 24h restart still triggers
  but now preserves cookies through the persistent profile.

  Once persistence landed, the aggressive 5-minute fetch heartbeat
  became unnecessary. Three previously-hardcoded intervals are now
  user-tunable via `app_config.json` keys, exposed through a new
  Settings → "Session keep-alive" section:
  - `session_keep_alive_fetch_interval_min` (default 30, was 5)
  - `session_keep_alive_navigate_interval_min` (default 30, was 30)
  - `session_keep_alive_lead_time_min` (default 30, was 10)

  All three accept 1–360 minutes; out-of-range values clamp silently.
  Read via `global_config` on every scheduler iteration — operators
  can change them in Settings without restarting the service. The
  module-level constants (`FETCH_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_SEC` etc.) remain
  as fallbacks when the config key is unset or invalid.

  Backend POST allowlist in `/api/global_config` extended for the three
  new keys with clamp-on-out-of-range behaviour matching
  `watch_interval_sec`. SettingSection added with three numeric inputs
  under Downloads/Network/System. `GlobalConfigSubset` type extended.

  Also shipped under this unit: Playwright e2e coverage for U10–U15
  (`frontend/e2e/d3_u10_u15.spec.ts`, 13 tests with skip-if-no-data
  guards) — closes the gap flagged in OPEN_THREADS 1d post-v3.64.1.

* **Unit 2 — Desktop shell + modal click-outside fix.** Pre-v3.64.2
  the SPA's `AppShell` rendered the mobile chrome (`PageHeader` +
  `BottomTabBar` + `max-w-2xl <main>`) at every viewport, including
  desktop. Operator reported `/m2` on a desktop browser felt
  "phone-shaped on a wide screen" — the visible problem was the
  `max-w-2xl` on `<main>` clamping content to ~672px regardless of
  window width.

  Fix: `AppShell` branches on `useMediaQuery("(min-width: 1024px)")`.
  At lg breakpoint it renders the new `DesktopShell` component
  (sidebar nav + top utility bar + `max-w-7xl` content). Below 1024px
  the mobile chrome is unchanged.

  DesktopShell composition: 220px-wide sidebar with brand + version
  + nav items (Home/Sites/Queue/Activity/Settings with live count
  badges) + status footer (running/idle + uptime). Top utility bar
  with page title + trailing slot. Content area expands to max-w-7xl
  centered. Polls `/api/health/v2` for version + active_downloads
  + uptime; cross-tab queue badge data comes from the existing
  AppShell-level query (single source of truth).

  Modal popup-stickiness fix: previously a stray click on the dialog
  overlay closed the dialog and lost any state the user had entered.
  `DialogContent` now sets `onPointerDownOutside={e => e.preventDefault()}`
  and `onInteractOutside={e => e.preventDefault()}`. Esc still works,
  the X button still works, any caller-supplied Cancel button still
  works — but stray scrim clicks no longer dismiss.

  CommandPalette mounted in both branches so ⌘K works on either shell.

* **Unit 3 — 31 named themes restored.** The legacy `/` UI had 31
  themes (Default Dark, Default Light, Console, Editorial, Midnight,
  Nord, Solarized, Paper, Monochrome, Terminal, Ember, Forest,
  Rosé Pine, Crimson, Daylight, Neon, Dracula, Gruvbox, Tokyo Night,
  Catppuccin Mocha, Catppuccin Latte, One Dark, Monokai, Everforest,
  Ayu Mirage, Sepia, Steel, Mint, Wine, Synthwave, Carbon) that
  collapsed to three modes (system/light/dark) in v3.64.0. No
  decision recorded; quiet regression.

  Restored as a catalog at `frontend/src/lib/themes.ts` — all 31
  themes with their full CSS variable maps (`bg`, `surface`,
  `surface-2`, `ink`, `ink-2`, `ink-3`, `primary`, `primary-soft`,
  `green`, `green-soft`, `amber`, `amber-soft`, `red`, `red-soft`,
  `hairline`) and an `isDark` flag computed from `bg` luminance so
  Tailwind's `.dark` class still toggles correctly under any named
  theme. `useTheme` rewritten to apply the theme's vars to `<html
  style="…">` overriding `index.css`, write the `.dark` class based
  on isDark, and update the iOS `theme-color` meta to match.
  `applyStoredThemeOnBoot` invoked from `main.tsx` (unchanged
  signature) still works.

  ThemeToggle UI: System/Light/Dark quick buttons remain at the
  front for the common path. A new "More" dropdown opens a scrollable
  list of the 28 named themes; each row shows a 3-color swatch
  (bg / surface / primary) so the operator can preview the palette
  before picking. Esc closes the dropdown; click-outside also closes
  (it's a transient picker, not a confirmation dialog, so the
  dialog-style click-outside hardening is NOT applied here).

* **Unit 4 — Widget catalog restoration.** The legacy `/` UI shipped
  36 KPI widgets across 7 categories via `/api/widgets/data`. The
  v3.64.0 SPA collapsed to 5 hardcoded widgets and never wired the
  API endpoint. The full catalog is restored.

  Catalog lives at `frontend/src/lib/widgetCatalog.ts` — 36 widgets
  with declarative `spec(data) => KPISpec` functions. Categories:
  Activity (4), Performance (5), Capacity (4), Health (4), System (5),
  Collection (8), Diagnostics (6). One generic `<KPICard>` component
  renders any spec (value + optional delta, meter, sparkline, valueKind
  tint, extra text). Null-guards from legacy v3.63.6 preserved for
  the cpu_ram, gpu, workers, and lib_watched widgets.

  Data flow: `useWidgetData` hook polls `/api/widgets/data` with
  adaptive cadence (3s when busy, 30s when idle, via the existing
  `adaptiveInterval` helper). Single shared query — every widget
  derives from the same cache entry, so adding more widgets to the
  dashboard doesn't multiply network calls.

  Widget library: `<WidgetPicker>` overlay opens from Home → Edit →
  "Add widget". Category-tab filter (All + 7 categories), grid of
  preview cards with live data, tap to toggle. Uses the project's
  Dialog primitive — inherits the click-outside-disabled fix from
  Unit 2.

  Selection persists in `localStorage["bd-widget-selection"]`,
  cross-tab via the storage event. Reconciles against the catalog on
  read (drops unknown IDs from old configs). Defaults to the same
  four widgets the legacy `/` UI defaulted to: done_today,
  throughput, queue_depth, action_req.

  Integration with U13 grid: `useDashboardLayout` extended with an
  `extraIds` parameter — accepts the current KPI selection and
  reconciles it into the react-grid-layout `Layouts`. Legacy 5 widgets
  keep their custom React components; KPI widgets are rendered via
  KPICard tiles below them. Drag/resize/reorder work on both.
  Layout-reset preserves the KPI selection (separate storage key);
  selection-reset goes back to the 4 defaults. `WIDGET_IDS` constant
  kept in its inline form so the U13 contract test
  (`test_u13_dashboard_layout_widget_ids_complete`) still matches —
  `LEGACY_WIDGET_IDS` is added as an alias.

What's deferred (NOT in this release):

* **Per-site widget config.** The legacy backend has `/api/widgets/<sid>`
  for per-site overrides. The SPA only wires global. Tracked in
  OPEN_THREADS as Unit B-2.

Test baseline: **4733 / 4733 / 0 / 2** on Linux (Ubuntu 24, Python
3.12) under the project's custom `run_tests.py` runner in 6 foreground
batches. The 2 skipped are pre-existing pre-v3.64.2 skips
(test_d3_u1_scaffold tier-1 environment-conditional). +6 new tests
this release: 5 themes catalog tests, 8 widget catalog tests, 12
session_keeper persistence + interval tests, minus pre-existing tests
that were re-counted in different batches.

Net new test files: `tests/test_session_keeper_persistent_context.py`,
`tests/test_session_keeper_user_intervals.py`,
`tests/test_themes_catalog.py`, `tests/test_widget_catalog.py`.

Net new SPA modules: `frontend/src/lib/themes.ts`,
`frontend/src/lib/widgetCatalog.ts`, `frontend/src/hooks/useMediaQuery.ts`,
`frontend/src/hooks/useWidgetData.ts`,
`frontend/src/hooks/useWidgetSelection.ts`,
`frontend/src/components/DesktopShell.tsx`,
`frontend/src/components/KPICard.tsx`,
`frontend/src/components/WidgetPicker.tsx`,
`frontend/e2e/d3_u10_u15.spec.ts`. No new npm dependencies —
everything builds against the existing v3.64.1 lockfile.

## v3.64.1 — 2026-05-22

**D3 follow-up — six previously-deferred Tier-3 items shipped on
operator request (bypass of the "deferred" status).** Six units U10–U15,
all SPA/`/m2` surface, no download/login/extractor runtime change. The
legacy `/m` UI is untouched.

What landed.

* **U10 — Bulk select on Sites + Queue.** Two new endpoints,
  `POST /api/sites/v2/bulk` (pause/resume/start/delete on a list of
  sids; hardcoded action allow-list — no `getattr` on raw input) and
  `POST /api/queue/v2/bulk_cancel` (cancels a list of `{site_id, url}`
  pairs through the canonical `runner._update_job` path). Both
  CSRF-gated, partial-failure-tolerant, input de-duped before dispatch.
  Frontend: new `useBulkSelection` hook (generic string-keyed selection
  with `pruneTo` for refetch handling), `BulkActionBar` + `BulkActionButton`
  components, `SiteRow` + `WaitingJobRow` extended with optional
  `selected` / `onToggleSelect` props (zero behavior change when those
  are absent). Sites tab and Queue tab gain a "Select" mode toggle in
  the header; selection mode disables swipe-to-cancel on the same row
  (gestures would conflict).

* **U11 — Drag-to-reorder on Queue (per-site).** The pre-existing
  `POST /api/sites/<sid>/jobs/reorder` endpoint had a latent: it
  persisted `ord` to DB but didn't update `runner.urls`, so a reorder
  in a running session never affected dispatch. Fixed: handler now
  routes through `runner.reorder_urls(ordered)` with a `queue_reorder`
  fallback for failure cases. Frontend: `@dnd-kit/core` +
  `@dnd-kit/sortable` + `@dnd-kit/utilities` added to
  `frontend/package.json`. New `SortableWaitingJobRow` (drag handle
  with `aria-label` naming the file; keyboard nav via dnd-kit's
  KeyboardSensor), new `SortableQueueGroup` (focused per-site
  reorder mode with `DndContext` + `SortableContext` + optimistic
  local state; POSTs ord values 10/20/30 with gaps for future
  inserts; rollback on error). Queue tab gains a "Sort" chip ribbon
  — one chip per site with ≥2 waiting jobs. Sort and Select modes
  are mutually exclusive; sort auto-exits when the site's waiting
  list empties. Native swipe-to-cancel preserved outside sort mode.

* **U12 — Queue tab badge mode toggle (live %).** New
  `useQueueBadgeMode` hook + `aggregateRunningPct` helper. localStorage
  key `bd-queue-badge-mode` (modes: `count` [default, dot-or-not] and
  `percent` [aggregate running progress as a numeric badge]). Cross-tab
  sync via the `storage` event. `BottomTabBar` gains
  `queueBadgeMode`/`queueRunningPct`/`queueHasRunning` props. Percent
  mode falls back to the count dot when nothing is running (no
  misleading "0%"). `AppShell` re-types the existing `queue-v2-badge`
  query as `QueueV2Full` so it computes the aggregate from
  `running[].progress` — no second poll. Settings → Downloads gains a
  Count/Percent radiogroup. Per-device preference by design (same
  scope reasoning as theme/sound: silencing one device shouldn't
  silence others); explicitly NOT routed through `/api/global_config`.

* **U13 — Configurable dashboard (react-grid-layout).** `react-grid-layout`
  + `react-resizable` + `@types/react-grid-layout` added to package
  deps (~60KB gzip; concentrated on the Home route — accepted bundle
  cost for the customization feature). New `useDashboardLayout` hook
  with five canonical widget IDs (`attention`, `today`, `throughput`,
  `now-running`, `by-site`), validates persisted shape on read,
  reconciles unknown/missing widgets against `WIDGET_IDS`, cross-tab
  sync via storage event, separate `lg`/`sm` breakpoints (4-col
  desktop vs 1-col mobile). Home tab gains an "Edit" toggle in the
  trailing slot; in edit mode, tiles get a dashed primary-ring + a
  grip handle; `draggableHandle` is the grip only (tile bodies don't
  start drags). `isDraggable`/`isResizable` gated by edit mode.
  `onLayoutChange` only persists while in edit mode (initial-mount
  layout computations don't overwrite stored state). "Reset Layout"
  in edit mode reverts to defaults. Layout persists to localStorage
  key `bd-dashboard-layout`. `index.css` extended with U4 grid
  overrides (placeholder uses `--primary-soft` instead of vanilla
  red).

* **U14 — Log-diff side-by-side.** New endpoint
  `GET /api/queue/v2/job_log_diff?a=<sid>:<url>&b=<sid>:<url>` —
  returns both job logs (events + current) plus a precomputed
  unified diff (via `difflib.unified_diff` — server-side so the
  SPA doesn't ship a diff library). URL spec parser splits on the
  FIRST colon (URLs contain colons themselves). Partial-result
  tolerance: an unknown side returns `ok=false` in its own block
  while the response itself is 200. Frontend: new `/logs/diff`
  route + `LogDiff` component with two-pane side-by-side layout
  (scroll-synced via paired listeners with `requestAnimationFrame`
  lock to prevent bounce), unified diff renderer below with
  color-coded `+`/`-`/`@@` prefixes. `JobErrorModal` gains a
  three-state Compare flow: pick THIS job (stash in sessionStorage),
  Compare now (when a DIFFERENT job is stashed), Cancel pick.
  `bd-log-diff-pick` is `sessionStorage` not `localStorage` —
  comparison picks are per-tab, not per-device.

* **U15 — Site-health sparkline per Activity row.** New endpoint
  `GET /api/activity/v2/site_health?days=14&status=*` — one
  windowed query against `history` grouped by `(site_id, day)`,
  status allow-list checked BEFORE the SQL with bound parameters
  on both branches (no interpolation). Returns
  `{by_site: {site_id: [n0, n1, …, nN]}}` zero-filled to length
  `days`, oldest → newest. `days` clamped to 1..90; default 14.
  Frontend: new `useSiteHealth` hook (cached by `(days, status)`,
  5-minute fresh window), new `InlineSparkline` component (pure
  SVG, no Recharts — at one-per-row, Recharts' ResponsiveContainer
  cost is non-trivial; the inline SVG is `role="img"` with a
  descriptive `aria-label` including total count). `ActivityRow`
  accepts an optional `sparkline` prop typed `number[] | null`;
  `undefined` omits the slot entirely (avoids first-paint flash
  before data resolves), `null` renders an empty baseline (site
  with no activity in window). Activity route calls
  `useSiteHealth(14, "*")` once and threads `lookup(r.site_id)`
  per row.

Source-grep pins added for every new endpoint and helper: 89 new
contract tests across six files
(`tests/test_d3_u10_bulk_select.py` ... `tests/test_d3_u15_site_health.py`).

**Two items remain explicitly deferred from the original D3
dropped-without-regret list and were NOT undeferred in v3.64.1:**

* **Pre-built `frontend/dist/` in the release zip** (Option B from
  v3.63.10 planning). Still declined — current install-time build is
  working; flip is a one-line change in `tools/build_release.py` if
  install-time builds become annoying on stash.
* **Sound preference syncing through `global_config`.** Intentionally
  per-device — same reasoning as theme/badge mode. Syncing through
  `global_config` would mute the laptop when the phone gets muted at
  night. Not on the roadmap.

**Suite baseline at v3.64.1:** **4710 total / 4708 pass / 0 fail /
2 skip** on the Claude sandbox (curl_cffi-absent skips, unchanged
from v3.64.0). Up from 4617 at v3.64.0; the +93 is dominated by the
six U10–U15 contract test files.

**The v3.64.0 deploy chain (items 1a–1d in the v3.64.0 OPEN_THREADS)
is fully superseded by this release** — v3.64.1 contains every
v3.64.0 fix (the curl_cffi `stream` → `request(stream=True)` fix
carries forward; the install_windows.bat quoting fix carries
forward; the PT9 parser fix carries forward) plus the six U10–U15
features. The single deploy of v3.64.1 to stash replaces what would
have been a v3.64.0 deploy plus this update.

## v3.64.0 — 2026-05-22

**D3 ships.** Nine units across nine sessions delivered the React SPA
mobile UI at `/m2` — Dashboard, Sites, Queue, Activity, Settings,
Advanced. Both UIs (`/m` legacy, `/m2` new) coexist this release;
`/m` becomes an unconditional redirect at v3.65.0, the legacy template
drops at v3.66.0. See `D3_OPT_IN.md` for the operator-facing how-to.

Opt in by visiting `http://<host>:5555/m?ui=v2` once. The choice
persists via a `bd_ui=v2` cookie. Opt out: `/m2?ui=v1`. The desktop
`/` UI is unaffected and on no retirement schedule.

What landed.

* **Scaffold + opt-in mount (U1, U9).** New `frontend/` tree with
  Vite + React 18 + TypeScript + Tailwind + TanStack Query + React
  Router + shadcn/ui + Recharts. Flask serves the built SPA at
  `/m2/*`. Install scripts (`install_linux.sh`, `install_windows.bat`)
  added non-fatal Node detection + `npm run build` — install
  completes even without Node, `/m2` returns 503 with installer-aware
  message until built. Opt-in cookie + bidirectional ?ui= mechanism
  added in U9 with explicit retirement schedule.
* **Six v2 API endpoints (U2).** `/api/dashboard/v2`,
  `/api/dashboard/v2/sparkline`, `/api/sites/v2`, `/api/activity/v2`,
  `/api/queue/v2`, `/api/health/v2`. SPA-shaped adapters over the
  existing v1 data sources — no new state, no new locks, no new
  threads. v1 endpoints unchanged so `/` and `/m` keep working.
  Deterministic `avatar_color` via djb2 hash → 12-hue palette
  (matches mockup signature).
* **Dashboard tab (U3).** Real Home page composing AttentionBanner
  (with Resolve dispatcher → `runner.start_manual_login` /
  `runner.login_async`), TodayStatsCard, ThroughputSparkline
  (Recharts), NowRunningList, BySiteList. Adaptive polling per widget
  (3-12s on dashboard, 2-10s on sparkline). Loading skeletons.
  Header + bottom tab bar mounted in shared AppShell.
* **Sites tab + cookie_file fix (U4).** Filter tabs
  (All/Active/Paused/Issues), search, list, undo-style delete via
  sonner. Add Site wizard with **debounced inline validation against
  `/api/sites/validate`**. The v3.63.10 trigger bug class
  (cookie_file pointing at a directory) is now a hard ERROR in
  `site_editor.validate_config` — caught before save instead of at
  first download. Missing cookie_file is a WARNING (path may be
  created later by an export). The whole D3 redesign was justified
  by this bug class; that justification is now structurally
  enforced.
* **Queue tab (U5).** Counter chips, Now-Running with SSE-driven live
  progress smoothing (subscribes to `/api/stream`'s
  `download_progress` events, overlays per-URL pct on TanStack Query
  data), Waiting list with cancel + priority, tap row → error modal
  with last 50 log lines + Retry. Optimistic mutation pattern for
  per-job cancel (onMutate + rollback on error). Pause-all/Resume-all
  in header trailing slot. Two new endpoints: `/api/queue/v2/cancel`
  (per-URL cancel, mirrors `/retry_one`) and `/api/queue/v2/job_log`
  (last N events for one URL, backs the modal).
* **Activity tab + ⌘K palette (U6).** Window filter (24h/7d/30d/All),
  debounced search across history, headline count card with
  delta-vs-prev-period math, list of completions. `/api/activity/v2`
  extended with optional `?q=` substring filter (200-char cap on
  pattern; existing v2 contract preserved). New
  `/api/activity/v2/export.csv` endpoint streams CSV with
  Content-Disposition (100k row cap; same filters as JSON, no 200-row
  cap because the export IS the "give me everything" affordance).
  Shared SQL helper `_m2_activity_query_fragments` keeps the JSON +
  CSV endpoints semantically aligned. Command palette globally
  mounted in AppShell with ⌘K shortcut — three groups (tab nav,
  actions, jump-to-site).
* **Settings + Advanced + visible dark mode (U7).** Three grouped
  Settings sections (Downloads / Network / System), Advanced sub-page
  with live health checks reading `/api/health/v2`. Three-position
  theme toggle (System / Light / Dark) persisted to localStorage,
  syncs with OS `prefers-color-scheme` when in System mode.
  `applyStoredThemeOnBoot()` called pre-render in `main.tsx` so the
  first paint matches stored theme (no FOUC). The dark-mode CSS
  pairings actually invisibly shipped in U1's `index.css`; U7 made
  them togglable.
* **Polish (U8).** Sound-on-completion fires (Web Audio API, two-tone
  ping; reads `localStorage["bd-sound-on-complete"]`, reuses the
  existing queue-badge query). Swipe-to-cancel on Queue waiting list
  (pointer events; no dnd-kit / framer-motion — pure ~80 lines).
  Targeted a11y audit: `role="alert"` on AttentionBanner + 5 error
  cards, `role="log"` + `aria-live` on JobErrorModal event log,
  `role="img"` with descriptive aria-label on Recharts sparkline,
  `aria-hidden` on Skeleton. Static bundle audit confirms zero
  unused runtime deps + zero heavy-import anti-patterns; estimated
  ~155-180KB gzip total. Playwright e2e smoke suite (11 tests,
  desktop + mobile-Chrome projects) wired with `npm run e2e` script
  — operator runs against a real instance.

Backend additions.

* `/api/dashboard/v2`, `/api/dashboard/v2/sparkline`,

* `/api/sites/v2`
* `/api/activity/v2` (extended with `?q=`), `/api/activity/v2/export.csv`
* `/api/queue/v2`, `/api/queue/v2/cancel` (POST),
  `/api/queue/v2/job_log`
* `/api/health/v2`
* `/m2/*` SPA mount (UI files served from `frontend/dist/`,

Frontend (new).

* `frontend/BUNDLE_AUDIT.md`

Docs.

Test results.

* Full suite at the v3.64.0 cut: 4617 cases, 4615 passed, 0 failed,

Deferred from the original D3 scope (per the OPEN_THREADS

Operator verification steps after deploy.

1. `cd frontend && npm ci && npm run build` — confirms SPA builds.
   Skipping this is harmless (Node-missing path → installer-aware
   503 on /m2; legacy /m unaffected).
2. Visit `http://<host>:5555/m2/` — confirm SPA loads.
3. Visit `http://<host>:5555/m?ui=v2` — confirm cookie + redirect.
4. `cd frontend && npm run e2e:install && BD_E2E_BASE=... npm run e2e`
   — run the e2e smoke suite against the deployed instance.

Tracking.

* Path B (React SPA) was activated v3.63.10, completed v3.64.0.
  Tracked at the optimistic end of the 9-15 session estimate.
* `/m` retires at v3.65.0; legacy `mobile.html` template removed at
  v3.66.0. The `/m` route itself stays as a permanent 302 to `/m2/`
  so old bookmarks keep working forever.

## v3.63.10 — 2026-05-22

Bug-fix release on top of v3.63.9. **Three real bugs found during the
first live deployment of v3.63.9 to stash.** All three were latents
in v3.63.9 that shipped with `Failed: 0` because the contract tests
didn't round-trip the actual API surface.

Fixed.

* **`bulk_downloader/runner.py` — curl_cffi module-level `stream`
  call doesn't exist.** Two call sites (single-stream HTTP
  downloader at L9117 and parallel-chunk downloader at L9574)
  called `cffi_requests.stream("GET", ...)`. curl_cffi 0.15.x
  has no module-level `stream` function; only `Session.stream()`
  and module-level `request(stream=True, ...)` exist. Every
  direct HTTP download raised `AttributeError: module
  'curl_cffi.requests' has no attribute 'stream'` and fell back
  to the browser path. Functional but ~5-10x slower and triggered
  the 15-min worker-hung watchdog under load on real sites.
  Both call sites now use `request("GET", url, stream=True,
  ...)`. Surfaced on the first real session against UltraFilms
  on stash; root-caused via the visible journal AttributeError
  once a config-side issue (P1) was cleared. Caught by new
  contract test `tests/test_curl_cffi_api.py` which pins both
  the source-grep shape and the runtime API surface.
* **`install_windows.bat` D1 — `"%PYTHON_CMD%"` quoting wrong
  after multi-token assignment.** v3.63.9's D1 change made
  `set "PYTHON_CMD=py -3.12"` (the documented-target launcher
  invocation), but the consumer line at L162 wrapped the
  expansion in outer quotes: `"%PYTHON_CMD%" -m venv ...`.
  cmd.exe treated the entire quoted expansion as one executable
  name (`"py -3.12"`), aborted at step [3/7] with
  `'"py -3.12"' is not recognized as an internal or external
  command`. Fix: drop the outer quotes — `%PYTHON_CMD% -m venv
  ...`. Safe because PYTHON_CMD's value is always a launcher
  invocation or single command name, never a path containing
  spaces. Caught at first install on a fresh Windows VM during
  the v3.63.10 D2 diagnostic walkthrough; pinned by new contract
  test `tests/test_install_windows_bat_d1.py` (4 tests covering
  the corrected shape, the absence of any `"%PYTHON_CMD%"`
  occurrence, and the presence of the D1 assignment).
  `_bat_lint` (v3.63.8) does NOT catch this — the bug is a
  quoting class, not a paren class. No new lint rule added; the
  v3.63.7 lesson against rule-inflation applies (don't add a
  rule for a one-off quoting mistake; pin the file).
* **`tools/check_skip_baseline.py` (PT9) — parser shape mismatch
  with runner output.** The parser looked for the literal
  string `Skipped:` (capital S, colon) per the comment at L74-77.
  `run_tests.py` at L857 writes the runner's stdout one-liner as
  `Total: N | Passed: N | Failed: 0 | Skipped: N`, but at L934
  writes SUMMARY.txt's result line as `result : N total | N
  passed | N failed | N skipped` (lowercase, count BEFORE the
  word). The parser saw only the first shape; SUMMARY.txt only
  contains the second; every `--update` call on a fresh deploy
  failed with `FAIL: could not read Skipped count from
  SUMMARY.txt`. Parser now recognises both shapes (primary
  regex on the SUMMARY.txt shape, fallback on the runner-stdout
  shape). PT9 baseline initialized cleanly on stash after the
  fix. Caught by new contract test
  `tests/test_skip_baseline.py` (11 tests including a
  round-trip pin that reproduces the runner's exact SUMMARY.txt
  format).

Added.

* `tests/test_skip_baseline.py` — PT9 parser contract tests
  (11 cases) including `test_parser_reads_real_runner_summary`
  which reproduces the runner's actual SUMMARY.txt line shape.
  Closes the gap that let the v3.63.9 PT9 ship broken — no
  prior test ever round-tripped runner output through the
  parser.
* `tests/test_install_windows_bat_d1.py` — D1 install_windows.bat
  regression pin (4 tests). Asserts the quoted `"%PYTHON_CMD%"`
  shape is absent from the file, the unquoted form is present,
  and the D1 assignment is in place.
* `tests/test_curl_cffi_api.py` — curl_cffi API contract pin
  (4 tests). Source-grep pins for the bug-shape absence and the
  fix-shape presence; runtime-API check that the installed
  curl_cffi exposes `request` and `Session.stream`. Skips the
  runtime check if curl_cffi isn't installed (intentional).

Process notes.

* **The three bugs share a lesson:** v3.63.9 shipped with
  `Failed: 0` (4443/4443) but had three latents because no
  contract test round-tripped the actual surface. PT9's parser
  was never run against the runner's actual SUMMARY.txt; the
  install_windows.bat D1 quoting was never run on a real
  Windows install; curl_cffi's `stream` API was never exercised
  against the real library. v3.63.10's three new test files
  each close one of those gaps. Lesson added to
  LESSONS_LEARNED in the next merge.
* **Suite count after this release: 4458/4458/0/0** (4443 +
  11 PT9 + 4 D1 + 4 curl_cffi tests, with 2 of the curl_cffi
  tests skipping in environments where curl_cffi isn't
  installed). Skip baseline stays at 0 on stash (curl_cffi
  is in `requirements.txt`).

## v3.63.8 — 2026-05-21

Tooling release. **No download/login/extractor runtime change.** Two
delivery units that accumulated post-v3.63.7: a full-parser upgrade
to the `.bat` linter that closes the v3.63.7 bug class as a release
blocker, and the remote-teach noVNC stack that makes manual-teach
usable from any LAN device including phones.

Added.

* `bulk_downloader/_bat_lint.py` — paren-aware tokenizer for `.bat`
  files. Quote awareness, caret escaping, `^`-line-continuation
  joining, REM/`::` comment skipping, `for ... in (...)` argument
  recognition. Four paren roles (`block_open`, `block_close`,
  `for_open`, `for_close`) so rule checks consume a single tokenized
  stream. Rule **L4 paren-in-arg** detects paired unescaped `(...)`
  in command args inside a `(...)` block — the v3.63.7 bug shape
  exactly. 27 unit tests in `tests/test_bat_lint_parser.py` cover
  the parser and each rule in isolation, plus a corpus integration
  test that exercises every shipped `.bat` file.
* `tests/test_dev_suite_tier0.py` — two new contract tests:
  `test_bat_lint_all_shipped_files_clean` (every shipped `.bat`
  file must lint clean — `with_issues == 0`, supersedes the prior
  shape-only check) and `test_bat_lint_catches_v3_63_7_bug_class`
  (regression pin against weakening the L4 rule).
* `install_remote_teach.sh` / `uninstall_remote_teach.sh` —
  Linux-only installers for Xvfb + openbox + x11vnc + noVNC +
  websockify. Four `bd-*` systemd units, soft-dep drop-in for
  bulkdownloader.service (`Wants=` not `Requires=` — Xvfb dying
  doesn't take BulkDL with it). VNC password generated at install
  time, stored at `~/.bd_vnc_passwd`, rotatable via
  `--reset-password`. LAN trust model (matches port-5555 shape);
  explicitly NOT for internet exposure.

Changed.

* `bulk_downloader/dev_suite.py::bat_lint()` — implementation
  rewritten to delegate to `_bat_lint.lint_bytes()`. Return-dict
  shape preserved for back-compat. The old regex-based detector is
  gone; the parser is the only implementation now.

Fixed.

* `tools/sast.bat` L96 — `echo semgrep: findings present (see semgrep.txt)`
  inside an `if (...)` block was the same v3.63.7 bug class.
  Escaped to `^(see semgrep.txt^)`. Latent — would have aborted the
  script when the findings branch fired. Caught by the new lint
  against the shipped `.bat` corpus.

Process notes.

* **Rules L5 and L6 were prototyped and removed before integration.**
  The post-v3.63.7 work briefly encoded "labels inside `(...)` blocks
  are illegal" and "`::` comments inside `(...)` blocks are illegal"
  as lint rules, based on the v3.63.7 session's first (later
  disproved) diagnosis of `install_ai_ollama.bat`. The corpus
  integration test immediately false-positived on `gpu_check.bat`
  lines 404/427/434 — which work fine on Windows. The rules were
  wrong; cmd.exe permits labels inside blocks when reached via
  `goto`. **Lesson encoded in LESSONS_LEARNED:** retract the rule,
  don't whitelist the working corpus.

## v3.63.7 — 2026-05-21

Windows-verification release. **No download/login/extractor runtime
change.** One operator session that drove the Windows posture from
"dev-confirmed without artifact capture" (OPEN_THREADS item 1) to
**verified with artifact capture** by walking the full 8-phase
checklist on a Windows Server 2025 build 26100 VM (Tesla T4
passthrough, Python 3.14 in venv). Three real bugs surfaced and
fixed; T55 timing tolerance loosened for heavy-load environments.

Fixed.

* `install_ai_ollama.bat` had unescaped `(` / `)` in echo lines
  inside `(...)` blocks at line 47 (`echo ... on CPU (slow).`) and
  line 93 (`echo ERROR: download failed (exit !DL_RC!). ...`). cmd.exe
  counts unescaped parens in echo arguments inside parenthesized
  blocks; the `(slow)` prematurely closed the outer `if errorlevel
  1 (...)` block, the next `.` (in `(slow).`) landed at top level,
  fired `. was unexpected at this time.` Escaped as `^(slow^).` and
  `^(exit !DL_RC!^).` Pinned by the bisector pattern documented in
  this session's LESSONS_LEARNED entry. Diagnosed only after four
  wrong theories were each disproved by a real probe (labels-inside-
  block, PowerShell-line-continuation, em-dashes, file-not-deployed);
  the bisector replaced theorizing with measurement.
* `run_tests.py` `_PINNED_TOGETHER` now includes
  `test_v3_43_55_csrf_bootstrap.py`. Under `--workers` the parallel
  path gives each test file a fresh `BD_HOME` tempdir; on Windows the
  app's first-boot init under that fresh BD_HOME produces a `/`
  response whose CSRF meta tag the three failing tests
  (`test_index_mints_session_inline`, `test_csrf_meta_matches_session`,
  `test_concurrent_posts_no_403_storm`) cannot match. The
  flaky-classifier in `_retry_failures_serial` couldn't recover them
  because its retry runs in the parent process with all ~4400 other
  tests' imports already loaded — a different contamination shape
  that on Windows compounds rather than cancels. Pinning runs the
  file in-process before parallel dispatch with no forced `BD_HOME`,
  matching the conditions where the tests pass (`run_test.bat` and
  `diag_csrf_bootstrap.py`). The underlying Windows + fresh-BD_HOME
  asymmetry remains as a deeper open question.
* `run_tests.py` `--workers` (auto-detect) now caps at 60 on Windows.
  `ProcessPoolExecutor` enforces a hard limit of 61 workers on
  Windows (`WaitForMultipleObjects` caps at 64 handles minus 3
  reserved); on a 100+ logical-CPU VM the un-capped auto-detect
  raised `ValueError: max_workers must be <= 61` at pool
  construction. Manual `--workers=N` still respects N. Cap is 60 not
  61 to leave a one-handle safety margin.
* `tests/test_t55_live_test_harness_timeout.py`
  `test_run_all_records_timeout_and_continues`: timing bound loosened
  from `elapsed < 3.0` to `elapsed < 4.5`. Under 60 parallel Windows
  workers on the 100+ CPU verification VM the post-cutoff cleanup
  pushed total `run_all` time to 3.22s (the 0.3s cutoff still fired
  correctly — the wedger sleeps 5.0s; the test was just verifying
  the run didn't block on the full sleep). 4.5s preserves that
  semantic with ~1.5s of scheduler-pressure tolerance. Sibling test
  with `_run_with_timeout` and 1.5s bound passed under the same load
  and was left alone — don't preemptively loosen what didn't break.

Process notes.

* Counter at cut: 1 bug-fix delivery this session (three patches
  shipped together in one `changed/` drop, per the unit-definition
  rule). Cut on operator request, well below the 10-bug-fix /
  20-feature thresholds.
* `bat_lint` in `dev_suite.py` has two gaps surfaced this session:
  (1) doesn't flag unescaped `()` in echo lines inside parenthesized
  blocks (the bug class above), (2) doesn't flag non-ASCII bytes
  per file (the test only checks `file_count > 0`, not the lint
  results). A robust paren-tracker with quote-aware depth counting
  is non-trivial to write and a flaky lint is worse than no lint;
  deferred rather than built on the fly.
* The full-suite Windows run under `--workers` produced one FLAKY
  classification: `test_session_keeper.py ::
  test_lifetime_observations_basic` failed parallel, passed serial
  retry, correctly not counted as a failure. One-off - leave it; if
  it recurs, add to `_PINNED_TOGETHER`.
* Python 3.14 in the Windows venv. `install_windows.bat` builds the
  venv from whatever the system `python` resolves to; on the
  verification VM that was Python 3.14, not the documented 3.12
  target. The full suite passes 4414/4414 under 3.14, so Python 3.14
  is now *de facto* compatible — but it's untested ground in the
  sense that no CI exercises it. Tracked in OPEN_THREADS for the
  next merge to decide whether to pin to 3.12 or formally bless 3.14.

## v3.63.6 — 2026-05-21

the operator asks"; (3) widgets fix-up — diagnosed via real stash
capture that `cpu_ram` showed misleading "0% / 0%" due to psutil

widget bugs in an audit pass, fixed all of them, and added a
proper GPU widget.

  stash-local, so KB-documented fixes never deployed). The v3.63.5
  KB claimed step [3] would import the module-level `app` and
  step [6] would re-enable L3 in `LIVE_IDS`; both required hand-
  patching on stash because `capture.sh` wasn't in the v3.63.5
  zip. v3.63.6 moves it into the repo and pins it with a
  contract test (`tests/test_u45_capture_sh_shipped.py`, 7

  L3 from LIVE_IDS, reverting the `from bulk_downloader.app

  was removed at v3.63.3 but four call-sites in the codebase

  consumer. CHANGELOG.md's v3.62.6 historical entry is
  intentionally NOT touched — that release shipped while
  live_check.py existed, and rewriting history to pretend

  instructions side of this drift remains for the next merge

* `app_widgets_api.py::_collect_data` — disk_free_gb call. Pre-
  v3.63.6 it was `gb = disk_free_gb()` with no argument, raising
  TypeError which the bare `except Exception: pass` swallowed
  silently. The `disk_free` widget therefore showed '—' on every

  fresh install showed "0/16 workers" — a lie. Now emits None
  when no fleet exists; the widget renderer null-guards and
  shows '—'.
* `bulk_downloader/static/widgets.js` — `cpu_ram` renderer null-
  guards `d.cpu_pct`/`d.ram_pct`. Pre-v3.63.6 the `pct(null)`
  helper returned 0, so a deployment missing psutil rendered
  "0% / 0%" — a misleading "system is idle" reading rather than
  a "this widget has no data" state. Now matches the

* `bulk_downloader/static/widgets.js` — `workers` renderer
  null-guards `d.workers_total`. Matches the cpu_ram pattern;
  shows '—' on no-fleet rather than "0/16".

Added.

* `tools/vpn_kill_switch_probe.py` — T46 active VPN kill-switch
  probe. The v3.63.0 L-29 inspector verifies the kill-switch
  *configuration* is wired; this probe is the *active*
  counterpart that temporarily exercises the kill-switch on a
  running host and measures whether outbound traffic actually
  fails closed when the VPN drops. Default mode is dry-run
  (detection + ufw snapshot + plan-printing, no mutation);
  `--apply` requires `--reason "..."` and prompts the operator
  per-toggle. State is restored in a finally regardless of
  outcome — including on KeyboardInterrupt or uncaught
  exception. The restore that itself fails is exit code 4 with

  convention — see `gpu_check.sh`; the operator's stash runs

[3] CSRF diag clean). v3.63.6 is not yet stash-deployed; the
deploy itself is mechanical and the engineering side carries
no runtime risk.
