## v3.63.5 — 2026-05-21

Ten units shipped across one operator session. **No
download/login/extractor runtime change.** The release groups four
unrelated arcs: an extension test fix that surfaced a real packaging
defect (missing icons), Linux uninstaller + Windows Ollama installer,
GPU detection + driver-install across both OSes, and a long-tail
cleanup pass (`tools/*.bat` ASCII+CRLF, optional-deps pin removals,
patched `capture.sh`).

Fixed.

- **Extension service worker registers headless.** `extension/`
  was missing `icon16.png`, `icon48.png`, `icon128.png` referenced
  by `manifest.json::action.default_icon` and `background.js`'s
  notification call. Chromium was rejecting the entire extension
  on load (`Failed to load extension... Could not load icon
  'icon16.png'`); no service worker ever registered, the three
  `test_extension_live.py` tests skipped with "this Chromium build
  may not run extensions in headless," and the v3.62.1 attempted
  fix via `--headless=new` couldn't help because the symptom was
  identical to the genuine headless-extension-incompatibility case.
  Diagnostic correction worth recording: the long-standing "headless
  Chromium can't run MV3 extension service workers" assertion was
  wrong (or at best incomplete) for this codebase — a 10-line
  direct `chrome --enable-logging=stderr` probe surfaced the real
  error in plain text. Three additive PNGs (placeholder blue
  solids; replace with branded art at leisure) fix the extension.

- **`tests/test_extension_live.py` uses `channel="chromium"` + event-based
  serviceworker wait.** Two layered fixes. (1) Playwright's default
  `pw.chromium` binary is the **headless-shell**, a stripped Chromium
  that cannot host MV3 extension service workers regardless of
  `--headless=new`. `channel="chromium"` swaps to the full
  Chromium-for-Testing build that the same `playwright install
  chromium` already pulls alongside. Verified by binary inspection:
  no-channel launches `.../chromium_headless_shell-*/chrome-linux/headless_shell`
  with no SW; channel="chromium" launches `.../chromium-*/chrome-linux/chrome`
  with SW present at launch. (2) The 6-second SW poll was flaky on a
  real host under load (one of three tests reliably passed within the
  window, two reliably timed out, even though all three had a working
  SW seconds later). Replaced with `wait_for_event("serviceworker",
  timeout=30_000)`. Plus a latent CSRF bootstrap bug in
  `test_lookup_url_surfaces_blocked_state` — `/api/csrf` requires a
  prior session cookie (which only `GET /` mints), the test called
  `/api/csrf` with no prior visit so the response had no `csrf_token`
  field and `KeyError` followed. Fixed by visiting `/` first via a
  cookie jar. The CSRF bug was hidden as long as the file always
  skipped.

- **L3 `mv3-extension-service-worker` (live-test) gets the same
  channel + event-wait fix.** Identical defect to the unit test —
  `live_tests/checks.py::l3_mv3_extension_service_worker` was
  launching default-channel headless-shell with a 6-second poll.
  Now passes (`MV3 extension service worker registered -- the
  extension loads correctly on a capable browser`). 6/6 of the U35
  tests (which assert the harness contract, not the verdict) keep
  passing. `capture.sh` correspondingly re-enables L3 in its
  `--only` list.

- **`capture.sh` step [3] CSRF diag.** The pre-v3.63.5 version
  imported a non-existent `create_app()` factory from
  `bulk_downloader.app`, ImportError'd on every run, and left a
  harmless traceback in every capture's `03_csrf_diag.log`. Switched
  to `from bulk_downloader.app import app` (the canonical
  module-level Flask instance, matching `tests/test_dev_suite_tier0.py`'s
  import shape). Diagnostic output now clean: `status: 200`, meta-tag
  present, marker absent, Set-Cookie for the session. Header refreshed
  for v3.63.5+; L3 unblocked.

- **`install_windows.bat` structural fixes.** Three real defects.
  (1) `set "PIP=...\pip.exe"` followed by `"%PIP%" install ...`
  violated the NEVER rule about direct `pip.exe` invocation; switched
  every site to `"%VPYTHON%" -m pip` (matching `install_linux.sh`).
  (2) `"%VENV_DIR%\Scripts\playwright.exe" install chromium` with a
  `-m playwright` fallback became just the `-m` form directly.
  (3) The xcopy + per-file `copy /Y` block copied only the
  `bulk_downloader/` package, `downloader_ui.py`, `downloader.spec`,
  `requirements*.txt`, and `uninstall_windows.bat` into
  `%USERPROFILE%\BulkDownloader\` — leaving `tests/`, `live_tests/`,
  `extension/`, `tools/`, `fixtures/`, `run_tests.py`, and the
  `.bat` helpers entirely missing from the install target. The new
  v3.63.5 extension/test files would have been silently dropped.
  Replaced with a single `robocopy /E /XD __pycache__ .git .venv
  venv build build_tmp dist node_modules /XF *.pyc *.pyo .DS_Store
  Thumbs.db sites_config.json` (the install_dev.bat exclude list).

- **`install_dev.bat` pip.exe fix.** Same `set "PIP=...\pip.exe"`
  defect as install_windows.bat; same fix via `"%PYTHON_EXE%" -m pip`.
  Comments in the file already explained why the `-m pip` form was
  needed for pip-upgrade (v3.47.6 added the comment but only fixed
  the upgrade site, not the install sites).

- **Optional extractor pins purged.** Two pins in
  `requirements-optional.txt` were noise on every fresh install:
  `xnxx_api` (pulled from PyPI entirely, was already commented out)
  and `beeg_api>=1.3` (wheel intermittently 404'd). Both removed;
  the historical comment now records what went and why. The
  adapters in `extractors.py` are unchanged — `_try_import()`
  correctly returns None for both, and the fail-open path falls
  through to BD's generic teach-based extraction. Affected-test
  sweep (352 tests across everything importing `extractors`):
  352/352 pass.

- **`tools/dast.bat` and `tools/sast.bat` ASCII+CRLF cleanup.**
  Pre-existing defects that survived release gates because
  `bat_lint()`'s contract test only checks shape, not per-file
  `ok` status. dast.bat carried 891 non-ASCII bytes (289 `─`
  light-horizontal box-drawing, 8 `—` em-dash) and 287
  LF-not-CRLF line endings; sast.bat carried 594 non-ASCII
  (190 `─`, 8 `—`) and 232 LF lines. Both would have failed on
  Windows machines whose default code page (cp437/cp1252) didn't
  accept UTF-8 — the same v3.43.16 failure mode that motivated
  the installer ASCII fixes. Decorative substitutions only:
  `─` → `-`, `—` → `--`, LF → CRLF. No logic touched.

Added.

- **`extension/icon16.png`, `icon48.png`, `icon128.png`.** Solid
  blue (#2C5282) placeholders at the correct sizes; valid PNGs that
  load cleanly in Chrome. Operator can swap with branded artwork
  at any time.

- **`tests/test_extension_live.py`** patches (channel + wait + CSRF).
  See the corresponding Fixed entry.

- **`install_ai_ollama.bat`.** Windows companion to
  `install_ai_ollama.sh`. Same 5-step flow (GPU check, runtime,
  API wait, model pull, verify), same models (`qwen2.5vl:7b`,
  `qwen2.5:7b`), same endpoint (`http://localhost:11434`). Uses
  `OllamaSetup.exe` from `https://ollama.com/download/OllamaSetup.exe`
  via curl (Win10 1803+) with PowerShell fallback. Prompts before
  downloading; prompts to continue on CPU if no GPU.

- **`uninstall_linux.sh`.** Undoes what the three Linux installers
  do, with prompts before every destructive action. Removes the
  `bulkdownloader` systemd unit, the project's `venv/`, optionally
  the Playwright cache, optionally the Ollama service + binary +
  model cache. Preserves the source tree, `downloader_history.db`,
  `logs/`, `live_recordings/`, `sites_config.json`. Flags: `--yes`
  (accept every prompt for scripting), `--purge` (treat Ollama
  removal as default-yes), `--help`. Exit codes: 0 completed,
  1 aborted before any change, 2 a step had warnings worth looking
  at.

- **`gpu_check.sh`.** Standalone Linux GPU detector. Sections:
  PCI inventory (lspci with sysfs fallback), NVIDIA deep dive
  (name/VRAM/driver/CUDA/compute-cap), AMD ROCm via rocminfo,
  Intel iGPU vs Arc, Apple Silicon, boot environment (UEFI +
  Secure Boot via mokutil), recommendation block sized to the
  largest VRAM card (≥12 GiB / 6-12 / <6 / no GPU), optional
  copy-pasteable driver-install suggestions when hardware is
  present but no runtime is loaded. Flags: `--quiet`, `--json`
  (stable schema for installer/dev-tool consumption), `--install-drivers`
  (see below), `--help`. Exit codes: 0 accelerator usable or
  install completed-please-reboot, 1 CPU-only or operator
  aborted, 2 detection failed.

- **`gpu_check.sh --install-drivers`.** Opt-in execution of the
  printed NVIDIA suggestion on Ubuntu/Debian. Hard guards
  (refuses on non-apt systems, refuses without sudo, refuses
  when there's no NVIDIA hardware, refuses with --json since
  prompts can't coexist with machine output). Confirmation block
  documents kernel-module rebuild + reboot requirement; if
  Secure Boot is enabled, prepends a MOK enrollment warning
  with the password reminder. Prefers `ubuntu-drivers
  autoinstall` (knows the right series); falls back to
  `apt-get install nvidia-driver-535` with its own confirmation.
  Post-install reboot prompt with 5-second countdown; deferred
  reboot also supported. AMD and Intel paths deliberately not
  automated — the matrices are narrow enough that operator-driven
  manual install is safer.

- **`gpu_check.bat`.** Windows parity. WMI inventory via `wmic`
  with PowerShell `Get-CimInstance` fallback. NVIDIA deep dive
  via the same `nvidia-smi --query-gpu` queries plus dashboard-view
  CUDA-runtime parse. AMD/Intel by name substring. Secure Boot
  via `Confirm-SecureBootUEFI` (informational only; Windows
  handles signed kernel modules automatically). Same recommendation
  block + JSON output schema as the Linux side.

- **`gpu_check.bat --install-drivers`.** Browser-handoff to NVIDIA
  App + winget option for CUDA toolkit. Windows reality (May 2026):
  there is no clean winget package for "just install the NVIDIA
  driver" -- `Nvidia.CUDA` stopped bundling the driver at CUDA 13;
  the NVIDIA App is the canonical driver path but the open
  microsoft/winget-pkgs request (#140696) is blocked on a known
  manifest issue. Honest two-option prompt: (1) open
  `https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/software/nvidia-app/` in default
  browser, (2) `winget install --id Nvidia.CUDA` (only if you also
  want nvcc). Deliberately does not silently winget-install
  Nvidia.CUDA-as-a-driver since that would mislead an operator who
  only wants a driver into a 3 GB toolkit install that may not
  deliver one. AMD declined politely with the `https://www.amd.com/en/support`
  link.

Changed.

- **`install_ai_ollama.sh` step [1] delegates to `gpu_check.sh`.**
  Drops the inline 17-line NVIDIA-only check in favour of a single
  `"$SCRIPT_DIR/gpu_check.sh"` call (with a `nvidia-smi`-only
  fallback if `gpu_check.sh` isn't present alongside). Exit code 1
  from the detector triggers the original "CPU fallback, Ctrl+C
  to abort" 5-second window; exit 0 proceeds straight to step [2].

- **`capture.sh` step [6] re-enables L3.** The earlier exclusion
  was because L3 wedged on the headless-extension symptom; with
  the channel + wait fix in `live_tests/checks.py`, L3 PASSes
  cleanly. `LIVE_IDS` now reads `L1,L2,L3,L4,...,L35`. Header
  comment also refreshed for v3.63.5+.

Notes.

- This release is dev-tooling + installer + diagnostic surface
  only. Download/login/extractor runtime paths are byte-identical
  to v3.63.4. Stash deployment is mechanical (`unzip -o` the
  release zip on top of v3.63.4 + restart the service).
- The KB carries OPEN_THREADS entries that are deliberately not
  closed by this release: the F6 `runner.py` refactor (long-deferred
  for load-bearing-dispatch reasons), T46 active VPN kill-switch
  probe (dedicated-session deferral), AMD ROCm install (out of
  scope by design in `gpu_check.sh --install-drivers`). These
  are deferred-by-rationale items, not TODOs.

## v3.63.4 — 2026-05-20

Two L34 `full-route-smoke` fixes that surfaced from the v3.63.3
stash captures. **No download/login/extractor runtime change.**
Full-suite gate from the source tree in 6 foreground batches:
4340 / 4337 / 0 / 3 — clean. Stash verified live: live-tests
18 pass / 10 warn / 0 fail (exit 0) against the deployed tree
before the cut.

Fixed.

- **L34 streaming-skip** — `live_tests/checks.py` now carries
  `_L34_STREAMING_SKIP = frozenset({"/api/stream"})` and L34's
  target filter excludes those routes. Root cause: the harness's
  `ctx.get()` uses `urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=N)`, whose
  `timeout` arg bounds connect + headers only — `r.read()` on a
  streaming response is unbounded. L34 GET'd `/api/stream` (SSE),
  sat in `read()` for 77s of a 90s window, and was killed by T55's
  wall as a misleading FAIL. `/api/stream` is the only
  parameter-free streaming route in the codebase as of v3.63.3
  (verified by grep); the other two streamers `/api/import/stream/
  <job_id>` and `/stream/<token>` are already excluded by L34's
  existing `<`-parameter filter. New streamers must be added to
  the set. The log line now announces the skip count and the
  skipped routes by name so the operator reading a capture can
  tell skip from miss.
- **L34 4xx-is-OK** — L34's loop got a three-branch shape:
  `if rok` (success), `elif rstatus is not None` (HTTPError: the
  route responded, just with a non-2xx — count as wired, only
  5xx FAILs), `else` (truly unreachable, `rstatus is None` —
  connection-level failure). Pre-fix the loop only branched on
  `rok`, so every 4xx route hit the `not rok` branch with
  `rbody = None`, "timed out" wasn't in `""`, and it got bucketed
  as `unreachable`. L34's docstring has always promised "A 4xx is
  treated as OK — the route is wired and responding"; the loop
  was silently violating that. Surfaced by the streaming-skip
  fix: with L34 finally completing the sweep, the 21:16 stash
  capture showed 10 routes "unreachable" with `None` bodies, all
  real 4xx routes (legitimate auth, missing-param, dual-method
  `["GET","POST"]` like `/api/quick_add` and `/api/route_preview`).
- **Regression pin** — 12 tests in `tests/test_u44_l34_route_smoke.py`:
  registration + non-disruptive, `_L34_STREAMING_SKIP` exists +
  type + `/api/stream` membership + skip-set-only-contains-streaming
  sanity, source-grep that L34's filter references the set,
  source-grep that the loop discriminates on `rstatus is not None`,
  plus functional tests via a fake Context that L34 doesn't GET
  streaming routes, announces the skip, treats 4xx as wired
  (PASS), still FAILs on 5xx via HTTPError, and still FAILs on
  truly-unreachable routes where `rstatus is None`.

Verification arc on stash this cycle: three captures, each one
unit shipped between them. **20:44** — initial v3.63.3 deploy,
L34 wedged at 90s (250/300 routes attempted before the wall).
**21:16** — post-streaming-skip deploy, L34 completed 299/300
(the `/api/stream` skip) but FAIL'd on 10 4xx-as-unreachable.
**21:31** — post-4xx-fix deploy, L34 PASS with "all 299
parameter-free GET routes responded < 500", overall live-tests
18 pass / 10 warn / 0 fail, exit code 0. T56's systemd-unit
fixes (v3.63.3) confirmed clean on stash in all three captures.

Closed in the same cut: stash now verified clean at this release
boundary; the deploy-v3.63.3 + re-run-capture operator-action
item from v3.63.3's OPEN_THREADS is satisfied as a byproduct of
the v3.63.4 verification cycle.

## v3.63.3 — 2026-05-20

The real fix for the 5 systemd-test failures that v3.63.2 was
supposed to close but didn't. v3.63.2's T54 (env-probe timeout)
was a defensible robustness improvement but addressed the wrong
root cause. The actual bug was in `live_tests/checks.py`:
`systemctl show <missing> -p Restart` returns the systemd default
`'no'` with rc=0, and `systemctl is-active <missing>` returns
`'inactive'` with rc=3 — and the live-check helpers treated
those identical-to-real-unit returns as REAL misconfiguration,
flipping L25 and L27 to FAIL on any host where the test suite
runs before `install_service.sh`. **No download/login/extractor
runtime change.** Full-suite gate from the source tree in 6
foreground batches: 4340 / 4337 / 0 / 3 — clean.

Fixed.

- **T56** — `live_tests/checks.py` mis-FAIL'd on missing units.
  Added `_unit_exists(name)` helper that uses
  `systemctl is-enabled` (the only systemctl query that uniquely
  returns the literal `not-found` for a missing unit). Gated
  `_svc_property()` on `_unit_exists`: it now returns None for
  a missing unit instead of the systemd default. Added a
  `_unit_exists` gate to `l27_survives_logout` BEFORE its
  is-active read (l25_restart_on_crash is fixed transitively
  by the `_svc_property` change — it short-circuits to WARN
  on `restart is None`). The `_systemctl` helper's docstring
  was updated to flag the
  ok=True-means-"ran"-not-"unit-exists" trap that started this.
- **T56 (continued)** — rewrote `tests/test_u41_systemd_live_tests.py`
  assertions to a three-branch truth table covering all three
  environments: (a) no bus, (b) bus exists but no unit installed
  yet, (c) bus + unit. The old two-branch logic conflated (a)
  and (b), which is exactly what failed on stash during step [2]
  of the fresh-machine capture (suite runs before install_service).
- **T56 (test infrastructure bug)** — `tests/test_live_harness.py`
  used `setup_module` / `teardown_module` for registry snapshot/
  restore. The custom `run_tests.py` runner does NOT call those
  pytest module-lifecycle hooks (it only honours class-based
  setup/teardown and autouse fixtures), so the restore never
  fired and every test_u32..u43 + test_t46 in the same batch
  saw a poisoned `_REGISTRY` containing the fake `T_A` / `T_B`
  registrations from the last harness test. Replaced with an
  autouse fixture that restores to a module-load snapshot
  around every test. Applied the same pattern in
  `tests/test_t55_live_test_harness_timeout.py` (which had the
  same fragile try/finally). LESSON: the custom runner's
  autouse-fixture discovery rejects underscore-prefixed names
  (`not name.startswith("_")`), so module-level autouse fixtures
  must be public-named (`autouse_*`).

Internal.

- Test counts at v3.63.3: full-suite gate 4340 / 4337 / 0 / 3
  in the sandbox (was 4330 / 4322 / 5 / 3 in v3.63.2 on stash;
  +10 tests from T56's 8 new tests plus 2 additional cases in
  the rewritten u41 assertions). The 5 v3.63.2 failures are
  resolved — both root cause (checks.py mis-FAIL) and test-
  side ambiguity (u41 three-branch logic).
- T54 stays in v3.63.3 — it's still a valid robustness
  improvement (the env probe IS load-coupled; the fix prevents
  a different failure mode under heavier `--workers=N` load).
  It just wasn't the cause of the 5 failures.

## v3.63.2 — 2026-05-20

Patch release covering the two issues surfaced by the v3.63.1
fresh-machine deploy: a test-side env-probe timeout that caused
5 spurious failures under `--workers=4`, and a live-test harness
that wedged forever on any check that didn't return. **No changes
to the download / login / extractor runtime.** Full-suite gate
run from the source tree in 6 foreground batches: 4330 / 4327 /
0 / 3 — clean.

Fixed.

- **T54** — `tests/_env.py` 2-second `subprocess.run(timeout=2)`
  on `_has_systemd_bus()` and `_has_bulkdownloader_unit()` was
  too tight under `--workers=4` parallel test load. A single
  transient stall cached `HAS_BULKDOWNLOADER_UNIT=False` for the
  rest of the worker, even when the unit WAS installed and
  active — flipping every environment-branched assertion in
  `test_u41_systemd_live_tests.py` to the wrong branch (5
  failures). Fix: bumped the timeout to 8 seconds via the new
  `_SYSTEMD_PROBE_TIMEOUT_S` constant, and wrapped subprocess
  calls in `_run_with_retry`: a single `TimeoutExpired` now
  retries once before concluding "no bus / no unit". Same True/
  False return semantics as before, but forgiving of a single
  transient stall. The five v3.63.1 failures now pass on a real
  deployment.

Added — live-test harness robustness.

- **T55** — per-check hard timeout in `live_tests/harness.py`.
  The v3.63.1 fresh-machine capture confirmed twice that a
  wedged check (L3, the browser-extension MV3 service worker
  test on a host without MV3 support) blocked the entire run
  forever. New: every check now runs in a daemon thread via
  `harness._run_with_timeout(fn, ctx, timeout_s)`, with default
  `DEFAULT_PER_CHECK_TIMEOUT_S = 60.0`. A check that doesn't
  return in time is recorded as FAIL with detail
  `TIMEOUT after Ns (limit 60.0s) — the check did not return in
  time; thread leaked`, and the harness continues to the next
  check. `run_all()` gained a `per_check_timeout_s` kwarg;
  `live_tests/run.py` exposes `--per-check-timeout`. Wedged
  threads are intentionally LEAKED rather than killed (Python
  has no safe way to terminate a thread holding native
  resources such as Playwright pages or ffmpeg subprocesses);
  they are daemon threads and die with the process at run-end.

Added — tests.

- `tests/test_t54_env_probe_timeout.py` (9 tests) — constant
  range, `_run_with_retry` happy path / retry-after-one-timeout
  / give-up-after-two-timeouts / non-Timeout exceptions not
  retried, source-level grep guard against re-introducing
  `timeout=2)`, cached-constant types, ordering invariant.
- `tests/test_t55_live_test_harness_timeout.py` (7 tests) —
  default constant range, helper presence, fast-function
  outcome, raise outcome, slow-function timeout (with a wall-
  clock check that the helper doesn't wait for the slow body),
  end-to-end through `run_all()` with a wedging check followed
  by a quick one (asserts FAIL+TIMEOUT for the wedger, PASS
  for the quick one, exit code 1, total elapsed under 3s
  despite a 5s sleep in the wedger), CLI `--help` documents the
  new flag.

Internal.

- Test counts at v3.63.2: full-suite gate 4330 / 4327 / 0 / 3
  (was 4314 / 4306 / 5 / 3 on the v3.63.1 fresh-machine
  capture; the 5 failures are resolved by T54 and 16 new tests
  were added by T54+T55).
- The standing "every-5-units full-suite gate" cadence rule
  fired naturally at this release — T47, T49, T50, T51, T54,
  T55 = 6 units, gate-clean.

## v3.63.1 — 2026-05-20

Patch release covering the four autonomous open-task items from the
v3.63.0 KB triage — one storage-tier UTC-cutoff bug, one
runner-timing prerequisite + the D-71 dev tool that consumes it,
and the regenerate-goldens CLI that pairs with T42. **No changes to
the download / login / extractor runtime.** Per operator
instruction, the every-5-units full-suite gate was skipped for
this release; affected-test sweeps covered the touched surface
(140 + 32 = 172 tests, 0 failures).

Fixed.

- **T47 (D-?)** — `storage_tier.find_candidates()` built its
  `cutoff_iso` via `time.localtime(cutoff_ts)` and compared it
  against the UTC `queue.ts_updated` TEXT column. On any non-UTC
  host the per-site migration sweep missed or extra-included
  files by the host's UTC offset. One-line fix:
  `time.gmtime(cutoff_ts)`. Test forces `TZ=Pacific/Auckland`,
  inserts boundary rows 5h either side of the UTC cutoff, asserts
  only the older row is selected; fails under the bug, passes
  under the fix. Pairs with LESSONS_LEARNED A2.

Added — runner instrumentation and dev tooling.

- **T49** — per-test wall-clock timing in `run_tests.py`. Result
  tuples gained a `duration_seconds` field; all ~10 unpacking
  sites updated. `--json` artifact gained `schema_version: 2`
  and a full `tests` list (with per-test durations for passes
  too, not just failures/skips). Worker-subprocess
  reconstruction prefers the new `tests` list, falls back to
  the old `failures` + `skips` + `passed`-count reconstruction
  for back-compat. `--summary` gained a `SLOWEST 20 TESTS` tail
  block; the top-of-file header format is unchanged so existing
  parsers are unaffected.
- **T50 (D-71)** — `/api/dev/test_timing`. Read-only dev tool
  that loads the latest `run_tests.py --json` artifact and
  returns the slowest N tests + per-file totals (count, total,
  avg, max seconds). Reuses the existing `_load_test_results()`
  helper. Schema-gates artifacts older than v2 with an explicit
  error rather than silently returning zero-duration results.
  Query params: `?path=` (default `test_results.json` in cwd)
  and `?top=` (default 30, capped at 200). Standard dev-mode
  guard.
- **T51 (D-75 follow-on)** — `tools/regenerate_goldens.py` CLI.
  Pairs with the read-only T42 dev tool: T42 reports drift
  between `.golden` and `.current`, T51 lets the operator
  regenerate baselines under explicit consent. Dry-run by
  default; `--apply` requires `--reason "..."` (recorded in an
  append-only `tools/regenerate_goldens.log` with timestamp +
  git rev). Refuses to act on a dirty goldens directory
  (`--force` overrides), refuses to copy from an empty
  `.current`. Atomic writes (`.tmp` sibling + `os.replace`).
  Off-network. Updates `<stem>.golden.meta` with
  `last_regenerated_ts` / `_reason` / `_rev` on each apply.

Added — tests.

## v3.63.0 — 2026-05-20

Tier 4 of the dev-tools backlog (T34–T46) complete. Minor bump — 13
new units, two new lightweight subsystems (feature flags + request
replay), and the read-only version of the VPN kill-switch live
test. **No changes to the download/login/extractor runtime.** All
new `/api/dev/*` routes are dev-mode-gated; mutating routes are
POST + CSRF-gated.

Added — Tier-4 dev tools (T34–T43).

- **T34** (D-107) — `/api/dev/dead_css`. Scan shipped CSS files for
  selectors not referenced in templates or JS. Reports unused
  classes/ids and an "ambiguous" bucket for selectors that look
  like they might be built dynamically (template literals).
- **T35** (D-117) — `/api/dev/storage_tier_status`. Surface the
  `StorageTierScheduler` state plus per-site dry-run counts via
  `storage_tier.find_candidates` (read-only SELECT).
- **T36** (D-122) — `/api/dev/maintenance_mode` (read),
  `/api/dev/maintenance_enable` + `/api/dev/maintenance_disable`
  (mutating, CSRF-gated). Rides on the existing
  `maintenance.py` windows subsystem — an immediate override is a
  one-shot window starting now, tagged with `_immediate_override_`
  so the toggle can find and remove it. Real scheduled windows are
  untouched by the disable path.
- **T37** (D-56) — `/api/dev/token_estimate` (POST, body-carrying
  read-only). Char-based heuristic per provider (ollama, claude,
  openai, gemini). Cross-provider table on every response.
- **T38** (D-108) — `/api/dev/i18n_coverage`. Diff strings extracted
  from templates against each shipped locale's catalog. Reports
  uncovered strings (in source but no translation) and stale
  entries (in catalog but no longer in source). `_meta` keys
  correctly excluded from translation counts.
- **T39** (D-58) — `/api/dev/model_pull_check`. Verify Ollama-installed
  models against the configured/requested set. **Honours the DANGER
  rule against hardcoded registry tags** — requested set comes from
  `OllamaProvider.default_models` + `_app_cfg.ai_models`. Returns
  exact `ollama pull` commands for missing models. Read-only.
- **T40** (D-121, A-flagged) — `/api/dev/feature_flags` (read),
  `/api/dev/feature_flag_set` + `/api/dev/feature_flag_delete`
  (mutating, CSRF-gated). New tiny module `feature_flags.py` —
  atomic .tmp + replace, mtime-keyed cache, fail-open. Flag names
  must match `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{1,63}$`; values must be literal
  bools.
- **T41** (D-16) — `/api/dev/window_simulate` (POST, body-carrying
  read-only). Stateless simulation of `download_window.site_in_window()`
  against synthetic timestamps. Reports per-sample open/closed,
  transitions, and open-fraction.
- **T42** (D-75) — `/api/dev/golden_files`. Inventory
  `tests/fixtures/golden/*.golden` and diff each against an optional
  `.current` sibling. Reads `.golden.meta` JSON sidecars. **Regenerate
  path is deliberately not exposed via HTTP** — that's a future CLI
  script the operator runs by hand.
- **T43** (D-47) — `/api/dev/tls_check` (POST, opt-in network).
  Connects to each host, walks the cert chain, reports expiry / SANs /
  issuer. Hosts must be passed explicitly OR derived from
  `site_configs` HTTPS URLs via `derive_from_sites: true`. Per-host
  timeout clamped to [0, 30]s. First Tier-4 unit that makes outbound
  network calls — never auto-run.

Added — Tier-4 dev tools (T44–T45).

- **T44** (D-46) — `/api/dev/request_replay_list` (read),
  `/api/dev/request_replay/<id>` (POST, CSRF-gated). New module
  `request_replay.py` — bounded deque(maxlen=200), captures /api/*
  requests when the `request_capture` feature flag is on (off by
  default). Sensitive headers (Cookie, Authorization, X-CSRF-Token)
  redacted at capture; bodies truncated to 4096 chars. Replay
  re-issues through the SAME flask app so auth/CSRF middleware
  applies — replay cannot bypass auth. Refuses to replay if the
  original body was truncated at capture.
- **T45** (D-27) — `/api/dev/login_flows` (read),
  `/api/dev/login_flow_save` + `/api/dev/login_flow_delete`
  (mutating, CSRF-gated). New module `login_flow_recorder.py` —
  thin registry over the existing `macro_recorder` infrastructure,
  using a canonical `login_flow` tag. **Tag invariant**: only
  macros carrying the tag are visible through this surface, and
  `delete_login_flow` refuses to remove a macro that lacks the
  tag (defends against accidental delete of an unrelated macro
  that shares a name).

Added — Tier-4 live test (T46).

- **T46** (L-29 read-only) — `live_tests/checks.py` entry
  `l29_vpn_kill_switch_config_check`. Confirms `vpn_kill_switch`
  module loads, `list_kill_states()` works, `get_auto_recover()`
  is introspectable. Three verdict branches (PASS / WARN / FAIL).
  **disruptive=False** — the active network-leak probe with
  iptables/nftables toggling and DNS leak verification stays
  deferred per the backlog rule. PASS verdict explicitly notes the
  active probe is not part of this check, so operators don't
  mistake green for proof of leak-blocking under load.

Tests added: 174 new (suite total 4101 → 4275).

Real bugs caught + fixed during gates.

- **T36 framing.** D-122 description suggested a brand-new
  "maintenance mode" subsystem, but `maintenance.py` already
  shipped scheduled-window infrastructure that the runner consults
  via `is_action_paused()`. Reframed as an immediate-override on top
  of that surface — much smaller and avoids a parallel state machine.
- **`storage_tier.py` UTC-vs-localtime mismatch** at line 299–300.
  `time.localtime(cutoff_ts)` builds an ISO string compared against
  the SQLite `ts_updated` UTC TEXT column — exactly the DANGER
  pattern. Found incidentally while wiring T35, flagged in
  OPEN_THREADS, **not fixed this release** (out of scope; left for
  a deliberate bug-fix unit).
- **T40 test isolation.** First T40 run had 5 failures because
  `constants.INSTALL_DIR` is captured at module-import time
  (LESSON L2). `clean_workdir` only chdirs — doesn't reset
  INSTALL_DIR — so the JSON state file path is shared across tests
  in a run. Fix: per-test isolation by monkeypatching
  `feature_flags.state_path()` to a tmp_path sibling, mirroring the
  existing `test_i18n_phase191.py` pattern. New tests in T44 reuse
  the same pattern.
- **T45 test bug.** Initial `test_record_invalid_name_rejected`
  expected `"INVALID NAME"` to be rejected, but
  `macro_recorder._normalize_name` lowercases + replaces spaces
  with hyphens. Switched to `"bad!name"` (the `!` is genuinely not
  in the allowed set).
- **dev_suite `_repo_root` dup.** A throwaway helper I added during
  T34 duplicated the existing one at line 618. Caught by the
  DANGER_NOTES dup-def audit; removed the duplicate and used the
  existing helper. LESSON L6 in action.

Decisions.

- **T36 reframed** (above): immediate-override on existing windows
  subsystem, not a parallel global flag.
- **T40 (A) handled with atomic-write contract.** Same pattern as
  config snapshots — `.tmp` sibling then `os.replace()`, mtime-
  keyed cache, value coercion (any non-bool dropped at load time).
  HTTP toggle is POST + CSRF; values must be JSON literal bools,
  no string-truthiness coercion.
- **T42 regenerate path NOT exposed via HTTP.** The route reports
  drift; regeneration mutates test inputs and stays a future CLI
  script.
- **T43 outbound network calls are opt-in.** Caller must supply
  hosts explicitly or pass `derive_from_sites: true`. Per-host
  timeout clamped. No auto-scan.
- **T44 capture default-off.** The feature flag pattern means a
  freshly-deployed v3.63.0 captures nothing until the operator
  explicitly turns it on. Per-request cost when off: one cheap
  `is_on()` call.
- **T45 tag invariant on delete.** Refusing to delete an untagged
  macro via the login-flow surface is a defensive choice — a macro
  named "main" that happens to be a scroll macro shouldn't be
  removable by a generic "delete login flow main" call.
- **T46 disruptive=False, active probe deferred.** Per the
  DEV_BACKLOG note about L-29 needing deliberate real-network
  setup. The read-only inspector ships; the active probe waits for
  a dedicated session.

Tier 4 is now fully complete (T34–T46). No tier work remains in the
backlog. Future work: speculative items the backlog didn't tier,
operator-driven feature requests, and the OPEN-threads bug-fixes
(storage_tier UTC mismatch, etc).

## v3.62.7 — 2026-05-20

A continuation of the Tier-3 dev-tools arc opened in v3.62.6 plus a
test-environment fix. **No changes to the download/login/extractor
runtime.** The `/api/dev/*` surface grew with seven Tier-3 units
(T11–T17); the test suite now branches on whether the host running
it has a systemd bus, the `bulkdownloader` unit, and a local Ollama
listening.

Added — Tier-3 dev tools.
- T11/D-37 + D-38 — dedup-hash explorer and partial-download finder.
  Surfaces the perceptual-hash registry (`video_hashes` table)
  contents and walks every configured `download_dir` for `.part`
  resumable tempfiles, classifying each as resumable (with `.meta`
  sidecar) or orphaned.
- T12/D-40 — filename-template previewer. Renders a template
  through `fname.resolve_filename_template` against the canonical
  sample context from `KNOWN_VARIABLES`; surfaces unknown
  placeholders (silently stripped by the resolver) and verifies
  path-traversal sanitization.
- T13/D-41 + D-43 — VPN config renderer and provider-rotation view.
  Pairs each stored tunnel config with its live `Tunnel` state,
  redacts secrets via the canonical `vpn._redact_config`, groups
  configured tunnels by provider, identifies the next cycle target.
- T14/D-42 + D-49 — VPN connectivity probe and egress-IP monitor.
  Calls `vpn.check_health()` per registered tunnel and reports
  per-tunnel SOCKS URL + last-known public IP + freshness; flags
  shared IPs across tunnels.
- T15/D-45 + D-48 — FlareSolverr health and captcha-relay status.
  Read-only ping + cumulative solver stats; pending-captcha queue
  grouped by type and resolution state; flags when the runner's
  takeover starter/ender callbacks aren't wired.
- T16/D-50 — UA / stealth audit. Per-site UA + stealth-flag review;
  reports `playwright-stealth` library availability via the
  existing probe; flags misconfig like `use_stealth_library=True`
  with the library absent, `headless=False`, or `use_stealth=False`.
- T17/D-112 + D-113 — disk-usage breakdown and download-folder
  scanner. Shared filesystem walk over configured `download_dir`s.
  D-112 reports bytes per extension, age bucket, and site; D-113
  reports zero-byte files, very-small files (<10 KB), orphan
  `.part` files (no `.meta` sidecar), and duplicate filenames
  across sites. Path-allowlist enforced; `max_files` cap.

Routes added under `/api/dev/*` (all dev-mode gated, read-only):
`dedup_hashes`, `partials`, `filename_template`, `vpn_config`,
`vpn_rotation`, `vpn_probe`, `egress_ip`, `flaresolverr_health`,
`captcha_relay`, `stealth_audit`, `disk_usage`, `download_scan`.

Fixed — test environment branching. Seven tests that asserted the
sandbox environment (no systemd bus, no Ollama listening) as the
expected outcome now detect the host's actual environment and assert
the right branch. The deployment host `stash` has the
`bulkdownloader` systemd unit installed and Ollama listening; tests
on that host previously reported 10 failures purely because the
contract was inverted. (Three CSRF-bootstrap tests in the same group
are still investigating — a diagnostic at
`tools/diag_csrf_bootstrap.py` ships in this release; output from
that diagnostic on stash is the next datum needed.)

Test baseline: ~4105 pass / 0 fail / 3 skip on the sandbox (6
foreground batches). The 3 skips are the expected
`test_extension_live.py` headless-Chromium MV3 ones — not a
regression.



A large internal-tooling release: the dev-tools backlog (Tier 0–2 and
the start of Tier 3) plus a standalone live-test suite. No changes to
the download/login/extractor runtime — this release is dev/ops
tooling and one dead-code cleanup.

Added — dev-tools suite expansion. The `/api/dev/*` surface (all
dev-mode gated; state-changing tools also CSRF-gated) grew with
read-only inspection and validation tools and a set of maintenance
actions, including: release-integrity checks (version-consistency,
CHANGELOG lint, .bat/.sh lint, zip-manifest verify), CSRF-coverage and
auth-surface maps, backup verifier and integrity-check runner,
structured-log search, stuck-job and rate-limit inspectors,
session-keeper heartbeat monitor, Ollama model inventory, endpoint
latency/error panels, exception ring-buffer, thread-dump and
deadlock detector, the `_process_one` dispatch-chain tracer and
dry-run, config schema audit and import preflight, duplicate-site and
orphan-row scans, cookie-jar and login-template inspectors, the
extractor capability matrix, ffmpeg/resolution previews, HLS/DASH
manifest probe, event-broker tap (with a dev SSE-tap UI page),

for completeness), `dev_events.py` (bounded event ring-buffer behind
the event-broker tap) and `dev_metrics.py` (shared in-process
per-request timing used by the latency/error tools).

Added — `live_tests/` package: a standalone live-test suite (separate
from the unit suite and from `live_check.py`) that runs against a
running deployment. 28 checks covering browser launch, DB/WAL
concurrency and integrity, the session keeper, the download/HLS
pipeline, login, AI/Ollama, backup-restore, SSE, and systemd
lifecycle. Disruptive checks (real downloads, systemd lifecycle) are
opt-in via an explicit flag; every check degrades to WARN when it
cannot conclude rather than failing.

Changed — removed the dead `events` table. Three modules
(`timeline.py`, `eol_export.py`, `diagnostics_bundle.py`) queried a
`SELECT ... FROM events` table that nothing in the codebase ever
wrote to, and `migrations.EXPECTED_SCHEMA` listed it — so
`detect_drift()` false-flagged it as missing on every fresh DB. The
dead reads and the manifest entry were removed; all three readers
already failed open, so no observable behaviour changed. A fresh DB
now reports no schema drift.

Tests — the suite is ~3914 pass / 0 fail / 3 skip on Linux (the 3

## v3.62.5 — 2026-05-18

Completes the internal dev-tools suite with maintenance actions.

Added — four maintenance tools, all dev-mode gated; the three
state-changing ones are also CSRF-gated:
- `/api/dev/gc` (POST) — run a full garbage collection and report
  objects freed.
- `/api/dev/wal_checkpoint` (POST) — flush the WAL sidecar into the
  main DB; reports sidecar size before/after. Mode arg PASSIVE | FULL
  | RESTART | TRUNCATE (default TRUNCATE).
- `/api/dev/log_level` (GET/POST) — view or set the runtime log level
  for the bulk_downloader logger tree; reversible.

  client count and per-connection age.
- `/api/dev/sql` (POST) — run a single read-only SELECT against the
  DB. Multiple statements, any write/DDL keyword, and PRAGMA are all
  refused; the keyword filter is token-boundary based so a column
  named e.g. `updated_at` is not mistaken for an UPDATE.

This completes the 16-tool dev suite begun in v3.62.4 (8 inspection +
4 validation + 4 maintenance).

## v3.62.4 — 2026-05-18

Reliability fixes plus a new internal dev-tools surface.

Fixed:
- Login submit loop kept firing further submit methods after the page
  had already closed/navigated, producing noisy "Target page has been
  closed" errors. The loop now detects a closed/navigated page and
  stops on the first effective submit.
- "Page closed mid-submit + at least one cookie = success" was too
  loose and could mark a failed login as succeeded. Cookie-based
  success now requires a plausible authenticated cookie set
  (an auth/session-named cookie, or several substantial cookies).
- AI status icon could stay on ✗ even while the backend was healthy:
  `refreshAIStatus()` early-returned because the toolbar status dot
  was removed when AI settings moved into the Settings overlay in
  v3.62.2. Status is now updated unconditionally.
- Live-update audit: the Activity Timeline and Sessions modals fetched
  once and never refreshed. Both now poll on a 10s timer while open
  (paused when the tab is hidden).
- `mass_import._jobs` retained every finished import job indefinitely;
  it is now bounded to the 50 most recent finished jobs.

Added:
- Perf lab — an internal, dev-only memory audit (`/api/dev/mem_audit`,
  with optional tracemalloc tracking) and load injector
  (`/api/dev/load` — memory/threads/objects/queue profiles, every
  profile cancellable and reversible).
- Dev suite — 12 read-only dev/inspection endpoints under `/api/dev/`:
  `routes`, `threads`, `db_stats`, `runner_state`, `logtail`, `env`,
  `config` (secrets redacted), `proc`, `invariants` (runtime
  DANGER_MAP audit), `template_audit`, `leak_scan`, `config_check`.

All new dev endpoints are gated by the existing dev-mode guard.
Test baseline: ~3502 pass / 0 fail / 3 skip (Linux, `run_tests.py`).

## v3.62.3 — 2026-05-18

Bug-fix + UX release for the Ollama AI integration.

**Fixes**

- AI settings: the model picker in the AI-settings modal kept its own
  copy of the Ollama model tags and still used the dead
  `qwen2-vl:7b-q4` / `qwen2.5:7b-q4` names — the v3.62.2 fix had
  corrected only the Python backend. Accepting the AI-settings
  defaults could therefore save non-existent model tags into the live
  config, after which every Ollama pull and health check failed. The
  frontend now uses the real registry tags (`qwen2.5vl:7b` /
  `qwen2.5:7b`), matching the backend. Stale tags in the
  `install_ai_ollama.sh` header comment and two test helpers were
  corrected in the same pass.

**New**

- AI settings: the vision and text model fields are now dropdowns
  populated from the models the configured provider actually exposes —
  Ollama's pulled models (live `/api/tags`), or a cloud provider's
  model list. New `POST /api/ai/models` endpoint and
  `aiassist.list_available_models()`. A ↻ Refresh button re-queries
  the endpoint after a model is pulled on the host; an "Other…" option
  preserves a free-text escape hatch for a model not listed yet. This
  makes the dead-tag class of bug structurally hard to hit: the
  operator picks from what the endpoint has instead of typing a tag
  blind.

**Tests**

- `test_v3_62_2_guards.py` gained a check that greps `app.js` for dead
  Ollama tags — the existing guard was Python-only, which is why the
  frontend copy survived v3.62.2.
- New `test_v3_62_3_model_dropdown.py` covers the model lister, the
  `/api/ai/models` route, and the dropdown UI.

## v3.62.2 — 2026-05-17

Feature + UX release. Adds operator-facing features (bulk site
import, login templates), a parallel test runner, and a round of
dashboard/header polish. Suite: ~3435 pass / 0 fail / 3 skip on
Linux.

**New features**

- CSV bulk-add: import many sites from a CSV (name, login URL,
  credentials, optional template). New `csv_bulk.py` module, a
  downloadable CSV template listing every built-in template, and a
  `POST /api/sites/bulk_csv` endpoint. The CSV template is data-first
  (header + example row on top, instructions below as comments). An
  XLSX template is also offered (`GET /api/sites/xlsx_template`) — a
  formatted workbook with a fillable "Sites" sheet, a dropdown on the
  template column, and an "Instructions" sheet; the importer accepts
  uploaded `.xlsx` as well as `.csv`. Adds `openpyxl` as a runtime
  dependency.
- Combined-auth site wizard: the wizard's login step now accepts a
  cookie file AND username/password together, instead of three
  exclusive radios.
- Auto-teach template skip: a site with a template applied no longer
  opens the first-run teach window — `runner.py` treats an applied
  template as already-taught.
- Consolidated Settings: an app-wide Settings overlay (header button)
  gathers performance, watch folder, logging and AI options, plus
  links to the credential vault, notifications, AI assist, HTML
  template creator, UI event logging and backup editors. Five
  controls moved off the header into this overlay to declutter it.
- 30-theme picker: 29 new themes alongside the original dark theme,
  selectable from a header dropdown, persisted in localStorage.
  Generated by `tools/gen_themes.py`.

**Parallel test runner**

`run_tests.py` gains `--workers[=N]`: runs each test file in its own
subprocess, pins the fixed-port fixture-site files to run serially,
and re-runs any failures serially to classify them flaky-vs-real. No
flag = the original serial behaviour, unchanged.

**Bug fixes**

- `/manifest.json` returned HTTP 500 on every page load — the route
  referenced an undefined `PWA_MANIFEST` constant (lost in the
  v3.62.1 mobile_view cleanup). It now serves the real
  `static/manifest.json`.
- Adding a site did not refresh the sidebar until a manual reload —
  the post-create refresh was short-circuited while SSE was active.
  Site create/edit/import now force an unconditional refresh.
- The Basic/Advanced field toggle did not visibly do anything: it
  was a header button affecting only the site editor, and its
  section-tagging missed most sections. The toggle moved into the
  site editor's header; Basic mode now shows exactly the essential
  fields (site name, concurrency, download dir, login URL,
  credentials, cookie file).

**UI**

- Dashboard widget bar: a toolbar toggle hides/shows the whole
  widget block, remembered per scope (Global and each site
  independently).
- Per-site cookie manager: a Cookies button in the site detail panel
  exports the site's saved cookies, and imports cookies by pasted
  text, a file path, or an upload — always copying them into
  BulkDownloader's own cookies folder.
- New sites default to `headless = true` (the form previously forced
  it off, overriding the headless-by-default backend). Manual Teach
  and login takeover continue to force a visible browser regardless.

**Login templates**

- Login-page HTML extractor: `template_extractor.extract_login_from_html()`
  parses a login page's HTML into a `learned.login` selector block
  (user / password / submit). Handles honeypot fields, JS-wired
  submit elements, non-standard input types, multi-form pages, and
  attribute-less elements (structural-selector fallback). Username and
  password inputs that share a class get distinct type-qualified
  selectors so credentials never cross. Endpoint
  `POST /api/template/extract_login`.
- Login templates as a first-class concept, separate from download
  templates: a site selects one of each independently. New
  `login_templates_data.py` ships 28 ready login templates extracted
  from real login pages. Endpoints `GET /api/login_templates` and
  `POST /api/sites/<sid>/login_template/apply`; a "Login Template"
  picker in the site detail panel.
- Bulk importer gains a `login_template` column alongside `template`
  — in both the CSV template (with a LOGIN TEMPLATES reference list)
  and the XLSX template (its own hidden-sheet dropdown). Applying a
  login template writes its selectors into the site's `learned.login`,
  so the first-run manual-login teach is skipped automatically.
- Templated-login failure fallback: when an automatic login using a
  login template fails, the site falls back to a manual-login
  takeover (the flow the template-skip bypassed) instead of dying.
  Worker-initiated relogins keep report-only behaviour for their
  auth-retry backoff.

## v3.62.1 — 2026-05-16

Cross-platform fix release. v3.62.0's test suite was green on Linux
but had not been run on Windows; doing so surfaced one real app bug
and a set of Linux-only test assumptions. All are fixed here. The
suite now passes on Windows and Linux both (3389 pass / 0 fail /
4 environment skips).

**App bugfix — bandwidth chart was empty for non-UTC users**

`bw_chart.py`: `hourly_bandwidth()` and `hourly_jobs()` grouped rows
using SQLite's `strftime` over the `ts` column (UTC), but built the
dense-series lookup keys with `datetime.datetime.now()` (local time).
On any machine not in the UTC timezone the keys never matched the SQL
buckets, so the dashboard bandwidth/jobs charts showed all zeros.
Both functions now build their series in UTC to match the database.
This affected every real user outside UTC, not just tests.

**Test-suite cross-platform fixes**

- Encoding: ~49 `open()` / `read_text()` calls across 16 test files
  had no `encoding=` argument, so they used the platform default
  (cp1252 on Windows) and crashed with `UnicodeDecodeError` reading
  UTF-8 asset files. All now specify `encoding="utf-8"`.
- POSIX-path assumptions: 7 tests asserted hardcoded `/`-style paths;
  the app correctly emits native paths (`C:\...` on Windows). Tests
  are now OS-aware (`os.path` / basenames).
- Windows file-locking: `run_tests.py` `make_clean_workdir()` and
  `test_session_keeper.py` `_isolated_cwd()` now close logging
  handlers before temp-dir teardown and pass `ignore_cleanup_errors`,
  so an open log file no longer crashes the run with `WinError 32`.
- VPN provider tests now force the offline path deterministically
  (they previously depended on the API being unreachable, which is
  false on a networked Windows box).
- SOCKS test accepts a Windows connection-reset as a disconnect.
- test_js_smoke.py wrote JS to a temp file with Path.write_text() and
  no encoding= - cp1252 on Windows, which fails on non-Latin-1 chars
  in app.js. Now writes (and decodes node's output) as UTF-8. This
  surfaced once Node was installed; before, the test only skipped.
- test_extension_live.py now requests Chromium's new headless mode
  (--headless=new) so MV3 extension service workers can register.
  Falls back to a clean skip on Chromium builds that still don't
  support it, so it can never become a hard failure.

**`run_tests.py` improvements**

- `--json` / `--summary` flags are now case-insensitive (`--SUMMARY`
  works).
- `--summary` writes a self-contained plain-text `SUMMARY.txt`;
  `--json` writes `test_results.json`. Both are paste-ready for
  failure analysis.

**Duplicate routes resolved**

The two same-method route collisions that v3.62.0's contract tests
documented as KNOWN_DUPLICATES are now fixed:
- `/m` and `/m/` — the dead `mobile_view()` handler (163 lines of
  superseded server-side HTML building, shadowed by `serve_mobile_view`
  plus the client-fetch mobile.html) was deleted.
- `/api/sites/<sid>/export` — `api_export()` (download-history CSV /
  URL export) was unreachable behind `api_sites_export()` (config
  export). It was moved to its own URL,
  `/api/sites/<sid>/history/export`, so both features now work.
  Clients wanting history export must use the new path.
The contract test's KNOWN_DUPLICATES allowlist is now empty, and two
regression guards were added so neither collision can silently return.

**Test deltas**

- 3391 pass / 0 fail / 3 skip on Linux; 3392 / 0 / 3 expected on
  Windows once the js_smoke fix lands. No regressions.

## v3.62.0 — 2026-05-16

Test-hardening release plus a self-hosted test-fixture site. No
behaviour change to the app itself — this release is about making the
app verifiable.

**Test hardening — 134 new tests (3232 → 3366)**

Four new test buckets, none of them happy-path padding:
- `test_edge_phase7_13.py` (36) — malformed input, wrong HTTP methods,
  boundary values, corrupt in-memory state across every Phase 7–13
  endpoint.
- `test_contracts.py` (16) — cross-cutting invariants: JSON-shape,
  route-registry uniqueness, widget-catalog Python/JS lockstep,
  version/CHANGELOG/health consistency.
- `test_preflight_checklist.py` (19) — environment sanity: core
  imports, DB init, migrations, static assets.
- `test_negative.py` (19) — things that *should* fail, failing
  correctly (validators rejecting bad configs, etc.).
- `test_fixture_site.py` (44) — covers the new fixture site (below).

**Two route-duplicate findings (documented, not yet fixed)**

The contract tests surfaced two same-method route collisions where one
handler is dead code — the same class as the resolved `/metrics` bug:
- `/m` and `/m/` — `serve_mobile_view` shadows `mobile_view`.
- `/api/sites/<sid>/export` — config-export shadows history-export.

Both are recorded as `KNOWN_DUPLICATES` allowlist entries in
`test_contracts.py` with a self-cleaning companion test. They need a
maintainer decision on which handler to keep; no code was changed.

**New: `tools/fixture_site.py` — self-hosted test-fixture site**

A standalone Flask app (no dependency on the bulk_downloader package)
that serves synthetic pages shaped like real download targets — HTML
matching the selector shapes in `templates.py`. It exists so adapters,
the download path, and throttle/error handling can be tested against
something deterministic instead of live sites.
- 5 login prefixes: `/formauth` (form+cookie), `/basicauth`,
  `/tokenauth` (Bearer/API-key), `/csrfauth` (two-step), VIP4K-style.
- 5 download techniques: `/direct`, `/range` (206 partial/resume),
  `/redirect` (302 chain), `/lazy` (JS-injected URL), `/hls`.
- 5 player-markup prefixes matching `templates.py` selector shapes.
- Throttle simulation (`/flaky` 429s under concurrent load).
- A fault injector with a management UI at `/_control`: 15 fault
  types (connection-lost, timeout, 404/410/500/502/503/429,
  slow-trickle, truncate, corrupt, redirect-loop, flapping, refused,
  resume-fail), each path-scopable with a times budget. A fault armed
  with no path applies to all requests. `/_control` has no access
  control — it's a localhost test tool.

All synthetic: placeholder content, tiny generated MP4s. It mimics the
*structure* of sites, never their content — no live site involved.

Helper scripts: `start_fixture_site.bat` launches the fixture site;
`start_fixture_site2.bat` launches the second fixture site;
`run_all_tests.bat` runs the full suite; `run_test.bat` runs one test
file. `run_tests.py` gained `--json` and `--summary` flags that write
a machine-readable result file / plain-text SUMMARY.txt for analysis.

**New: `tools/fixture_site2.py` — second test-fixture site**

A second standalone mock site covering the awkward shapes the first
fixture doesn't: infinite-scroll catalogs, JSON / GraphQL-style APIs,
Cloudflare-style challenge interstitials, subscription paywalls, and
single-page-app shells. Same safety profile — synthetic content only,
no fault injector, no command surface. +24 tests.

**#98 — Universal bdctl `--json` output mode**

Before: only 3 of bdctl's 44 subcommands accepted `--json`. Now every
subcommand and sub-subcommand does. Rather than editing 44 `add_parser`
calls by hand, a post-hoc loop walks `subparsers.choices` after the
parser is built and adds `--json` to any parser that doesn't already
declare it — including the nested sub-subcommand parsers
(learned/dedup/site/library/scrapers).

A new `_maybe_json(data, args)` helper centralizes the behaviour: if
`--json` was passed it prints `data` as indented JSON and returns True
so the handler returns early; otherwise it returns False and the
handler does its normal human-readable formatting. It's wired into the
modern command set — health, audit, pause-all, resume-all, doctor —
which previously had no machine-readable output. Exit-code semantics
are preserved: `health --json` still exits 1 when degraded.

Commands that don't yet route through `_maybe_json` still *accept*
`--json` (no "unrecognized arguments" error) — a later sub-release can
wire the remaining legacy handlers.

Standalone script that runs every site in sites_config.json through the

**#99 — Daemon-only mode (`BD_HEADLESS=1`)**

When set, the startup banner collapses to a single line suitable for a
systemd / Task Scheduler / nohup log, and the LAN-IP probe is skipped.
The app behaves identically otherwise — this is a presentation change
for unattended deployments.

**#55 — One-shot mode (`BD_EXIT_WHEN_IDLE=1`)**

A background watcher polls every runner; once all queues are empty and
nothing has been active for the grace period (default 30s, override via
`BD_IDLE_GRACE_SECONDS`), the process exits 0. Lets BD be driven from
cron or a script: queue URLs, run BD, it exits when done. The grace
period guards against a false exit in the gap between consecutive jobs.

**#125 — Stuck-job watchdog (`GET /api/jobs/stuck`)**

The runner already detects stuck jobs internally; this surfaces them.
Scans every runner's job table for entries in an active state
(running/downloading/processing) whose `last_progress_at` is older than
`?minutes=` (default 30). Pending jobs are excluded — they're waiting
their turn, not stuck. Read-only; sorted most-stuck-first.

**#79 — Token-rotation script (`tools/rotate_token.py`)**

Standalone script that rotates the API bearer token: generates a fresh
256-bit URL-safe token, atomically writes it into `app_config.json`'s
`auth_token` (preserving every other key), and prints it. `--print-only`
generates a token without writing the file (for seeding `BD_AUTH_TOKEN`
instead). Warns if a `BD_AUTH_TOKEN` env override would shadow the file.

Phase 7 of the v3.48+ roadmap: bd-doctor. A diagnostics companion that
runs an on-demand health pass over the install and pattern-matches
failure errors. This folds in the roadmap's high-priority "selftest
extension" item — but as a separate `doctor.py` module rather than
bloating `selftest.py`, which runs on every boot and must stay fast.

**New module: `bulk_downloader/doctor.py` (~280 LOC)**

Four diagnostic groups:
- `environment_checks()` — Python version, ffmpeg / ffprobe presence
  and version (probed via subprocess), Playwright. Missing ffmpeg is a
  WARN, not a FAIL — the features that need it degrade gracefully.
- `dependency_checks()` — every optional dependency reported with a
  friendly name and a plain installed/not-installed, plus what each
  one unlocks ("curl_cffi: TLS-impersonating HTTP downloads"). A
  missing optional dep is OK-level, never a warning wall.
- `cookie_freshness(sites_config)` — per-site `cookie_file` age. A
  cookie older than the threshold (default 14 days) is flagged before
  the runner hits an auth-expiry mid-download; a configured-but-missing
  cookie file is a WARN.
- `diagnose_failure(error_message)` — pattern-matches a failed /
  needs_review error string against known signatures (rate-limit,
  captcha, auth expiry, selector drift, disk pressure, network,
  content-removed) and returns `{matched, cause, suggestion,
  confidence}`. Specific signatures are ordered before general ones,
  so "waiting for selector … timed out" reads as selector drift, not a
  generic network timeout. An unrecognized error still gets a generic
  next-step rather than a confident wrong answer.

`run_diagnostics()` runs the first three groups and returns a report
shaped exactly like `selftest.run_all` — `{ok, checks, summary,
elapsed_ms}` — so the same UI code renders both.

**API: 2 new endpoints**

- `GET  /api/doctor` — full diagnostic pass for the Status tab.
- `POST /api/doctor/diagnose` — pattern-match a failure. Body takes
  either `{error: '...'}` or `{hid: <history_id>}` to look the error
  text up from a history row.

**bdctl: `bdctl doctor`**

- `bdctl doctor` — runs the full pass, prints a per-check report, exits
  0 if no FAILs / 1 otherwise (usable in a monitoring script).
- `bdctl doctor --diagnose "<error text>"` — just the failure
  diagnoser; prints cause + confidence + suggested next step.

**On bd-tray**

The session roadmap paired bd-doctor with a "bd-tray" system-tray app.
That needs OS-native GUI libraries and can't be meaningfully built or
tested in a headless environment, and the project KB roadmap
(`07_ROADMAP.md`) doesn't list it — so it's deliberately not included
here. bd-doctor is the testable, roadmap-aligned half of Phase 7.

**Test deltas**

- 3159 pass / 3 skip / 0 fail (+20 new Phase 7 tests covering every
  diagnostic group, all twelve failure signatures, the specific-beats-
  general ordering, the empty-input guard, and both API endpoints
  including history-id lookup). No regressions.



Phase 6 of the v3.48+ roadmap: power-user tooling. The `bdctl` CLI and
the in-app command palette are both mature, but neither surfaced any of
the features added in Phases 1–5. This release wires the Phase 1–5
surfaces into `bdctl` so the whole feature set is scriptable.

**Nine new `bdctl` commands**

- `bdctl health` — hits the `/api/health` probe. Exit code 0 if
  healthy, 1 if degraded — drop it in a cron heartbeat or a monitor.
  Prints version, uptime, queue depth, active downloads, DB status.
- `bdctl pause-all` / `bdctl resume-all` — pause or resume every
  site's runner in one call (the Phase 2 endpoints).
- `bdctl audit [--limit N]` — print the recent config-change audit log
  (Phase 1) as a table: when, action, target, actor.
- `bdctl library stats` — collection size, total bytes, watched /
  unrated / missing counts, top studios (Phase 3).
- `bdctl library scan [--root DIR ...] [--wait]` — kick off a library
  folder scan; `--wait` blocks and streams progress until done.
- `bdctl library scan-status` — current/last scan state.
- `bdctl site export <site> [--out FILE] [--include-secrets]` —
  export a site config (Phase 5). Secrets stripped unless asked.
- `bdctl site import <file|->` — import a config as a new site.
- `bdctl site validate <file|->` — dry-run validate a config file
  without importing; exit 0 valid, 1 invalid. Accepts either a raw
  config or a full export envelope.

`library` and `site` are grouped subcommands (`bdctl library …`,
`bdctl site …`); invoking either without a subcommand prints its help
and exits 1, matching the existing `learned` / `dedup` / `scrapers`
pattern.

**Five new command-palette entries**

The in-app command palette (Ctrl+K) gained entries for the Phase 1–5
surfaces, so they're reachable without the mouse:
- *Go to Library* — jumps to the Phase 3 library tab.
- *Scan library folders* — kicks off a library scan via
  `/api/library/scan/start`.
- *Pause all sites* / *Resume all sites* — the Phase 2 bulk runner
  controls.
- *Export selected site config* — downloads the selected site's config
  JSON (Phase 5).

The async entries use the existing `window.csrfFetch` wrapper (so the
CSRF handshake is honored) and `window.bdToast` for feedback — no bare
`fetch` that would skip CSRF.

**Test deltas**

- 3139 pass / 3 skip / 0 fail (+17 new Phase 6 tests). Fifteen drive
  `bdctl` as a subprocess against a live in-process Flask server,
  exercising the full argparse → command → HTTP → endpoint path; two
  are static checks that the command-palette entries are present and
  use the known helpers.
- The test harness pins cwd to the server's home before every request:
  the custom runner chdir's to a fresh temp dir per test, and the live
  server resolves its SQLite path relative to cwd — without the pin,
  requests hit an empty DB and 500 with "no such table". This is a
  test-harness fix, not a product change.



Phase 5 of the v3.48+ roadmap: site-editor UX. The site config modal is
a large form, and until now the only feedback on a bad config was a 400
on save. This release adds dry-run validation, config export/import,
and a change-preview diff.

**New module: `bulk_downloader/site_editor.py` (~360 LOC)**

Pure logic over plain config dicts — no Flask, no DB — so it's cheaply
unit-tested:
- `validate_config(cfg)` — checks required fields, URL well-formedness,
  numeric ranges (15 fields with explicit min/max), string-type
  coercion, login/credential/selector consistency, filename-template
  brace balance, proxy scheme, scheduling consistency. Returns
  `{ok, errors, warnings}` — errors block a save, warnings flag
  likely-but-not-certain mistakes.
- `export_config(cfg, include_secrets=False)` — portable JSON envelope
  (`schema` marker + app version + timestamp). Secrets stripped by
  default; the stripped field names are recorded in `_had_secrets` so
  the operator knows credentials need re-entering on import.
- `import_config(payload, known_fields)` — validates the envelope,
  drops any key not in `known_fields` (a hostile or stale import can't
  smuggle unexpected keys into `sites_config.json`), runs full
  validation on the result.
- `diff_config(old, new)` — field-by-field change preview. Secret
  fields report `(set)`/`(empty)` booleans, never values.

**API: 4 new endpoints**

- `POST /api/sites/validate` — dry-run validate a config, no save. The
  editor calls this on field changes for inline feedback.
- `GET  /api/sites/<sid>/export` — download a portable config JSON.
  `?include_secrets=1` for a personal backup; default strips them.
  Sent with `Content-Disposition` so the browser saves a file.
- `POST /api/sites/import` — import an exported config as a NEW site.
  Validates, drops unknown keys, audits the create.
- `POST /api/sites/<sid>/diff` — preview what a proposed config change
  would alter, field-by-field, against the current saved config.

**Bug fixed during development**

`diff_config` initially diffed the union of old+new keys. Because the
site editor sends a *partial* config (only the form fields, not all
~150 config keys), every absent field showed as "removed" — a single
edit produced 159 spurious diff entries. Fixed: `diff_config` now only
considers keys present in `new`. A key absent from `new` means "this
edit doesn't touch it"; a genuine removal is the operator clearing a
field, which arrives as the key present-but-blank.

**Test deltas**

- 3122 pass / 3 skip / 0 fail (+33 new Phase 5 tests covering every
  validation rule, the export/import round-trip, secret-stripping,
  the partial-config diff bug, and all four API endpoints). No
  regressions.



Packaging fix. The v3.48–v3.51.0 release zips were built with an
incomplete file manifest — the top-level entry point and its support
files were omitted, so `install_windows.bat` aborted at step 1 with
`downloader_ui.py not found next to this script`. This release ships a
corrected zip and fixes the root cause so it can't recur.

**Release-zip manifest corrected**

The zips were missing every top-level file the installer and runtime
need: `downloader_ui.py` (the entry point), `bdctl.py`, `preflight.py`,
`downloader.spec`, `requirements.txt`, `requirements-optional.txt`,
`uninstall_windows.bat`, `sites_config.example.json`, `LICENSE`,
`SETUP.md`, `CHANGELOG_archive.md`. Only `bulk_downloader/` and a few
others were included. The corrected zips contain the full manifest as
documented in `08_BUILD_DEPLOY.md`, and explicitly exclude operator
state (`app_config.json`, `downloader_history.db`, the `.integrity_*`
/ `.fts_optimize_last` runtime sentinels) and — for the user zip —
the dev-only `install_dev.bat` / `requirements-dev.txt`.

**Installer version banner — fixed root cause**

`install_windows.bat` and `install_dev.bat` both carried a hard-coded
`set "BD_VER=3.47.7"`. `08_BUILD_DEPLOY.md` step 1 states the version
should be bumped in exactly one place (`bulk_downloader/__init__.py`)
and claims the installers derive it from there — but they did not; the
literal had simply gone stale, which is why a v3.51.0 install showed a
"v3.47.7" banner. Both `.bat` files now derive `BD_VER` at runtime:

    for /f "tokens=2 delims== " %%V in (
      'findstr /b /c:"__version__ " "%~dp0bulk_downloader\__init__.py"'
    ) do set "BD_VER=%%V"

`%~dp0` resolves to the script's own directory regardless of the
working directory, and the `findstr` pattern's trailing space excludes
any `__version_info__`-style line. Falls back to `unknown` only if the
package file is genuinely absent. The build doc's "bump in exactly one
place" instruction is now actually true.

Both `.bat` files remain pure ASCII with CRLF line endings, per the
build-doc invariants.

**No code changes** — `bulk_downloader/` is byte-identical to v3.51.0.
Test suite unchanged at 3089 pass / 3 skip / 0 fail.



Phase 4 of the v3.48+ roadmap: dashboard widgets. The dashboard widget
system gains a sixth category — Collection — that surfaces the library
and audit data added in Phases 1 and 3. Until now that data was only
reachable by opening the Library tab or hitting the audit API directly;
now it can be pinned to the at-a-glance dashboard like any other KPI.

**Eight new "Collection" widgets**

The widget catalog grows from 21 to 29 KPIs. New `collection` category:
- `lib_total` — total files in the library
- `lib_size` — total bytes across the collection (formatted)
- `lib_watched` — share of the library marked watched, with a meter
- `lib_unrated` — files with no star rating yet
- `lib_missing` — library rows whose file is gone from disk (warns
  amber when non-zero)
- `lib_recent` — new library entries in the last 7 days
- `lib_top_studio` — most-represented studio in the collection
- `audit_recent` — count of audited config changes in the last 24h

All eight respect the existing widget machinery: pinnable to global or
per-site scope, sm/md/lg sizing, drag-to-arrange, the category filter
in the widget picker.

**Data collection** (`app_widgets_api.py`)

`_collect_data()` gains a library + audit collector. `library_stats()`
provides the file/size/watched/missing/unrated counts and the
by-studio aggregate in one cheap pass (indexed columns). A direct
`COUNT(*)` on `library.added_at` gives the 7-day recent count, and a
`COUNT(*)` on `audit_log.ts` gives the 24h config-change count. Every
collector is soft-wrapped — a missing table (e.g. `audit_log` before
any audited write) just leaves the widget rendering "—" rather than
500ing the dashboard.

**Empty-library safety**

`lib_watched` percentage math guards against division by zero — an
empty library reports 0.0%, not a crash.

**Catalog validation** (`widgets_config.py`)

`VALID_WIDGET_IDS` extended with the eight new ids. The Python set and
the JS `WIDGETS` array stay in lock-step; the drift-detection test
enforces set equality both directions.

**Test-suite hygiene**

The widget drift test previously hard-coded "21 widgets" as a literal.
Per the project's no-hard-coded-counts principle, it now derives the
expected count from `len(VALID_WIDGET_IDS)` and additionally checks
that the JS `WIDGETS` array contains no duplicate ids — a more
meaningful invariant that won't need editing every phase.

**Test deltas**

- 3089 pass / 3 skip / 0 fail (+10 new Phase 4 tests: catalog presence
  in both Python and JS, the `collection` category, the watched-%
  math, the empty-library zero-division guard, the audit count, the
  top-studio aggregate, and the end-to-end `/api/widgets/data`
  response). The one drift test that hard-coded 21 was rewritten, not
  counted as a regression.



Phase 3 of the v3.48+ roadmap: the library tab. The collection browser
— one row per file-on-disk the app knows about, populated both forward
(downloads) and backward (folder scans of existing files).

**Library tab (new)**

A sixth top-level tab. Card-grid browser with:
- Search across title / performer / studio / notes
- Filter by site, watched/unwatched
- Sort by newest, largest, title, rating
- Per-card: watched toggle, 1–5 star rating (click-to-rate), tagging,
  reveal-in-file-manager, delete (with optional file removal)
- Stats strip: file count, total size, watched count, unrated count,
  missing-file count
- Cursor-paginated "Load more" — O(log N) regardless of collection size
- Folder-scan launcher with live progress polling

**New module: `bulk_downloader/static/library.js` (~470 LOC)**

Drives the `#tp-library` panel. Lazy-loads on first tab open + refreshes
on every subsequent open. All actions go through the `/api/library/*`
endpoints. Re-themeable via `app.css` design tokens.

**Backend** (`bulk_downloader/library.py`, ~770 LOC — substantially
pre-existing, completed + corrected this release)

- `library_record()` — forward path: runner records completed downloads;
  backward path: scanner records files found on disk. Idempotent —
  `file_path` is UNIQUE, second insert updates in place.
- `library_browse()` — filterable, sortable, cursor-paginated. Whitelisted
  sort keys (no f-string user input).
- `library_set_watched/_rating/_notes`, `library_delete` (optional file
  removal), `tag_upsert/_list/_delete`, `library_add_tag/_remove_tag`,
  `library_stats`, `library_orphans`, `library_missing`.
- Background scanner: `scan_start/_status/_cancel`, walks roots, hashes/
  sizes video files, reconciles with existing rows + history.

**Bug fix: `tag_delete` cascade**

`tag_delete` relied on `ON DELETE CASCADE`, but SQLite doesn't enforce
foreign keys unless `PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON` (which BD doesn't set
globally — it has perf side effects). Now explicitly deletes
`library_tags` junction rows before the tag row.

**Test-runner improvements** (`run_tests.py`)

The minimal pytest-compatible runner gained real fixture support so the
v3.50 library tests (which use pytest's `monkeypatch` + `tmp_path` +
autouse fixtures) run correctly:
- `_MonkeyPatch` shim hoisted to module scope; added `chdir()` and
  `syspath_prepend()`.
- `@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)` detection — autouse fixtures are now
  discovered and invoked generator-style (setup → test → teardown) per
  test, with proper reverse-order teardown.
- Fixed a kwarg-leak bug where fixture-only parameters (`monkeypatch`)
  were incorrectly passed to test functions that didn't declare them.

**Schema migrations (v1–v6)**

Six migrations registered in `migrations.py`, all verified through the
v3.48 dry-run system (`apply_pending(dry_run=True)` against an in-memory
schema clone) before landing:
- v3 `create_library_table` — 21-column `library` table + 8 indexes
- v4 `create_tags_tables` — `tags` + `library_tags` junction
- v5 `add_history_library_back_ref` — `history.library_id` column +
  index for one-hop history→library navigation
- v6 `add_history_removed_at` — soft-delete column on history
Existing installs upgrade in place; the `library` table backfills from
the history table on first folder scan.

**API: `/api/library/*` (17 endpoints)**

`browse` (cursor-paginated, filterable), `<id>` GET/DELETE, `<id>/watched`,
`<id>/rating`, `<id>/notes`, `<id>/tags` POST + `<id>/tags/<name>` DELETE,
`stats`, `tags` list, `tags/<id>` DELETE, `missing`, `orphans` (GET — the
new v3.50 variant, distinct from the legacy POST endpoint of the same
path), `scan/start`, `scan/status`, `scan/cancel`. Scan-root paths run
through the same `_validate_path` allowlist as `cookie_file`.

**Forward-path hook**

`db_log()` is the single chokepoint for "a job changed state". When
status is `done` and a filename is present, it now also calls
`library_record()` — so every completion site in `runner.py` feeds the
library without N individual call-site edits. Bidirectional link:
`library.history_id` ↔ `history.library_id`. `failed` / `needs_review`
rows correctly create nothing.

**Lazy schema-ensure**

Every public `library.py` function calls an idempotent `_ensure_schema()`
that runs `db_init()` + `apply_pending()` once. Lets the library module
work in unit tests and direct-API contexts without a full app boot.

**Test deltas**

- 3079 pass / 3 skip / 0 fail (+44 new Phase 3 tests: migrations,
  `library_record` idempotency, browse filters + cursor pagination,
  tag CRUD + cascade, watched/rating/notes, delete with/without file
  removal, orphan detection, scanner idempotency + missing-mark +
  decoy-skip, every API endpoint, and the `db_log`→`library_record`
  forward path). No product regressions.
